I really didn't care for this book.  It was quite boring.  I finished it only because it was so short.  George takes Millie as a mail order bride at the urging of some of the women at his church because six months after his wife's death they can see that he desperately needs help with his four children (and quite frankly they are tired of being the ones to give him that help!)Millie lives in an orphanage where she has been since childhood.  She is almost eighteen and it is time for her to leave, but she has nowhere to go.  The director of the orphanage gives Millie a stack of letters from men looking for mail order brides and tells Millie to "pick one."  After reading all the letters Millie chooses George.Unfortunately, George, a 26 year old widower with four children, is looking for a mother for his children.  Millie responds to George's letter.  She meets all his requirements for a bride except one, so she lies. George and Millie meet at the altar when they are about to take their vows.  George shows up in his dirty work clothes for the ceremony.  After they are married George hardly says a word to Millie before returning to the farm and getting back to his chores.  As the days go by George and Millie exchange a few words and here and there.  They don't really spend any significant time together.  After being together for two weeks they are professing their love to each other (Please note that up until this point there has been no intimacy between the two and Millie has been sleeping with George's two daughters.).I was completely flabbergasted as I figured I must have missed something (and I had....it was the romance).The book is supposed to be a Christian historical romance, but it was completely missing the romance element.  The writing was ok, nothing outstanding.  As for the characters they were pretty much one dimensional.  I have no idea what Millie or George look like, except that George has brown hair, green eyes and a scruffy beard, ugh!  The story was told completely from Millie's point of view.....by which I mean we are privy to her thoughts and emotions, but we are given no information from George's POV.  Therefore, the only way we know what George is thinking or feeling is by what he says.  When he told Millie that he loved her I was completely bowled over, because at that point I wasn't even sure he liked her very much, much less love!I also couldn't see why Millie was in love with George.The only thing made clear by the story was that George helped guide Millie towards being a good Christian.  This story read more like a sermon about two people who happend to get married than as a romance about two people whose love grows with their faith.  I've read a number of Christian romances where the authors manage to interweave the Christian aspect in the story in such a way that it has a powerful impact without overwhelming the story.  That's absolutely not the case here.Bottom line, I would not recommend this book.  Happy reading!

What a good book! You don't see many romance/women's fiction titles that take on subjects like this so unflinchingly, but maybe more should. I liked how Ms. Talley was able to entertain and educate me at the same time. I learned a lot about having a child with Down Syndrome, such as the expected delay in milestones, and also the incredible strides that people can make with the help of loving family members and dedicated medical professionals. Ethan and Lauren were an easy couple to root for, and I completely understood Lauren's "once bitten, twice shy" approach after the way her husband treated her. This is not a conventional romance where a man sweeps a woman off her feet.I think that anybody who gives this book a chance will enjoy it, and will find that it sticks with you longer than a typical romance.

All of Me is a short story that is part of the Dreamspinner Press Daily Dose “Mended” Anthology 2014.Able and Kai are destined to be together.  Their parents, both Alphas of their packs, stepped outside the norm for wolf shifters and became best friends.  They thought it would be a good idea if their children were bonded mates as it would bring strength to both packs.  With this in mind, Abel and Kai were bonded before they were even born.  Even though there was a five year age difference between them, it did not stop the bond that they felt for one another and their love and friendship grew as they approached adulthood.Per custom, Abel and Kai must wait until Kai turns eighteen before they can complete the mating bond. This does not stop them from secretly keeping in contact with one another and planning for the day they will be mates.  When Kai’s father dies, Kai is still too young to take his role as Alpha.  His mother remarries, then when tragedy strikes again, Abel does not hear from Kai for over a year.  He is concerned but thinks it is due to Kai grieving. He waits until Kai turns eighteen before deciding he is going to go to him and find out what is happening so they can then finish the bonding.  When he arrives at Kai’s home, what he finds shatters his dreams and he leaves without even asking why.For ten years he leads his pack alone, always wondering why his mate betrayed him, until one day an unexpected visitor arrives at the pack house demanding to speak with Abel and opens old wounds that have never healed.  When he is asked to help Kai, can he put those feelings aside?All of Me is an interesting take on Alpha mating/bonding and pack politics.  It moves quickly, as it is a short story rather than a full length novel, and pulled me into the world and the relationship between Able and Kai.  The story is told from Abel’s point of view and although it has some serious and tragic events, it is interspersed with the humor that I have come to associate with this author.  The lack of communication between them was a little frustrating but the reuniting and rekindling of their love for one another was sweet.  The story had some fun secondary characters, I especially enjoyed Kelly, Kai’s younger sister and Ben, Abel’s youngest brother.Overall, I enjoyed how the story unfolds, and how the relationship develops.  I was also very happy with how the epilogue wrapped up the story.Originally posted at "Live Your Life, Buy The Book"
summary: Perfectly wrapped (up) little gift of a story!

Brian O’Hare weaves a spellbinding tale in this Irish thriller.  Jim Sheehan, a Chief Inspector, investigates a series of grisly murders committed by a radical, ruthless killer who appears to be driven by an unstoppable religious fanaticism.  The plot unfolds with a myriad of intriguing characters, clever crime scene portrayals, and a fascinating theological undercurrent.Sheehan’s character is multi-faceted, and his emotional arc drives the story.  The brisk pace carries the reader along, and O’Hare skillfully provides a balance of witty interaction between the detectives and an in-depth forensic approach to the investigation.  Thought-provoking, emotional, and gut-wrenching, The Doom Murders is an exceptional crime thriller and a must-read for any thriller lover.

Contol is a joint effort by two authors:  Mary Calmes and Cardeno C.  I've read both of their works and enjoyed them.  Control is the story of a bear shifter Robert and his meeting Vy, a hawk shifter.  The focus is on them and how their relationship advances and retreats as they become friends as well as mates.I read a lot of shifter stories and one topic that comes up from time to time is 'instant mating' -- The sniff, mine, and mate 'romance' which really isn't romantic at all.  CONTROL has an interesting take on shifter mates.  Both men don't know what to expect in the mating process and come at it differently.  Robert, the bear, wants to know Vy as a person, as a friend, and go from there.  Vy is more aware of his other half and has conflicting feelings when Robert doesn't acknowledge the mate drive.  Since Robert doesn't shift into his bear, of course he won't know Vy is his mate.  So it's an interesting concept and very well done.  Kudos.There were a few things that distracted from my enjoyment.  It seemed like each chapter was written in a different point of view from the last.  Vy and Robert kept interchanging so one would be speaking, the other next, and back and forth and so on.  At times I got caught up in which arm was around who's shoulder and the use of 'he' and 'his' was used so many times I got confused as to which person was now talking.  I am a fast reader and I slightly remember it was Robert's POV right now, but I can't be completely sure, and my kindle is difficult to page back and double check. . . Because then I'd lose my place.  If I was to backtrack, I'd have to go back and figure out which chapter I'm in and then page forward, which I have done in the past, but not for this book.  So I ended up half the time not knowing who was talking and who was being talked about.  It was distracting and frustrating.I enjoyed hearing about Vy's flock and his interactions with them.  Even better was seeing their leader in a job, any job.  I can't tell you how many stories I've read where the alpha/leader doesn't have any means of support and lets his pack support him.  Not in this.  Vy is a construction worker, getting down and dirty - Think hard hat, sweat, and dust.I would have liked a bit more bear / hawk play time.  It was alluded to but never pursued.  At least not in details.  I mean finally Robert overcomes his bear and it's a big part of this story.  So it'd be nice to see the continuing result - Robert and his bear and interacting with his 'just recognized' mate in their animal forms.The angst from Robert's adoptive parents was a bit too over the top.  At this time Robert and Vy are friends and mates.  They've experienced a lot for a newly bonded pair.  You would think they'd talk over everything and not let in-laws get in the way.  Vy was a bit too bird brained about that whole thing.  It was really silly.I never did grasp if Vy's second in command, Louisa, was mated or just married to her husband.  The wording in the opening chapter made me think she's just shacked up with someone until her own mate arrives.  I also had that feeling with the way she treated her husband, not as she would treat a beloved mate.  *shrug*I never got a feeling on how large Vy's Ket is.  Sure there are tons of cars at a meeting and the house and yard are packed, but I wondered.  I seldom read about bird shifters.  I was curious.If this is the first in a series, I'd definitely check the next one.  But as this one, CONTROL stands, it needs better flow. That is surprising because so much of this story is between the two main characters, Robert and Vy.  The back and forth should flow on it's own.  - Dan's Wife
summary: M/M Shifter Story With A Few Flaws

This is an incredibly helpful book to read if you're wanting information on OCD.  As I read the description I found myself understanding OCD in a way I haven't before, for example how perfectionism comes into it, and how OCD and OCPD are distinctly different to each other.  The author then follows up with some incredibly practical advice on how to cope with and even down-grade OCD. He recommends CBT (Cognitive Behavioural Therapy), and as a huge fan of CBT myself I really enjoyed this advice section.  Very accessible and useful!I was really wanting to understand more on this topic so I could understand some other people in my life more – and this book was the perfect answer to that.  It goes into the relationship issues that come up between people who suffer OCD and others in their life, which I appreciated.  As an introduction to understanding OCD I definitely recommend this book.

“I woke up when I met Jamie. The world became louder, crazier, more exciting, and more achingly beautiful.”This. This is exactly how I felt about Jamie. Not only did Kate (his Katy) wake up, I did too. Jamie is one of my favorite book boyfriends – from his sweet and sexy nature to his vulnerabilities. I was a goner. Right in the beginning, Kate’s voice shines through the pages. I could feel her pain, her loss, and her depression. It was so easy to relate to her and that helped me connect with her story.Jamie barrels into her life (okay, she kind of does that to him…) and captures her attention and attraction when Kate goes to interview R.J. Lawson, the reclusive genius, who owns the winery where Jamie works.  I loved how Kate doesn’t pull punches with R.J. when she meets him and has a backbone. Life threw her some curve balls but she’s still strong in many ways. Jamie and the beauty of the vineyard brings that out even more.Renee Carlino has a beautiful, poetic way with words. I felt the same way with Sweet Thing and Sweet Little Thing. (I'd be remiss to not add I loved the inclusion of Will and Mia in this story! <3 ) It’s as if the story is more lyrics than manuscript. I love that about her writing along with the elements of fate and interconnectedness that are woven in, using secondary characters to enrich the story even further. Just Bob stole a big piece of my heart and if I rode the train every day, I’d hope to find someone like him to listen to share his wisdom.One thing in particular that had me turning pages and staying up late to read Nowhere But Here was the unexpected twist to the story. I was reading merrily along thinking it was following a more traditional storyline when I was hit with a part I didn’t see coming. It added so much more to the story. My heart ached for Kate and Jamie; for the hurdles they had to face; for the misunderstandings and the consequences. Yet, all of those combined with all of the other moments make this a must-read for me.
summary: Renee has a poetic way with words...so beautiful!

The mix in genes in Alphas Unleashed was 50/50  - two sci-fi romances and two paranormals. While I do read the occasional sci-fi romance, paranormal romances are my staple and I liked those the best. That said, it might be that since the sci-fi stories jumped straight into fairly complex, and apparently established worlds, they will probably work better for the fans of these series dying to get a peek at favorite supporting characters.It is rare for me to read an anthology in order - and I actually bought this for the My Immortals short -but I missed the table of contents when I looked, so first to last it was.Warrior's Heart -SE Smith - Smith's story was a twofer - two alien sisters each paired with one of two human brothers. This was a bit ambitious for the short space - I found one pair far more interesting and would have been happy with just their story instead of trying to squeeze into this story two sex scenes and two HEAs, plus cameos by characters who are obviously important in other books in the series. (Ok)Sealed with a Kiss - Mina Khan - This story had all the right stuff  - with the Djinn chef leading man and the heroine with a magical problem. And although I did like this, I really wish it had been longer to take advantage of all that setup and to allow for a more solid transition from what essentially was enemies to lovers. I do have to admit that I had WTH moment near the end too <spoiler>when they've just crisped the bad guy and then they are kissing- that gave me pause.</spoiler> (pretty good)Dead Drop - Carolyn Jewel - My Immortals -  Again this short had  a good enough setup that it could have easily been longer, but the transition in the relationship worked for me and Jewel still managed to deliver the intensity that made me a fan of her series even though I am pretty vanilla in my comfort zone  and the stories do have a touch of kink to due to inhuman/human 'couplings'. (I really liked it)Chimera Born - Michelle Callahan - The world building here is pretty complex for newbie me. There were definitely things I liked about this story - the hero assimilating memories of an elderly man's life, loves and losses -and I liked the heroine, so this would have probably worked better for me if I'd been familiar with this series.(ok plus)

Thank goodness for Laurie that she has a guardian angel who turns into her knight in almost shining armor! Forest Ranger Jeff Dawson is perceptive and not afraid to act. He manages to rescue Laurie only to have Eli snatch her once the felon pins the unlucky couple in an abandoned building in the ghost town of Grantsville.The good guys don't give up yet. Star Berkley had never seen the likes of Sir Edward. He was so deuced arrogant. He was so dashingly fashionable and just as insolent. Added to this, was the fact that he was the most handsome man she had ever come across in all her twenty years of life!Sir Edward, for his part, could do without the pert country airs of a chit like Miss Berkley. She was impish, plain-spoken and went about clothed in virtual rags, and obviously not his sort, which, was just as well for it seemed she had stolen the heart of his closest friend.And then—Sir Edward stumbled onto a most sordid secret: the Berkley's estate teetered on ruination, and brother and sister were being brutally blackmailed by a vile den of thieves. Sir Edward meant to save them if only Star would allow him to do so. She was determined to keep him and his help at arm's length, but he was just as determined to do otherwise.A clash of wills ensued and a web of passion flourished.Above is the description of the book and it sounded just up my alley.  I really really really wanted to like it but I couldn't.  First off, the cover... the book goes on and on about Star's ***short*** hair.  So it seems truly irresponsible to pick a cover with a woman with long flowing locks.  Just saying.As for this "web of passion." Uh huh.  No such thing.  The seduction was unconvincing and the sex boring. Boring.  One would almost think the author had as little experience as the heroine.Then there are the things I find inexcusable in an author and that is a failure to know the basics of the English language.  If you don't know how to punctuate, you have no business being a writer.  This author apparently chose to avoid the pitfalls of the over use of the comma with a decision to use no commas at all.  That just bugs the spit out of me.Another basic of the English language is vocabulary.  If a writer doesn't know what a word means, then the writer has no business using it.  This author consistently used the word "clamored" when she meant clambered.Even though this book was free for my kindle, I still feel cheated.  I seriously do not understand how some people get into print.  And if this is author is self-published, it is mistakes like these that give self-publishing its bad rep.

All in all a well written and enjoyable book. The hero is a stockbroker! Who would have thunk it?One of his favorite clients dies unexpectedly a week after marrying a gold-digger.  It turns out the investment account came from mob money and Matt, the stockbroker, is being pursued to return the funds. Plus of course the gold-digger comes after him for refund of commissions and damages.How Matt resolves his problems with the mob and the gold-dgger, and also works toward getting over some personal tragedies, is the story and somewhat enjoyable.A few annoyances -  1. The country in South America is Colombia, spelled with two "O"s. The author fell into the practice of spelling the country like the university in New York, Columbia. Amazon will let the author make this correction at no cost for future readers and usually will allow owners of copies to download a corrected version.2. There are entirely too many irrelevant mini-details. Such as - Matt is having lunch with his investigator and the author described an interruption by the waiter and lets us know that Matt ordered coffee. This annoyance adds zilch to the story. There are a lot more, especially restaurant and bar details. The bartender's response when the investigator ordered a glass of wine? Really?3. Plot fault 1 - NASD would not have seized all  his records and files based on just an allegation/complaint. At most they would have performed a "data copy" of his digital records and photocopies of his paper files.4. Plot fault 2 - When the mob insisted that he obtain the deceased client's portfolio, Matt merely had to give them the name, address and contact number of the gold-digger and her lawyer5. Remember Elmore Leonard's rules for writers, especially "Leave out the parts that readers skip over". Matt's dreams and his discussions with his therapist got wearisome. Enough already!6. Did Janet, the gold-digger, every get the estate? The last 20% or so of the book I was skipping chapters and may have missed that part of the resolution.
summary: A decent read, likable main character - could use substantial editing

He was bored since moving to this town and with few friends he needed some excitement. At school one of the teachers talks about the mine and that gets his heart pounding. But none of his new friends want to go. They are locals, they had heard the whispers about the mine--whispers about creatures or ghosts. And although no one really believes it, everyone avoids the mine.Tim is determined. He fakes being sick and kicks off from school. He has his bag packed with essentials he thinks he needs and off he goes.What fate awaits him? It may not be what you think.This is an interesting and fast paced book. It is a novella, after all. And it is a good real.4 out of 5 stars from me.

reviewText: After having read more than my fair share of paranormal romance stories about werewolves, vampires, and angels, the idea of a story centered around dragons had me intrigued.  I wasn't sure what to expect, but Liliana Hart's Drakan were far more mysterious, dark, and sexy than I expected. In an unforgiving and violent world like theirs, only the strong and determined survive, and emotions are a weakness that few can afford to feel.Rena was essentially stuck with her life.  Stuck between her dragon and human sides, stuck living with a father who hates her, stuck suffering from his wrath, and stuck with powerful gifts of the mind but lacking other abilities that she craves.  Unlike most of her kind, she doesn't want to forget about her human side, and her role as an Enforcer just makes her stand out even more.  She just doesn't seem to fit in anywhere, and even though she has this darker side that calls to her, there's a part of her that has a huge heart and wants desperately to be loved. She was a misfit in every way, and in every way the perfect heroine!"I couldn't transform into a dragon, but just because I couldn't make the change on the outside didn't mean my dragon wasn't inside me."  ~Rena, Loc 1177Rena's Drakan, banished to Earth when their Realm was destroyed eleven thousand years ago, believed wholeheartedly in the Prophecy.  It was their chance of restoring their Realm, but it was also a warning of what could happen if the one called the Destroyer is not stopped.  As Rena found herself right in the middle of the fight to find and put an end to the one who would become the Destroyer, she also found herself in the arms of Julian, the mouthwatering leader of the Belgian clan of Drakon who she couldn't seem to stay away from.  He was powerful, unrelenting, and lusting after Rena like nobody's business!!  Julian was the epitome of the alpha male with his cocky refusals to Rena pushing him away, and the passion between these two was HOT!! I thought the whole "sex on the ceiling" warning was just a joke, but it's not...and I'm so glad because WOW!  Rena tried hard to resist Julian's temptations, but between that crazy blue mating fire engulfing them and her human side falling for him, she was in for a struggle.  And the whole time I was thinking "why are you bothering to fight it??!!" because well, he's just that delish!!"You lie." His voice whispered across my skin.  "Your resistance wears thin."  He ran his hand over the swell of my breast, and it sent shivers down my spine. ~ Julian Loc 2108"I didn't want to hurt Julian, and my mind didn't want to love him.  My body, on the other hand, needed his flesh between my teeth and thighs more than I needed to breathe." ~Rena, Loc 2345The gruesome violence that is essentially the way of life for the Drakan definitely warred with Rena's good side.  Not knowing much about her mother, it's as if half of her is hidden even from herself.  As this secret side of her started to reveal itself, it became clear that she's going to be one hell of a force to be reckoned with. And she's going to need to be, because Liliana Hart didn't hold anything back and it's clear this is going to be a very bumpy ride!As far as the love triangle goes, I'm not sure what I think yet.  To be honest, Noah's character wasn't around much and didn't leave much of an impression with me.  He seems almost inconsequential to the story in this first book, and I really loved where things had the potential of going with Julian.  With an ending that leaves you wondering what the rather precarious future holds, it remains to be seen if this will be Noah's chance to make his mark.  I'm in for the long haul with this series either way, but in the meantime I know whose team I'm on!!  The Rena Drake series gets an absolute thumbs up from me, and I look forward to more from Liliana Hart!

reviewText: Always You is the story of Wrenn and Dalton, her history teacher.Sweet, sexy, beautiful, and downright heartbreaking at times, this book was what I needed after reading more conventional romances over the holiays.This story is more than just a forbidden love....student and teacher get together story. It's a story about healing and not taking life for granted, because each single day is a blessing. Life is precious. Yes, I know it's a cliche but it's true and we forget. We get caught up in the day to day and the little things that bring us down. Not so with this book.Wrenn and Dalton act much older than they are...the curveball life throws you will do that. I like how they handled their forbidden love and the eventual obstacles they encountered.Missy tackles something I've never read in a book so that was refreshing. Maybe I learned a little something.I wonder if there will be a sequel??? ♥

reviewText: Might be some spoilers here.Story 1) IMMORTAL OPS: Lukian and Peren--he's a were working for black ops, he's supposed to take out the target, Peren, but can't bring himself to do it.  Really interesting idea, not well written or executed, shallow characters.Story 2) CRITICAL INTELLIGENCE: Roi and Missy. Roi is number two to Lukian. Missy is a friend of Peren's, she's a supernatural and works for military ops but top secret. Roi is a romeo but Missy is not interested. He can't believe it. They piss each other off but are continually thrown together.  Again, really interesting idea, not well written or executed.Story 3) RADAR DECEPTION Green and Melanie. She's the third of the girlfriends trio, also a supernatural fae (none of them ever shared their super powers with each other) big plot hole--her brother is fae and works with Missy, Missy would have to assume Melanie is supernatural--never comes up. This one grated, Green was portrayed as such a bozo, the author did disservice in painting him a macho hero braniac but he couldn't get over his own selfish issues to step to save this woman's life that he's fiercely attracted to? Ugh.Story 4) STRATEGIC VULONERABILITY: Wilson and Kimberly. In the previous story it ends in the jungle and Wilson is supposedly killed by the master vampire while saving Melanie. No body, no mind connection with his brothers, so they jack around for a few days and then go home. What? Bad ass ops brothers, tight knit team, they give up in two days without proof? The trio of women can't accept it and escape back to the jungle of Brazil --all of them preggers--to see if they can find Wilson. Back to where the psycho maniac will do anything to impregnate supernaturals... In the meantime, Wilson is held by the diabolical maniac Krauss. He tortures Wilson daily. Then Krauss arrives with new prisoners, Kim is one of them. Turns out it's Wilson's mate and there's some interesting tension built in them trying to protect each other. It got stupid at this point. The worst is when they break out and they're in the jungle on the run. They stop to rest and Wilson hands her his gun while he's doing something...Excerpt:"Someone was shooting at them. He glanced around and then down at Kim.  'Stay down. I need to...Kim? Kim, honey?' She stared up at him with wide eyes. Kim?''Wilson!' The sound of this name being shouted by a familiar voice grabbed his attention. He turned and couldn't believe his eyes as he found three women standing in a row. Each one was armed to the teeth.The tallest, a white blonde, didn't seem as comfortable with the idea of being armed as the other two. 'Melanie? Peren? Missy?' Melanie grinned and rushed towards him. He pushed up and off Kim, still shocked the were there. His eyes widened as he realized what that meant. 'Oh s***, you three went against your mates.'A short raven-haired hottie with the ability to kill just about anything wagged her brows. 'We came to get your sorry ass. We missed it.' Melanie nudged her. 'Missy' She rolled her eyes. 'Fine, we missed you too'A medium height, auburn haired beauty smiled. 'How bad are you hurt?' He lifted his hand. Still in shock to see his friends had come for him. 'Just a scratch.,' Missy snorted. 'You must bleed like a madman then, unless the blood on you is from the chick who was holding a gun on you.' 'What?' he asked, glancing down and noticing for the first time that he was indeed covered in blood."...*********There's more comment from the trio and THEN he remembers his mate. Kim appears to be dead and yet he continues to have a rational conversation with the trio. Really? This is where I laughed out loud, and not in a good way.Overall Roth had interesting ideas but that's where it stopped. The first story was rough and sophomoric, stories 2 and 3 started to show more maturity and then it went to hell.

Elle St. James releases the first installment of a new series, BADLANDS.  Her heroes are two men who have been the best of friends their entire lives.  Both men are looking to share one woman for the rest of their lives.  That woman turns out to be Clarissa Barnes, a MAIL ORDER BRIDE FOR TWO.Clarissa Barnes had to leave her employment suddenly when she was accosted by her lecherous employer.  With no money and no way to get another job, she agrees to become a mail order bride.  Arriving in South Dakota, she is upset to find out that the man who paid her way West has already gotten married.  Help comes in the form of Logan Granger and Derek Brand.Derek Brand and Logan Granger have been friends their entire lives.  They also have been sharing lovers for quite a while.  Both men have decided that they are tired of being alone, so they have paid a lawyer to head east to find them a mail order bride.  Waiting on her train, the men are anxious but can't wait to become a family of three.  Finding out that their affianced bride jumped off of the train to her death sets heavy on them, but their luck hasn't completely run aground. It seems that the lovely lady who told them about their bride is also husbandless and has been left standing in the train station.  That's when they decide then and there to make her their bride.  All she has to do is agree.MAIL ORDER BRIDE FOR TWO made me blush more than once.  The men, Logan and Derek, are sin personified and totally dreamy.  Their treatment of Clarissa was tender, yet forceful.  They knew they wanted her - they knew she wanted them.  The rest fell into place quite nicely.I am addicted to ménage love stories. I can't help it. There is just something about being cherished by two alpha men that just makes me swoon. MAIL ORDER BRIDE FOR TWO by Elle St. James is such a book.  Provocative and naughty loves scenes mixed with a stirring plot made me enjoy MAIL ORDER BRIDE FOR TWO from cover to cover.Natalie S.

I had to wait a bit after the Hayle Coven series, all 26 or so books, until it all settled in my mind, and also wait for Meira's trilogy to be finished, so I could read all the books back to back.  Which is the best way to read a Patti Larsen series.  Even though she's one of the fastest writers in the Universe, even waiting a day is painful.So, I'm reviewing all three books here.I didn't think we'd get a really powerful story in those three books.  Hayle Coven is a hard act to follow.  I was wrong.  When Patti Larsen creates a world, she gives it all to you, and it all makes sense.  It's all beautiful, and ugly, and ordinary, just like real life.  To be fair, we already knew all the main characters, and already loved them, so Larsen's job was a lot easier.This series covers the four years that Meira holds the First Seat in Demonicon, although the first 3 and a half are touched upon, mostly in retrospect.  In this story, Meira becomes the Hayle sister she's meant to be, and grows into, develops, is given, or takes control of her Demonborn sorcery.  She becomes the most powerful demon in the world, and saves Demonicon from being splintered, and it's people enslaved.In these books, Larsen develops, fully, the idea of Demonicon: its history, its science, its politics.  We finally understand, (or at least I finally did) how the planes all originally became connected, what role the Drach played in the history of the Universe, (including some very interesting history that is personal to the Hayle sisters), the history of the Maji, and a whole lot about sorcerers.  All of this was just breezed over in the HC books, and I never had a grasp of it, or had any real understanding of who any of these players were.Larsen's world building skills are extraordinary.  She is also an economical writer.  She writes about what we need to know, writes it very well, but doesn't waste a lot of time or space on superfluous stuff.  She's a spare writer.  All her words count.  You can't really skim a Larsen book, or would want to.  She writes so fast, that there will be a lot waiting for you when you are done, and you won't want to spend time rereading.  It's also a pleasure to read her books.  Because of her style, her books are never boring, and yet, as a result of the fascinating interior life she grants her characters, you will own them.The primary series (that really is what Hayle Coven is) ripped me to pieces as it ended, and then brought everything together in a more satisfying way than it had been before.  (There were a few things that felt off.  Sebastian, for instance.  The end to his story just wasn't right.  It just wasn't.)  But, in Meira's book, I was thankful that I didn't have to be put to that test again.  Meira gets the right man, finally, and sets that House in order.So, you will want to read this if you want to move forward in the Hayle universe.  Syd DOES play a large part in these books.  There is no sign of Quaid, Mom and Dad, or any of the Coven people, other than the very first scene, a birthday party scene, which simply sets the tone the book opens to.  Syd is Meira's back-up in these books.  She plays a completely different role.  Sass is, of course,  there.  There couldn't be a Hayle book without him.  But, the book belongs to Meira.Don't hesitate on these.  They're all 5 Star additions to the Larsen library.  What I like to call "Pattiland".

reviewText: We are The Unofficial Addiction Book Fan Club, to know more about this book, go to the post in our website.REVIEW:Goddess Born is one of those historical novels, filled with magic and romance that would captivate you until the very first page.So back into the 1700s, Selah is a good and caring woman that tries to help people whenever she can. With a unique gift for healing, Selah has gained a lot of friends, but also has the attention of others who want her no matter the cost. And when Nathan proposes her and she refuses to marry this horrible man, he threatens her with saying she's a witch.But not all is lost. A cousin is coming to marry her and "liberate" her from Nathan and his future accusations, but an unfortunately he dies on the trip. Selah might seem to have a lot of bad luck, but with the help of a servant named Henry who poses as her husband, Selah will try to survive in her era when being a woman was not that easy, and with a gift like hers, it was simply deadly.Goddess Born is beautifully written and with such passion that makes the reader interested in every single detail of the story. The story is not also filled with the obvious romance that the synopsis promises or the amazing gift that Selah has, but also there's a constant "fear of living" what Selah was living and what was happening to her. There are also some unraveling moments during the story that were definitely not expected and that it makes the reader eager to know what's going to happen next.I loved how Kari Edgren brought the celtic mythology into this amazing story and I am beyond fascinated with everything in the story. I can say how happy I am to have had the chance to read this book. For those who like mythology and historical novels, this is definitely a must read. And even if you don't like as much historical novels, Selah and her story will make you a fan of them. If I were you, I wouldn't miss this story
summary: The Unofficial Addiction Book Fan Club Review: Amazing!

reviewText: * I received this novel in exchange for an honest review *Mirror X left me speechless...for a while. Having finished this thrilling Dystopian novel late into the night, I stayed awake for quite a while thinking about it. This was truly different for me, all in a good way, and left me wishing I had more of the story.Mirror X was full of surprises, each one, something I wasn't able to predict. The main character, Cassie, from our time, has been frozen and reawakened 1000 years later. Of course this being included in the synopsis, I expected her to find the world quite changed, and boy was it ever.She awakens to find herself in a genetics hospital that turns out to be far more sinister than what's on the general surface. We immediately meet Michael, a young doctor, who has been with Cassie throughout her dormant phase and now is with her as a guide into this new world.It doesn't take long before the author kicks Mirror X into full gear. We find out that this new world was plagued with a deadly disease that left women infertile and the current population is 100% made up of clones. This shocking revelation creates a serious burden for Cassie as she is able to assimilate on her own that she is the only woman on earth who is fertile.I applaud the author for creating such a moral dilemma and then tackling it beautifully. Of course Cassie is only 17 and is now faced with having to save to world by repopulation where the hospitals intentions are to use every single last one of her eggs to produce daughters who will grow up and face the same expectations that is being placed into Cassie's lap now.At first the expectation is offered to Cassie with the hope she will comply and understand the world's dilemma, but for a 17-year-old girl, that is frightening and expecting too much. Cassie feels the pains of the world's current issue, but having woke up 1000 years later, she is also left to grieve after everyone she's lost.We soon find out that Cassie really has no choice and was actually already artificially inseminated while she was comatose. Now discovering she is 3 months pregnant, Cassie is faced with having to become a mother. When she meets the father of her child, she finds the boy she liked 1000 years ago, now cloned, Travel, willing to raise a family with her. Oh, this part was so tragic. While having formed an attachment with the Dr. Michael, being presented the one boy from her past as the new father of her child...it was tragic on so many levels.Travel was a wonderful boy and it broke my heart when Cassie has baby Victoria only to realize the truth depth of the hospitals horrific intentions. Mirror X made me think of what I would do in Cassie's shoes. Being the only female on the planet would I willingly turn myself into a baby mill?These characters had such depth to them, all believable making me devour this novel in a few sittings. There are so many things to go over and review, but I cannot say enough how Mirror X is a novel that needs to be read and experienced for yourself.I loved the way the author introduces Michael in the very beginning and how it's obvious that Michael love's Cassie but to find out at the very end why he's so strongly connected to her...that's where the speechless part comes in and I won't give any spoilers on that. It was truly a shock for me and I did not see the connection coming.The novel leaves off with Cassie, Michael and baby Victoria escaping into a different region under the more sympathetic care of a different president. But there is so much more to the story I can't wait to find out where Cassie and Michael's story will go.Mirror X was such a wonderful novel to read. I would highly recommend this to lovers of YA Dystopian novels. It was fresh, original, moving, and left me thinking of the fate of all the characters long after I read the last page.

I really enjoyed the first book of this series and this one is of an equally high calibre. Darman can write. His research is good and the whole story comes to us with a sound historical basis combined with a fast moving plot full of heavy political intrigue, devious villainy and high voltage action. Pacorus is a truly engaging hero and the majority of his followers are also superbly developed characters. One of the things that bothered me here though, was the total breakdown of the character of Gallia; wife of Pacorus. From the feisty, wilful and fierce beauty of the first book, here she becomes headstrong, arrogant, aggressive and just plain stupid: her totally unbelievable histrionics become a seriously annoying side-show to the more believable events taking place. After each military engagement, regardless of the result, I was longing to see Gallia do us all a favour and finish up in a body bag. In this she disappoints, but I do hope in the third episode she is presented in a far more sensible role, or has the decency to die early.I also found that, despite the desperate, bloody battles taking place there seem to be absolutely no deaths of any of the central characters that form part of Pacorus's inner circle. Apparently, anyone close to the King automatically bears a charmed life.I take a exception to those reviewers on this page that complain about grammar/typos, etc. I complained about editing in the first book but found the editing here to be acceptable, certainly way above the usual Kindle standard.I solidly recommend this book and look forward to reading the last of this excellent trilogy.

Alice's passion is reading.  Reading transports her to elegant locales and privileged surroundings where she is pampered like a delicate and beautiful Queen.  She is a sun goddess of the desert, and  revels in  its warmth.  Alice's real life is anything but exotic.  Forced to forsake her job as a travel agent to be caregiver to her aging mother, life is a daily drudge of unpleasant smells, sponge baths, serving meals and dispensing pills.  She dreads taking her wheelchair-bound mother to doctor's visits, where she perceives the behavior of its medical personnel as saccharine and phony.  Every good result and positive outlook for her mother's survival is met by increasing despair from Alice.So, she turns to her beloved travel books as a form of survival.  In the escapism the books provide, she flourishes and thrives.  Indeed, they feed her, body and soul..literally.Author Nancy Christie chose a theme that many people can relate to as caregivers, and melded it with an unexpected twist.  Well done for this short with just the right amount of bite.

Love Has A Name (The Billionaire Brothers)Up and coming gym owner, Axia Blacksille, rolled her eyes as she talked on the phone with her best friend and wipe sweat off her face as she had just gotten off the treadmill. Earlier, Trudy had tried to eat a candy bar and they had a tug match of Trudy's purse.  It appeared Trudy's presentation had been on a thumb drive  that fell out of her purse, and she needed ASAP! Axia knew she had worked months on it and Trudy said she had fifteen minutes to get it to her.  Well don't that be all?  She had no time to shower and refresh herself so she jumped into her Jeep and hauled tail to Corded Solutions.  She parked and race to the entrance and asked the floor for her best friend and sprinted to the elevators.  Once the doors opened, she saw Trudy pacing and leaped toward her.  Just then a door opened and a gorgeous man stepped out...........Multi-billionaire, Lovello Nelson stepped out to get his assistant as he was tired of waiting her presentation as he had a business to run, yet when he saw Axia, he got pole axed!  She had a sculpted body that wouldn't quit and her shorts emphasized her round butt that was to die for.  She was the most perfect woman that he had ever seen and when she placed her hands on her hips and stood toe to toe with him he knew he had to have her at least for a while as he always got what he wanted!Book two is the story of Natlio's younger brother and the trials that Axia put him through when he didn't take no for an answer! Both Love and Axia were wealthy and got whatever they wanted, but Axia had vowed to never marry as when you did you had to submit to your husband and that wasn't happening! Ann Cole penned a very funny story and I found myself laughing so hard at the tiny woman taking on a six foot three man time and time again.

***I received a copy of Naked Submission in exchange for an honest review.***Naked Submission continues the story of Natalie's and Tanner's relationship. As with the first book, it moves at a fast pace, and if possible, the sex scenes are even STEAMIER!!! In fact, the reader gets to see exactly what Tanner's tastes in the bedroom are. You also get to see a bit into Tanner's past.I really enjoyed this book, but I have to say there were times I wanted to yell, scream, hit, and shake them both!!! I was so angry with Tanner when he took his rage at his stepmother out on Natalie, and I could have shaken her when she took him back so easily. I wanted to say, "Girl, get a life! Find somebody worthy of you!" However, I do realize that served the purpose of getting Tanner to open up to Natalie about his past. When a writer gets a reader to have emotions towards his or her characters, then they have been successful!I would like to see more of the relationship Natalie has with her family, especially her mother, since she is so ill. I do like the direction Jazzy and Ellis are going. Might we see more of that in the future?My favorite thing about Emily's writing is both characters' points of view. She incorporates it flawlessly in her writing...not separate chapters about each of them. It seems more natural this way. You are never guessing how Natalie and Tanner feel about one another. Looking forward to the next one!
summary: Naked Submission, Definitely Not Your Average Love Story!

Actual rating 4.5 stars. It's official, Jennifer has managed to write a whole new spin on angels. I thought that this novel would be based on all of the similar mythology that other angel books have, but JLA, writing as J. Lynn, has crafted a whole new world that explores a much seedier side to angels. While the cover wasn't my favorite (I liked the previous cover sooooo much better), it actually really sets the vibe for this novel and the main character herself.Lily, who is Nephilim, was a kick-ass, sarcastic character that I absolutely loved! While it did take me a little bit to actually get into her character, I did love her by the end of the novel. She's dedicated to her career of hunting down minions and Fallen, and she's extremely good at that job. One of the things I greatly enjoyed was her growth over the novel. She developed into a more open character that realized that there is more to the world than just black and white. There are shades of gray. Julian, holy mother of God! From the minute he was introduced (which is literally within the first couple of pages) I knew he was amazing!! There are literally no words to accurately describe him. So the best way is to say he is definitely swoon-worthy, mysterious, and makes your heart go pitter-patter oh so very fast. Anyone would be crazy not to love him!! The other side characters I liked as well, however the reason I couldn't give this 5 stars was because I wanted a bit more of Michael. I know that the story was focused on Lily, but since we are given bits from Michael's POV, I would have liked to see him have more of a presence in the story. Towards the end, he was definitely in the story full force, so that gives me hope for the next book in the series.The whole world was incredibly well written and very well described. I was a bit confused at first, but everything was cleared up almost immediately. So don't worry, you won't be sitting through the whole book wondering what the heck is going on, and what certain terms mean. Even though this book was written several years ago by JLA, you would never be able to tell. This book is just as amazing as any other of her books, and fans will be excited to read JLA's journey into the angel world. There are definitely some steamy scenes (so it's for older readers), but those scenes are extremely well written, and leave you begging for more. Jennifer expertly set this book up for future novels, and I can't wait to see what happens next. Unchained is full of unexpected twists and turns, and you will never believe who is the betrayer. I am eagerly awaiting the next book in this series, and while it wasn't perfect, it is still a must-read! Go and get this now...happy reading :)

"I want answers!"As the words leave Rick's mouth, his voice carries up the hill, and I know we've been spotted.And this one I really like I won't say who the guy is, lol"Kat," he whispers.Unable to stop myself, I rise on to the tips of my toes and bring my mouth to his. He tastes like salt and mint and the faintest trace of cinnamon.Overall a great paranormal romance, with some magic, danger and some steam too, with some fantasy too. What can I say but wow!! The previous books were great, but I loved Angelsong, so much so, that I would say that it is my favourite!! I was immersed into the gripping, action packed storyline from start to finish, and I just couldn’t pull myself away from it.Alyx and Jordan are on a mission to save Isaiah by rescuing Mayrekk from Michael. They face a lot of obstacles on the way and do so with banter and humour, but they are constantly looking out for one another. The connection that they already have strengthens and at times you could cut the sexual tension with a knife. Don’t get me wrong… Isaiah is Alyx’s priority, but something happened to her that shifts her thinking (which I won’t tell you about), so that she can get the job done and I think it was a very well planned idea on the authors’ part. Jordan I absolutely adore! My heart goes out to him and he says some of the sweetest things in this book. There is so much I want to say about it, but they would be spoilers for sure!!Now even with all this action, there are a number of tests thrown in for Alyx and Jordan which I found exciting. They were do-or-die scenarios and I thought the author did a remarkable job of plotting it all together. They were clever and well thought out games that I enjoyed watching, as the characters put their trust into one another to figure it all out.Angelsong was remarkable… to put it simply. It has everything I love from the paranormal world: angels, demons and mortals. We travel to numerous destinations and into the dreamscape. A lot of the things that we have learned from previous books are rolled into this book too, and even though it has been a little while since I have read the other books in the series, I was able to grasp everything with ease. In my opinion, I think that Hanna has grown so much as an author, through Angelfire, Angelstone and Angelsong. Although… she always leaves the book open so I want more!! I can’t wait to get my hands on Angelblood next year, to see where things go now…I received a copy of this book from the Author in exchange for an honest review.

reviewText: A Russian princess is the focus - Tatiana Ivanov, who has gained an MBA and come to work in her brother Alexander's Atlantic City casino, though we don't actually see her doing much work.  She doesn't know that an international jewel thief is stalking her family.  Tatiana's family uphold traditions by making marriage arrangements and have pledged her to a Grand Duke's son whom she's not met.  Stubbornly certain that in America she can marry as she likes, Tatiana still doesn't want to hurt her parents.Tatiana meets again a detective friend, Peter Roman.  He changed his name and dropped his titled identity when he came to America. In reality he's the Grand Duke's son, a prince, and now he's obliged to come clean with the princess he desires.  But Tatiana is tired of people being less than honest with her, and finds it hard to forgive him.I found it hard to feel any sympathy for such wealthy people, who are rich because they encourage others to gamble. We don't meet any ordinary folks in this tale, and Tatiana is aware of the cheaper nature of the suits her detective friend can afford. Once he reveals himself he taps into his family wealth too, so that's okay then. Imagine if he'd stayed in cheap suits. Peter is the best character because he is steadfast and Tatania's to-ing and fro-ing about whether she could trust him seemed wrong given they were spending quite a lot of time in the bedroom.The author also tries to make us feel sympathy for the jewel thief who is stealing to order, but it doesn't work with me.  Overall this is a one-sided romantic suspense but it is certainly not the only one and many people will enjoy the descriptions of Monaco and Jersey.

I do know Amber, we met on Twitter, and she's a laugh riot, with an honest heart, who is warm and bracingly original (My confession's up front, as honest as I can be); so, please, take what I say with your grain of salt.I love poetry. I read it. I wish I wrote poetry better. Amber risks much in sharing her poetic mindset with us in collected form. Amber displays her raw honesty in the work, along with a playfulness, and uses a patterned rhyme scheme with a majority of the poems. Her singular voice, mingled with the rhyme, entwine to beat out a steady, natural cadence.I read the poems in order, one a night, to catch the imagery and not let them speed by. I believe poems strengthen the more they are contemplated this way (again, only my opinion - and the same goes for short fiction), where the coloring of the next poem, or subject, cannot bleed into the next too much. (That said, there are poetry collections that are meant to be read as a whole . . . and Amber's collection IS meant to be read as a whole, all touching on the same or similar subjects of love, loss, giving of one's self completely, and finding, at times, that this yearning love is not returned.) Those poems centered on unrequited love were my favorites in The Color of Dawn.Amber reveals her heart, and it's a big one, and that is reason enough to buy her book.
summary: Find your own color . . . at dawn.

Unlike most free Kindle ebooks--which are often unimaginative attempts at books in sore need of plot/character development, and severe doctoring from a bevy of editors--The Whiskey Tide is both well written and well crafted. Engaging storytelling, with interesting plot and subplot twists, the book is replete with complex character development, realistic dialogue. Who could ask for more?The Whiskey Tide really captures the era of the Prohibition, when social mores were in flux. It's a rollicking rum-running tale--replete with a a nod to the gangster underworld, the jazz age, flappers. Imagine The Great Gatsby meets Road to Perdition on the high seas.Though the characters are somewhat stereotypical: smart rich girl falls for handsome, working-class guy, a gullible widow, evil plotting uncle, a gangster, a fallen sister, a damaged WWI vet--they each rise above their character flaws--except the gangster, who is a bad guy, of course.Morally upstanding heroine, Kate (who reminds me of Katharine Hepburn), overcomes the straitjacket imposed by a privileged upbringing, is believable, even though she breaks the law for all the right reasons to support family and home. However, we don't get a backstory of her being conflicted by the (lack of) justification of her illegal actions but the arc of the plot is solid. It holds.Authentically told historical fiction at its best: I found myself wishing for a sequel. I will miss the supporting character, Mrs. Cole. I've read far too many bad ebooks--which I delete from my library as soon as I'm done reading them--this book is a keeper. Four point five stars.(FWIW, I am using real n-lines, not double hyphens; it's an Amazon typo, not mine.)

I gave this book a 4 because in spite of the author it is a remarkably good one. That being said, this book could have used a better editor. I understand it is a Harlequinn and a 'risqué regency' at that, but really it could have been exceptional in the right hands. The characters were excellent and the plot was really fun. But the hero constantly complaining in mind-voice about wanting to shove his clock inside the heroine was as jarring in the story as it was here in my review. Regencies are charming because of their manners and elegance. Yes, sex and desire and lust can be used within the confines but a regency reader expects those topics to be handled with finesse even in mind-voice. For the author to use such a crude way to introduce those moments really lowered my opinion of the overall work. It seemed very immature and not true to the style of Regency at all. And it's a shame because I really liked the story. The other thing that annoyed me was the presentation of the book. Only about 70% of the file is story. 20% is spent sampling other books by the author at the end and 10% is spent before the book even starts on ramblings. This story borders on novella length with the sample chapters and long-winded credits in the beginning filling up otherwise empty pages.

It just fit the entire tone of the story, even though it was difficult to read at some points.I cannot wait to see what happens next.Verdict? STRONGLY recommended. By an adult.

reviewText: Weirdly, I bought this book BECAUSE of the bad reviews. I read them and the good reviews and wondered if it was really as bad as they were saying. Yes, she was ANNOYING, but that was the way her character was written. She was indeed pushy, and maybe a litte out there, but I didn't really see it as a strike against the book. And after the characters married, I didn't mind her character so much, she became almost likeable.*That he saw her blood on their wedding night and refused to go any further. The review made me think he was a total pussy, but my take on that part is that he was being considerate and didn't want to hurt her. Sure, most guys would have probably continued, as she did say it was alright.. but it wasn't something that made me think the book was terrible just because he didn't.*Someone said that she was supposed to be a virgin but she seemed to know too much with no explanation of how...I agree that after the first time she did seem to be quite forward and pursue her husband for sex, but I really did not see how it was totally out there... It was kind of explained that she was always shy, and quiet but once the hero got to know her he saw a different side to her. In my opinion she did not seem to "know" things it seemed more like she was eager to try new things. As well I thought it was well explained that after finding out her husbands secrets she liked him even more.Everybody is entitled to their opinions, these are just mine after having read the reviews of this book and the book. This book is  about a guy who went from 78 hours a week working for someone to working for himself. Just 2 hour per week and netted $9K every month. He's show you how to find a special service business that you can charge more than $200 per hour.  Also how to hire the best person to do the work for you.I have always wanted to start a small service business, however the capital start up and how much I would net after expenses did not seem worth it. The business I looked at usually only paid about $15 to $30 per billing work hour. After paying for help and other expenses not really much left. I would like to put extra money away for retirement. However after reading this book I can see how I can easily charge $200 per hour for the right type of service business model that he calls Super Service Niche. I'm excited to have found this book. Tired of the J.O.B.(Just Over Broke). He say's any body can do this, I think if you put some work in to it. It will not be overnight but I can see how it can be done.I have paid a lot more money for good business information, this is a good value for the tips he presents, I recommend  buy the book if you have a service business already or what to start one.

SUMMER'S BOOK BLOGAnother find and another success! I was kindly offered to review this book by the author herself and was excited at the notion. I just knew from the synopsis and cover photo, this was my kind of read and I was not disappointed.Dangerous is part one of the Dangerous Trilogy.It's about a sexy motorcycle riding bad to the bone player with a heart ( don't worry you will see it ) named Stone. The name is fitting because when we are first introduced to him, he is as I mentioned before a player, only wanting to be in no strings attached relationships. No mess no fuss.However every bad boy needs that one girl who will put him in his place right? Well ... in walks Dara Golding, a beautiful young but troubled in her own way girl.Both have drama and baggage for young adults and the emotional struggle that is inside of them, breaks your heart at times.One is dealing with feelings of guilt and loss in regards to a beloved deceased family member and trying to prove that they are worthy of praise and love. The other has all of the praise and recognition but something inside that is missing.The up and downs of this couple is so heart wrenching at times and the pain that they are feeling so poignant but the way that they find each other is absolutely moving. With a little bit of patience and whole lotta love, you only can sit there and hope that they do find the way to each other and reach that HEA.Will misunderstandings and lies keep them apart? Will they find true love? Will either of them find what they were searching for? Read it and find out !With a relate able and flowing story line, this book has everything you would want to find in a contemporary love story. Told thru both their voices and some great secondary characters like Granny, I would highly recommend this book and can't wait to read more of the series.

We should all have girlfriends like that. The community they live in and the people who they interact with are so much fun!  Loved the characters! I loved the first 2 books in this series, but was a little disappointed in the 3rd. This, the 4th, is written much like the first 2. There is plenty of action, great plot twists, and character development. I love the way the author makes each character different and believable, adds plenty of witty conversations that make me laugh, and others that bring a tear to my eye (rousing speeches and the love the characters have for each other). I can't believe how much frustration and hope I have for Gawain and Elayeen's relationship, almost like they were real and part of my family. I love Gawain's interaction with "The Keeper of the Stick" and Martan the dwarf. This is turning out to be one of my top ten fantasy series and I hope it continues in this vain in future installments (no Martin or Jordan missteps I hope, and slight spoiler: maybe Gawain and Elayeen could stop fighting each other). I was given this book in exchange for an honest review.This is the first Karen-Anne Stewart book that I have read and I really enjoyed it..The story flowed really well going back and forth between the main characters giving the whole story.We meet Emma, small town virgin on her way to the big city to finally live her life.  In Boston she meets Breck, your typical hot, womanizing bad boy. I was given this ARC in return for a honest review. Clarissa Wilde hit this one out of the park. I instantly became a fan of hers after reading and reviewing the first two books in this series. Ms. Wilde continued this story of Hunter and his Leafy right where the previous book ended. The story started off with the main characters going to pick up Jessie (Hunter's brother) from jail and going back to Hunter's childhood home. With this event happening it forces Hunter to face and finally explain to Autumn some of his childhood demons. We as readers get a chance to learn the unfortunate events that cause not only Hunter to act the way he does but also sheds light on some of Jessie's issues as well. We learn of the horrible situations that both boys were put in by their mother and their reactions. Reading this section brought tears to my eyes. It is raw and very much real to some. Also in this book we are given the opportunity to meet Autumn's parents. How they interact with other and also the constant ups and downs that effect her life. With a dying mother and a disapproving father,Autumn soon will have to learn to either grow a backbone or retreat back to her old self.Throughout the story the underlying theme (in my option) is Redemption. The Characters have to constantly prove to not only to each other but to themselves that they are worthy of love. This story is definitely not a stand alone and the first two books are a must read. The epilogue kicks butt and I definitely needed to get a tissue. I won't spoil the entire thing but I feel it is one of my new "Go To" books and Hunter just made my list of book boyfriends. So sad to see this series end but can't wait to see what is is to come next from this author.

This book was really well written and brought out all types of emotion.  The storyline was unusual, but it held my attention from start to finish.  The gist of the story.  Jenny and Aisha are best of friends, more like sisters.  They met in college and developed a life long friendship.  Connell was Jenny's husband, (also met at the same college)  and they have been married for nearly ten years when Jenny developed cancer and didn't have much time left.  Prior to dying she decided to  organized her husband's and kids life so that when she passed, they would be loved and cared for.  Enter Aisha (African American), who Jenny has asked to take her place (yep, giving up her job and moving to the middle of nowhere to be mother and eventually wife to Connell) and look after her two kids.  This is where the book really gets interesting because both Aisha and Connell always had an uneasy alliance/relationship based on underlying feelings.  Anyway, to cut a long story short, the book was detailed (too detalied) but was excellent.  The secondary characters were lively and made you laugh out loud.  My favourites were Ben and Helen.  Oh, let's not forget Connell who was hot, hot, hot!Overall, a great read. reviewText: Right from the start we're put into an action scene which I just love because I hate all that beating around the bush crap, just get to the good stuff you know? In this book there are more then one POV but I try to focus on the blurb's characters and that would be Nora and Daniel. I mean I love to see how the other characters are doing but I just wish the author would put whose dang point of view and couple we're reading about (figuring out what couple we're reading about is easy) but sometimes the point of view is not. Sometimes I think Daniel is just too honest and it just doesn't help him out any, "I went out with Vincent on occasion. Although, there was never any promises of a relationship. Any girl I picked up knew it was just a one-time thing. Vincent was the one who led girls on and took them out a few times before moving on to the next." Then there were the times that Daniel was honest that I loved him for it, "I can see where it might bother someone," Daniel exhaled. "But, I'm just glad to have you in my life." Nora smiled peering up into Daniel's eyes. He rolled over, draping himself over her. As he entered her again, she realized that maybe he really didn't care." (by the way that doesn't mean Daniel doesn't care about Nora this is from a scene where something happened before this and Nora asked a question.) I liked this book so much more than the first and second. Once again there was a scene I did not approve of and I really did get on the computer and yell at the author the woman is so lucky that I no longer want to kill her because I read the next little outline for the next book.

When I read a book  - I read everything about the book – from covereth to covereth  . . . including the reviews! Geez – some reviewers are so harsh! Makes me wonder if they’re as interested in reading/reviewing as they are in putting others  down?I’m not much of a romance novelist – per say  – and don’t have a lot of experience  or comparisons to draw from in that respect; but this book is not just about romance – it is about personal growth, and the people and relationships ‘evolving’ in and around that growth!  It’s about courage, and finding the will to change, and about understanding what it takes to accept the truth once you find it.I love the book – it’s a good read!In addition, for anyone not appreciating the author’s style and colorful use of ‘stigmatic’ words [watch that come back to bite me!], I have this to say – “Ever hear of using ‘picturesque speech’? ‘Ever hear of reaching out in an unusual and unexpected way to describe that which has been described ‘millions upon millions’ of times . . . the same old way? ‘Ever hear of giving new life to otherwise boring situations by the irreverent use of words? [Guess not!] Finally, to those ‘critical, shortsighted reviewers’ . . . have you never heard of “Sex and The City?” Good Grief – those ‘grown’ women squealed at the drop of a man’s pants- and we all squealed with them!!If you’re reading this then you must be considering reading Stubborn Love. Please do! I believe you’ll like it. I did!

In The Last Night, author Nico Rosso presents a very stark and desolate post apocalyptic world filled with creatures - called Ashers - that are basically a type of zombie with a bit of a twist. They were once humans who lost their flesh, turned to stone and feed on ashes. They set everything ablaze in pursuit of their next meal which includes charred humans.I was really impressed with the world building in this novella. Rosso gave a plausible theory for the apocalypse and the Ashers. Earth was rocked by a chain of earthquakes resulting in long dormant viruses being released, infecting humans and giving life to the Ashers. Given the time constraints in a novella I was pleasantly surprised at how easily I was pulled into the world and kept on edge wondering how everyone would survive.The romance took me a little longer to warm up to. Erica has been living with a group of survivors in a crumbling hotel in Phoenix, AZ behind a make shift fence as they live day to day looking for supplies and fending off the Ashers. They really have no weapons that work against the creatures other than just bludgeoning them and hoping the fence stays up long enough to hold them off.Most of the group longs for the "good old days" but Erica wants more. Even in this hopeless world she sees hope over the horizon. She watches the rain storms in the distance and knows that must mean water, food and possibly other people. She doesn't want to just survive, she wants to live. Just when it seems that Erica will never get that chance during a particular nasty attack, our hero Jake comes riding in on a motorcycle saving the day. He has a weapon that works against the enemy but he rides alone and he trades for his knowledge. He doesn't give it away for free.At first Erica is aghast at this. Why wouldn't you help your fellow man/woman survive? Share your knowledge? To Jake he needs supplies and trading information is the way to get it. Their relationship is very antagonistic at first. Once he sees Erica fight though, Jake sees that she's a survivor like himself. He takes a chance and finally shares his information freely and falls hard for Erica.I actually had no problem with them hooking up so quickly. Hey - life is tough during an apocalypse and if you can find someone to be with why not? What bothered me was his over the top instant adoration of Erica. It was pretty intense on both their parts. I'm not sure I bought into that level of intensity at first sight.However, I felt Rosso redeemed that by having them back up a little later in the story and examine their pasts and discuss their future. Jake and Erica didn't always agree on what that meant and it was interesting to watch how that played out.The ending is clear but leaves an opening for future adventures. I hope if the series continues it features Erica and Jake. they make a great team and it would be nice to see how their relationship plays out.Final thoughts: I had a few problems with Erica & Jake's relationship at first but I was won over in the end. I did in enjoy the stark, post apocalyptic world and the original take on zombies.
Near death, seduction, vampires and romance... what more could a girl ask for?  Throw in a few more complications and you have a complex legend revolving around redheads.  Loved it.

The hero (and I use the term loosely) is such a jerk to his wife (who he marries only because he needs a wife to help run his ranch, not because he loves her), and this is just not my idea of a romance at all.Only days after they're married, Burke allows his ex-wife to move in with him and Annie. No man worth the name 'husband' would allow this, especially considering how poorly the ex treats Annie.  It is obvious from the first that the ex is here to cause a rift between the newlyweds, and the husband makes it way too easy for her.  Despite the fact that Annie is vulnerable, sweet and sincere, and his constant mention that Alice is an untrustworthy bitch, he believes the ex over his wife EVERY. SINGLE. TIME.  This got old really fast and reading this book was one long frustration.  The hero ultimately becomes so unlikable that I couldn't root for a reconciliation, even knowing everything that led to their separation were misunderstandings.  Not only is he clueless, he is careless and even cruel towards his wife in his lack of attention, respect and faith. I have no idea what she saw in him.The author got carried away with her attempts to build angst and conflict, and ended up making the supposed hero irredeemable.  I really like Annie, but Burke isn't deserving of her.  She took him back way too easily for my taste. I was actually hoping the twist would be some decent guy sweeping her off her feet - it's not a romance if you can't love the hero.
summary: This one was hard to get through - too frustrating, too many "misunderstandings" and too much presence of an evil ex wife

reviewText: I received this from Library Thing to read and review. This is a great book about Christmas and love.  There are four short stories and a novella, all of which concern Amish young people searching for meaning in life and all of which relate to the Christmas holiday. The way the Amish celebrate the holiday compared to the commercialism most of us experience is very interesting.  I found myself wondering whether I would enjoy one more than the other or whether I would enjoy both equally as much. In most of the stories, the main characters are searching for answers, the most prominent of which is whether to make a life in the Amish community or in the outside/"English" world. Most of the characters are living within the "English" world and feel compelled to return to the simple but quietly beautiful world of the Amish community and Amish celebrations. The choices the characters make are not easy ones, but I doubt I would find them easy were I in their positions. Throughout the book, the theme of love, for "the one" (as they say), and for other family members and Amish traditions and community life is prominent.  One thing I did miss was an index.  At first, this might not seem too important, but if you somehow lose your place reading (oh, the wonders of modern technology!), it becomes important, as you try to figure out just where you were in the book. I also like to know how much longer I have until a chapter or story end, especially when I have something to do (like make supper or leave for an appointment), which will require me to leave the book for a time. The author has once again given us a good look at the Amish community, the people and the culture with these heartwarming stories.

A tantalizing, time twisting, introspective journey back and forth between post apocolyptic futures, as experienced by a couple of those who had lived during the  nightmare and well afterward. As the tension builds, these 'time jumpers' are tasked with, or obligated to try and prevent the collapse. Of course, everyone does things for their own reasons.The characters are very well done. The time swapping is accomplished in smooth and perceptible fashion. The trials and tribulations of the characters seem real and palpable. I can honestly say that I felt these characters.This writer has talent, and I will be looking for his other work.

I really give this book just a shade over three and a half stars.  One star gets deducted because it is so short.  It's really much more of a novella, and had it been priced as such, I wouldn't complain.  But I want to feel like I'm getting value, and this series seems like every book gets shorter and less . . . okay.  This book is the least of the series in a number of ways.I've generally enjoyed Cape High up until this point, and I liked this book well enough, but I can't pretend that this series is in the same league as Wearing the Cape.  The series is what it is, light escapist reading, and it's done well enough, but no book in the series has been better than just good.  Dialogue is okay, although it's pretty cheesy - and not the fun Tick sort of cheesy.  Same thing goes for the characterization.  Ms. Ross writes action just fine, but this book was really short on it.  The conflict in this book was nearly nonexistant, as was the character development.  Also, the series changes POV characters from book to book, and they are all starting to blend together by this point.  Picking one or two and sticking with it would have aided clarity.And the book itself.  I was fifty percent through before I realized it - and not because I was enjoying the book so much.  Very very little happened.If you've made it this far in the series, then you might as well buy this book.  I realize that doesn't sound like a ringing endorsement - mostly because it isn't.
