Regina Puckett packs a big punch in this short story about love and loss. Writing on a topic near to many hearts, Puckett introduces April, whose Marine husband Adam is killed in action just days before his tour ends and their child is to be born. Heartbroken, April questions whether God was even listening to her prayers for Adam's safety, and He answers her with a visit from a unique angel. In IF LOVE WAS ENOUGH, Puckett reminds us that no matter how alone we may feel, a greater power is always present, and we are never truly alone.

22 pages is NOT enough!Darn you Becca!“Pulled” is a short story in Becca Campbell’s Flawed series and the only complaint I have is that it’s TOO SHORT!I want more! And I’m sure you will too!She give us just enough of these new characters to whet our appetite and then she yanks the rug out of from under her reader.Hopefully, we will see the characters again soon in one of the other novels planned for her Flawed series!You can find this short novella for Kindle and Nook and I’m told it will shortly be available on iTunes as well.The story is not a continuation of Becca’s first book in the Flawed series, “Empath”.  It is a stand-alone side story in that same universe. We meet Juniper, a “runaway” foster child and Becca gives us just enough background to make us want more.She also introduces us to several other characters who are “gifted” – like many of the characters we met in “Empath”.It may be labeled YA and it may be a story about an 8 year old girl but Becca caught me with the very first sentence – which would be why I was so shocked at the sudden ending. I’m sure that was part of her evil plan…lolAll told, a most intriguing story and well worth the sticker price of $.99Don’t miss it! And watch for Becca’s next story in the Flawed series: “Outsider”I received a copy of this novella free in exchange for an honest review.

This is the first book in The Midnight Hunter Trilogy, and I have to say, it's definitely a great start! I enjoyed this book from the very beginning even through the author bio in the back! Yes, I said it! I even read the author bio and it made me giggle!Midnight Hunter mainly focuses on a young woman named Donna. Even from the beginning, Donna has strange dreams that seem to get a little too close for comfort. Soon enough, she even starts to sustain injuries from things that happen in her dreams.Donna's friend, Mo, decides she wants to take Donna to a club. What Donna wasn't aware of at first is the fact that girls matching Donna's description had been disappearing from this club. Preferring to stay further away from crowds, Donna head to a more secluded place in the club where she meets Hunter, your typical broody male vampire. We soon find out that Hunter is the brother of the man responsible for the disappearances.While there are some pieces of this story that do fall into the category of "typical vampire romance," I found myself drawn into this story by parts that were really very unique. I even found myself loving a few of the lesser characters. Really that's something that Bonnie Bernard does very well. She knows how to bring amazing characters. In fact, there was even one character, specifically a weapons dealer, that we only got to meet through a phone call and a few brief mentions in conversations, that I would love to be a fly on the wall to watch inside his shop even for a day!Overall, I loved this book from cover to cover! If you haven't read it yet, you're missing out!

This is a triple review covering all three books.It did take me a while to get into this series. I wasn’t really crazy about the voice used in these books. I prefer 3rd person to be past tense rather than present tense, it just didn’t read very smoothly, it didn’t feel natural and kept me from really getting into the story. There was also a lot of unnessasary descriptions. I don’t need to know how many spoonfuls of sugar everyone take or that they stirred it after adding the sugar. (Who wouldn’t?)  Sometimes the descriptions would be so lengthly and detailed I would get distracted and not know who they were talking about until after the two pages of reading how one person got dressed.However, I did enjoy the plot very much. Once it got going itThe first book was pretty slow to get going but it also had a lot of background and building of the world the characters lived in so that by the time you get to the next two there is quite a lot more going on.The second book had less detail than the first, which was good, but still had a bit too much.The take on fallen angels and the other supernatural creatures that were features was different than what you would expect which I really liked. It gave them a bit more depth. I loved how the plot became more detailed and the twists throughout the book were not super predictable.The final book is no longer about Lisa and Alex, but about Samuel. It’s a great continuation to the story with some of the other characters who need their story told. This one could be read as a standalone (unlike the first two) and you’d understand it, but I think it would have more meaning if you read books 1 & 2 first. The amount of detail in this book has once again improved.I probably would have rated this series a 5 if it didn’t go overboard with all the description. It had an original plot, which is something I love. But  as much as I enjoyed it I found it a tiny bit difficult to get pulled in completely like I wanted. While it did get better from book to book, in the end it was still way too much, to the point where in some parts I didn’t know what was going on but I knew every detail of the setting and every move each character made. This series is great, but the amount of detail in much of it was a little too excessive, but it’s defiantly worth a read. I think this series speaks a lot of the amount of growth this author has had in their skill and would recommend this series to any who like Angels, demons and more.Rating:3.5 out of 5

I didn't know what to expect of a book with three stories in it that at first look a bit different. Luckily, I ended up enjoying a book mainly about life and about survival, fear, death and our conscience.In Shades of Grey we found three short stories. They are very different but similar stories, about men at a breaking point of their lives. At first it may look like they don't have nothing in common but after you finish I think you would find out that they share a lot of characteristics.They are united why the way they see life and death. They share the fact that they have their past really present in every move they made. Each one of them deals with death in a different way.  Their stories show us things that sometimes we believed are wrong, without trying to justify them. The purpose of the book is tales us about these men (although one is a little boy) and what's going on inside their heads, but without act like a redeemer for them. You never feel like somebody is trying to find a reason of why they act this way.The author have the ability of transports us into each one of the stories. You can feel yourself strapped out to a chair, in a hole during a war and as a child trying to deal with life. Every feeling is really well described and I found a couple fragments very funny.My favorite one was the last one Down the Rabbit Hole; in this one the author really makes a good job.  Tom as a little kid still has that innocence where he doesn't distingue between good and bad. Tom doesn't understand yet the idea of taking some choices that would bring consequences, and has his imagination as his ally.In the other two we found John and James, the first one is sort of a spy, which I love, and has a really interesting mind. Everything he says sounds funny. And then we have James, who is in the World War II, I really like his story. I'm a fan of historical books, but in this one we focalize in him and how he sees war.Overall, a great book, that proves us that what matters is quality, not the length of the book.

When you find the "one who holds your heart" Are you willing to fight for them?"At least I can take with me the knowledge that he read them. He read my words. The words that are only meant for him and only him. Time to grow a set and write my letters to Luca."Leighton Parks was a sweet, innocent, shy girl in high school. After a brief encounter one day with Luca Ferro, Leighton begins to notice him more and more. To shy to tell him how she feels, Leighton begins writing him anonymous letters to express her growing feelings for him.  " My dearest Luca,  I know you want to find me; I can see it in your eyes every day I see it.But alas, I cannot reveal my idenity for fear that I would not be what you wanted. I know in the letter you wrote back to me, you said you lost sleep over finding me I cannot have that, my love your well being means more to me than anything. Let's just have this I like it this way. I get to tell you all thed things I love about you, and you accept me for who I am without even knowing me. I know that you are a good person. You are strong, smart, handsome, and you love your family. Maybe someday our parts will cross, you will look into my eyes and you will know it's me. I wouldn't have to say anything, we would just know. That time is not now for us my Lucas, remember this* "In true love the smallest distance is to great, and the greatest distance can be bridged." We will find our path some day, Luca have faith. Forever yours, The one whose heart you hold"Luca Ferro is not your typical Jock. Drafted in high school to play Baseball, he decides instead to go to college and play for the University of Miami., after blowing out his elbow, not once but twice Luca turned to the letters from his "letter girl" to get him through.The book starts out with Leighton in bed with her steady man Michael and Luca running his Father's resturaunt and coaching his old high school baseball team. Leighton the secret author of 3 contemporary romance novels get's  her invitation to her high school reunion and it's being held at none other than Luca Ferro's place!  I can't get into to much detail without spoiling it for you but I can tell you that fate steps in and takes hold of the reigns.After pining for his "letter girl" for years Luca is about to get the surprise of a lifetime, but will the betrayal of his "letter girl" be to much for him?I love each and every one of the character's in this book... from the Sleezy and slimy, Michael and Val to Luca's sweet lil old Italian father. The depth of emotion in this book is something I've personally never experienced while reading a book before. I went from hopeful to angry, heartbroken, and sad, and finally to happy. I really did laugh out loud, cry and at points even yell at the book while reading it.Luca is the type of man we want our sons to be and our daughters to marry. An Leighton, well, we find out that even as a woman Leighton may still have a bit of growing up to do emotionally.Letters to Luca has it all, secrets, lies, laughs, but most of all it has Love.  Not story book romance kind of love, but real, raw love.  The love of everyday real life that can consume you at times. The kind of love that you feel so strongly that you don't know where he ends and you begin.This book showed me the importance of communication in a relationship, it reminded me that relationships take hard work, compromise and most of all understanding and forgiveness.M.R. Joseph weaves a story of soulmates fighting  and sometimes failing to love one another in the way the other one needs.She makes you question, is love, even true love, always enough?

I studied Recreation in college and one of the things we worked with all the time was how to keep fit after retirement.  Learning how to avoid the rocking chair and stay in the action for many years longer was the aim of several courses. We knew even thirty years ago, that one of the major keys to enjoying life and staying fit during the 70's, 80's, and even longer was regular exercise.CrossFit: The Beginner's Guide to Great Health takes all the fitness knowledge we have gained during the last three decades and packs it into an easy to read and easy to follow guide that can move you from the couch to really being active and enjoying your life in ways you never thought possible again.Make a commitment to stick with the program for six weeks and you will find yourself back in the swing of things.  Did you like to dance, but are now too tired to hunt down the remote control?  Do you automatically leave things like skiing to the youngsters?  What if you could get in shape to ski again?  CrossFit may be the answer you are looking for.  It gives you a good cardio workout while at the same time strengthening and building muscles.  Give it a chance; you may like it for life.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!

reviewText: This story tells us about Benji, a closeted police officer whose life is turned upside down first with a series of tragic events from work, then when he falls in love with Neal, a coffee shop owner. This book was well written and the dialog was really good. The events, while not always exciting or pretty, paints a pretty accurate picture of what occurs on the job as a law enforcement officer. It also shows how difficult the job can be for a gay cop. Although I really liked this story, I will admit that Benji character was not likeable. Not even at the end. He was closeted to the point of being a coward. I can understand him being in the closet, but there comes a time when a person has to man up. And he never really did. It's one thing to be in the closet, but when you enter into a relationship with someone, you can't make that decision for them. And that is exactly what he did with Neal. Neal was out and accepted by his family and friends; the people that mattered. Neal offered that same warmth and acceptance to Benji, but Benji just wouldn't reach out and take it. Not only that, I felt that he was forcing Neal back into the closet with him. I was irritated at Neal's character because he was willing to go into that closet just to keep Benji; he became pathetic and needy at one point. The scene where Benji was rude to Neal's mother made my blood simmer and when Neal apologized for his mother made my blood boil. I felt that Benji did not deserve Neal's mother's forgiveness and his (Neal's) family's acceptance. I actually liked Benji's friends better: his sometimes inappropriate, sometimes crude, and all times idiotic friend Matthews and his enlightened friend Cazé. In the end, it was rumor and speculation that brought Benji `s sexuality to the forefront. Even though he had support from some of his colleagues, Benji still chose to remain closeted, which was certainly his right, but it eventually led to Neal removing himself from the relationship. This is when Benji decides that maybe Neal had a point and begins to really take a hard look at himself. In the end, Benji never really comes fully out of the closet, but he opens the door to it. If an author's writing is able to make you feel anything for the characters, good or bad, then you know that they did a great job. This author did exactly that. The story doesn't have a HEA ending, but the HFN ending that it did have was more realistic. Despite my dislike for the lead character, I truly enjoyed this story and would definitely recommend it.Kiwi's 4 sweet pea review appears at mrsconditreadsbooks.com/index.php/?p=13451

This book has a lot of mixed reviews and after reading some I confess I lowered my standards thinking this book would be awful. Truth is--parts of it was. Not so much awful--just ridiculously far fetched. The whole psychic link bonding between our two lovers was totally laughable at times. But I'm getting ahead of myself.What can I say about this book? I expected more from our antagonist Therese. The dream-torment scenes, though erotic and  intimate, were creative and showed a bit of her absolute need for sex and control. But the big battle at the end was a joke. The fact that it was resolved in 1 chapter with minimal action was a huge let down. I wanted more before the situation was resolved.Sir Sidney was perhaps more likeable to me than Katherine and Adrian. Kat was just a sexually inexperienced female running from a bad life and Adrian was a new vampire struggling with his nature but really just passing through life and from the moment they saw each other it was like BAM! You're mine and I must bed you and do nothing else. Sidney had depth to him. Depth, intelligence, and humor. I liked reading his conversations with the others and seeing his true affections for his adopted son. I'll admit his stance on trying to cure Adrian of his vampirism put a new spin on the vampire legend especially since this book is set in a time period where women had to use chamber pots and dress behind screens. I'm curious as to whether his science experiments will bode well in future novels.Reviewers commented that this book had a lot of sex in it, perhaps too much. As as avid PNR reader I can say it was no more or no less than the usual amounts in say a Kresley Cole or J.R. Ward book. The language was perhaps a little cruder. Not so delicately described, Kelly loved to throw around the words c--k and p---y. But that didn't bother me. Kat and Adrian got hot and heavy quick, but as they continued getting to know each other true love came and I really believed their romance despite the wacky chemically induced psychic-destined-love bond they shared.I have mixed feelings about this book. Halfway through I just wanted to stop reading it because the plot seemed stagnant, but it did pick up, though I didn't like the ending. This book is the 1st in the trilogy and as of right now I'm not sure I'd pay money to read the other two. Im slightly curious about who Therese is and why she is the way she is, but its not a pressing need that I buy the next two books right this minute. Its a tossup.This book isn't bad. It's just not that good either.

reviewText: Reviewer: BexRating: 4.5 out of 5Disclosure: This book was provided by the author in exchange for an HONEST and not necessarily positive review.Ivy from the onset captured my attention and pulled me into the paranormal world Dahlia Donovan had created. D R Gordon displays the populist touch in a collection of horror and dark fantasy stories that is eminently readable. ‘From Darkness’ is an impressive debut.Gordon kicks off in high style with ‘The Suitor’ a baroque tale with a twist on a well-known literary figure. 'The Portrait' maintains the Gothic tradition in a nod to Wilde's 'The Picture of Dorian Grey.' 'Club Diablo' comes next, perhaps my favourite inclusion: a perfectly timed contemporary tale with a great twist. 'The Dark Man' is an effective chiller replete with dollhouse, disfigured mannequin and the dark man of the title. 'Karnak's Rest' has the cosmic dimension of horror to be found in Lovecraft; although Gordon's take seems to be an allegory about today's earth and the potential man-made crisis threatening it. 'Terrible Beauty' (the phrase borrowed from Yeats' 'Easter' perhaps?) is an appropriately nasty little vignette, sharp as a knife. 'Mountain Air', a longer story, had about it for me that effortlessly involving style of Stephen King's. (Indeed, as a general point, Gordon has an enviably accessible  and effortless style, sure to garner him an even wider readership than the one he has so far amassed.)'Reddening Tide' continues a well-respected literary tradition of stories dealing with doubles (one thinks of Fyodor Dostoyevsky). 'The Bird' is a deceptively innocuous title for a tale about an avian menace. The next two offerings, 'Witches' and 'The Beast’, demonstrate Gordon's range to great effect, the first in his handling of ‘olde worlde’ vernacular and the theme of mob insanity (and sanity at the last minute), the second in its apparent borrowings of science fiction tropes – a tale that reminded me of Ray Bradbury. 'Alice' also highlights Gordon's inventiveness, and is perhaps his most serious inclusion. What begins as an amusing riff on a famous children's book soon steps into a very real world of abominable crimes committed on children. Perhaps the most disturbing in the collection.'In The Woods' was the first tale of Gordon's I read, which a friend shared from D R Gordon's facebook page. Gordon had the clever idea of asking his facebook fans to suggest story ideas or opening sentences which he then weaved complete tales from. It was great to see with 'In The Woods' that the young’uns are still reading the old masters of weird tales like Algernon Blackwood and taking inspiration from them.'Zombies' puts on display another facet of Gordon's writing I've so far neglected to mention: his humour. 'The Fairy' does not deal with a benign fairy, of course, and 'The Wo'gey' successfully continues a trick up Gordon's sleeve of leading the reader to believe he is writing about one thing, before pouncing with another. 'The Tail' is a good choice to round out the collection, amusing and upbeat.In a collection of short stories one might expect some filler. But these are all carefully crafted and highly inventive pieces. ‘From Darkness’ has deservedly already proved a hit. I eagerly await, as I’m sure many do, Gordon's first novel. It's sure to be a feverishly imaginative and surprising treat.
summary: An Exciting New Talent on the Horror Scene

We met Melisa in the first two books of the "Moments in Time" series and this book is Melisa's story of getting her happily-ever-after. I had immensely enjoyed the first two books in the series and am supremely happy to say that I loved this book even better. This is the best book in the series in terms of the plot, characterization, events construction and the narration.Dori Lavelle has grown as an author which shows when you read this book. I was able to compare her previous books with this one and could clearly see the improvements. The characters are better woven, the mystery and suspense is better paced and the romance is sensuous as usual but more emotionally linked. I was pulled in the story right from the start and whenever I felt like the plot was getting predictable, the author threw a new twist in the tale and totally shocked me.I loved Melisa's growth as a character. She is more approachable and real in this book than in the previous ones. She is trying to turn her life around and willing to take proactive steps. Heat has always loved Melisa and I loved his dedication in making his relationship with Melisa work. He loves her and shows her enough times that he will do anything to take care of her. I loved their scenes together and was very happy with the overall progress in their relationship. Not that I had any say in it! :)Carlene and Nick are happily married and I just loved the new developments in their life. Carlene and Melisa's friendship is so beautifully nurtured and developed in this series. In this book, Dori introduces readers with more people from Melisa's past and I loved Melisa's long lost friends like Josie. Wrapping up all the loose ends in this book, the author does a great job in bringing this beautiful series to a closure.Although there is a sort of a cliffhanger at the end but it didn't affect my happiness at seeing two so lovely people together.All in all, a very sweet and totally engrossing love story between two people who have made their fair share of mistakes in their lives and are now trying to finally listen to their heart and turn their life around.A must read for all romance lovers, I give Bittersweet Moments a 4.5 out of 5 and look forward to reading more from this author in the future.This review is also available on the blog Njkinny's World of Books

reviewText: This is the second story in The Master of Whitehall series. I really enjoyed it!Alexis (Lexi) Gordon is Katelyn's friend at college. She is a wonderful character. She is funny, sweet and a little naive. But, when her life is turned upside down, she accepts her friend's offer to become immortal. This is her story.Having read the first story, I was looking forward to reading this one. I started to read the story and, although it mirrored some of the scenes from the previous book, it was interesting to see them through Lexi's eyes. Becoming a vampire actually suits Lexi. She gains more confidence in her abilities, but she is still young and impetuous. The story is told mostly through Lexi's point of view, but Katelyn and a new character, Gale, has their say too. Gale is an intriguing character, who is a 1600 year old vampire. She is one of the "Old One's" and is extremely powerful. Gale comes into Lexi's life after a distressing event that, because of Lexi's vampire youth, she is not able to cope with. The story has many twists, but I did find some of the dialogue to be still a little gushy at times. However, it was intriguing to see how Lexi's experiences have shaped her, and made her grow emotionally. I was a little surprised at how she dealt with Mikey, after their relationship ended badly. I certainly wouldn't want to be on Lexi's bad side; she's a woman scorned, and that's all I'm going to say! The story is not full of action, nor is it a romance novel, although there is a bit both, but it is more of a journey of self discovery and emotional growth. The story does not end on a cliffhanger, but I am looking forward to reading the next book in the series as soon as possible.Rick Veal has written an intriguing story of love, friendship and emotional growth. His characters are lifelike and likable. His writing style is not as fast paced compared to other authors I have read, but the story was written in such a way that I couldn't not keep turning the pages. The flow of the story was wonderful.There are some scenes of a sensual nature that are a little on the hot side (although not as explicit as some books I have read), so I do not recommend this book for younger readers. I do, however, recommend this book if you love paranormal romances with sexy vampires. - Lynn Worton

The author, Cannon, somewhat succeeded in creating solely two of her characters. Harper, the main character and her primary love interest, Jackson who both pushed me to prevail. However, their short-lived relationship was the only part of the novel that I had enjoyed, aside from the ending (since the book was finally over).Even with what I like about the two characters, they still had more than their fair share of flaws as I only favoured the two with a lack of a better option. Jackson incessantly refused to explain the situation to Harper, as also leaving me in the dark to what the actual conflict is. As for Harper, she was oblivious to her surroundings. This was especially frustrating as her "amnesia" caused her to forget the start of her relationship with Jackson, which was one of my highlights of the book. Not only did she develop "mysterious" amnesia, she immediately chose to conform to society as a cheerleader, something which she previously claimed had no appeal when it was out of her reach. The other supporting roles were also incapable of peaking my interest, such as Harper's closest friend, Agnes and her "shocking" secrets and sealed fate.Cannon only succeeded in writing a story centred upon a quintessential high school hierarchy and a self-absorbed sophomore who is incapable of staying conscious for more than a couple of days. Personally, this does not suit my taste, in spite of the regular action and romance that I often find appealing. Only if this sounds intriguing to other readers would I recommend this novel, because in the least, Cannon' s writing style was not as shocking as what plot points consisted in "Beautiful Demons".

reviewText: "Air" is short sci-fi work by author William Esmont. This is a Kindle e-book that is a 117 Kb download and was free from Amazon.com at the time of writing this review.SPOILERS throughoutFor reasons that no one is completely sure, a few people have been turning into zombies. Initially confined to a small areas, the continual bites and wounds by these undead, turn into a problem of pandemic implications.This particular story follows Chris and his brother Dave, who has been taken to the local hospital after a motorcycle accident. When Chris, who is unaware at this point of the impending danger, arrives to see his brother, the OPD is in chaos...but not for the usual reasons.This tale is one of escape and survival from the hospital. It reminds me so much of the excellent TV series 'The Walking Dead' on the AMC channel.Author Esmont has written this tale with skill...walking that fine line of a providing the reader with a scary atmosphere filled with terror and a sense of foreboding. You just never know what awaits our protagonist when they are about to round the next corner.Conclusion:Tense, scary and all with a superb sense of timing and pace.I loved every word of this Zombie novel. I will actively seek out more of this author's work.As it is...5 Stars.Ray Nicholson
summary: A short Zombie novel of the highest quality.

The hardest thing about reading these prequel novellas is I know what will happen to a few characters and I really like them so I don’t want to get to attached. But let’s face it Sam is pretty adorable, in an I can kill you kind of way, so it is impossible to not get a little attached to him.Celaena is back from her time in the desert certain that she will pay off her debt and leave Arobynn. At least that was the plan until she sees him and he apologizes for beating her. It is complicated thing when someone saved your life and treated you like a daughter for so long.This was another great tale centering mostly on Celaena finding a way to break free from Arobynn and become an independent young woman. She has looked to him for so long for reassurance and support but now her feelings for him have changed. Also changed, are the feelings she has for Sam and Celaena isn’t quite sure what to do with those.Arobynn seems genuinely sorry for the way he treated her. He gives her gifts and a great contract for a job that is supposed to be to stop a slave ring from happening. But is it what it seems or something else entirely. The King of Assassins doesn’t seem like the sort to forgive and forget.I love Sam in this novella. He really comes across as a three dimensional character and I love/hate that I know his fate. You can really see in this one all the ways Celaena will fight for those she loves and how what sacrifices she is willing to make. She has such a strong heart for someone trained to kill. I really like there love story and everything Sam tells her about his feelings for Celaena.He brushed his lip against hers. “I love you,” he breathed against her mouth. “And from today onward, I want to never be separated from you. Wherever you go, I go. Even if that means going to hell itself, wherever you are, that’s where I want to be. Forever.”This novella is another great glimpse into our assassin with a heart of gold. I’m reluctant to read the next novella just because the happiness can’t last and we all know it. But I also can’t wait to see how events led up to before Throne of Glass.

I received a complimentary copy of this book as a part of a book tour in exchange for a fair and honest review.Fans of cozy pet mysteries need look no further than Sparkle Abbey’s latest addition to the Pampered Pets series, Fifty Shades of Greyhound.  Filled with well-developed characters, precocious animals and a murder mystery that needs to be solved, I found myself quickly turning the pages to discover what would happen next.  While the fifth book in the series, I was able to pick up this installment and read it on its own.Invited to one of the pick social events of the year, the Fifty Shades of Greyhound Charity Ball, pet psychologist Caroline “Caro” Lamont is dressed to the nines and enjoying what she hopes will be a successful fund raising event for Greyhound Matters, a local rescue operation she is occasionally involved with.  When a stranger dropped dead at her feet during the party, Caro finds herself once again in the center of a police investigation.  Wondering which of the rich and successful guests at the party had something to hide, Caro soon finds herself pulled into investigating the murder.A well-established character, and the heroine of the series, Caro Lamont is beautiful, educated and devoted to the care and love of animals.  While originally licensed to treat humans, Caro now spends her days treating the “social” maladies of her four legged patients and their owners.  Devoted to her friends, Caro does have some emotional baggage (don’t we all), which helps make her an ideal investigator.  She has a real sense for people and knows when they’re hiding a problem.A handful of well-developed secondary characters help provide color, emotional angst and additional animals to the story.  I especially liked Caro’s best friend, former actress Diana Knight, and Caro’s office assistant, Verdi.  While the story begins somewhat slowly, the plot’s pace really picks up and the mystery is well developed.  While I did guess the identity of one villain, the “top dog” caught me completely by surprise.Will Caro and her friends be able to solve the mystery and clear an innocent man who gets caught up in the investigation? Will Caro’s slow developing romance continue to develop or take a blow? And will her ongoing battle over Grandma Tillie’s brooch finally get settled? You’ll have to read Fifty Shades of Greyhound to find out, I enjoyed it and look forward to reading more of Sparkle Abbey’s books.
summary: Fun Addition to Established Pet Mystery Series

When young cousin Felicity, a perfectly coiffed and manicured city sophisticate, comes to Misty Point farm, home  to Daniel and his sister Sophie, for a visit, strange things start to happen, beginning with the sudden death one night of all the chooks (aka chickens). Felicity is all agog over this jovial newcomer and falls all over herself trying to gain his attention.Concerned for the fate of their farm, Daniel and Sophie set upon separate investigative trails into the who and why of the inexplicable deaths of the chooks. The mystery starts to break when Patrick, Daniel, and Felicity go eeling late one evening and come upon their mean-spirited neighbor.The book gives a delightful bird's eye view of life in rural New Zealand. Told from ten-year-old Daniel's point of view, it is humorous and fast-paced. I started reading this book at the tail end of the second of two grueling international flights and was engrossed immediately, pausing only to admire the wonderful illustrations sprinkled throughout the narration. What to do, what to do? A brilliant character comes up with a secret solution to save the species. He wants his equally brilliant half brother to help him achieve it. The solution is something I've often wondered about and probably many of you have, too. So we get to share in the dilemma: if you were the half brother, what would you do?The author sets a fast pace while giving us time to relish plenty of smart future-tech and hard science.I can't wait to read the upcoming sequel!

reviewText: Originally posted at: [...]Out and proud Sebastian thinks he's seen it all until he finally meets Bella's brother and is thrown for a loop. Sebastian is an outgoing, gregarious, fun loving guy who's BFF's with his best girl Bella. Bella and Sebastian met at college and have been side by side ever since. Through bad boyfriends and unfortunate clothing choices, the two are as thick as thieves. So when the chance comes up to bunk at her brother's house for the summer before heading off for Sebastian's second doctorate, the two friends jump at the chance. Little they did realize that summer would change their lives.Bewitched By Bella's Brother is another great story from Amy Lane. This one is a contemporary romance that is pretty sweet with the only tension from Sebastian's commitment issues. The writing is great with a lot of fun banter and the friendship between Bella and Sebastian is really touching. They are catty, bitchy, and loving with each other. Bella's brother Asa has an adorable son Jordan and is openly bisexual. He's immediately interested in Sebastian but the two gradually fall in love. There is physical chemistry but they build a fulfilling emotional connection as well. Too often in books the characters have sex immediately and live happily ever after but this story shows that happening gradually and is all the better for it.The story is incredibly quick to read and I definitely was sorry to see it end. It's funny, witty, entertaining, absorbing, cute, and romantic. The sex between Asa and Sebastian is pretty hot but the dynamics of the family as a whole, including Bella and Asa's mother, father, etc, make for a well rounded cast. Sebastian is the star though and well worthy of the spotlight. The only hiccup in this engaging story is Sebastian's empty insistence on following his plans regardless of everything else. This keeps the tension in the story but the obvious happy ending is hanging over this conflict in neon lights so I could have done without it.Other than that, Bewitched By Bella's Brother delivers a thoroughly enchanting story from start to finish. This feels like a real love story and one you'll just adore reading. Asa's son Jordan threatens to steal the spotlight with his antics but he's just one of the cast that's likely to vie for reader hearts. Pick this up and choose your favorite. With as wonderful as this is, you're bound to have a tough time choosing.

There was a time when I would have pooh-poohed the concepts that traditional Chinese medicine are based on. Things like qi energy, yin and yang, and meridians seemed like so much pseudoscientific gobbledygook. Then, in 1998, I traveled to Beijing as a tourist. Prior to leaving home, I met a Chinese lady online who lived in Beijing and wanted to become a professional tourguide. She offered her guide/interpreter services in exchange for the opportunity to improve her English. Having her with me every day when I went out sightseeing was great, but what I learned after arriving was that she worked part-time in a traditional Chinese medical clinic. Out of curiosity, I went with her to the clinic a couple of times, and the doctors there were very happy to meet a westerner and talk about their practice. While I was there, I had a pulse diagnosis (it was pretty accurate) and got an acupressure massage. The result was that I was not nearly as skeptical about traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) after firsthand exposure to it.I apologize for the long preamble, but had it not been for that experience, I doubt if I would have had any interest in reading "Chinese Medicine for Healthy Skin." Author Michelle O'Shaughnessy has written a very interesting introduction to TCM, including the history of its development. The purpose of the book is to present a complete picture of how and why TCM works, and the healing benefits it offers. She explains the concepts of qi energy and the difference between heavenly qi and acquired qi, yin and yang (opposites), the twelve main meridians (channels in the body that facilitate the flow of qi), and the five elements (a way of categorizing life, nature, and the human body). All of these elements must be in balance in order to maintain good health.The book then describes various means by which harmonious balance can be restored, including the use of Chinese herbs, acupuncture, acupressure massage, and restorative foods. There are recommendations for using specific herbs to treat certain diseases, and there's a chapter on where to obtain these herbs and how to prepare them.I recommend the book for anyone who's interested in an introduction to traditional Chinese medicine, plus some recommendations on treating certain ailments, including skin conditions. Personally, I'm still a bit skeptical about some of the concepts behind TCM, but it's hard to overlook the success stories that I've heard. If you can keep an open mind and want to try some of the healing methods of TCM, this book may be the introduction you need.

reviewText: Brooke has reeled me in with this novella… This is one of her best yet since Kitchen Affairs. He is in charge of training the new intern, who ends up being Cecilia.What these two didn’t expect was to have a mutual attraction they cannot seem to fight, no matter how hard they try.  They also have more in common they have yet to find out.I love how the story is developed in this first part of the series.  It isn’t too fast where you would feel ripped off.  It isn’t too slow where you would want to gouge your eyes out wanting the author to get to the point already.  It is slow enough to torture you and fast enough to keep you waiting for the other shoe to drop!I have always been a fan of Brooke’s.  If this story continues on with how it started, there is a good chance this could be my favorite series of hers yet!

reviewText: "How to Relax - Mind Body & Soul" is a self-help book for people who are uptight and could use some tips on how to let go of stress and relax. This book is for everyone, since we all need to relax sometimes. The book is written with calming language that makes it relaxing just to read. It is a helpful and informative book.This book covers the following topics: external and internal stressors, taking control of your stress problem, self-awareness, putting yourself first, living in the present, quieting your inner voice, relaxing the body, sleeping, eating, taking vitamins, exercising, breathing, drinking water, meditating, being mindful, getting a massage, doing Reiki, Yoga, and Tai Chi, performing progressive muscle relaxation, and various relaxation techniques - both physical and mental.The book is short and to-the-point. It gives you a way to discover what you need to do to relax and what relaxation techniques you can try to find the ones that work for you. I recommend this book to everyone, since most of us could benefit from relaxing more. Plus, the book is informative and a good guide to decreasing stress.
summary: An Informative Guide to Relaxation and Reducing Stress

reviewText: I really enjoy Kim Dare's books, but this one was definitely not my favorite.  I'm not sure if it was just that I didn't "get" the point of the book, or whether I'm just tired of shapeshifters (although I adored "Duck!").  Or maybe it was that I didn't get enough world-building to get into the premise of the shifter packers, or it may just be that this particular series isn't for me...MILD SPOILERS FOLLOW:The book begins with Marsdon and his unknown "pup" in a BDSM club.  Marsdon, a were/shapeshifter, knows his sub is wolf, but doesn't know the other man's identity.  The man under the leather mask is Bennett, who Marsdon finds out later is another alpha-male.  Both men are deeply moved by their experiences together, and I have to say the sex at the beginning was incredibly hot - the best of the entire book for me.The two men/weres meet again, only this time, they are being joined as mates for a new were-pack.  Neither knew the other was his mate until the moment they meet, but both men recognize each other, in spite of the fact that Bennett's face and scent had been masked from Marsdon and Bennett could not see Marsdon through his mask.  The men are mated, and this is how the main story begins.Bennett comes off as incredibly insecure and unsure about what being an "alpha" means.  He has a deeply submissive nature (at least in the bedroom), but he is powerful and a born leader.  Marsdon is thrilled that he is being mated to the one man he has ever truly felt something for, but he continues to call Bennett his "pup" and manages to totally alienate Bennett.The book turns on the issue of what being an alpha is, and whether submission in a relationship, behind closed doors is the same as submitting in the pack hierarchy.  This is where I got lost.  Bennett is so anxious to prove himself, he's willfully blind to the reality that these are two different concepts, and Marsdon doesn't do a heck of a lot to convince him otherwise.  I just got bogged down in the various concepts of dominance and, although I like BDSM in general, I just couldn't get into the whole angst thing here.Dare's writing is always strong, but I felt as though I just wasn't "connecting" on an emotional level in this one.  That said, the book was probably worth the price I paid just for the prologue scene in the BDSM club with the two men.  That was one of the hottest slash scenes I've ever read (and I've read a lot).  So, split verdict for me...

reviewText: Things have moved along quite well for Lily since we first got to know her. The town of Ashford is gearing up to celebrate Easter in a big way. The romance between Damon and Lily has progressed to something pretty serious and Lily and Charlie are forging a wonderful relationship. Does it all sound too good to be true? Naturally, something has to happen to throw a kink in all that contentment. Joel, Lily's ex-husband is in Ashford and is wanting to meet with Lily. He claims he has something really important to discuss with her. After attempting to charm Lily, who doesn't fall for his " car salesman" tactics, he come out with the blunt truth. He's broke. His attempts to marry into money failed and now he is worse off than ever before. The only thing he can think of that could get him a little money is to fight Lily for the ownership of the cafe. He did lend her the money to start the business so now she either has to come up with twenty thousand dollars or go to court to fight his demands.This second novella in the series is just as good as the first one but can be read as a stand alone book. Damon is just as dreamy as before.Joel on the other hand... what a jerk.The other cast members are all wonderful. I always feel like I am right there in Rebecca's books the way she explains the decoration of the chocolate goodies or just about one of the characters how they say something you always can see them say that sort of thing in the way they do say it. Recommend book for sure. Loved it Rebecca keeping on bringing amazing books.

I purchased this book for my brother and decided to read it as well. Typically I'm not into dramas and suspense stories (more of a childhood literature, fairytale sort of gal). But I love reading and can't really pass up a book- so I gave this one a shot.Although the book has complex themes it's relatively easy to follow. For people who are interested in science and action themes- they will love this book. They aren't usually themes I read, but I enjoyed it nevertheless. The main character is a scientist working on a federal project to eradicate cocaine. Obviously he's a very intelligent man which sets him apart from many of the people who will be reading this story. We're not all biotechical geniuses. And at first I wasn't sure if I could truly relate to him as a character. Over time though, you begin to see him more as a human and less as a high IQ being. He becomes normal- although the storyline he's involved in is in no way average.Essentially a death sentence is put upon him by, who else, but one of the largest cocaine drug lords. Obviously they don't want him finishing his project, right? This creates a very tense atmosphere for a majority of the story. People who love suspense will love the fast pace of this novel. It definitely motivates you to flip from page to page with barely a breath in between. There are both high points and low points in the book. Quick moving action scenes and resting periods. It keeps you on the edge of your seat and you're not entirely sure what to expect as you continue reading. I find that to be a great trait for a suspense novel- as too many are too easy to read ahead of. This one keeps you guessing.As the story goes, the scientist has an allie keeping him from his murder. The 'heroic' aspect of the story. And a unique one. I've never really read a story with these theme before. The closest relation in storyline that I can think of is the television show 'Breaking Bad'- and to be honest it's not anywhere near that, but the nature of the drug theme is prevelent in both (although they essentially have opposing sides to the main character).The book is well-written and easy to follow. Although there are a lot of scientific-based parts, the book could easily be read by anyone with a basic knowledge of science. I'm not a biotechnology-fanatic so I'm not accustomed to many science-oriented terms. This kind of detered my from reading the book to begin with- I was afraid I wouldn't be able to follow it. But I followed it quite easily and enjoyed it too. My brother, who I originally bought the book for was really excited about it. He's into science, technology, and loves action. Combined all three aspects into this book and he was in love with it. Five stars from him for interest. Five stars from me for the unique read that I wouldn't typically find myself liking.

A brilliant look at our amazing brains and how we can fully utilize their seemingly limitless abilities. The power of the mind can accomplish so much. It can build civilizations, create fantastic inventions no one believed possible, and change the world for the better, and yet even with all that we've barely scratched the surface. In fact, most of us barely use our noggins for anything more taxing than navigating in traffic and balancing a budget.This book explores and explains the brain's potential to do more than we've ever imagined, to use thoughts to override long held subconscious beliefs, to actually change the brain by essentially rewiring  the neural pathways that drive your thoughts and actions. It's a spellbinding discussion, and though there's a lot of scientific data it isn't beyond the scope of the average reader. I'd recommend this book to anyone who is interested in putting that supercomputer between their ears to more productive use.

This turned out to be a tough read to review.  I read this darkly humorous short story twice.  I found that in one way I enjoyed it more the second time, because I picked up more of the little twinges of humor that were thrown in along the way to the twisted ending, and in another way I picked up on how, for me, it fell short of reaching it's full potential.  This was most obvious when I read parts of it aloud.It has a bit of a slow beginning - I would have liked to have met the main characters sooner.  Also, their reaction to poor Justin, while understandable to a degree, seems extreme given that we haven't witnessed enough other quirkiness to explain it.  It would be nice to have additional exposition on this, to explain why Clara and Esther were so quick off the mark, and why they reacted so similarly.Since in a short story there isn't enough character development for a reader to form an attachment to (or aversion to) the characters, and it's difficult to create tension with such a brief plot line, there has to be something else to reward the reader's attention.  In Murder at Shady Oaks, it's the off-the wall humor.  With a little more polishing of the timing of the dialog, this short story could be real gem.  As it is, it's funny.  It just left me with the impression that it could have been funnier.I'd still recommend it, though.  Not to give anyone ideas, of course.  Poor Justin.
summary: Dark, twisted humor.  I like it.

reviewText: Late August, 1882 in town of  Dennison, Montana Territory everyone but 23 year old Katherine Holmon has  gathered in town to watch the hangings of five outlawing rustlers. Katherine has come to town to get a husband! Her father's will didn't leave her any choice. She had to have a husband within six months to inherit her father's ranch, and the town of Dennison has a rule, a woman can save a condemned man by claiming him, and marrying him.Seems like the answer to her problems so  she chooses a badly beaten Wesley Austin Merrick, and her plan is to marry him,collect her ranch and then he can be on his merry way. As Wes recuperates at her ranch,she soon learns that Wes isn't what he first seemed, and that when the heart becomes involved plans often take a detour!The premise of a woman being able to "claim" a criminal and marry him was something I haven't read before,and it really drew me in. Once I started reading the story I really couldn't put it down. I had to know how things would work out for Katherine, after all she married an outlaw. I thought the author provided rich details,easily allowing me to visualize the story as it unfolded.I thought the story moved along at a pretty brisk pace and never found myself being bored. I was interesting to find out who Wes was and I thought the story line between Katherine and  Martin Denty added another to the story.  I also thought the character of Hannah was delightful.Overall, if enjoy reading well written historical  fiction that weaves together the elements of suspense,mystery and romance to give you a page turning story then look no further because your going to find it in "Montana Territory."  The story has me anxious to read  more of Ms. Limber's work!A complimentary copy of this book was provided in exchange for an honest review, and I can honestly say I loved this book!

reviewText: Everyone knows a Rebecca Banks in real life. She’s the kind-hearted, people-pleaser who wants to see the best in everybody, but who allows herself to be taken advantage of by a series of loser men. You can only feel sorry for her for so long, then after a point you want to slap her, and shout, “wake up.”That’s pretty much what happens in this book—only physical therapist Rebecca Banks gets spanked. She is taken in hand by a man from her past (a firefighter) when she is unable to do what she should do and break free of her verbally abusive, drug-using deadbeat boyfriend. Unfortunately, this does not happen soon enough and Rebecca is embroiled in legal troubles when her ex-boyfriend and his pals implicate her in a serious crime.I liked this book a lot. It is a well-written, slightly edgy novella that skates the line between spanking romance (domestic discipline) and BDSM. As the reader, I cheered when Sawyer, the man from her past, took her in hand in an effort to get her to do the right thing for herself. Rebecca is exactly the sort of woman who needs a keeper.I could see author Natasha Knight writing a sequel to this novel involving Rebecca and Sawyer (hint, hint) because I can see them further exploring the BDSM side of their relationship. I also liked the peek at Rebecca's attorney’s relationship with his wife, and think they deserve their own book too.Nicely done!

Sweet and emotional, Dominique Eastwick's short story gives readers a charming view of true love and second chances. Though the story's length prevented full exploration of many of the story's elements, this was still a fun read with heartfelt and realistic characters whose connection is undeniable in spite of all the history that lies between them.For as long as she can remember, Callie Sherman has been in love with her childhood best friend, Aiden Marshall. Along with their mutual friend Zia, the three were inseparable, but a childhood pact with Zia ensured that Callie could never act on her crush...even when Zia announced that she and Aiden were engaged. A single kiss in their childhood hideout seemed like the only thing that Callie and Aiden would ever share, and Callie has convinced herself that her dreams were never meant to be.What she doesn't know is how deeply that kiss affected Aiden as well. Though he had loved Callie for years, Aiden believed that she could never return his feelings and tried to move on. Now that his divorce is final, however, Aiden is determined to do whatever it takes to win Callie's heart and make her his, but will all the mistakes of their past get in the way of their happily ever after?For such a short story, these characters were well-developed and very sympathetic. Callie's mix of personal accomplishments and inner self-consciousness made her an easily identifiable and empathetic. Aiden is very clearly an upstanding and honest hero, and while I would have loved to know more about his early history with Callie and learned more about the evolving nature of their relationship, it was clear when they were together that their bond was a strong one and their chemistry was fantastic.Callie's reunion with Aiden was tender and wonderfully heartwarming. However, other than their own nerves, there was very little keeping them apart by the time their reunion took place. In a novella of this length, there wasn't room for a great deal of tension, but I would have wanted a bit more anxiety over their eventual happy ending. It was very interesting to see Aiden's side of the story and understand the way that one kiss affected him. However, because readers are aware of his thoughts and experiences, they know more than the characters, which is a tricky situation for an author, making it difficult to build suspense.I enjoyed seeing other members of Callie's family and getting to learn a bit about all the relationships that make up her world. Though very secondary to the character-driven plot, the setting and supporting cast added a good deal to the world of the book and understanding of our hero and heroine.Dealing with a love triangle is never easy, but I found the way that Dominique Eastwick dealt with Zia's involvement in the plot helped develop the characters that she had created and also provided a satisfactory conclusion to this story . All in all, this is an engaging, emotional story of redemption and second chances, making for a fun single-serving read.Reviewed by Bridgetfor TheRomanceReviews.com

I remember the phone call well.It was the summer of 1988. I was a skinny, self-conscious teenager with raging hormones, no girlfriend to speak of, proud owner of a part-time job in a local stationery store, and horny as hell. (Hey, I'm honest!)I happened to be sitting in the living room, thumbing through the local newspaper, my attention riveted to the baseball box scores, when a small, innocuous advertisement situated in the lower-right-hand corner, just below an AP blurb about a California Angels-Montreal Expos trade, caught my eye.I took a closer look and saw that it was one of those 1-900 numbers that featured hot, explicit phone chat with a beautiful lady. I was incredibly tempted to make a call right then and there, but I also was cognizant of my parents' habit of scrutinizing every bill that arrived in the mail. I figured that having an adults-only number prominently displayed on next month's phone statement wouldn't put me in very good stead with either of my folks, and so I surreptitiously hid the sports section in my room until it could be put to use later that night.I determined that, if I made the call after midnight, excess charges wouldn't apply, and, as such, wouldn't even show up on next month's bill. (Keep in mind that this was eighteen-year-old logic and reasoning being applied here.)I ended up waiting until about one in the morning. I tiptoed downstairs and retrieved the cordless phone (!) from its kitchen cradle and snuck back upstairs into my room, which was a refurbished attic floor.My hands shaking, I punched the digits and waited for what seemed to be an interminable length of time.Then a woman's voice answered. "Phone sex," she stated, in about the most monotone, matter-of-fact, decidedly un-sexy voice I had ever heard.I immediately hung up without even responding. The whole affair had lasted approximately eight seconds.Looking back upon my youthful indiscretion, I was definitely more scared than aroused. I also wrestled with conflicting feelings of innate curiosity and self-loathing: after all, what sort of mental defective would stoop so low as to place a call to some anonymous woman who, in reality, was probably old and fat and wrinkled and sagging?As Dierks Bentley would sing: what was I thinking?Turns out that more men---and a few women---did such so-called stooping than I realized, which put me in the category of "Curiosity Didn't Kill the Cat, But Came Very Close to Maiming It."I never called back, and had no desire to do so. Eventually I was able to come to some sort of internal resolution, and that was thus: chalk it up to an unpleasant experience, and stick to self-improvement by chatting it up with girls at the high school dances. Oh, and don't sneak around your parents' collective backs, either. Not too cool. (I attended an all-boys' Catholic school, so the fair sex was at a premium.)My fumbling experiment with phone sex in the pre-Internet age was, in retrospect, fairly standard fare. Nowadays, a person can simply download free porn and store it in their iPhone in a matter of seconds. (Perhaps it's a good thing that my cell phone is pre-paid and lacks Internet access.)This trip down memory lane is a segue into Sandra Ross's book "Phone Sex: Erotic Fantasies and Sexual Fetishes." The protagonist, Sydney, is certainly far more attractive and alluring than the unknown maven at the other end of my awkward phone call from over two decades previous.Of course, Ross has a tremendous talent for creating characters that cater to most mens' fantasies. Her physical description of Sydney and her wardrobe evokes images that bring forth mental comparisons to the ubiquitous centerfold: "(Sydney) walked into her bedroom and picked up (her) royal purple teddy. . .(i)t was trimmed in black with black front lace ups. She chose black silk thigh-high stockings to top off the outfit. . .(Sydney) stood at 5'8" with long, toned legs, rounded ass, cinched in waist and D cup breasts." (ch. 1)Sydney's bountiful assets are both a prequel to, and a prerequisite for, her job as a phone sex operator (PSO). Despite the lurid, unsavory reputation such an occupation entails (similar to that of a stripper or a prostitute), she is a rarity in the world of work: she loves what she does and she is very good at it.Although working as a PSO certainly isn't a conventional, nine-to-five career, it's fairly obvious that she has been able to carve out a lucrative career simply by utilizing a speaker phone and her dulcet tones. For what she is charging (and I'm guessing it's a fairly large sum, based upon Ross's vivid descriptions), it's her dream job. Not many people can honestly say that their occupation is something for which they eagerly hop out of bed in the morning.I admire Sydney for doing something she loves, and for making informed choices that have directly benefitted her and her customers: by making her clientele feel emotionally and sexually satiated, she in turn derives happiness and satisfaction for doing her job well. This is demonstrated when Sydney engages in a hot tete-a-tete with Steven, one of her favorite clients whose sultry words turn her on as much as her conversation does the same for him."Phone Sex" provides some well-written, highly erotic dialogue that is a Ross forte. She delivers a fast-paced story that is eminently readable and satisfying.
summary: E.T., Don't Phone Home Until You've Read This

I also enjoyed the time travel aspect, and I really liked how the heroine resigned herself to her fate and tried to make the best of it without dragging her feet for half the book.While I overall really liked this book, there are some disturbing things as well. Is cholesterol really the great killer it's been made out to be? Do we really need all of the medications to control it we're being sold? According to John McArthur, whose informative book  looks to overturn much of what we believe about our bodies and our health, the answer is no. The book also contains a TON of great, heart-healthy recipes.

As always, J.D. Favor has given us a fun read. Her characters, even the secondary ones, are well developed. Her descriptions are beautiful, pulling the reader in and making him feel part of the story. Add plot twists and a sizzling romance. What more could a reader want?

P.D. Singer is an excellent writer. I previously enjoyed her "Donal agus Jimmy" tremendously and was not disappointed with "Scrum." This story has a theme similar to that of "Dancer" by B. Alexander in that both stories center around a smitten fan of a star in a particular field who yearns to meet the object of his fascination. I don't know which I liked more, being neither a fan of rugby or dance. However, I can say I enjoyed each of them. "Scrum" is expertly written without a word out of place. The story is well constructed and takes the reader just where the author wants one to go.  The only thing I can say to the contrary is that the author employs the seemingly almost standard female writer's take on lovemaking between men, which I gather appeals to female readers. That's perfectly fine. (Of course!) But reality may be a bit different. Nevertheless: great story from a great writer!

My wife and I have been avid gardeners for years, and we try really hard to only use safe, natural products on our plants. One of the most frustrating issues for us has been dealing with a myriad of pests without resorting to chemical means of eradication. This guide offers a wealth of information on how to get rid of the pests without harming the good bugs or our health. The recipes for organic sprays were great, especially the tomato leaf one which I'd never heard of. The section on diseases and organic means of curing them was also very helpful. I would recommend this book to any gardener who is interested in going organic in the garden.
summary: Very helpful information for our organic garden

Feeling depressed? As this book makes clear depression is a common condition that is more complicated than many people think.Over Coming Depression is a short read that in its 28 pages clarifies the many different types (levels) of depression and makes some common sense recommendations to overcome or to at least gain control of the many unpleasant symptoms depression can bring on.The main take away is that lasting depression in any form should not be taken lightly. While everyone at times is subject to some form of depression medical help should be used for long lasting or deep depression.Several suggestions for overcoming bouts of common depression are given. Hint: Maintaining a healthy lifestyle is important.
summary: Don't Stay Depressed. Read this Book

I wanted to understand the reasons behind his player lifestyle; his need to remain unattached from anyone but Brax and Elle. Shay's relationship/closeness with Elle proved to me that he was more than capable of love, so I knew the loss that Brax tiptoes around with Shay was beyond devastating, and boy was I right!One Year Earlier - this is where Shay and Brenna's story begins, and even though their first encounter doesn't go so well, the attraction between them exists from the very beginning. Despite Brenna's father's ploys to break them up, they remain together and fall hopelessly in love, but readers already know that the end to their story is not a happy one, and the events that lead to Brenna being stripped from Shay's life are excruciating, especially when her father told Shay to not let anything happen to Brenna.After reading their story, it totally makes sense why Shay was the way he was in the other two books in the series. Lost Without You completed the series for me; I needed to know Shay's past to accept what happened in his present. Shay's life was never complete after Brenna, and even though, the ended of Lost for You was hard to accept - Shay got what he wanted....what he needed to be whole again. The words BJ Harvey wrote at the end of the text from Shay's perspective are beyond amazing...they are the perfect sentiment of Shay's love for Brenna. I couldn't have asked for a better story!Complimentary copy provided by author/publisher for an honest review.5 poison apples! (The Fairest of All Book Reviews)

reviewText: Brenna Halsted's last photo shoot has gone terribly wrong, leaving the fashion model mentally and physically scarred.  The love and friendship of her platonic and long-time friend, Drew Constantine, can not give her respite from the phantom pains she feels or mend her damaged confidence.  His declarations of love can't thwart her plans to find sexual release and, hopefully, freedom from her pain in the arms of a mystery man, Kostas Drakos, provided by Madame Eve.  Kostas has loved Brenna from afar for years, and he wants to gift Brenna with a night of happiness freeing her to soar above the mental and physical pain she feels.  This is a gift he desperately wants to give Brenna, but for her the gift could come at a high price.EROTIC HEALING is a prime example of why I've become addicted to the "One Night Stand Series." Becca Dale has authored a superb tale of beauty lost and a damaged soul in the character of Brenna Halsted.  Her beauty is damaged and confidence is so shattered she can't see the true love Drew offers her.  Drew Constantine is a wonderful character with charm and compassion who only wants the best for his friend, even to the point of encouraging her to try Madame Eve, though he regrets it later and attempts to talk her out of it. Kostas Drakos is a dream of character whose sole desire to heal Brenna will melt your heart.Ms. Dale's writing is exquisite in the sexual scenes between Kostas and Brenna as he struggles to control his growing passion and maintain his emotional distance while using sweet sexual torment to help Brenna break through the physical and emotional barriers preventing her from getting past the accident and living again. These scenes are graphic, intense, but also, extremely touching.There is a happily ever after for Brenna, although for a moment I thought Madame Eve had lost her touch.  I haven't read any of the latest entries in the "One Night Stand Series."  I hope the later ones are up to par with those I have read and reviewed thus far.  I can only say my addiction to the "One Night Stand Series" continues. Heaven help me, I'll be broke by the time I've read them all.
summary: Superb Characters, Sexual Heat & An Absolutely Wonderful Story!

I bought Marked yesterday and finished it today. It's yet another Kaylea Cross hit for me. There's a different feel to Marked than to her last couple of series which were largely set on military bases or in foreign countries. But, as usual, the heroine is more than equal to the hero. Rachel is smart, beautiful and an accomplished architect. Jake is a highly trained, handsome federal agent. They have a history, dating back a few years, which didn't end well. Regardless, when she calls on him to help her with something that she has a really, really bad feeling about, he's there for her in a heartbeat. There's no re-living how things went so woefully wrong in the past. They start with a breakfast meeting and simply move forward. Over time, they take it one step further and agree not to lose touch again because each recognizes how much they care about the other. Meantime, it turns out that Rachel's gut feeling was spot-on and the "badness" was about to take a turn that would put her brother, Brandon, in the path of a misguided evil guy and place some of the fine citizens of the DC area at risk. Jake and company to the rescue!Marked is good from start to finish and I think it's a quicker read than some other books because there are far fewer bad guys to keep straight, and because of its US setting. Rachel and Jake don't immediately fall into bed with each other but when they get there the sheets are singed. There are three rather hot bedroom sequences; quite frankly, though, the scene where Jake is determined to get some food into Rachel before she collapses was hotter for me. How can you not love a man who takes such good care of his woman (so to speak) when she is so stressed that she can't take care of herself?So, 5-stars for a good plot, solid chemistry, and having not one, but two, strong female characters. Can't want for Celida's story. Wouldn't mind hearing about Brandon's once he grows up, too, but I suspect/hope there are lots of other KC stories to be written before his.

reviewText: Rockstar Daddy was a pleasant and easy read; one that I was able to get through within a couple of hours on a Sunday afternoon.The story of Jax and Kendal though reminiscent to a few other romance stories out there had a different taste to it which I really enjoyed. What differentiated Rockstar Daddy was that the author was really able to portray the mother and son connection between Kendal and Finley. The few other books with similar plots fail to do that, they only truly focus on the relationship between the hero and the heroine. By giving her readers a taste of Kendal’s bond with Finley, it gives her character more depth which is always a win for a book heroine.I love second chance romances and this one was no exception. During the times that they were apart due to a misplaced selfless act, Kendal and Jax still very much loved each other. They both longed for each other throughout the entire years they were separated and their love for each other never faltered, even after having relationships with other people (or in Jax case, many, many other people). I was surprised not to have read any steamy, sex scenes in this book at all- with a title like Rockstar Daddy and with a cover like that, I was expecting it and was a bit disappointed. With two very good looking, virile characters, I’d think that the author would have at least given us a hint of their sexual chemistry.My biggest complaint about Rockstar Daddy would be the inanimate, unneeded details that are littered all over the pages of this book. I mean, I get it; authors want their readers to be able to visualize what is happening; a way to get their readers to live through their words… But to me, there were too many minute details which quite honestly, took me out of the zone. Just when a great dialogue is finally taking form, it would revert back to the characters dress color, the kind of shoes Kendal is wearing, the etc., etc. I wish that the details were done more with purpose rather than come off as fillers.Overall, I enjoyed this book. Again, it’s short and sweet and I am looking forward to see what is in store for Jax and Kendal and I am truly pulling for them to have their much deserved happily ever after.For our full review click here: http://welikeitbigbookblog.wordpress....

As I set out to review this book, I found that it would be best to separate my thoughts into two categories: the book, and the book the book is about!The Book:My Age of Anxiety by Scott Stossel: A 30-minute Chapter-by-Chapter Summary: Fear, Hope, Dread, and the Search for Peace of Mind is a well written, concise summation of My Age of Anxiety that was bite-sized enough to read through in an abbreviated amount of time, but in depth enough to leave me feeling like I could grasp the content of the source material. The brevity of the book did not seem to detract from the presentation of the content, and at no point did it seem to me that the author lacked understanding of the source, but rather they helpfully (and quickly) guided me through the big picture ideas. Indeed, there was a surprising amount of detail for such a compressed version.The Book the Book is About:My Age of Anxiety seems like a compelling read. I didn’t realize how recently the movement toward dedicated study of anxiety and anxiety-related ills had actually taken off. The nervous stomach section was relevant to my interests, and I appreciated that I could skim through, catching the overarching information, and decide whether to investigate the topic in more detail on my own. The anxiety related topics covered range from the history of study to social constructs to medication and nature vs. nurture theories.I would definitely recommend this book for anyone interested in the subject, but unable to dedicate a large block of time to studying it.

This plan starts out with advice laid in chapter three-to organize "sex dates" with your partner. Then you will learn how to communicate sexually with your partner in a successful manner. Ms Gray also gives a lot of useful information about helathy nutrients for the improvement of libido, and talks about sexual desire at different stages of life. What I particularly loved in this book is the fact that in every chapter you have number of useful tips and advices how to apply particular idea from that chapter. reviewText: I loved Save My Soul. Zoe Winters has amazingly polished her writing and the story flows smoothly through the whole book. The plot is set up brilliantly and things you thought were just fillers in the story gets picked up later. In the end there's several twists, each one of them making you speed up your reading to see what happens next. I have to admit, I did not see THAT coming.In the beginning we get to know Anna, who after her fathers death returned to the town she grew up in. With a heritage she doesn't really need to worry about money, so she buys a house she loved as a kid and settles in. Anna is not one to believe in ghosts and magic, but when it becomes evident, that she's not alone in the house with her cats the story starts to unfold.We're introduced with Luc, the sexy incubi, who can't leave the house. Tam, Anna's childhood friend, coming back into her life. Horrifyingly realistic nosy neighbors, more demons, priests, hookers, gypsies, a van that plays the ghostbusters theme. The range of the secondary characters is astounding and all of them so well written. Makes you wonder which one Winters will pick to be the heroine in her next book - asuming she still continues with the same fictional world. I guess it would be Tam, though one of the hookers would be a really interesting choice to read about.And when you're reading a book where there's an incubi, you should know to be ready for some steamy moments. All the sexual tension and sex scenes are - as the rest of the book - very well written and leaves you with a craving. The scenes don't feel misplaces as they can in some books - in Save My Soul they have a rightfully claimed spot.I can't find anything real to criticize and I might end up repeating myself, but it's just that good. There was only one minor thing with Anna's thoughts about Cecelia Townsend, that snapped me out of the book when I read it, because it seemed to be contrary to what had been told to us just a bit earlier.Anyway Save My Soul is a great book. Go read it. :)
