Miss. George’s Second Chance by Heather Boyd(Novella #2: Miss Mayhem Series)Source: PurchaseRating: 4/5 starsPeter Watson has a serious problem; OK, Peter Watson has a few serious problems: he loves to gamble but isn’t very good at it, he is on the verge of losing absolutely everything and, the woman he is engaged to doesn’t love him at all.  More to the point, the woman Peter is engaged to asked him to marry her so that she may use her considerable fortune to help save him.  Yeah, that’s just how every marriage should start out.Imogen George has a serious problem; OK, Imogen George has a few serious problems: she is losing her sight which will most certainly impede her ability to write, her blindness will (in her own head!) render her nothing more than a burden to her brother and, the man she is engaged to just found out he won’t be going to the poor house after all so there is no reason at all for her to continue the engagement.  Somehow, nothing is going according to plan.Imogen and Peter have known one another for many, many years and though both is fond of the other, their engagement was certainly never based on a great love or passion.  Once Imogen learned that Peter would no longer need her fortune to help him, she set him free to pursue his own life and perhaps even find a great love and passion.  Ever the practical woman, Imogen truly believes she is doing what is best for Peter and won’t hear any arguments to the contrary.  Because of Imogen’s extreme stubbornness and with no other option available to him, Peter leaves his home and Imogen in order to set in order the new fortune and title bestowed to him by a distant relative.  For the next year, Peter and Imogen both attempt to lead their lives as best they can.  For Peter this means making some serious adjustments to his new lot in life and for Imogen, it means watching her career and future diminish as her eyesight becomes worse and worse.One year later . . . .Sir Peter Watson has returned home and is one very, very determined man.  Almost immediately upon his arrival, Peter begins making inquiries about Imogen and her current situation.  Though he is surprised to learn that she is completely blind, this fact in no way changes Peter’s mind regarding Imogen becoming his wife.  One year earlier, Peter played by Imogen’s rules and he ended up walking away from the one and only woman who has ever been able to hold his interest and ignite his passion.  Now all he has to do is convince one thoroughly stubborn woman that he is right and she is wrong.  The wooing of Miss Imogen George is completely entertaining and quite sweet.  Peter understands that Imogen is very scared about her condition and distraught that she has no way continue writing and so he sets about soothing her fears and showing her that there are ways for her to write even without her site.  With Peter’s attention and unwavering affection, Imogen slowly begins to “see” the error of her ways as well as the possibility of a future that involves not just marriage but a marriage based on mutual love and great passion.The Bottom Line: Boyd continues the Miss Mayhem Series with one exceptional character, Imogen George.  Though Imogen is ridiculously stubborn, she is also very practical, quite creative and not willing to compromise anything where her writing and expectations for marriage are concerned.  Imogen desperately wants to believe Peter and so she allows him to both help and woo her; watching as Imogen truly begins to believe and accept Peter is a true treat.  In all, this is a solid and fine new addition to the Miss Mayhem series and one I am feel confident recommending to lovers of Regency reads, HEAs, novellas, continuing series and, second chance stories.
summary: More mayhem is on the way . . . .

reviewText: If you have a need for a keyboard on your Kindle, this is a great one.  The case fits either the Kindle Fire HD 7", or the Kindle Fire HDX 7".  I have the latter model.I use the 7" tablet because it is so versatile while also being small and convenient.  The beauty of the Belkin QODE is it adds the functionality of a keyboard, while also serving as a protective case, and manages to keep the Kindle lightweight in doing so.The QODE is a combination of a nice case and a very thin, highly functional keyboard.  Although new for Kindles, Belkin has similar product lines for iPads already in stores.The box include the case/keyboard combo, a micro-to-USB charging cable, and a user manual.  The manual is basically a card and contains little information.The exterior is a synthetic leather-looking material.  It seems to be of good quality and durable.  The case folds over the front of the Kindle, while the tablet sits in the case with the back fully covered.  The case uses a magnetic closure, which is different from its bigger brother, which fits the 8.9" Kindle (that model has an elastic strap which secures the case when closed).The case interior is covered with a soft material.  The easel which holds the Kindle is plastic. The QODE can be positioned at two viewing angles.  And yes, you can still use the tablet in portrait mode (the keyboard is landscape only, of course).  The keys are large enough to type without difficulty.  I am a man with good-size hands but don't have any issues typing, or hitting keys accidentally due to keyboard size.  It is a smaller keyboard though, as it has to fit the Kindle.The keyboard is super thin so kudos to Belkin on making a Bluetooth keyboard product which adds such functionality, but doesn't increase bulk much at all.The case pairs easily to the Kindle.  All Kindle buttons and ports are accessible in the case.  The keyboard is well thought out, and has a couple of nice features such as a microphone key and a browser key.  It also has a Home key, which can double as a Lock key when used with the Function key.  Other keys are Save, Cut, Paste, up/down/let/right, and volume up/down.  Basically, it's a nice way to type on the Kindle, but still use tablet tap commands.Charging the battery is done through the included USB charging cable (no AC adapter included).  The charge is separate from the Kindle, so you can leave the keyboard off and turn it on only when you need it, if you like.  The case will put the Kindle to sleep and wake it up when closed/oepened.This is Bluetooth, so you can pair it with other devices.  Just keep in mind it is made specifically for the 7" Kindle, so, for example, you can certainly pair it with something else, but you'd be able to use it only as a freestanding keyboard, not a case.Overall, this is a nice case.  I have a couple of minor gripes with it, which keep it from being a `5'.  I would have preferred that the case interior not become part of the bottom of the stand when in viewing mode.  This, to me, seems like it will accumulate dirt over time, and since it's the case interior.....eh.I also am not crazy about the way it folds when closed.  It does not close like a portfolio, but more like a tri-fold wallet.  I realize this was necessary as a concession to the keyboard, but I am concerned that the keyboard could come in contact with the Kindle screen.Don't get me wrong, I thoroughly enjoy the QODE.  I just think it's "very nice" as opposed to perfect.
summary: Excellent Keyboard - Very Nice But Not A Perfect '5'

3.5 Stars!!This is the second book of Tracy Wolff’s that I have read and I have thoroughly enjoyed both. Both series are written differently, Crash Into Me is from 3rd person perspective, whereas Ruined (Ethan Frost) was from the 1st person. However it is evident that Tracie knows how to write romance novels as she blew me away with this rocker story and I'm excited to read more from this world.Jamison has had a rough trot losing her car, boyfriend and her job and just wants to relax by watching her brother and his world famous band, Shaken Dirty, perform. She has always had an attraction to the lead singer, Ryder, since they were children. He has never seen her as more than his best friends sister, so she has done her best to move on with her life. Seeing all the troubles that she has been though is a little sad, and she is not confident with her looks or her body, so she believes that there is no way she has a chance with Ryder. I was secretly rooting for her and soon she could see things a little differently.Ryder has had women around him since he lost a girlfriend many years ago, to something he couldn't prevent. He tries to keep people at a distance and we discover his little secrets along the way. He really is a sweet guy and has a soft spot for Jamison, which he doesn't understand. She pushes his buttons like none has in a long time. Watching him unravel his feelings and seeing them interact was excruciating at times, because the sexual tension was pretty intense!As it is a rocker story, I was taken into the world of rock n roll and we dive into the world of touring, babes and drugs. There is a side story in this book that becomes quite dire and I was shocked as to what happened. So much happened in such a small amount of time that I was left speechless. Tracy Wolff has done a spectacular job opening up this series with this book. There is plenty of lust, sizzling scenes and day to day action that will keen you engrossed in the story and wanting the next one immediately, to see id others in the band can find their HEA!!I received a copy of this book from the Publisher, via NetGalley in exchange for an honest review.
summary: Plenty of lust, sizzling scenes and day to day action that will keen you engrossed in the story

Sam and Lily have been friends since they were 14 years old. Sam has been in love with his best from since they first met but has never told her or acted on it in any way. He's watched from the sidelines as Lily became engaged to another man and then was there for her as she suffered through a traumatic breakup before she tied the knot. Although Sam did not the all the details of the break up, he was there for her unconditionally.Lily has feelings that go beyond friendship for Sam as well but due to the circumstances of her break-up with her fiance, she doesn't want to become in involved with any man, much less her best friend. She feels that Sam is a forever kind of guy who deserves a woman who can give him the same. But when mutual caring and attraction lead to a very hot encounter, Sam is ready to push for more from Lily. Lily puts the breaks on fast but then has a change of heart later when she realizes she misses sex and proposes that they enter into a friends with benefits situation, no strings attached, and then they'll end their affair after a period of time.I loved Sam. He had a hard childhood, took care of his younger sisters and has worked hard his whole life. He's loyal, and steadfast and head over heals in love with Lily. But he's no saint--his dirty thoughts about Lily and the things he'd like to do with her are just enough to scuff up that squeaky clean image and make him a swoon worthy hero.Lily on the other hand was a bit of a mess for lack of a better word. She has quite a lot of emotional baggage but still, I had a hard time excusing her behavior toward Sam at times. She feels Sam is deserving of a forever kind of girl, and so she keeps her distance romantically even though she has feelings for him. But then she flips and proposes a friends with benefits relationship when she decides she misses sex. The reason this didn't totally work for me is because Sam and Lily are supposed to be best friends so she must have picked up on at least some kind of "I have stronger feelings than friendship for you" vibe from Sam. I had a hard time believing they could be so close and she could be totally oblivious to his feelings and so her proposal seemed selfish to me. On the other hand, it only fueled my sympathy for Sam and I really wanted him to have his happily ever after.Something So Right is filled with emotional angst and smoking hot sexual tension. Two best friends who have a mutual admiration for one another with one secretly in love with the other for years is a wonderful set up for a very romantic story. And this is a romantic story with a nice little happily ever after at the end. Despite a few problems I had with the heroine, I enjoyed this emotional story of two friends who eventually find love with each other.
A really good paced read with characters you can relate to. Can't wait until the next book in the series!!

Sheila Donahue is a very noble heroine with a lot of pressure on her shoulders. Her mother died a few years before, leaving the responsibility of caring for Mely on her shoulders. Mely has multiple sclerosis, and Sheila cares for her as best she can. She is also working on her doctorate, which doesn't leave much time for a love life.When she is offered a job as a translator for a week, she allows herself to be convinced to take it, despite her already busy schedule. The pay is extremely well, and the money will definitely come in handy. Sheila knows the life insurance money from her mother's passing won't last forever.Immediately I like this heroine. She's in a tight spot, but she continues to plow away at life in the hopes that things will get better. When she meets Cruz Terranova and realizes he's her boss, she's immediately physically attracted to him.... In a very steamy way. The author is very descriptive with this initial attraction, and boy could I feel the heat. By the time she was done with this scene even I was wondering what he looked like naked.... *wink*!Monica Hart has created a book right up there in quality with Harlequin novels (which I adore) and pumped them up a notch, with steamy sex scenes that practically sizzle off the pages. This is not your everyday, romantic read. The plot takes twists and turns that are extremely realistic and exciting to read. It's a real page turner that kept me engrossed to a tearful, cliffhanger ending.If you enjoy reading epic romance, you will love Castilian Heat. I give it five stars for the creative plot, steamy sex scenes, and emotional, heart-filled writing. Can't wait for the next one!Author Rose Wynters

One tragedy changes the lives of a once happy couple forever. Moon Over Alcatraz is Brandy and Weston's story. This is an emotional fiction novel that follows the pair after their loss, and how things change so quickly, they try to get back where they once were- happy and in love.I feel so terrible for both Brandy and Weston. Each character handles things differently, some of them i felt upset about, some I understood.  It's like being in the middle, trying to not take sides, but in a way, I saw things through both of their eyes.The author takes readers on a journey of learning how to deal with what life throws at your. One decision leads to a different outcome, some of which I never saw coming.Moon Over Alcatraz is a fiction novel that is moving, heartfelt, and so true to life.  Things can make or break a couple, and reading this made me realize the act of doing something will lead you on a different road sometimes, and there's nothing you can do to stop it or go back.I enjoyed the book.  I was sympathetic towards the characters. I got mad, I shed some tears, i rejoiced in the happy moments- yes, this story touched my heart. If you enjoy reading a fiction novel that has the power to bring out the tears, a few laughs, and an experience you won't soon forget, check out Moon Over Alcatraz.

Isolation picks up where Devastation left off, all of the kids spread out in the Safe Zone, after a long, terrifying journey to get there where they suffered through starvation, dehydration, and debilitating fear. Even after reaching their destination Fallon, Desiree, Sandi, Brody and Guy are left to realize that there is nothing SAFE about the Safe Zone. America is still in the war with Canada, life is hard and nothing like before the war, and the kids have been forced to grow up way to fast. Living in group homes and working wherever the government tells them to work, school and being a normal kid is a thing of the past. Fallon and Desiree are finally back together again after being branded as traitors and then pardoned, but they only have a few days together before Fallon is sent off to war, as every able-bodied person, male or female, over the age of 17 is. Brody and Sandi have started a new relationship even though they know that they will both be sent off to war soon and who knows when they will see each other again. Guy, the Canadian that saved their lives, is fixing to be thrown into a situation that he might never get out of, spying on his own country to help the Americans. Will the kids make it through alive? Will their relationships last? What else can the world throw at them that it hasn't already? Apparently, it can throw so much more at them as their journey continues...in the Safe Zone...and in the war.Isolation was a very enjoyable, action packed read. I found myself holding my breath on multiple occasions and also crying my eyes out. These kids have went through so much, in the first book and the second. The setting just seems like it could be realistic, like it could happen tomorrow. You instantly connect with the characters and you bond with them in ways that have you fully invested in their futures. In Isolation, new characters are introduced and right off the bat they are just part of your heart as well. 12 yr old Danny will break your heart and make you root for him till the end and Demsey is just a straight up hero in my book. I highly recommend that you pick up the Built on Fear series. I am eagerly awaiting the third installation. I actually tried to turn the page on my kindle for like 2 minutes on the last page because I just could not believe that it ended that way! I give Isolation 5 stars!Quotes from the Book:"Your faith, your perseverance, the fact that we're even here! I mean...there has to be something, right?"We'll see each other again. In this life or the next.""But, life is now and none of us know if we are going to be here tomorrow, so I'm just living it.""I hate you because I want to ask you what to do. You're the only one I trust but...I don't know if I should be bothered by you, scared of you, or standing behind you."I received this book in exchange for an honest review. I was in no way compensated for reviewing this book.
summary: Awesome Adventure...I just hope it never really happens :)

reviewText: I've read every one at least once and keep them as a fall back when I want something great to read.

101 Moments of Trust by Marion Bond West is a compilation of Marion's favorite devotionals over the years she has written for Guideposts.Marion's selections are God moments in her life that touched my heart, as I could relate to many of her articles.  She is adamant about learning the truth of His will for our lives and our obedience to Him when He sets us in specific circumstances to minister to others.Some of my favorites are:Test My Faith; Let God In; There is Peace, Sone-yah (this one is super special!); Reminders and Grow; Laughter Heals; Persistence Pays Off; and Take a U-Turn.Pick up a copy and read about the author's life and glean truth for your own life.This eBook was provided by Amy Lathrop and Christen Krumm of Litfuse Publicity Group in exchange for my honest review.  No monetary compensation was received.

Then, Again by Karen Stivali was such a sweet, romantic, and heartwarming story.  It made me swoon, it made me laugh. it was a true love story, one where that made me feel better for reading it.I was consumed and elated while reading this book.  The one word I would describe this very romantic story would be perfect.This is the love story between Kay and James.  Kay has just found out her grandmother has passed away.  She heads home to New York after being on location for a photo shoot.  She discovers her boyfriend has been cheating on her.  So she heads back to her grandmother's house to take care of her affairs.  While back in town she runs into James a man she had a childhood crush on when she was younger.  They are both adults now and a lot has changed since they were kids.  First off they are insanely attracted to each other, they have so much fun together.  Their feeling start to grow and they enter a romantic relationship.  The problem is Kay has a demanding job and being with James has made her feel things she never felt before.  They have fallen for one another and what the future holds is a mystery.  Will Kay's highly demanding job come first for her?  Or will James convince her that they are worth the risk?I thought these two had to be the most adorable couple I have read about in a very long time.  These are two very good people who want the same things from each other.  It seems a shame if they can't make things work between them.  He is there for her during one of the worst times in her life.  Her mother isn't really emotionally available to her and her grandmother was the most important person in her life.  Not only does James understand her, he want to be everything he can to her.  There are a few obstacles they have to overcome in order to be happy.  I just think these two are meant to be happy together.  I want to see them get their happily ever after in a very bad way.

What a lovely tribute this author gave of his mother, Iris.  It was not only heartwarming but it gave the reader a personal perspective of what the times and life was like during the budding years of medical breakthroughs, specifically polio.  The polio vaccine would not be introduced until over a decade after the first setting in this book.  Hence, the Sipolski family would be facing primitive views and treatment for the said condition.  At that time (here, 1940s) the public didn't know the cause of such an affliction so it made sense that some believed in old wives tale preventive measures and have disrespectful attitudes about the illness.  Even Iris found herself caught making a derogative remark only later to discover that her second son (the author) would be diagnosed with polio. That, plus being widowed at a young age and having to raise two very young boys, Iris sure had difficult challenges on her plate.  Luckily for Iris, she was strong and patient.  It appeared that every choice she made was in consideration for her boys' well being.  Including to marry again so as to have a father figure for her children.  She was stern and proactive in the care of her polio son and overall set a loving environment for her family.  Thereby instilling confidence, particularly in her children, to go after an enriching life.  Certainly a woman deserving of admiration.  Don't get me wrong, she made mistakes but she lived her life with faith and heart.Considering that this book was based on a true story involving the author, I got emotionally vested.  I couldn't help but get all choked up at the poignant part regarding the eldest son.  It was the first point where I felt heartache for the author.  There had been several trying times by then but that one incident just struck me hard.  Then the ending took me by surprise and left me feeling uneasy ...too sad.This really was not all a downer.  In fact, I enjoyed several quiet chuckle moments.  For the most part,  this was a life inspiring piece and contained multiple love stories (I liked Bill).  I'm not surprise that it is optioned for film.  I would definitely see it!One of my favorite quotes:"Sometimes everything can't be explained for one reason or another. In life you have to kind of look at all sides of things to understand people. That's the difference in somebody being smart and being wise." Iris Sipolski Mondy
summary: Can Inspire You To Live An Enriching Life

I received this product today. It's a replacement for the Marware Vibe Standing Case that I returned, which in my opinion was cheap junk. The OtterBox seems to be well made and offers substantial protection. I found the included instructions very easy to follow and had no problems inserting the Kindle into the case and reassembling the case; it took less than five minutes from the time I took it out of the box until everything was assembled. The protective screen seems to be extremely thin but perhaps this was necessary in order to retain the touch features of the Kindle. I have a Zagg Invisible Shield on the Kindle so I'm not particularly worried about it. I haven't noticed any excessive glare, and in fact the glare seems to be reduced, which could be because of working in combination with the Zagg Invisible Shield. Glare is not a problem anyway if one doesn't have the Kindle too close to a lighting source or laying flat on a surface. The OtterBox protective screen seems to enhance the clarity of whatever I am viewing, but that could be wishful thinking on my part or it could be because of the Zagg protective screen I have on the Kindle. I like the exposed on/off and volume buttons and the ability to protect the charging/HDMI ports from dust and moisture. The only negative is the price, which I feel is too much. Nevertheless, if one wants the product one must be willing to pay the price.Edit: I've noticed that where the OtterBox protective screen touches the Kindle screen the areas are darker, creating many dark, splotchy areas, which makes it very distracting when reading books or viewing videos. There is no moisture present and both the Kindle and OtterBox are perfectly dry.I spoke with someone at OtterBox today. She informed me that the splotchy areas of the Kindle screen are due to static electricity and that the problem is not uncommon. The "fix" is to disassemble the OtterBox and rub a fabric softener sheet over the screen on the Kindle and also on the OtterBox screen. The "fix", as applied, lasted for about thirty minutes until the static electricity built up again. Sorry, but I'm returning the OtterBox to Amazon. The splotchy, dark areas of the screen are too distracting to me and OtterBox's "fix" is not a fix at all.
summary: OtterBox Defender Series Protective Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black

reviewText: My best friend bought me a Kindle Fire for Christmas this year, and I needed a cover/case to go with it. I'm still looking for the perfect screen protector, but for now, the case is enough. She almost didn't buy it based on the reviews that talked about the smell of the product, since I'm on oxygen therapy and am very sensitive to smells. She chose to get it anyway, knowing she could send it back for me if the smell was too much to take. Well, I'm going to be honest, the smell was pretty strong and it definitely was odd. However, my son was the one who noticed that it really wasn't the case that smelled--it was the eco-friendly packing the case came in, a little brown recycled paper sack and with some brown papers wrapping it. But the papers themselves only had a trace of the odor - the cardboard wrapped around the case is what stank. So we took the case, sprayed some Febreze on it, and let it sit in the sunlight outside on the picnic table in the backyard for a little while with the fresh air and brought it back in and it was much, much better. I figured I'd give it a week before deciding. By the end of the week, the smell was nearly gone unless I put my nose right up next to it. We repeated the Febreze and leaving it outside again in the second week,and the smell is completely gone now.The packaging we finally threw away, even though I usually save electronics packaging in case something goes wrong and I need to send it back, but I figured by this point I'd be keeping the case, and the packaging smelled, so we tossed it.So now that the smell is gone, let's look at the feature - it's soft, plus interior and harder slick exterior. Not leather-like, but more plastic-like, but soft, just firm enough to provide some protection. There is a hand strap through the back of the case when it's zipped in the 'open' position, which makes reading at night in bed on the Kindle Fire really nice. You don't have to 'hold' it, but rather, just slide your hand through the strap and relax. The downside is, the strap's elastic stretches over time, and it loses its elasticity (it actually sort of 'tears' the elastic so it's not tight any more). It still works great for holding it at night, but it doesn't fit as tightly on the hand any more. The Kindle Fire fits in tightly. I had it fall out one time, and it was my fault for really knocking it around pretty rough while I was getting into my wheelchair. Other than that, it's stayed in really tightly and hasn't fallen out, but it's not so tight that it isn't easy to take out if you know how to do it. You just have to push it up and then out, instead of trying to 'pop' it out. There's a little trick to it, but it's easy once you figure it out.The two minor downsides that prevented a five-star review: 1) the zipper is made so you can zip it closed with the Kindle Fire inside, but they also will allow you to zip it 'open' with the case flipped over for reading and using. The problem is, the zipper tags for pulling it zipped and unzipped only go one direction, so when you're trying to zip it while it's 'open', you have to stick your fingers inside and feel around to grab the zipper tags to pull it. It would have been better if it had zipper tags on both sides of the zipper, for both open and closed zipping. 2) When it is zipped closed, there's a little pocket on the outside with a zipper to store things in, but the pocket is so 'tight' you can't fit anything in that pocket without risking damage to the Kindle Fire screen inside. For example, I once put a battery in it, a small double A batter, and it was such a tight fit, I worried the battery would crack the Kindle screen on the other side of the pocket. However, I do frequently slide my debit card inside the pocket and grab my Kindle to go somewhere and skip taking my wallet or purse, so it's good for that. But anything much thicker than a credit card or ID card and it's going to be a super-tight fit, so I'm not sure why there's a 'pocket' there at all.All said and done, I'm really happy with the case and glad I stuck with it when it smelled instead of returning it, but when/if this one ever wears out, I'll likely look for a different brand before deciding to purchase this one again. I'm not disappointed in it, but I do think they could have made it a bit better than it is.

I made it through two Zombie novels last year.  One of them was Belinda Frisch's CURE.  As soon as I opened it, the quality of the writing became apparent and the author's vision hooked me.  This was no half-baked, first time/first draft homage to the subgenre (not that I discourage such efforts--everyone has to begin somewhere and there is no indication that the Zombie revival is letting up yet), but CURE was exceptional.  It was clear right away that Belinda Frisch was a gifted novelist.  Her style was straightforward, unobtrusive; her handling of the multifaceted plot, sure; her characters distinct and believable; her way with mayhem shockingly effective.I finished the book eager to read more and was not disappointed when it came.  AFTERBIRTH, the sequel to CURE, is marvelous.Something happened between the writing of the two books.  I can't say what, exactly.  That would be for the author to discuss.  What I can say is this: as solid an offering as CURE was, AFTERBIRTH is even better.  And better on all counts.  Frisch's style is now so sharp and clean and precise that I stopped to re-read passages, in order to see how she had pulled them off.  She gives you just what you need to follow the tale and stay locked in the moment.  Every detail matters.  There are no distractions, no calling of attention to herself.  The focus throughout is remarkable.  Though the scenes are arresting visually, they aren't presented in widescreen cinematic fashion, but evoke an immediate, claustrophobic, handheld camera feel.  You are a participant-observer.  You are there, in the thick of it, as things are going down.  There is plenty of action and gore, as there was in the first novel, yet there are also situations that are emotionally stunning, in some cases heart-wrenching.  There are surprises and cliff-hanging incidents.  There is drama and suspense.  There are personal transformations among the protagonists.  What more could you ask for?I'd like to add that I love the artwork by Sarah Hansen (which would be equally suited to a graphic novel version) and thought A.J. Brown did a terrific job editing.From cover to cover, this book rocks.  I recommend both to those who are curious.  If you read and enjoy the first, you'll definitely want the second.Once again, I finish a novel by Belinda Frisch with anticipation for the next.

Downright scary. That's the only way I can describe this novella.Julia and her mute daughter, Amy, head to an old Inn thinking a weekend away will be good for them. From almost the moment they arrive, odd things start happening. Secret hiding spaces, mystery friends, drafts, voices...this is a quintessential haunted-house story.The story itself involves some seriously dark topics - from bullying to abandonment, child trauma to child prostitution - though most everything is only touched upon, not written in any sort of detail. Amy, the daughter of the main character, is a sweet but sad little girl who needs more than a weekend away. The way Jan Coffey writes her thoughts and actions makes you feel for the child, and I worried about her from the first time her thoughts danced across the page.I wasn't the biggest fan of Garrett, Julia's perhaps-boyfriend. His indecision was a bit irritating and his actions and words didn't always match up, but the romance between him and Julia was a tad sweet so I'll give him a pass.Overall I rate this one at three stars. Scary scenes, violent ghosts and a decently built history behind the haunting make this a perfect fall read if you want to give yourself a decent spook.

I'm Brianna, I hate flying and I talk way to much when I'm nervous so I'll apologize in advance."Tomas is a straight laced business man, loves writing lists,  has given up his home in Australia  to enjoy the wonders of Italy, and help his widowed aunt with her marina business.Brianna Ballantyne is a Clinical Pschychiatrist specializing in sex and couples therapy, taking a vacation to write, and hopefully find her birth mother. Let’s start this review off with a warning:If you are one of those readers that can not get past grammatical deviations (I’ll explain this in a moment), then I will say you most likely will not enjoy this book.From the start of this book it seemed obvious to me that English is not the author’s first language.  To me this was not a distraction, considering I grew up in a community where most folks did not speak English, did not speak it very well if they did (yep, I am fluent in Spanglish), or spoke a very proper version because that’s what they were taught.  There are a lot of passages in this book where you can tell that translation of a word is literal and not what a native English speaker would have chosen (we all know how things can get “lost in translation” sometimes).  So, if you are one who likes everything to be as it should, then you will probably grit your teeth and have to force yourself to get through this book.That aside… I really liked this book.  We follow Elizabeth (Beth) as she comes into powers that she was unaware she possessed.  Along the way, we find out there are others with powers similar to hers.  All of them must join forces in order to save their town.  Aside from odd sentence structuring, I didn’t find any major flaws in this book.  The storyline stays true to itself, details are followed consistently, and the story moves at an enjoyable pace.  The main group of characters are all young adults (17+), so while some of the conversation or reactions may seem juvenile (let’s not forget that I’m old… so the reactions I have in my head aren’t the same as a 17 year old), they really are mature based on the 17 year olds I come into contact with daily. I thought that maybe I would not be able to connect with the characters because they were so young, but once I really got into the story I found myself connecting and by the end of the story I was really rooting for them… especially Beth and Leon (so I’m sappy).  The story is original; definitely not something that has been rehashed over and over recently.We aren’t left with a huge cliffhanger at the end.  The situation that the group sets out to fix is fixed in this book.  We are left wondering what is going to happen with the characters and what their next adventure might be.  There is an excerpt of Book two at the end of this one; and I can’t wait to read it.  This is a good foundation for what can easily turn out to be a great young adult series.
summary: Good foundation for what could be a great series

Awesome, awesome book! I actually couldn't put it down. Believe me, it's hard to read and work at the same time, but I managed. It did end on a dreaded cliff hanger though. It's been a while since I've been able to read a long book that has more story than sex without getting bored. Don't get me wrong. There was plenty of steamy sex...Evelyn (Scout) has led a HARD life. She has been homeless since birth when she was born in an alley addicted to heroin. When she was old enough to take care of herself she began to take care of her heroine addicted mother, Pearl, as well. She never learned to read or do anything that we take for granted like how to do anything but basic hygiene. Lydia introduced me to the darker side of life by giving me Scout's perspective on the world. Believe it or not in the 22 years she has been on the streets, she was still innocent. She gets a job at Patras Hotel as a maid and is determined she is going to get herself off of the streets and be able to take better care of herself and her mom. When she meets Lucian Patras while cleaning his suite one day, he makes her an offer she can't refuse. I know it sounds generic and cheesy, but I promise that the author was able to do this in a way where I wasn't rolling my eyes. It's been a while since I have found a strong female lead that had my emotions so wrapped up in what she was going through in the book. I couldn't help but feel compassion for her or fear with her or even excitement.This book was broken up into 4 parts. Two of the parts were from Scout's point of view, 1 part from Lucian's point of view, and one from Parker's ( Scout's best friend from the streets.) Lucian is a typical rich boy who doesn't realize the hardships that the other half lives. But the good thing about this book is that we get to see Lucian become aware of circumstances for certain people throughout the book. I enjoyed watching him grow as a person and his love for Scout is unbelievable. I know there are things we are going to find out in the next book about his past, but the author didn't do that annoying thing where she over hinted at it. That is always a plus on my end.

reviewText: Fantastic way to start a book! I mean having Keara's parents die is horrible, but in doing that it gives this book a great platform to take off from.After Keara's parents death, her weird aunt Aingeal moves in with her from Ireland and life as she knows it comes to a complete halt. And I mean complete and utter halt. Home school, in-her-room hermit with no outside contact for 2 months! That is until her gay best friend Jared (I love that he's gay) comes swoopin' in to bust her out of her rut by going to a concert that involves her favorite band EVER. While out that night Keara gets an uneasy feeling that someone is watching her....that's when she spots Channing. Blond hair, piercing eyes that make her melt on the inside, you know the whole teenage heart throb thing. She's not sure what it is about him that makes her senses go wild, but she likes it!After running into Channing again at Night Secrets, a new club in town, she knows she's got the hots for him.  She also notices that she's catching the eye of the mysterious club owner, Corbin. After coming to Keara's rescue she feels as though Corbin would do anything to make sure she's safe....that is until he's suddenly attacking her in the parking lot of his club. Or is he?Now with secrets revealing themselves at every turn Keara must trust those around her to keep her safe, but more importantly she must learn trust what is locked inside herself and believe she can tap into before it's too late.Ok....coming down from this read I was initially SUPER excited about it. I enjoyed the twist that was given on the paranormal side of things, but I wanted to book to be longer. The plot was good, laid out well, I just know it could have used a couple more chapters. Oh and assuming that this novel is YA simply because the main characters are in high school is an epic fail on my part, because man there was a scene, or two,  that had me blushing!One thing that I really liked was, if a decision was made that would contradict what a previous character stated, the author was able to pull the plot & side plots together to make it all run together extremely well. This is hard to do, and I've found myself lately asking authors, "Why are you letting that happen, it doesn't make sense!", needless to say the book doesn't give me answers & it's frustrating as hell!All in all, this was a really good read. I'm looking forward to where BK takes Keara on her journey, and hoping the next book is a tad bit longer.4/5

I received a free copy of this book in exchange for an honest review.The Benighted is a dark read filled with mystery, dread and suspense. It’s set in a mythical, epic-fantasy world with princesses, knights, and the ancient battle between good and evil. With a set of characters so real they feel like you could walk up and talk to them, and a plot that doesn’t shy away to explore some of the darker sides of humanity, this is an interesting, enjoyable read.Skylar, the princess of a fallen kingdom, daughter of a murdered king, is captured and imprisoned for helping the escape of Harlin Brien, the knight who was framed for the King’s murder. But Skylar is convinced of Harlin’s innocence, and she’s certain the king’s advisor, Cross Lutherus, is the real culprit behind the murders on the royal family.When I read “princesses” and “knights”, I can’t help but think of an unimaginative, innocent fairytale that will have a happy ending you can see miles away. Princesses tend to be personality-less cardboard figures. Skylar…not at all. She has personality, wit, backbone, courage. What she goes through isn’t for the faint of heart, and even though she wants to give up several times, part of her always manages to cling on. This is the kind of princess I can root for.The writing is haunting and descriptive, and the fantasy world A.M. Dunnewin conjures up, is definitely intriguing, but also dark and unsettling. An inspiring story for anyone who enjoys the darker side of fantasy.

[...]My review for The Culling by J.C. Andrijeski thanks to NetGalley.  Now this book is not an ARC it is a re-release and the next 2 books in the series are already out.This is about 19 year old Jet, a skag, a human living free on Earth.  Yes Earth was taken over by an invasion of creatures called Nirreth and they allow humans to live in their cities but they are slaves so to be free you are always on the lookout.  Being outside the cities of the Nirreth is dangerous, not just awaiting capture by the culler ships but the Earth is not the same and resources are hard to find and so many things are toxic.  Jet is out trying to barter supplies when the unthinkable happens, she is taken by the culler ship.  No one knows what happens when you are taken, just that no one ever returns.This story was pretty short and was a quick read.  I finished it in one sitting.  It was an interesting concept and let's face it a bad ass looking chick on the cover with a samurai sword looked pretty cool.  I had a flash of Walking Dead for a minute.  Then add in aliens and the makings for a good invasion/fight back story and I'm all for it.You dive right into the world and you see what it has become and honestly it’s a future that is pretty bleak but still you see it from Jet's perspective and despite everything she is free and that is all that matters.  She is a good mix of strong, stubborn, and witty but she also has her moments which may cause more trouble down the line.  She is forced to confront her ideas and really lack of knowledge of the Nirreth and their ways in this new life of hers.  Also it brings up some interesting ideas, if you could be drugged into being compliant/numb would that be better to blindly serve or would you rather be aware of the servitude that you found yourself in?This is a quick sci-fi/dystopian read to lose yourself in for a little while.  I give it a solid 4 swords.  As I mentioned this is a re-release and the next two books in the series, The Royals and The New Order are already on sale and I look forward to reading them and figuring out what happens to Jet next.  How she adapts to being a slave.

Holding Her in Madness: Leo’s StoryBy: Kimber S. Dawn5/5 starsThis book is the sequel to A Woman Gone Mad told from Leo’s side. In the first book, there were a couple of Leo’s POV, but we never heard his side of the story.His story begins pretty much when he first sees Lil when she is babysitting. We do get his background story of how and why he moved from California. The author did an excellent job of not telling the exact same story, but also did a great job, when the important conversations showed up, the wording was the exact same as the first book. Which was nice, as that isn’t always the case.What we didn’t see from the first book was a detailed account of what happened to Leo when Lil’s dad went to confront him, and how that event actually pushed Leo into leaving. We don’t see Leo’s struggle with what he does to get over his heartache. And now we do. And, wow, poor Leo. My heart goes out to him. You see his devastation, his broken heart and soul. And damn, the author makes you feel. Even knowing how the first story ended, I just couldn’t put the book down.As we know from the first book, Lil tried to move on and so did Leo. We know that Leo kept an eye on Lil a watched her without her knowledge, so we get to experience that first hand. We get to experience more heartache from his efforts to move on, and how that leaves him and his ex-wife. It wasn’t easy, it’ll wrench your gut, it’ll make you feel, for both sides.Finally, there is a nice long epilogue that takes you well past the ending in the first book. And for that I love the author even more. You get a big ole happy sigh at the end but first, you’re gonna go through hell to get there.If you read the first one, DON’T MISS THIS BOOK!!

Sometimes, books in the humor or satire genre can be a bit of a hit-and-miss with readers--especially if the writer is trying too hard to be funny and jokes fall flat. I am sometimes also wary of glittery descriptions because I prefer substance to hype.At the time of this posting, the product description for this book mentions that the book is "intimate, snarky, and completely relatable." As I read the book, I was glad to be reminded of these adjectives in the product description--I was NOT disappointed as a reader and didn't feel misled or that the description was unwarranted.Topics like marriage, sex and pregnancy can be tiresome to wade through (depending on a reader's individual tastes and preferences). What I liked the most was the fresh vibe of Ms. Osterkamp's writing style, combined with an original prose structure (each chapter is quite long and covers quite a bit of range in terms of time). The content was contemporary but relatable enough that the themes of the story won't become dated and irrelevant (yes, even with mentions of a certain celebrity in the last chapter!).These lines from the first chapter in particular stood out to me:"...and he didn’t start out determined to stay single, like I had.""Because what you didn’t hear about from friends, what they didn’t show you on TV was how sloppy starting a family was.""Sometimes I wondered if marriages should be private affairs, meant only for the bride and the groom to quietly express their love and commitment."These are certainly things that many people think about, which make the characters and story instantaneously believable.A memorable book if you're looking for a thoughtful, contemporary story about self-discovery, that isn't dragged down by unimaginative and rehashed genre tropes.

Jesse Shaw is a famous soccer player in the US, and he's looking for a fun vacation with his best friend Hunter. They fly to London where he can get away from the spotlight and from the bad memories Jesse's former girlfriend left him. The last thing he expected to do was fall for a girl. And one of Hunter's cousins at that! Isabelle Mills is the sweet and quiet twin. The boys don't notice her until Jesse comes to stay at her house. Their relationship blossoms until everything comes to a sudden halt with a horrible prank gone wrong. Jesse's career hangs in the balance, and Isabelle doesn't know if he can ever forgive her.I'm blown away again by another one of Kyra Lennon's books. The story is sweet and full of the wonder of a new relationship. But it's the characters that hooked me. Jesse Shaw is unlike most of the arrogant Alpha males you see in romance. He's compassionate and genuine. Kyra does a terrific job of writing from his point of view making him honest and caring, but still one of the guys. Isabelle is the shy girl, feeling like she's in the shadow of her out-going twin. She's thoughtful and loyal, a young woman you can respect and wish your own daughter to model.It's an emotional roller coaster from beginning to end. Kyra paints vivid feelings that readers can relate to oh-so well. This book doesn't just tug at your heartstrings, but wraps around your heart like your favorite sweater and claims it.

reviewerName: L. Burns "Girl with the German Shepherd Tattoo"
reviewText: Kelsie Cole is looking forward to a solitary week at her twin brother's vacation cabin.  She gets unexpected (and unwelcome) company when her brother's friend and business partner, John McBride, pulls into the driveway.  Kelsie and John have known each other since they were kids, and something about John sets Kelsie on edge and makes her feel defensive.  The two have formed a pattern over the years of trading snide remarks and Kelsie suspects that John doesn't approve of her tattoos and piercings.John is fascinated by Kelsie and intends to use this week alone together to convince her to give him a shot romantically.  While he does succeed in piquing her interest sexually, he longs to break through her defenses and to make her see that it's possible for them to have a lasting relationship.I'm always looking for romances with characters that don't fit the Barbie and Ken mold, and Kelsie is a departure from the typical heroine.  At nearly six feel tall with pink hair and body art she may give the impression of self-confidence, but niggling insecurities and old wounds leave her feeling vulnerable.  John has the handsome and polished exterior, but his childhood has left him with his own set of baggage.This is an Erotic Romance, and sex is the primary focus of the story but it doesn't come at the expense of the plot.  There's enough room for solid character development, plausible dialogue and a decent storyline.  The sex scenes are pretty straightforward and explicit and involve only the two main characters.  And a toy.  Or two.  A pleasantly steamy, sexy, novella-length read.
summary: Wish MY vacation had been this...interesting!

Alicia knows she must move on, so she decides to do something that is totally out of character for her. She calls Dex, the one man who has made her forget Hunter for even a little bit. She is done playing it safe.Dex, our hunky rock star, hasn't been able to get the red headed beauty out of his mind after all this time. She was the one thing to make all the pain go away and save him from himself and the guilt that is eating him.Alicia calls Dex and he is thrilled to hear from her. She agrees to go to his beach house. Alicia can't believe she is really doing it. She thinks back to his proposition those months ago. "One week. No rules, no limits, just us. I can save you from this unrequited love of yours. And you...you can save me from myself."Their time together is amazing. Talk about chemistry and sexual tension flying off the pages. You will be fanning yourself! When they do get together it is like nothing either has ever experienced.Dex opens up to Alicia and he feels like she is helping him heal from his past. I received a review copy from the author on release day. In exchange for this I am writing my honest review.First of all, I really liked the new concept of this book, of a race of "Borg-like" humans who go to different "tainted" planets and assimilate their cultures to become one with Purity. Every concept of emotion is gone, what is left is pure logic. Beings are cloned and reproduced in simulated wombs. As they grow they are fitted into suits that control their emotions and stints their body's growth development. Any sort of touching is prohibited.Enter K, a fourth-level Paladin who leads her own raiding group against the "tainted" races and gathers slaves for their planets of Purity. During a set-up she is captured by a crew of "tainted" who need a Paladin to access a Purity slave planet to perform a rescue. K's suit is removed, and while it is off she is bombarded with something she has not experienced in recent memory: emotions. Feeling hunger, guilt, sadness, lust, all of this is new to her. It is also interesting to see how she manages everything, like a newborn.I was a little worried in the beginning how sensitive the heroine's plight would be treated by the author ... especially since this is an erotic romance. Anderson is wonderful in that she does not throw in gratuitous scenes from random characters in the novel ... she sticks to K's journey, so we don't see some real "action" until after the first half of the book. She learns things step by step.As K learns about herself with the suit off, she also learns about her past. (I will give no spoilers here, because this is revealed after you read about two-thirds of the book.)I did have a few questions at the end of the book ... it felt like there were a couple of things not really resolved, but most likely they will be done in the sequel.Overall, a very satisfying read. If you like her Kindred series and want to try something a little different, give this book a shot.

So first off, I have to give Ms. Winters MAD PROPS for including the novella Dark Mercy in the beginning of this book!  Seriously, by her doing that shows how much she cares about her readers by not saying, “Oh you HAVE to buy this other book before you can start this one or else it won’t make sense.”  Once again, this gives me another reason why I enjoy her writing so much!I have read the other books in this series, but it was so long ago that I was worried I was going to be a bit lost. But Ms. Winters isn’t lying when she says that they can be read as standalones. The only thing that I could see coming from this is that you will want to go back and read the other books in the series because there is so many interesting characters, you just want to find out what their stories are.But back to this story, I’m not usually a fan of vampire books just because they are so overdone in my opinion. You can imagine my surprise that once I started this book, I couldn’t stop reading it because I was so engrossed in what was happening that I didn’t want it to end!  There was plenty of drama, action, suspense, and just the right amount of smut that takes place in the book.Angeline’s character was one that my heart went out to every time Hadrian was being a jerkface. I mean seriously man! Cut her some slack!! She was willing to do anything for him, even breaking one of the most important rules, yet he still acted like a jerk. Even come the end of the book, I still didn’t like him. But that ended up working out because even though I had such strong negative feelings towards him throughout the book, I really don’t think that the book would have been this great without him being that way.I really enjoyed this book and I am planning on going back and re-reading the other books in the series as soon as possible because I can’t wait to get wrapped up in the world Ms. Winters has created.  And I really can’t wait for the next book in the series to be released!Reviewed by Crystal Marie for Crystal's Many Reviewers*Copy provided for review*

Shield. Allie's War, Book Two. JC AndrijeskiReview from Jeannie Zelos Book reviews.Many years ago, spurred by the you too can be a writer ads I gave it a try. They lied, I can't write! Even I was bored by what I produced, rejection letters came as no surprise,  so I've long admired those who Can write. I accept my brain Can't :)Most writers pull a story we love to read out of their imagination,  sparked maybe by something they've heard or read. Then there's a special breed of writers, the fantasy ones, who can produce such a riveting and imaginative world that's nothing like the one we know. JC has done all that and more to produce a fascinating series that's  kept me, a non sci fi reader, gripped in it's clutchesI enjoyed book one, though struggled to get my head around some of the complexities, read the Allie's early years novella that's currently free on Amazon, and that helped me to get things a bit more into context. Even though I was struggling with the world setting, and the way people were more than they seemed I was still transfixed, hooked, unable to let go of the developing romance between Allie and Revik. I love them both and yet they seem to be so full of misunderstandings, the way Revik's world works is so different to Allie's. For example - thinking with human concepts she caused a huge problem inadvertently in book one, when she thought she was simply offering the human gesture of letting Kat see Revik after he'd been injured, thinking they were friends and he'd want to see her, and yet in Seer terms it was something totally different and she was offering something very sexual. I think the Seers don't make enough allowances for Allie when she is puzzled by what they mean, or even when in situations like that she could cause such misinterpretations of a friendly gesture. Revik seems to be grasping it but there's still a lot of what Allie calls Fortune Cookie speech :) but then – what would the book consist of without those little things that lead to massive consequences ??Once again I’m hooked, still struggling with the concept of Seers etc and their abilities, which seem to vary from person to person, and keep on growing. Then there's all the different groups, who is allied with who, and for how long and what are the consequences. Allie doesn’t know who to trust, her life has changed so much in such a short while, and as Bridge it seems a lot is placed on her shoulders. Then of course the way they share light?? the constructs that seem to offer a sort of protection, the place where a sort of astral part of them can go and look at others and talk to others, and the whole body splitting thing...its a lot for my feeble brain :) and I may well have got it all wrong... I found if I concentrated on Allie and Revik – and they're by far what keeps me reading, interesting though the others are, and just let all the other things wash over, accept them as is, rather than struggle with understanding, I’m actually absorbing and beginning to understand more than I thought.Just when I thought things were finally coming together for Allie and Revik – and how – wow, some sensual and steamy scenes there! - then things go wrong. Badly wrong, Allie is captured by Terian – well one of them I guess :) - accompanied by a Syrimne boy, Nenzi. He's more than a boy though, an old soul in young man's guise, and a psychopathic, dangerous person convinced Allie belongs to him, and he's  dangerously jealous of Revik.  There's more plots and plans, more journeys into the other plane ( the Beyond?), more misunderstandings, rescues, trusting of people who may have another motive, and learning more about those collars that some wear. In the human world all seers have to wear them, and be owned by someone. Horrible concept that of ownership – like slavery really, and makes out that other races are lesser. The collars were described before as organic and I was puzzled, I’ve finally worked out that means they're living in some way, they have some kind of creature in them that sinks ...claws maybe, talons, spikes ? Something like that into the receptor's neck and blocks their powers. Eurggh, horrible. As much as I am confused I’m also getting a feeling for this world and its people, and I found myself getting out ( well searching kindle files )  book one so I could check on certain things I didn't understand but which became clearer. I have to be really interested to do that, and not just carry on, and surprised myself by wanting to do it.If you're a fan of sci fi no doubt you'll be far better than me at understanding this world, but even with my shallow understanding I find the series gripping, and want to learn more. The romance, the strong connection between Allie and Revik is what holds it all together for me, and my desperation to know that they make it through together in the end :) OK I’m a romantic sap, so what.. Priced at 3.08 for 426 pages it's a bargain for those who want something they can really get their teeth ( and imagination) intoARC provided via NetgalleyStars:  Four and a half.

Out of the three books in Ashenden's Billionaire's Club Trilogy, I would say The Billionaire Biker is the strongest. However, it has a few flaws that still left me disappointed, much like the previous books.It's hard to tell a complete story in a novella, and I'm often harsh when rating them. But the truth is I was easily able to put Sean's book down, and that alone is never a good sign, especially when the book in question is only 100 pages.I was curious about Sean's story from the beginning of the trilogy. I am not upset that I read TBB, but it did not live up to my expectations either. It was simply “meh”, the hardest opinion to explain, but I will try.I had a problem with Sean's “dark past”. I didn't like that he threw it at Abby so late in the story. Ashenden did not give time for Sean, Abby, or the reader to come to terms with this (also, I never felt like Abby's secret was ever truly handled, though it was told in the second chapter, and it's a big one . . .). The scene in which Sean tells about his mother read more like a spoiled boy throwing a tantrum and yelling, not a strong man admitting his problems and opening up to the woman he loves.The story was quick and the sex was pretty hot. It was an easy read, but also one I will no doubt forget within a week.As I have said before, I loved Ashenden's Talking Dirty with the Player, and I keep hoping I will love another one of her novels just as much. That has not happened yet, I'm afraid. But I will still continue to try her books because her writing voice is clear and I have seen an improvement in her last few books.For a hot quickie with a bad boy ex-MC enforcer, The Billionaire Biker may just work for you! On a side not, this series can be read out of order with no problem.Between 3 and 3 1/2 STARS!~ * ~ * ~For my full review, including some of my favorite quotes from the book, please visit my blog, TBQ's Book Palace.TheBookQueen

reviewText: We are The Unofficial Addiction Book Fan Club, to know more about this book, go to the post in our website:[...]If you are interested, you can visit our website:[...]The Unofficial Addiction Book Fan Club's Review:Blurb:She was broken when I met her, shattered from the death of her sister and running from love. Not to sound like an egotistical douche or anything, but I fixed her. Put her back together, filled in the cracks, and made her whole. A true fairytale in her eyes.But now real life is getting in the way: school, jobs, and the unexpected opportunity to travel the world under a legendary photographer. This internship will open doors not even my father's influence could. It's something I've been waiting all my life for. But so is Quinn, and accepting this internship will mean leaving her.And breaking her all over again.Review:We are happy to be part of this tour. We read and reviewed Stripped, the first book in this series, and enjoyed Quinn's and Torrin's story. It was something different, romantic and beautiful. But after every happy ending, there's a future waiting for everyone. And also for these two love birds.Now, with Without You, Brooklyn Skye wrote about the future of Quinn and Torrin. It just feels more realistic. Now these two have real problems and new plans they didn't have in the first book and it's more approachable for readers, because it's something that could happen to anyone in a relationship. They both have plans and dreams for their future, but maybe they not share the same plans and dreams and that bring them apart.About the characters, we like Torrin's personality, so we truly enjoyed this book since it's from his POV. It was something refreshing and it was nice to read what and how he felt about Quinn. And mostly, it was nice to "be" inside a male's head and what he thought about the situation he's now with Quinn and about their relationship. Although we might have missed Quinn's POV, we had a great time with Torrin and we enjoyed the change. Sorry, Quinn.However I can't not mention that this story broke my heart. All the doubt, the situations, the dreams and the difficulties... it simply broke my heart. Despite this, I have to say, too, that this story won't be the same without this. But, not everything's bad, because I loved the ending and Torrin's decision and well... it was more than enough to make me sigh and smile. And you cannot deny that these two are meant to be together and that they share something beautiful. You just have to love them. And I can assure you that you would want to know more about them, too.I totally recommend this book, not only because Brooklyn Skye did a wonderful work with this story, once again, or because it is a sweet, emotional and real romance story, but because I couldn't help myself with this story. I loved it and I am waiting anxiously for the next book, for sure.Book Addicts, this story not only has two amazing characters, but a beautiful story that you would love and fall for it, without even meaning it. That's why we gave it four gorjuss dolls and totally recommend it to you.
summary: The Unofficial Addiction Book Fan Club Review: A Sweet, Real AND Romantic Story

*Written By Connie Nicols*Let me start by saying that I liked a lot about this book despite a less-than-stellar rating. The premise was interesting--the main character had a lot of disappointments all at once and decided to kill herself and donate her organs to do some good in the world. Sounds depressing, but it was actually written well and handled, believe it or not, light-heartedly. She gets pressured into an organ-buying scheme which gives her some cash and some time to fulfill her bucket list. Since she has lived a very sheltered and ordered life, most of the items on her list are easily accomplished but way outside her comfort zone.  We follow her antics as she attempts to try new things, usually with over-the-top difficulties arising from her inexperience and naiveté.  Her former coworker becomes a mentor of sorts who encourages her to grow and helps her to lighten up quite a bit.  The title is a clever play-on-words based on the well-known phrase of “Carpe Diem” or “Seize the Day.”  What took away so many stars in my review was the main character herself. Because she had been so sheltered growing up, she had turned into a very small-minded and judgmental adult.  Not her fault, perhaps, but most of her comments and criticisms about other people were just downright petty and mean. It was too bad, really, because otherwise the book was enjoyable. But I couldn't relate at all to the MC, actually disliking her on many occasions.Because this is Part 1, we are left hanging in mid-story, with no resolution to Emily’s major decision and the resulting problems.PLOT: 3.5 starsThe premise of this story was, oddly enough, death and suicide.  When Emily faces a number of problems in her life, she reacts (make that OVER-reacts) strongly by deciding that she’d do better to die and donate her organs, thus leaving a positive legacy to the world.  No one would expect this plot to be enjoyable, but it somehow works, drawing us in to her thought processes and forcing us to wonder how we would handle the same situation.WRITING: 4 starsFord’s writing is light enough that she takes what could be a depressing premise and turns it into something quite amusing and very readable.  Her jokes are frequent and fairly off-color which often made me cringe with their raunch, but many readers might find them funny.COVER: 3 starsAnother graphic cover, this one shows Emily in one of her out-of-her-comfort-zone activities once she has made her decision about donating her organs.  It’s well-done, suggesting a sense of speed as she rides a “hog” for the first time.CHARACTERS: 1.5 starsThe characters were the biggest disappointment with this story.  Emily is judgmental and provides such a sense of entitlement that I couldn’t warm up to her.  She even alienates her boyfriend and the one friend she’s developed over the years.  Her coworker, however,  is friendly and warm, despite Emily’s off-putting attitude.

Six Naughty Nights is book two in the Love in Reverse series. While I didn't read Seven Sexy Sins, I had absolutely no problem reading this book. If you have read Seven Sexy Sins, then you will be happy to know that Faith, Eve, Rusty, and Dan all make appearances in this book.Esther and Toby originally met three years ago, while they were each on vacation. They ended up spending fourteen days together, having sex whenever and wherever they could. When it was time to leave, Esther asked Toby if they could still see each other. Toby said no, since they lived on opposite sides of the country and he didn't think a long distance relationship would work. Honestly, at the time, Toby wasn't looking to be in a committed relationship. Toby walking away broke Esther's heart, but it also did something to Toby as well. Once he got on the airplane, he realized his mistake and tried in vain to contact Esther. Shortly after returning home, Esther starts receiving messages from Toby. But with her heart broken in pieces, she refuses to speak with him. She soon learns that she's pregnant and chooses to not tell Toby as her way of punishing him for breaking her heart.In an unbelievable chance encounter, just seconds before an earthquake, Toby and Esther come face to face. Toby immediately knows that Charlie is his son. After Toby saves both Esther and Charlie, Esther is quick to confirm that Charlie is indeed his son. Immediately, they each know that their attraction for one another is still there.Esther's house is destroyed during the earthquake and Toby suggests first that they come and stay with him and then that they go with him to the Northland, while he attends his best friend's wedding. While looking through Toby's apartment, Esther discovers a card game called Naughty Nights. It turns out the game belongs to Faith and she wants Toby to help her with her latest article by acting out some of the adventurous cards in the game. Toby and Esther both come to an agreement that while they are in the Northland they will act out some of the Naughty Nights scenarios. Each goes in telling the other that it will be only physical, without any emotions. But they each know in their hearts that it isn't true. They just aren't willing to tell the other. What transpires is HOT on a whole new level.This was one of those books where I liked and hated the main characters all at the same time. Toby is a great guy, he's just NOT the alpha guy that I usually go for in a book. He's insecure and allows his family and friends to put him down constantly. At times, he even belittles himself. He's a go with the flow kind of guy, who doesn't seem to lose his temper and he never stands up for himself.Esther, while I respect her for being a single mom without help from anyone, I hate that she put herself in that situation. Her mother died years ago and her father died while she was pregnant. While she was in the hospital giving birth to Charlie, she was mad at Toby because he wasn't there to support her. She made the decision not to tell Toby she was pregnant, thus causing herself to be alone. She likes to blame Toby for never being around. She has several moments of immaturity when it comes to Toby. One thing I REALLY liked about Esther is that she had the guts to stand up for Toby when it came to his friends and family belittling him.At times I felt that Toby was too aggressive sexually, but it turned out that was just the way Esther liked it. Even with the character flaws, I still really liked this book. You will immediately hope that these two can work out their problems. I found myself looking forward to the next book in the series.While this is a hot steamy erotic romance, I found that it still has nice life lessons. One of my favorite quotes from the book is:"The thing about forgiveness is that it's not about forgetting. It's not about pretending it didn't happen. It's about accepting that someone made a mistake. That they did something because they were hurt, or angry. And it's about acknowledging that although it's not okay, providing they show remorse it IS possible to move on. You have to accept the other person isn't perfect. Loving someone--REAL love, not hearts and flowers stuff--is about recognising their faults and saying it's okay, I'm going to love you in spite of them."Source: PublisherReviewed for Read Your Writes Book Reviews

Everyone! Go run and get this while it is free on Amazon. Hurry now, go go go!I decided to take a chance on this self-published book with no reviews for no other reason other than... well... it was free. I don't turn down free M/M unless it is really really bad. I expected mediocrity but, to my shock, this book was not bad at all. In fact, it was really really good.Chase and Jimmy have been a couple for 10 years, since their college days. They live together blissfully in the North East but when Jimmy's mom falls ill, the pair journeys to Jimmy's hometown in Alabama to care for her. Though they are a strong couple, Chase is unprepared for the emotional baggage that Jimmy left behind in his small town. While Chase has no problem being out and proud, Jimmy is quickly reverted back to his country boy roots, which involve hiding who he really is. Amidst family crises, Jimmy and Chase must rediscover their priorities and face these new challenges head on or risk losing everything they have built together.I was very impressed with this book. The chemistry between the two guys is great and I loved their interaction with each other. Jimmy and Chase were very believable characters. I even liked the secondary characters, especially Jimmy's mom. It was surprisingly well done.My only major issue with this book is the POV switching. The POV changes from paragraph to paragraph, sometimes even from sentence to sentence. I occasionally had trouble figuring out who was talking when, which took me out of the moment. I also think that in some of the sex scenes, something felt a little off or unnatural, especially in the last one.However, overall, this was a fabulous first book by this author. I'll be looking for more of his/her(??) books in the future!

The "book" is not an unpleasant read, and the information in it seems to be well researched and accurate, but it simply was too short when I had expected a full biography - I had finished it in less than an hour, when I had really settled down with it for a long, comfortable read in my armchair.At 3.53 $, I think it is a bit expensive for just one article; you can buy a whole magazine for less than that.But it is my own fault that I was disappointed - I simply didn't check the product details properly. Being new to the whole eBook and Kindle "scene", I have certainly learnt a lesson!And I still want to read a "proper" biography about Michelle Obama. There are several available for Kindle, but now I am a bit unsure as to which one to choose. Any ideas?

Having said that, we all have different tastes so I'm really glad I didn't let that first knee-jerk reaction affect my decision to read this one.I knew very little about boarding schools, much less boarding schools in the 1970s, going into this. I felt the author's story was incomplete though. I get this was about his experiences at school, but I felt like it was missing a lot of the memoir pieces I have come to expect. Perhaps because the author was only eight during this time, his story wasn't able to be fully developed, but it felt incomplete.Having said that, he does a really good job of telling the story he does let us in on, he kept the story moving. However, a few times I did feel the story went a little disjointed. I wasn't sure what he was talking about or where he was going. Again, this could be just him piecing together his memories from being an eight-year-old.Well done, would have been better with more information about the before/after/etc. More meat about him and his family perhaps? Something was missing, but there's a really good story here. I think a good editor could pull it out of him - content editing is what is needed, don't get me wrong, the grammar was excellent.Recommended for those who may have been in boarding schools, but always for us die hard memoir fans.

I felt like she just went along with whatever Trace wanted and was just afraid to stand up to him, even though he needed someone to.  I did like how she was able to deal with everything that was happening, but on the same token, she also didn’t.  I was waiting for a big explosion to happen with her because she kept things bottled up, but that never happened.There were some good twists that were brought into this story, but I also did see them coming.  But I did like that the author had thought to add them.  When it came to Trace’s big surprise for Olivia, I was still left wanting for more because she didn’t really learn that much from them.  I had thought that she would want to know more, but she didn’t.Overall, this was still a good read, and if there is another book in this series in the future, I will check it out.Reviewed by Crystal Marie for Crystal’s Many Reviewers*Copy provided for honest review*
