Phaedra Michaels’ life is never boring. As a practicing small town psychologist, she’s had her share of up’s and down’s. Working at the hospital’s psychiatric ward, she’s come across of slew of lost souls. Though she’s done her best to help them through their various ordeals, it disheartens her that she’s unable to help a good many. Until the moment she discovers a strange book lying on her doorstep. It’s then that everything changes.Determined to make sense of the book itself, Phaedra dives head-first into a world she knows nothing about. Granted, her doing so is more of a sense of curiosity rather than actual practice. She knows she shouldn’t delve in the occult, but the lure of it all draws her in like a moth to a flame. The more she casts spells, the more she yearns to explore the dark side of the supernatural world.For a time, everything is fine and dandy. In her mind, everything is going just the way she wants it too. Sometimes, though, things are too good to be true. Practicing magic always comes with a price, most especially when someone isn’t quite knowledgeable in what they’re doing. As a dark cloud settles upon the town, Phaedra soon realizes that she’s in way over her head. She’s inadvertently unleashed a force that’s to be reckoned with. If she’s to succeed in vanquishing it, she’ll need to place her trust in those she never thought of trusting before. Only then, can they lay to rest an evil determined in gaining the upper hand.The Accidental Witch looks like it’s to be set up as a series. The story’s premise is definitely unique, one I enjoyed very much. Granted, it’s not often that I read stories about demons and witches like this. Jessica has crafted a world full of darkness and decay. A world where magic isn’t always what we think it is. Sometimes, it can get the best of us, even with the best intentions at heart. I look forward to more of Phaedra and the rest of the guild in the future. Thanks for a great read!Please Note: I was given a complimentary copy of this book in exchange for an honest review.

reviewText: This novella is very short and appears to be the beginning of a longer piece of work currently being written. It read like an introduction to a story and a rather large cast of characters and didn't turn out to be very satisfying all on its own and it ended extremely abruptly.  The prose is often beautifully written and almost has a dream-like feel to it which I loved and I see a lot of promise here with a little tweaking and expansion, especially when it comes to the characters and their plight.  The bones of the story are solid but it jumps around too quickly to get to know any of the characters on more than a surface level and it left me confused far too often for my liking.  The chapters are super short and just when I was getting into a characters point of view the story shifted to one of the many other characters.  Basically, there was too much going on for me to keep up and it was difficult to root for anyone because I didn't get to spend enough time with them to feel much of anything at all. Terrible things happen but most of it occurs off-screen and the reader is left with only the surface aftermath.  I'm the type of reader who prefers to be in on the action, experiencing the emotions along with the characters, no matter how horrifying they may be.  I just felt left out here and longing for more.Basically the story is about the inhabitants of Scarlock who are firmly under the thumb of a greedy money lender named Copeland. Nereia became a thief when her parents died and Copeland took possession of everything they owned.  Her only other option was to become a prostitute.  Either way, nearly everything she owns is tithed to Copeland and he keeps increasing the tithe.  Nereia fears that now that her younger sister Mary is old enough, she will be forced into prostitution.  Nereia will do most anything to save her innocent sister and Copeland uses that fact against her and a gritty adventure ensues when Nereia rebels.  Many other characters are introduced, many are interesting enough but as I said the focus is just too scattered to become fully invested in any of them.  I found the story too cluttered to fall into and it was a bit of a struggle to finish.  In the end, it all feels like trying to recall a hazy dream.

The order of the sections is natural, breakfast, main, soups, side and desserts, and thus far very easy to navigate. I wanted to try as many recipes as I could over last weekend so I picked the ones that sounded most delicious and started cooking…My favorites of the breakfast section were Apple Cinnamon Dish and Dutch Slow Cooker Pancakes…I mean seriously, who wouldn’t want to have pancakes for the breakfast and these ones…oh, my, add some fresh, crushed strawberries and you’re in heaven. For the main sections I tried several, but my absolute favorites were Chicken and Cauliflower, Indian Curry Chicken and Mexican Black Beans and Coconut. Lots of chicken you may think, and I agree, but that’s because I don’t eat red meat so I’ll let my family to review the meat dishes. I didn’t have time to try the soups but there were quite many that looked really good…okay, and now comes the confession…I didn’t have time because I wanted to try all of the desserts! And, yes, they were so worth making! I loved them, all of them, and my kids loved them. So I guess from now on we’ll be enjoying Mr. Smith’s delicious goodies in all of our parties.My only complain is that this book is not (but hopefully will be in the future???) available on paperback as if it were, I would be the one rushing to the bookstore to get it! One for the boat, one for the summer cottage, one for each of my friends…

reviewText: The Winter Wife: A Christmas Novella offers a tale of love and second chances. Anna Campbell has long wanted to do a Christmas novella and I quite enjoyed her first one. It's the tale of an estranged couple either too proud or too stubborn to work things out and their chance encounter on a deserted Yorkshire road in the middle of a snowstorm. Maybe it was the magic of Christmas or fate that brought them together but the tale that unfolded was delightful.This was a quick, entertaining read that I consumed in a single evening. Alicia Sinclair, Countess of Kinvarra has been ruined for any other man by her husband. After a series of misunderstandings and foolish pride, they separated and have lived apart for the past ten years. Sebastian Sinclair, Earl of Kinvarra has been plagued by the memory of his estranged wife and the mistakes he has made. Circumstances force them to spend the evening at an overcrowded in and I adored every snarky, romantic, passionate moment of this tale. My only complaint is that I would have liked this to be a full length novel.If you are looking for a quick historical romance with a little Christmas magic then The Winter Wife is sure to delight. Campbell's novella gave us a strong sense of the characters and an understanding of their troubled past. Filled with passion and second chances this is sure to get you in the holiday mood. My hope is that the author will deliver a full length Christmas novel next year. *hint* originally posted on caffeinated book reviewer dot com

I received Claimed from the publisher via NetGalley in exchange for an honest review.  Original rating is 4.5/5 Bullets.Welcome to my book review of Claimed by Stacey Kennedy.  I want to start with a full admission that I typically do not read or review BDSM focused books.  However, I do love dabbling outside my normal comfort zones - I think it keeps everything I read fresh!  If you have thought about trying a BDSM book and have been uncomfortable diving into the deep end of this genre - I think Claimed would be a great book to try!Claimed is a lovely and emotional story of Presley - fresh out of a long term relationship gone south.  Presley chooses to try an exclusive club and test her waters as a submissive.  Pulled out of her comfort zone, you take her journey into self exploration with her.  Dmitri is a brilliant character.  Completely self aware of his own flaws and keenly intuitive to others as well.  As the Master at Club Sin he takes Presley as his sub in training.What they discover and open up within each other is an emotional and beautiful story.  The added heat with scenes of BDSM play (in a safe and secure setting) completely add to the overall sexiness of this book.  Kennedy did a great job making you feel like you were stepping into the Dungeon with Presley and Dmitri.  I thuroughly enjoyed this story and all the characters.  I can't wait for more!

reviewText: Who doesn't happen to love popsicles in today's world of many numerous and countless variations of delicious indulgent different kinds of snacks? Personally, I feel like snacks are an essential part of any human being's normal diet. Sure, the main meals like breakfast lunch and dinner are the most important things that provide us with the most proper nutrition as well as the most energy and enjoyment when they are sometimes spent happily with family or friends or some other people that a certain individual likes to spend time with. However, a snack is what will also help keep you going throughout the duration of the day, in between those sometimes potentially very lengthy breaks of time that occur between mealtimes that are officially considered the most important and beneficial to our bodies. But snacks, especially if they are healthy and appropriate, can really help your body keep on going through the hardships of any kind of day- weather it may be actually good or bad. For instance, sometimes your energy levels might begin to drop after an especially exhausting travel from work to pick something up on the far side of town. That long and tiring walk will exhaust your body and use up a lot of fuel. A reasonable kind of snack will easily recharge and refuel you and your body up for any kind of possible work that you might yet have to complete before the next meal will be able to replenish and reefed your body fully. A snack can really power you up and ensure that your metabolism is kept running throughout the day so that not only will you actually have a lot of energy, but you will also have a good calorie burning ability and so food that you consume will get digested more easily and quickly, enabling a good and healthy weight maintenance plan- or potentially even an appropriate weight loss plan.However, while snacks can be truly beneficial, just like most things are in life in moderation, some people are afraid of including snacks within their day because they cannot correctly use the eating opportunity in a healthy and harmful way. Some people might binge on unhealthy snack foods for snacks- and this is why snacks have been acquiring a bad name- because of those fattening snack foods that we tend to splurge on because they're so convenient and seemingly appetizing at a quick moment of hunger. But there are alternate good options for snacks that are both healthy and easy to get anywhere you happen to go. The instant and efficient snacks mentioned in Popsicles: Healthy Snacks in an Instant are the best possible suggestions that someone might have when they are planning a healthy and nutritious diet for his or her day.

For how long?  Nobody knows.  He just has to have her.This story is all about Zandor in HOT pursuit of Bekah.  He will do anything, follow her everywhere, and he is doggedly relentless in his pursuit.  For a man who is into BDSM, love 'em and leave 'em, and never had a relationship at the age of 24 years of age, Zandor is ready to chuck it all in his pursuit of Bekah.  What he does not count on is in finding in Bekah the only woman that could ever please him.  She is his perfect match... and this creates anxiety.I loved this book. reviewText: I absolutely loved Willow (the first book in the Blood Vine series). The way Willow adapted to her pack, the way the boys reacted to her, the dynamic of the pack was awesome (and yes I'm becoming über aware as to how often I use that world lately). That however was nothing compared to Fern.Richie once again drags the reader into Willow's world and submerges you into the pack. What happens to the pact happens to you, which is why on more than one occasion I was in tears or laughing out loud. This pack was MY pack. And I wasn't happy to say goodbye to it at the end of the book.Still reeling from the discovery that Gage is in fact Mikhaul, the man she was raised to fear, Willow sets off to rescue him from the vampires she was raised to hate and face the woman who raised her. Willow grows so much in this book, she finally realises what it means to lead a pack and she has herself a Eureka! moment when it all falls into place. At this point I actually fisted the air and cheered... I kid you not, I'm just glad I was home alone at that point.This book was filled with story, there was no slow parts, no quiet parts. From start to finish this book was impossible to put down and I devoured it in two sittings. If you only ever read one Werewolf series make it this one. You wont be disappointed.

Roux's review:  “My Only Sunshine” is a story about two strangers who meet at a time when neither is in a position to begin a relationship. The tragedy is that the circumstances in each of their lives that made for poor timing were the same reasons that had both men desperately needing someone at their side. Mason, a rancher’s son returned to help out his family during a crisis, and Tanner, a young homeless man in need of a place to heal emotionally and physically, were both alone in dealing with extremely painful matters. Each is lonely and misunderstood. Really, really, alone which makes the burdens each is shouldering all the more heavier. Author Rowan McAllister does a splendid job of letting the readers understand the depth of the main characters’ emotional turmoil. You feel their pain, anxiety, sense of hopelessness and their intense need to find hope again. The characters were not written to portray perfect people. They came across as three-dimensional figures with flaws, needs and desires that made them vulnerable to balance their strengths that made them admirable. Mason came out of the closet years before and paid a steep price for standing by his convictions and being true to himself. He was forced to leave his family’s ranch, the place where he was happiest. He had to create a new life, one in which he was never truly happy but did not force him to live a lie. He dropped everything to return to the ranch to take over after his father suffered a stroke; back to small town prejudices, his sick father’s disgust and his tired, overwhelmed sister’s disinterest. He never gave up wanting his father’s approval and acceptance and struggled daily with the fruitless effort to obtain it. Tanner’s current reality was equally dismal. He was clearly at the lowest point of his life and fear of rejection kept him from attempting to seek safety and acceptance with his own family. Tanner and Mason felt real and so did their struggles. Neither was especially smart or successful but together they found the strength to protect and support each other —even through the strain of hiding their new relationship from everyone they cared about. Mason could not risk complicating his father’s slow recovery and Tanner had no choice but to honor Mason’s wishes. The stress of living a new lie was made easier by the loving support each offered the other.I enjoyed the portrayal of the simple, lonely and hard daily grind of living on a ranch in the American west. I like both Mason and Tanner and supporting characters Ed, Lucy and Brian. It pulled at my heartstrings to watch Mason continually swallow his feelings and pain to avoid making waves and I shared his frustration at the blind and selfish attitude of his sister. I wanted the couple to find peace and happiness together but the ending felt a bit too perfect. And I could have done without the subplot of a “who done it” mystery concerning violent animal torture. This storyline included scenes that are extremely brutal and horrifying to envision. These passages certainly brought forth great emotional responses-both by characters in the book and me as a reader. They were a significant but not an overwhelming part of the book. All in all, I believe that “My Only Sunshine” is a very good story filled with characters you will root for and a story line that will sustain your interest beginning to end. It is a good read!

reviewText: This has proven to be one of my favorites of all the Silo stories to date, because of the amount of exploration Ann Christy does into the daily life of the silo residents, as well as the work of the Fabbers and the Historians, two groups we haven't heard anything about in the past.  Other reviewers have mentioned that the story "bogged down" a bit for them, but I allowed myself to become engrossed in what was happening and let it unfold at its own speed, rather than trying to zip through to the finish line.  Christy's characters are all interesting and three-dimensional, and what's more, she obviously cares about her protagonist, which makes for a very interesting read.  If you're willing to give yourself a bit of extra time to make your way through the story (and allow yourself to live in the silo alongside Marina and her family), I think you'll find it as enjoyable as I did.  Now, I'm wondering what will happen next!

She must protect Xarion at all cost, even if she has to die doing it. Because if she fails, all is lost.Star's duty has always been to protect Xarion, who is Cleopatra's son. Being a Shythe Kythan, she can wield the power of Charge, or electricity. But, this also means she will always serve the Pharaohs because of a curse. She takes her duty very seriously, but it's hard to stay focused when you have feeling for the future ruler of Alexandria. Who also happens to be human. And it's forbidden for Kythan's to be with humans. Star has to put this all aside because there is a new threat to the throne. A new race of Kythan, that are far stronger that the Shythe's and Narcos, rise. Star thought that being in love with the heir to the throne was dangerous, but it's nothing compared to what's coming after them.There will be hope, there will be death and there will be the deepest of betrayals in this kick-butt novel by Trisha Wolfe.Oh how I love a good strong Heroine. And that's exactly what Star was. Throughout the book, duty always came first......well almost always *wink wink* I loved Destiny's Fire last year, and I loved getting more background on the Narcos, which wield fire and the Shythe's, which wield electricity. It's like all this is leading up to that book and...well.. it is..so I don't know why I said that. LOL. Anyway.. for all you romance lovers out there, this is a tragic one. A human and a Kythan are forbidden to mate with each other. What's even more tragic is that everyone wants to kill Xarion. Star is torn between love and duty. My thoughts are all over the place right now, and I don't even know what else to say. I loved this book and I need MORE.Star- She is fiercely loyal. She knows what needs to be done and the risk that she needs to take. She isn't afraid to take a hit and to shed some blood. I would not want to be on her bad side.Xarion- There was some times where he annoyed me, but all those thoughts vanished after the bathroom scene. ;) There is a sneak peek down below of that. :DPheonix- hahahaha. he is hilarious. He is the man whore in the book, and I love him. He might seem all bad, but he's really not.Favorite Quote:They are sisters to me, both Egyptian war goddesses, and I am a descendant- my name chosen for me by the gods.I am Astarte.I am wrath.

This book was not as good as the first, as usual.  I found the first book (The Mating)to be somewhat suspenseful, but this book was mostly repetitive.  When I say "repetitive" I don't mean repeating what the first book was all about (which is also annoying), but rather repetitive about what the characters were constantly thinking.  The following will not spoil anything and does not give anything away if you choose to read it- the base of this information is supplied to the reader in the first or second chapter... There is a reporter wanting to interview Ryne...well several times in the book Ryne talks to himself about having a thing for the reporter, but she could be his enemy, blah, blah, blah.  I bet that particular thought or something similar is repeated about four times throughout the book and it's like - we know what the reporter is up to already!-you don't have to keep telling us!.  We know he's attracted to her, we know he shouldn't be attracted to her-get on with the story already!  Te same type of thoughts occur for the reporter...she was attracted to Ryne, but thought he was a jerk - that was also a repetitive conversation to herself throughout the book...again...WE KNOW.  This book didn't get really good until 64% of the way through...when I got to that point I zipped through it in about a day, but it took me three weeks to get there because I just wasn't that interested.  I read "The Mating" (prequel to this book) in 3 days and highly recommend it, but I would suggest you stop there and don't waste your time with "The Keeping".  BUT...because the ending was fairly good, I might continue on and read "The Finding", just not right now.  I'm moving on to a different series for the time being and may or may not come back to this series.

reviewText: "There is something about the tragic stories of Shakespeare. It’s as if we all know how it will end, but the adventure makes it worth it. "This is how I feel about these forbidden romances. You know it is a train wreck… a heart-break waiting to happen and yet you have to experience it. And, what an experience Loving Mr. Daniels is! I have a new author crush on Ms. Cherry! She seriously blew me away. This is her DEBUT novel… WHAT?!??! Still can’t believe that! This is in my top three reads this year and absolutely somewhere in my top ten ever!Let me start with our MCs., Ashlyn and Daniel. Oh how I loved them both. These two have each been through extreme heartbreak and find everything missing in their lives in the wrong place, each other."I hated that I couldn’t tell her how beautiful she looked each and every day. I hated that, when she walked into my classroom, I had to pretend that she wasn’t on my mind…. I hated how close we were but how distant we felt."This starts off like most student/teacher romances. Girl and guy meet… there is an intense connection… walk into the first day of class and tadah!!!! That’s about where the similarities end though.What makes Loving Mr. Daniels more special than all of the others out there? The writing for one. It is so fluid… so poetic. The FEELS! From the first chapter I was on an emotional roller-coaster. From grieving to giddy, swooning to heart-broken, from extreme hilarity one moment to raging mad the next… this book takes you on a journey. More than one actually. This isn’t just Daniel and Ashlyn’s story. So many relationships are formed, tested, lost… It is a rare thing to feel as connected to supporting characters as the MCs but Brittainy does it and does it beautifully. Gabrielle and Ryan… WOW! I won’t even go into who these characters are bc I won’t spoil anything but they touched me to my soul."Being a teenager is a curse and a gift. It's the age where fairytales cease to exist and Santa isn't real but parts of our hearts want to say 'What if... "With all of the tragedy… and there is a lot in Loving Mr. Daniels. There is also love and trust. Above all there is hope. Where would any of us be without that? This is a book I feel that just about everyone can relate to and will be touched by. I cannot say enough good things. If you haven’t read it yet, seriously move it to the top of your TBR. You will not be sorry!

reviewText: Less the haunted house story I expected, and more a psychological study of loss and tragedy, Broken Sigil is a well-crafted thriller that manages to evoke an immediate and intense emotional reaction in the reader. William Meikle starts us off with what seems like a typical crime novella, complete with the stock jaded/damaged detective, a lonely, angry man who is an outsider even within the department.Things start to get interesting when Joe arrives at a crime scene to find his ex-partner dead, shot by another cop. The story doesn't really begin to get under your skin, however, until the coroner points out the five-pointed star carved into the flesh of the dead man's stomach - a scar that dates back to the tragic accident that left both men broken and alone.Once Joe returns to the scene of the crime, and starts talking with the odd inhabitants of the brownstone apartment, the story really begins to flow. It is a place of memories, a home to grief and longing, where whispers of the dead can be summoned almost close enough to touch. Of course, neither life nor death is ever that simple, and no detective could ever be content to simply accept the 'rules' as they're explained to him - and that's where the already dark tale of a Broken Sigil descends even deeper.
summary: A well-crafted thriller that manages to evoke an immediate and intense emotional reaction

Having been a court reporter for many years specializing in divorces, this story rings true to me.  It's appalling how many men go through similar situations when they marry and have children who, in turn, are used as pawns in the divorce.  As the author stated, it's one of the worst forms of child abuse because you are not only ruining your ex's life but, more importantly, destroying the parental relationship to which your children are entitled.  I've seen it happen with two of my close friends.  One became extremely wealthy and left his entire estate to worthy charities that he supported instead of to his children he had not seen for years.  But it's not about money, it's about the estrangement of a parent and child which is so emotionally damaging to the children.  This is something they will carry with them until death.  This book is written in memoir form and once I began reading, I was compelled to continue until the end.  By the way, I am a divorced woman and one intelligent enough to understand the wife is usually as much to blame for a marriage gone wrong as a man.

Talk about a surprising and enjoyable read. While admittedly I had a bit of trouble wrapping my whiskers around a lot of the computer hacking aspect of the book, I found the entire plot to be engaging. It definitely kept me reading long past the point where I should have stopped for the day. There’s a little bit of something for every reader in this one. =^.^=What stood out the most for me with this book was the dynamic characters. Alice was a great individual who not only grows considerably throughout the story, but also proves that women are just as capable as men when it comes to computer technology. It both annoyed and amused me that folks underestimated her capabilities throughout the book. It just goes to show that one should never judge another based on their gender (the same can be said of felines). Garrett was funny and your typical geek. I felt rather sorry for him when I found out what had happened not only to his company but also to his parents thanks to his brother, Gabriel. It was great to see him find hope again. And may I say that I simply LOVED Eric? Honestly, I don’t often glom onto antagonists much, but in Eric’s case he is a fantastic bad guy! He’s so sleazy, ruthless, and just plain mean…he’s perfect. Watching him lose his cool thanks to Alice was just priceless. I really hope that McCaghren brings all three of these guys back for a second book!Plot wise, like I said I had a hard time getting into all of the computer stuff, but that still didn’t stop me from enjoying the book. Every idea flowed smoothly, to the point where I literally made the comment to my fellow feline reviewer, “This could happen.” Yes, I firmly believe that one day we will be able to process tons of data using nothing more than our minds and as a result, computers will become obsolete. It most likely won’t happen in my time, but you never know. The minor down side that I had with this story was that it did sometimes feel like it dragged in spots, especially when Alice gets caught a second time. But there was still plenty of action and intrigue to keep me interested, so it wasn’t too bad a lag in action.On the whole I think this is definitely a book worth checking out. At present it is a stand alone novel, but as I mentioned earlier, I do hope McCaghren decides to do more in the future, murr!

In this short, suspenseful thriller, Doris Langford and husband, Gerald, have finished their grocery shopping.  Gerald doesn't like to shop, and is always in a hurry to get back to the car.  Enroute, a man, dressed in dirty clothes, approaches them asking for help.  He needs a few dollars as his car has run out of gas and he needs to get home to take care of his sick wife.  Gerald says, "Sorry."  He's not one to succumb to those who constantly look for handouts rather than look for work.  Doris would like to help these people in need, but their budget is too tight and at times they run out of money before the end of the month. Gerald then pulls into a gas station and he is approached again by an angry man wanting money. Gerald immediately stops pumping gas, jumps in the car, closes the windows and locks the doors.  While stopping at an intersection at a red light, Doris sees a young boy with a beggar holding a sign "will work for food."  Doris and Gerald need the lawns mowed and she'll feed them a hearty meal. Doris is so warm-hearted and happy that Gerald consents to this arrangement. She plans to make a wonderful meal of meatloaf and potatoes, and the beggar can take all the fixings home with him to share with wife and son.  When the task is done, Doris and Gerald load up their car with the food and drive the man and son home.  Well, I'll stop right here ... I'll tell no secrets! You'll have to read the rest of the story at night, with the lights off, to get the full impact of this thriller!  Regina Puckett is the best macabre author!  If you've read Edgar Allan Poe, you'll like her thrillers also!

reviewText: Green men with tentacle feet have invaded the Earth, and they're out to eat all the fat people (turns out they're delicious). Zack and Zoey, two elementary school children, are trapped in a world gone topsy-turvy. Suddenly lunch is a daunting prospect and any bad conduct is rewarded with cake and pudding cups. Is it up to these kids to repel the invaders while trying to avoid being fattened up like a holiday turkey?Zack, Zoey, and their remaining classmates have to use their wits to outsmart the aliens. There's action, a bit of detective work, and ~romance~. Or, there's romance on Zoey's side, and Zack wants nothing to do with it. The characters are introduced in rapid succession, so it took me a moment to get the names down, but they all have distinct characteristics that make it easier. The premise is wacky and silly, and within three pages I was laughing. This book also includes a good amount of color illustrations, usually 2-3 per chapter. These large pictures (they usually take up nearly the entire screen) add color and whimsy.Zack & Zoey's Alien Apocalypse is a short story, but I still enjoyed it quite a bit. This is definitely a book I would have enjoyed as a child, and it's very cute and silly, and sometimes quite witty as well. Zack and Zoey are interesting heroes who still act like the kids they are, and the plot was original. This looks to be the start of another great series of books for kids.

reviewText: The Psalmist by Jason Akley is a work of “fiction and not a history lesson” that details the life of a man whose music inspired the author to take the spur of a moment decision to write about him the first time he heard him sing on the radio. Akley was driving and lost in the melody of the song when he comes to a rail crossing. The deafening noise of the passing train couldn’t fade away the voice of the singer as Akley was lost in his own world. He admits, “I suppose that’s when I became a fan. And why I decided to write this book about him.”The Psalmist is not your average book. It is a lengthy and detailed story of David Threnody (1918 – 1988), a blues musician. Some important milestones in David’s life:1918: David Threnody born in East St. Louis1927: The Mississippi floods; David receives his first guitar1933: Gerald, David’s eldest brother, flees to France1938: David plays guitar for money the first time at a Soulard Mardi Gras1941: David joins the Army1945: David records his first album in New Orleans; meets Bethany; they begin an affair1946: David marries Bethany1948: David and Bethany divorce1951: David records his second album in Austin, Texas1955: David records his third album1960: David records his fourth album1965: David begins an affair with Maddie1966: Benjy attempts to kill Maddie, Maddie dies saving David1967: David returns to the crossroads in Mississippi; records his fifth album1988: David Threnody diesThe Psalmist will delight fans who have known David Threnody during his lifetime or have heard/listen to his music. The book as a whole is readable and enjoyable.

Like any ongoing series, if you haven't read the other novellas, you should do so before reading this review as there may be spoilers.These stories about the Fae are now on my list of favorites that I anxiously wait for and drop everything else when one is released.  Archer and Ravynheart have created a very enchanting tale with a unique method by which to deliver it.  The writing is great, the plot is interesting, the characters are multi-dimensional and the delivery is superb.The series is set up like a TV series with weekly episodes about the Fae.  Each story continues where the last left off.The main storylines of the series are Lugh's struggles as Champion of the Fae after the collapse of the Mounds, how Donovan, leader of the Unseelie Fae is rebuilding life on the earth realm after the collapse, and London's struggles to cope as a human cursed with the Sidhe Touch.The latest `episode' is Defender of Magic and picks up where Lugh's story left off in Champion of the Fey.________________________________________Previously, we have witnessed the collapse of the Mounds, the home of the Fae and the source of their magic.  Our Champion of the Fae, Lugh, has discovered that magic artifacts exist from when the All-Mother Danu originally created the Mounds.  Lugh decided to focus his efforts on finding these artifacts to create a new realm that will restore magic to the Fae and provide a new home for any who survived the collapse.In this episode, Lugh has now recovered several artifacts and is seeking a safe haven for them.  As well as for all the documents he was able to save from the sacred temples spread around Ireland.  He turns to a trusted friend, Rehnquist the Dragon Champion, for help only to find out that Rehnquist is dead and there's a new Champion, Jonathan Wyndracer.Danger is all around Lugh and his magic is beginning to fade.  With no source of replenishment, he cannot waste a bit of magic he has left.  This leaves him exposed to risks he never had before.  He has to rely on his wit and old fashioned fighting skills to survive.Physically, Lugh is starting to feel weaker, however more importantly, he is starting to despair over not finding any surviving Fae.  Besides the nasty goblins that is, who seem able to survive anything.  Lugh is also discovering secrets that were kept by the All-Mother.  Dangerous secrets that are making him question everything he believed in and may have something to do with the murder of the All-Mother and destruction of the Mounds.This episode showed a deeper side of Lugh as we see behind his brave faade and confidence.  We see a vulnerable side to him and his worries, not just for himself but for all the Fae.________________________________________Bottom LineThe Sidhe World is a great new series about the Fae and we're starting to see more dimensions to the characters and the storylines.  Archer & Ravynheart have delivered another great chapter and I hope you enjoy reading them as much as I do!Happy Reading!5 Stars - Absolutely Loved It!!!!
summary: If you're interested in the Fae or The Sidhe, then this is for you

reviewText: What She Doesn't Know is a romantic suspense novel, that takes place primarily on an isolated island of the Bay of Fundy. Gardiner known for her paranormal romances delivers a suspenseful tale, filled with a secret society and a group of greedy thugs who want to uncover treasure. I quickly became engrossed in the tale and its characters.The protagonist Raven Gale is determined to put the past behind her, but when it appears that someone is using her dead husband's identity she investigates.  A little over a year ago, her deceased husband tried to kill her, and a part of her is somehow afraid he is still alive. She learns the person using his identity is on an island in the Bay of Fundy. She hires a guide to take her there.  What she finds is a man who looks very similar to her husband, but before she can get some answers, she finds herself tied up, chased and running for her life. In order to survive, she will need to put her faith in Sloan (the man impersonating her dead husband). Raven soon learns that her parent's death and everything she thought she knew about them is wrong. A group of men are after a treasure they believe her parents safeguarded and think Raven may have the answers. It's a race against the clock as Raven and Sloan attempt to solve the mystery and stay alive.Gardiner's tale was action packed with likable characters. Raven and Sloan were the main characters, and I liked the interaction between them. While Raven clearly cannot follow directions, she is quick on her feet and remains calm while questioning everything.  I respected Sloan for not rushing into things, even though the physical attraction was intense between them almost from the onset. The fact that he was noble enough to realize it was more important that Raven have all the facts first, scored him major points.  The romance, while it progressed slowly, was delightful.The tale that Gardiner weaves was fantastic, with secret societies and hidden treasure. It reminded me of the movie, National Treasure. Overall, the plot moved at a good pace, revealing key points along the way.  This gave the tale, a genuine feel and added to the overall suspense. There were a few scenes where I question the plausibility of what occurred. For example, when someone is shot in Raven's apartment, she and Sloan are able to leave the scene and go to the hospital.  While the author provides an explanation, it wasn't realistic for me.  The EMT's witnessed them at the scene.  The author also stated the police where held up with a traffic accident and couldn't be on seen. For shots fired? Not likely..in Chicago? The next morning they return to that apartment and Raven showers. Wouldn't this still be a crime scene?  But do not be discouraged, this was my only issue and a small bump in a fantastic, action packed, suspense that kept me turning the pages to see it reach its climactic conclusion. I would enjoy meeting more members of this secret society and hope Gardiner decides to make a series from this novel.I want to thank the author for gifting me a copy of this book, in exchange for my unbiased review.
summary: suspenseful romance that will keep you turning the pages

reviewText: The reason for my headline is that the Higgs boson has no part in this story; not even a cameo appearance. The book is described as a thriller, but I think a better description would be the book version of a Hollywood disaster film, including all the silliness, but also exciting if you do not think about it too hard. The book starts with a Dr Reinhardt facing Göring et al in Norway, and persuading them that while the atomic bomb was theoretically possible, the critical mass was a hundred times bigger than actual, and it was not possible to get that much U235. This is an interesting postulate. Historically, Werner Heisenberg did much the same thing, except the evidence seems to be that he made an incredible mistake for such a famous physicist, namely he only integrated neutron flux leaving normal to the surface. Leaving that aside, this part has little to do with the story.We then have the disasters. We start with Fukushima. I have no idea whether what is described really happened, but it reads excitingly. We then have our protagonist: Tom Halligan is offered a job as Director of CERN, where they are trying to find the Higgs boson, however, as soon as he arrives and the collider is started up, there is sabotage. There follows further major earthquakes, Istanbul, the Coral Sea and San Francisco, and it is argued that the collider is responsible. Tom is set up as the saboteur, Tom works out some of what is going on, the real saboteur wants to eliminate Tom, and there is the race to save the planet. Any more and I would spoil it.The science is totally loopy. The cause of the disasters is magnetism. Apparently the collider's net field is so powerful it does something to Earth's field, and this generates the earthquakes. The collider has two opposing loops, so there is no net field at a reasonable distance. Also, the relative permeability of rock is so close to 1 that the energy required to generate these earthquakes would make civilization impossible to sustain. So, don't think about the science. The descriptions of the disasters are good, and the surfing a tsunami is great. The conspiracy part is suitably complicated and there are surprises, the thriller part is not too bad, although the odd fight scene is a bit silly, and for me, not gripping. The writing is good, and despite the flaws, I found myself reading it keenly. Yes, it could be better, and given time, I suspect Danser will be well worth following.

reviewText: I downloaded over a hundred of these type of books for my kindle this year.  Of them all, After Eden was one of my favorites.  So I was anxious to read this sequel  The concept of the book is original.  The chemistry between Devi and Oz is fantastic, and the dialogue between the two of them had me laughing out loud several times.  I love Devi and the way her character grounds this otherwise fantastical story.  I liked the inner struggle she had during this book between the girl who loves a demon, and also being attracted to the light of her angel, Camael.  And I loved Camael.  I mean, come on.  A protecting angel that also helps you with your math homework?There is a lot going on in this book.  If you're looking for a lot of romance between Devi and Oz, you may be disappointed.  But we do learn a lot more about who Devi is, and why she is important not only to Heaven, but also to Hell.  And while all of the information can get overwhelming and confusing at times, I think it comes together and starts to make sense by the end.  There's a lot more in store for these characters, and I look forward to it.  I think the author has done a great job of creating characters that we care about, who are not black or white, but who seem to have both good and bad inside of them and are more similar than you would think.  Even Forneus!  And I think I would read a book about Oz, just sitting at his bookshop, drinking coffee, if I had to (I can't help but love the demon with the heart of gold), so I'm grateful Katherine Pine gave me much more than that. . .and then some!  Just biding my time until the sequel.

There is really only one way to learn, to be taught, at the hands of a master.Marcus’s life has gone a long time without much not going his way. Beyond a college injury that changed the direction of his youthful life, he doesn’t have much to complain about. He’s been at The Den for six years, he’s an employed club Dom and now he is one of the owners. His submissives have always been contracted clients, never one that he had a desire to claim or collar.When Quinn is placed into the skillful hands of Marcus for her week long training, there is something that sparks within both of them. For her it is a desire to submit to him and to please, and for him it’s the craving to stake his claim and to take her as his own. As Marcus teaches her the basics of the lifestyle both by allowing her to watch it unfold in the public rooms and in private, by allowing her to finally free herself from the stress of a Hollywood lifestyle.The act of submitting comes naturally to Quinn. She’s done enough research to know what she should do and how she should behave, but Marcus doesn’t want the actress in her performing, kneeling at his feet. He wants the woman that has been buried inside to willingly give herself over to him.As they spend the week together, both gaining each other’s trust and exploring the ins and outs of the lifestyle, something breaks loose inside both of them. This was all supposed to make her more prepared for her new role, a role that would change her image from the child star to the woman she wants to be... But that changes when emotions come into play. With her time at the club coming to an end and having to return to California, both these two have to figure out what means more to them... their careers or what they can have together.There was something that was very vulnerable feeling with Marcus’s character. He wasn’t a broken mess of a man that needed saving, in all he was pretty well adjusted and put together. Yet there was something that made my insides soften at his tender moments and when he had to finally face the fact that her time at the club was coming to an end. Usually I need a severely broken man to get me in the feels, but somehow his normalness just worked perfectly for this story.Quinn was not overly Hollywood and I loved that the drama aspect of a diva really didn’t into play with her. I enjoyed that she did not fight her feelings too much or not give in to the experience that she was undertaking. There was something a little more erotic feeling about her journey of discovery. It was a new world for her and that allowed you to take in her experience as you read along.There wasn’t too much time to touch on the other characters from the prior books, but you get a bit of each of them in their own way. You are also introduced with a little more depth the newer characters that are slated to get their very own story. Each one is intriguing in their own way.Lynda Aicher has done a wonderful job being able to give us so many stories within this series without repeating anything. Each character is satisfying their own need in their own way throughout these series and so far they have all been so varied that you get a completely new experience with each installment.Another great story in this series and I am looking forward to Rock’s story next. He’s been the strong and silent type throughout most of this series and I am guessing he’s going to have one h*lluva back-story to showcase.
summary: This series just keeps getting better and better!

reviewText: I received a copy of this book for an honest review!When I started this book, I thought that it was going to be about Shane and David.  Turns out there are more to this story than just that.  Enter Matthew who is David's best friend and apparently the love interest of Shane.Overall I thought that this book was really good.  There were parts that left you wanting for more, but then there were parts that completely made the story worth it.  There were parts that were confusing to me personally.  For instance with David, I had hopes that there would be more about him overall.  After Shane and Matthew meet, David goes to the back burner.  Don't get me wrong, he was still in the story but I was left wanting to know more about his life.The characters themselves though I thought were written very well.  You could tell that Matthew has his ghosts in his past and they kept rearing their way up to his present.  When it comes to dealing with Shane though, who is everything that he isn't, he shows that he can change and adapt to those around him.Shane was freaking hilarious on so many levels, I couldn't stop laughing at him a few times with what would come out of his mouth.  You could tell that he has a large heart and cares about those around him, even if he is a little bit insecure at times.  Also immature.  But overall I really enjoyed him during this book.The thing that bugged me the most about this book, was all the drama in it.  (Yes there can be too much.)  It seemed like with each new chapter there was something else that was going on.  Another problem that was being caused.  I just wished that there was a time where you could just spend it with the characters and not have to be worried about what was going to happen next.Overall with this being Susan's first attempt at right a  M/M book, I think that she did very well with it.  And I look forward to reading more from her in the future!Review provided by Crystal's Many Reviews

My Rant:A Brutal Tenderness was breathtakingly beautiful. This book is much more than a companion novel to a Terrible Love, it is the missing piece to an unrelenting love story. Marata brings the story full circle by telling it from Cas's POV. Cas is displayed as an open book and he lets us into his world, his emotions, and his un-quenching love for Jewell.Talking about Cas just gives me goose bumps in a good way. His personality is hardcore and raw but what makes Cas appealing is his  heart and his dedication to his friends and the people he loves. He is the ultimate good guy with a twist.In the first few paragraphs you are gripped so tight by his persona. Cas wheels you in and life as you know it outside the book begins to fadebecause you are immersed in his story. When Cas got angry, I got angry, when he was sad, I was sad but when he showed his loving side you fall hard so hard that you need one of the panic buttons to call someone to help you get up.Marata has taken this story to a whole new level. Although I have read A terrible Love, I felt like A Brutal Tenderness was a story on its own that could basically stand alone. The action in the storyline was intense so intense my behind is gripping the seat until the permanent indents set in. LOL. Remind me to flatten my cushions.Anywhoo, Not only do you have a great story with some sexy FBI agents in it. You all know how much I love my alpha men. Cas is a brute and has no whelms of throwing his hand up when needed but he was also just as efficient as a lover. Marata heats up the pages with the smothering love scenes between Jewell and Cas. Those scenes were smoking hot. Hotter than a pop tart fresh out of the toaster as Little Kim would say. And although the scenes are blaring and your eyes are tearing because you are so close to the flame you get that connection of love, adoration and need from Cas and Jewell. They need each other on a level that is not normal almost supernatural and when they are apart you feel confined and constricted because you can feel it too.( Patting my eyes now , because I am getting emotional).I loathed Thad and Ben completely loathed them but you are also entrapped in their sadistic torture of their world and reasoning. Although they are not my favorite characters of the story they were interesting ones. In this story you get more insight to what makes Thad and Ben tic. The villains are also being put on display and I have no choice but to bow down and give Marata the credit due. Her imagination is amazingly twisted and vivid. I love every bit of it.Overall, I enjoyed this book. There is action, hot FBI studs, sex, bad guys, I mean really bad guys, a damsel in distress and a hero with a kick A$$ attitude and a heart of gold nope better than gold platinum.My Recommendation:I rated this book 5 out of 5 purple Rant Hearts and I am listing this book as one of my 2013 favs. I would recommend A brutal Tenderness to anyone one who loves a good Contemporary Romance.FTC Disclosure: I received this book for free from the author, editor, publisher, or Promo Host. This is my honest opinion about this book and I did not receive any monetary compensation for writing this review nor was I obligated to write a positive one.

reviewText: 3 StarsSparks by RS McCoyNew Adult Paranormal Fantasy RomanceBlurb:“Everyonein the world has a spark, a light inside that guides them, keeps them alive.”MyxiniSchool for Children specializes in training young men and women who havepowerful sparks. Strikers are taught to manipulate fire. Trackers learn to findanimals in the most formidable terrains. Handlers are instructed incommunication with large predators. But forty years have passed since the lasttime they had a Reader – a student with the ability to read minds.When LarkDavies enrolls at Myxini, he knows there aren’t many like him, but he doesn’trealize just how rare his abilities really are. He thinks nothing of beingasked to keep his spark a secret; after all, he can barely control it. Thoughtsand emotions flood unbidden into his mind until he can scarcely walk or hold aconversation. But just when he needs it most, his ability fails him.Larks meetsKhea, a small frightened girl who mysteriously insights his protective nature.He has no explanation for the curious strength of their relationship, and itdoesn’t help that she is one of the few people in the world whose thoughtscan’t be read. As he struggles to get to the root of their unique bond, Larkbegins to unravel more power than even his mentor expected, but in the processmakes himself a target to political leaders eager to take control.Buy Sparks on Amazon for $3.99:Teaser:Wearing only my loose brown pants, I crawled into the mostcomfortable bed I had ever known and sank into the soft down pillows. I had juststarted to drift off when I heard a knock at the door. I’m going to kill Avis.“What do you-“ I started until I realized it wasn’t Avis. Itwas a stunning blonde with blue eyes. Khea.“I’m sorry to wake you. I just- I had to see you.” Her armsmoved to wrap around my waist and hold me tight as I questioned if I was reallysleeping or not.“Uh, do you want to come in?” We both knew the rules about being in someone else’sroom after hours, so I pulled her in and sat down on the edge of the bed, stilla little surprised she was there.In the dim light her hair looked a little darker, but herface was still sweet and there was no denying that the last two years had doneher well. Who would have thought such a beautiful young woman would come fromthat skinny little girl in Lagodon?“How’d you know I was back?” I asked her, trying to appearless tired or shocked than I was.“A friend told me.”“I didn’t think you-“ Cared? It wasn’t the right word, but Iwas beyond amazed that she was interested in my whereabouts. I hadn’t seen hersince that night at the Moonwater and it had changed everything for me sincethen. But for her, I wasn’t aware that she had been affected in any way.“Ride with me tomorrow?”“Uh, yea, of course.” It was a struggle to cover how littleI wanted to wait. I would have given anything to have her stay.A wide smile erupted across her sweet lips as she said, “meetme at the lake at noon.” With a lingering kiss on my cheek, she walked backthrough the door and disappeared into the dark stone corridor.What just happened?I hadn’t seen her in person in years, and we were hardly close before that. Andnow she arrived in my room in the middle of the night and kissed me on thecheek. Was it a kiss like a friend would give another? Or more? I couldn’t makeany sense of it, but there was only thing I was sure of. I would be at the lakeat noon if it was the last thing I did.MY REVIEW:This book was a struggle initially for me as I was trying to get into the story. I didn’t necessarily get the OMG I can’t put this book down, but I did find myself still reading as there were questions in my head that needed to be answered from the beginning. The biggest one was “Where the hell are they going?” lol I know this question seems insignificant, but if you decided to read this novel, you will understand why that was my question. There were points in the book where i wished the author would have spent more time giving details or laying the foundation. Some of the book felt really rushed as though there wasn’t enough time to talk about what was happening and I believe it was because of that notion that someone how I felt cheated as if important points in the story were missing. Lots of the events that happened in the novel all happened so quickly whereas it reduced the probability of the readers truly engaging and enjoying the journey. Overall the story was a decent read and some what easy to follow, and ending was surprisingly better than the beginning of the book. I did enjoy the characters in the story including the bad ones…lol. They had a sort of camaraderie that really help transport the book and made it what it was. Though Lark had my attention, I really liked Khea’s  character. I must say, despite the fact that I did struggle reading this book in the beginning, as I continued to read things became more of an element of surprise.  Remember my question that initially kept me reading?  The author did have a way of making me feel like one of the characters in which I had to take the journey to the school with them, with absolutely no idea of what was going on or what to expect. If you like fantasy then this is a good book to read.

reviewText: * Book provided in exchange for an honest reviewWhat does a well bred, spirited and highly intelligent woman have in common with a low born pugilist? They both feel out of place in their respective worlds.Wynne Bedegrayne is easily the most beautiful of the Bedegrayne family and though she doesn't lack for admirers, she has a reputation among society for being cold-hearted when she's the total opposite. Warm, caring and defiant, Wynne has never met her match and is resigned to becoming a spinster when she meets prize pugilist Keanan Milroy. Keanan is out for revenge against the father who abandoned him and his mother to a harsh life. When he finds out that Wynne is unknowingly in the position to help him get his revenge, he begins to pursue her relentlessly, but in the process he gets to know the lady and begins to fall in love with her. Unfortunately for them, more than just society stands in the way of their happiness.I think I'm going to have to revise my opinion of entertainment fighters as heroes because I really loved Keanan Milroy. As rough and tough as he is, he is also a bit of a dreamer and he wants what he feels belongs to him. He has a kind and gentle side that not many people give him the chance to show. I love the way he looks after Wynne and the kindness he shows her aunt. Keanan never crushes Wynne's spirit and enjoys her blunt speech, something else he has in common with her.Wynne is definitely my favorite Bedegrayne. Sorry Devona but Wynne's tendency to be blunt when putting men in their places just won me over completely! Yes it makes her unpopular in the eyes of society but the fact that she does it anyway just made me love her more. Wynne doesn't waste time on superficial things, rather, she is passionate about helping others no matter their station in life. She's not the type to faint because a tough as nails fighter is attracted to her either.At first glance Keanan and Wynne don't seem like they'd have much in common but they do. Keanan is lowborn but his father is a titled man, Wynne is a well bred lady who doesn't care too much about pleasing her peers. Neither seems to completely belong in their respective worlds. In Keanan, Wynne finds a man who appreciates and even encourages her outgoing personality while protecting her fiercely and in Wynne, Keanan finds a well educated woman who can elevate his status in society but who is brave, interesting, intelligent and will accept him as he is. Their romance didn't start out as one, but it was passionate nonetheless.There's quite a bit of humor in The Scandalously Bad Mr. Milroy too. One of my favorite relationships besides Keanan and Wynne was Wynne's with her brother-in-law, the Viscount Tipton. They have a very quarrelsome relationship that just comes off as natural. Tipton may have married Wynne's sister and assumed responsibility for her family but just because society finds him intimidating doesn't mean Wynne does and she's definitely not afraid to scold him or argue with him. Their interactions, though few were fun.Sticking with the darker themes that were present in The Irresistible, No Good Viscount Tipton, this book had me entertained until the very last page. Keeping the villain's identity well hidden until the last possible moment made The Scandalously Bad Mr. Milroy very addictive for me. I enjoyed the darker themes and the feeling of "No one is safe" kept me on the edge of my reading chair until that last page.

One wolf is more attuned to his animal thus wilder and violent. The other is more of a peacetime leader, better at human/pack dynamics and such. Both are strong, and in their own ways domineering while at the same time passionate for their new mate. The mate in question is loving the attention but at the same time a bit lost in her new environment.IN THIS BOOK: We are introduced to the characters, there's lots of teasing, and there is a coupling but not the promised threesome. We are also given some world building somewhat relevant to the story, so the whole werewolf thing doesn't just end up being a nice wrapper to regular sexy time. The book ends in a cliffhanger so don't expect a wrap everything up ending.4 stars. A good beginning to a serial. Do not come in expecting an ending.

4 1/2 starsNot Until You Surrender is part 6 of the `Not Until You' serial by Roni Loren, continuing the tale of Cela as she has her limits pushed by Dominant Ian Foster.  Her tentative exploration of BDSM and her conflict about whether to comply with her family's expectations culminate in an explosive change in her situation when she panics at her interpretations of the demands placed upon her.The ongoing saga of one newbie's exploration of the dark sensual world of BDSM continues to enthrall as Dr. Cela Medina places her trust in her forceful lover.  Unfortunately, all of the pressures prove to be too much and the newly blossoming relationship threatens to spiral out of control.  This serial is a wonderful mixture of sensuality and character study and I always find myself impatient to read the next installment and this particular episode was no exception. Auctioned to the Honorable Dom may be a quick read, but the way Doris O'Connor wrote this short novel lacks for nothing. There is a complete story packed into it and it leaves you knowing the main characters inside and out.Laura is a sub looking for a real Dom, and finally finds him through an auction - but what a surprise for her when it turns out to be Slade, who is the person she's had a crush on since she was a child! Their reconnection is sweet and swift, with both of them finally learning more of what pleases the other. More importantly, they start a healing process that can only end in something good.Slade is indeed Honorable, in both action and profession (I love the twist on words here!) and shows Laura, or petal, as she is known as a sub, exactly what a true Dom is like. Pain with him melds with pleasure, and vice-versa. She's pushed to her limits, but he knows exactly just how far. Then there is that all-important aftercare, which a few 'BDSM' authors seem to disregard entirely. Follow through and finish, right? It's how it should always be done.Laura knows her heart is proven right when Slade treats her the way she'd been craving. He knows how to take her in hand, and she trusts him not only with sex and scenes, but also with letting him know the experiences she had gone through while he was away. It's a beautiful dynamic petal has with Slade, and a more perfect D/s partnership would be hard to find.Doris O'Connor has created such a wonderful story with the first of the Spectrum Auctions series. I especially like how the ending both becomes a cliffhanger and the introduction to the next book! I definitely need more...
summary: Quick Read That Packs A Punch!

reviewText: Wow! What a great first book by an awesome up and coming author!! I can't wait to read more for her!Hallie has just graduated nursing school and is ready to start her career path in the fast paced ER. As time goes on they get closer and soon they become inseparable, passion and romance, airplanes and picnics are their thing. Until one night when Ryan was walking home, that's when Hallie's life changed.Needing her friends more than ever she relied on them for everything.Needing her life back and wanting to move forward but not knowing how she turns to Sean, the man she met with Ryan. He is the rock she needs and he wants to be the rock for her. One night of bad decisions almost ruined that, can he get past what happened and be there for her still? reviewText: I do not know what it was about this story and the style of writing but it hooked me from the very beginning. The bouncing back and forth from past to present as the story unfolded was a great way to show how their love grew....then faltered...then blossomed through their individual healing. Bailey had more courage and fortitude then I certainly would have had in the face of Darren's cruelty. But, that is what was so unique about her in that she had spent all those years in isolation and through this process had gained great insight. She stuck it out more for him than for herself but, in the end, she ultimately had to protect herself. Such a great portrayal of an individual, Darren, unable to move through the grieving process and the damage, emotionally and psychologically, this can cause. Really well done. Also, well-done were the sex scenes. Yikes...he is an alpha who knows what do to...loved it.The secondary characters were fantastic. I loved Michelle and Darren's mom. Really tremendous supporting roles in getting these characters through the tumultuous waters of their relationship...I had a couple of issues with this book that kept it from a 5-star read but it would require spoilers...so, I will just say that some of the characteristics of the H/h did not feel true to who they were portrayed as so not all the pieces fit for me, in the end.  But....these characters were not created in my head so...there you go..

This concise little chapter book opens kids up to the idea that big dreams can lead to big things.Through the lessons and questions of his sixth-grade teacher Mr Garcia, Timmy's imagination and curiosity get the best of him when the moon is the topic of class study. What's so special about the moon, and what is the greatest treasure it contains?Timmy would find out!  Observing his neighbor, Cindy, on her trampoline, Timmy devises a plan and builds a device that will launch him to the moon, where he will discover the treasure!This is a fun read, and my own curiosity of whether Timmy could pull it off had me excitedly turning pages to find out!Megson and Gittle not only write a captivating story, but follow up each brief chapter with a related question to young readers.Award-winning illustrator, Carlos Brito adds the right magic with his stylish and colorful illustrations.On top of that, the story is followed with an inspiring worksheet where kids can describe and draw their own invention to get to the moon, plus, eleven line-art coloring pages of Brito's illustrations round out the book!A wonderfully imaginative, informative, entertaining and interactive book!

Rating: 4.5 StarsSome plots just never get old – just like More With You. It was something familiar, but can still bring some giddiness over some romantic scenes, and can still bring anticipation over things that you might have some idea on, but with the way the story goes, one can never be so sure.Aiden and Hailey – FINALLY!!!!Since the end of the first book, I was already rooting for these two. Liam and Allison had already their HEA, and it was time for them to get theirs too, but the problem is: he’s her best friend’s little sister and he doesn’t want their little group to be broken once things didn’t work out with the both of them. So they try to keep their feelings checked, afraid that one slip of emotion can cause major devastation not just to Liam but to the whole group.But he needs to decide now whether he wants her or not – Hailey is not a little girl anymore and she’s starting to draw attention from the opposite sex. Can he watch her be with other men? Or can he man up and tell her his feelings?Now, with all the wedding plans, and series of events that is bringing them close together, will both of them be strong enough to battle their feelings for each other?He could have just risk his balls, I mean if you really want something, if you really WANT it THAT BAD, you will cross mountains, swim rivers and catch some stars. So, it wouldn’t really matter if her older brother is your best friend. He – BOTH OF THEM- frustrate me at times. Everyone can see they are INTO each other, but none of them was sure about it, none of them would take risks. Their friendship means so much more, which I clearly understand. They needed to be sure with their emotions, of if they’re each other’s “THE ONE” before clearly taking a leap. Good thing people around them had more insight and was happy share it with them.I love seeing Liam and Allison living their HEA, and still head-over-hills in love with each other. Although Liam was quite busy with his new girl, he would still made sure that Hailey was well-taken care of by… Aiden. :D See?! He trusts her with him!!!!Just as when everything was about to be perfect because finally Aiden took the steps forward, something happened (out of context) that brought a huge wall between these two. I WAS NEARING my HEA – what in the world happened? I always appreciate a friend’s help but not at the expense of something that can hurt another person. It took some groveling, and a lot of heartaches before everything went back to normal again.Honesty, trust and taking risks – they can be just simple terms, but it can make or break a relationship. Both Aiden and Hailey needed to be honest with their feelings and with each other, and trust their emotions enough to take the risk.I think I love this more than the first one, I enjoyed reading the story and watch both Aiden and Hailey in their journey to their own HEA. It was sweet, not that long, the steamy scene – it was worth the wait.★ARC Copy was given in exchange for an honest review.★

reviewText: I was given a copy of My Sweet Valentine in exchange for an honest review.Sara returns to her small town of Pride Oregon, after living in Seattle for a few years. She comes back and is living with her mom and younger sister and has dreams of turning an empty store front into a bakery. She's hoping to leave something behind in Seattle, but no such luck.Allen is a retired Navy Seal, now in charge of the Coast Guard rescue station in town. He's at the point in his career where he's starting to hope that he'll find the woman of his dreams and settle down. Could Sara be that woman?I really liked this book in the Pride series. I haven't read all of the previous books, only the one immediately before this, but I really like how well the characters are developed when they are featured in a book while we still get glimpses of the current lives of the prior feature couples.I will definitely be reading all of the prior books in the series to see how everything got started, and I will also keep my eye out for any future books in the series!

I'm always on the lookout for the next Nuttall book and this one doesn't disappoint. It very much reminds me of Turtledove and Clancy, with the alternate history and multiple viewpoints on both sides of the conflict. Nuttall demonstrates a great knowledge of historical events that makes this alternate history entirely plausible. Nuttall talks about how no one battle can really be said to have been the deciding one in WWII and in this book you're never sure who will win. I've said this about other Nuttall books, neither side are idiots and they both pull off clever strategic victories. But the same tactic never works twice. The writing is crisp and the pace moves along nicely. A solid book for any Nuttall fans or a good introduction to his writing.

reviewText: I was given this book for free in exchange for an honest review. As a fellow author I know the first thing that grabs a reader is the cover. To be honest I probably would have passed on this book. Don't get me wrong, having offered two of my own books up for free in exchange for reviews the one that had the hottest cover garnished me nearly 5 times the readers. For this reason I am so glad she offered this book up because from start to finish she had me glued to the book. When a writer can do that, take you into their world and make you not only believe in the characters but actually feel the emotions they are going through than they have succeeded in their craft.While this book reminded me slightly of "Beautiful Stranger". Both had totally hot guys with great European accents and both start off with incredible sex between two strangers. Both take place in New York and both have leading characters that find themselves drawn to one another sexually. However the storyline is different and you find it quickly capturing you and taking you along for the ride. I look forward to her sequel "Liabilities" and will not only recommend this book to my friends and connections but will now seriously consider her other works to add to my library. Well done Ms. Dermott and thank you for the opportunity to read your work.
summary: Dont judge a book by its cover

reviewText: Oh...where to begin. I absolutely loved this book. The story line was very interesting and kept me captivated to the very end. I love the author's writing style because it is very easy to read and flows across the pages. The characters were well described and I could actually see them clearly in my mind when I was reading them. Wonderful story.I think the majority of everyone has had their heart broken at some point in their life. For Natalie it happened to her by the one guy she thought she was in love with. Needless to say we all deal with heartbreak in our own ways. Natalie decides to then leave her homelife problems behind her and move to Miami to live with a close friend. Burned by her past lover, Natalie has closed off her heart in hopes of keeping it protected. She does well with the walls around her heart until the seductive and passionate Nolan charges into her life.Nolan has been burned before by women and seeks to change his life and settle down. His eyes have fallen on Natalie and ever since then he has fallen under her spell. He will do anything possible to break down Natalie's barriers and claim her for his own.Will Natalie be able to let the walls down and fall for Nolan? How hard will Nolan fight for her heart? I loved this book and it is one book that I find is Hard to Resist reading.

The Seduction of Monet Dawson is a true account of author E. Clay's life as a soldier and hypnotist and his love for married military wife Monet Dawson. Already the accomplished author of Mogadishu Diaries 1992-1992: Bloodlines, Mr. Clay is very open about his life as a young military man who is trying to make ends meet and then finds success as a very talented hypnotist. Never a big believer in hypnotism, I found it very interesting to read the accounts of his experiences. The book opens with a 911 call and then takes the reader back to see how that event transpired. The event itself is gruesome to say the least but it's also how Monet came into his life. Although the love story with Monet seems to be what the author sees as being the main story of the book, I found it just to be an off-shoot. This book is about E. Clay and his struggles and how things come full circle. Throughout the book there are photos and documents that add to the story. I enjoyed the book and found the story interesting. It didn't grip me but the writing is quite good. I'd like to read more about his experiences with hypnotism and maybe that will become a future book.

reviewText: I've been a fan of Eric S. Brown for years despite not reading a lot of his work. I liked Brown from audio interviews and the kind of stories he produced. I fell for Brown as an author way back when he was writing zombie and comic hero stories. I loved the short story The Queen. It was so different than any other zombie story I had read, yet still very much a zombie story.Lately, I've been hearing buzz about Brown's Bigfoot series. This was my chance to dip my big toe in the pool of Sasquatch. The water was warm, blood warm.Bigfoot War: Frontier is action packed. Think of an unstoppable hairy Juggernaut roaring its lungs out as it comes barreling toward you as you lose all control of your bodily functions. It's like that and more. Eric S. Brown does great story and character development in such a short amount of time. Did I mention the action? Holy smokes, there is a lot of action and carnage from the Bigfoot clan. It is intense and very much like a zombie horde, no one is safe in this story.I highly recommend this story and this author.
summary: This was my chance to dip my big toe in the pool of Sasquatch. The water was warm, blood warm.

This is an extremely well-written and comprehensive Kindle ebook. If you know nothing about WordPress when you first start reading it, you will be well capable of setting up your own WordPress site (blog or static) by the end. If you are already familiar with the program, you will find much here to increase your capability with it.The layout is carefully thought out and at no point are you left wandering around among a lot of hard-to-follow content. Not only is the author an obvious expert, but he is also a gifted teacher, with a clear understanding of just what the beginning site manager will be wondering about and how to explain things to her or him. His whole tone is that of someone speaking directly to the reader, which is how it is with all the best instruction books.There are many Kindle ebooks on WordPress out there, some worth their cost and many not. For me, this one offers great value in terms of both money and information, and is going straight into the reference collection on my Kindle, because I know I will want to consult it again and again.
