Jaded Rein is a thrilling dystopian book that introduces us to a future with a new twist. After reading many dystopian novels, one would imagine that a new one would be a rehash of an old concept. Delightfully, A.G.Chambers has created a whole new concept that is novel and interesting.Jade, the strong and independent protagonist of Jaded Rein heads a team of DPs or Dopplegangers that are a part of this dystopian future, each gifted with an incredible ability and are well trained physically and mentally. Rein is a strong and sexy DP, whom Jade adds to complete her team. She has her hands full trying to integrate this new entrant into her team, while trying to control her growing attraction to him.Dealing with a nightmarish childhood and the demons that haunt it, while trying to neutralize a national crisis, Jade’s story keeps you glued to the book. There are surprise twists around every corner and it all comes together in a thrilling finale. An exciting book, from a brilliant young author and a must read!

This book contains a likable main character, Adam, who has psychic powers and talents.He helps the police find a kidnapped girl. He won a couple of major lottery prizes so he can not worry about grubbing for a living.There were apparently more adventures to come but I gave up about 35% into the book.Dialog is not very good - the characters often preach to each other.The level of inconsequential details is overwhelming - that is why I gave up on the book.For example, Adam is at the hospital with his sister and their dying mother. There is a discussion on why they should get their coffee from the cafeteria rather than the machine. Why is that even an issue? How does that help the story in any way?A discussion on which car rental company to get him a car? How does that help the story? Why is it even in there?And on and on and on and on and on...... One banal and inconsequential detail after another.One area of the book that was brushed over could have been expanded. That is his one year sojourn in Mexico. In a year he had no call on his psychic talents?Conclusion: Very uneven - horrid lack of editing - drowned in banality.Pass

reviewText: 4.5 starsSecond chance love! Gotta love it.When you first meet Mike he’s being blackmailed by his 80+ year old grandmother who asked for him to pose for one of her art classes, a senior art class. When he reluctantly agrees, he finds out quickly that he isn't going to pose alone. There in a sports bra and panties is his ex-girlfriend Kyra. Kyra broke Mike’s heart several years ago and he seems to not have gotten over it.Kyra is a newly divorced, broke, single-mother trying to survive. When she saw Mike after several years, she isn't sure what to think, let alone feel. Kyra knew she broke his heart, but he broke hers as well. And neither seems to be over it.After some scheming from Mike’s grandmother and her partners in crime, The OGs (The Original Grandmas), Mike and Kyra end up in sticky situations and are forced to talk it out. Now that they talked it out, and now that they are older will they work it out?MY REVIEW:I wasn't sure I was going to like this book. I thought it was slow in the beginning, and there were A LOT of details I wasn't so sure really needed to be included, but it ended up working out. I thought Mike was an ass when I first met him. I thought he was being super immature at 32 y/o. Kyra, I actually felt bad for, but then she made me mad, then went back to me feeling sorry for. I thought Sam, Kyra’s daughter, was so cute. She reminded me of my niece, and I just loved it. Now the OGs. O.M.G. FREAKING HILARIOUS! I thought their shenanigans was great, along with their text messaging skills.Overall, I thought the book was pretty good. The sex was H.O.T, and I was like phew, let me fan myself. You wouldn't expect for it to be so explicit, because of the story line. Didn't seem it was going to fit, but again it worked!I know this is a series, and I am so looking forward to reading more.

reviewText: You'd be hard pressed to find a more dedicated and loyal Stephen King fan than me, which is why it pains me to write this review. I really wanted to love this book. It had all the creepy "monster car" appeal of From a Buick 8, but the plot. It just petered out way before it had a chance to get interesting. And the ending felt really tacked on. All in all, this short story felt like more of an advertisement for King's upcoming 11/22/63. Looking forward to that book, but as a longtime fan of King's short stories, I know he's capable of far better. If this had been tossed into one of his collections, I might not care as much, but for $2.99, I expect more from my favorite author.

Ridiculous?  Yep?  Need to suspend belief and logic?  Yep again.  A funny, witty story?  Absolutely.  Will I be reading the next book?  You can count on it.Astrid has just lost her grandmother, the woman who loving raised her.  Astrid’s mother is still around, but the woman is as cold and un-motherly as an iceberg.  Needing to quit smoking, Astrid goes for hypnosis and wakes up in her own bed, a vampyre.  And of course not just any vampyre, but The Chosen.  How?  Why?  We get pretty far into the story before that begins to unveil.And who helps guide Astrid as she begins her new life?  Her best friend Gemma, who learns she’s not human either.  A very loving angel that looks like Oprah but swears like a sailor.  And The Kevin, a powerful fairy that looks like Arnold Schwarzenegger.  We’ve also got characters with other famous names that are nothing like their namesakes adding to the fun.Astrid is a self-proclaimed Prada whore who is also incredibly compassionate and loyal.  And it’s instant lust between them when she first lays eyes on Ethan, the ruling vampire of the continent.  A lot of well described lust.The book contains a number of f-bombs, but most are stopped mid-word.  Also, staunch conservative republicans will need a sense of humor to enjoy this book as some of the humor is pointed in that direction.But all in all, a fun story – with a cliffhanger.

So this book starts off with Mace trying desperately to plan her wedding and trying to still maintain a relationship with her brother, while trying to ignore her feelings for Shame, her brother's VP and bestie.  I gotta say I will agree when people say this book is angsty.  It truly is!  I had to really work hard to get past the high school drama feeling of it.  But once I did that, I actually enjoyed the book.Hem isn't really allowed to be a part of the family, he is sort of looked at as trash by his step-father and his mom being so frail in character and body has little influence to change that.  So he joins a MC that makes him feel like he is part of a family.  His biological sister, Mace, and his mom are the only ties to his old life.Mace and Hem's mother becomes ill and we start to see a huge shift from what we thought we knew with these characters, to what is actually truth.  We see secrets and pain and betrayal.  It is rather daunting towards the end, to wrap your head around all that is happening, but at the core is a love story between a man and a woman, and a brother and a sister.  The Epilogue is amazing though!Sacrifices are made...I give this book 3.5 lipsticks.  It is good, if you can get past the bad editing and angst!~B~

I hope to go to Europe one day, so I was eager to read this authors first person perspective on his travels there, and I was not disappointed. This short book is full of chatty information and observations that should come in handy one day. Nothing is left out here: from the graffiti, trash, and overzealous street vendors to the sweeping beauty, sense of awe and utter delight at being in the midst of historical places. One thing that really stood out was the descriptions of Westminster Abbey and the Sistine Chapel.  These churches are still used as places of worship but are regularly overrun with tourists who are decidedly non-reverential. That would be a jarring experience and one I would not have anticipated, so I was glad the author touched on the fact that the noise level/inane chattering was unacceptable. I suppose I thought that I, too, could try and wing it through London, Paris and Rome in a week, but really, it just sounded completely exhausting and overwhelming trying to cover that much ground in such a short period of time. This was a funny, quick and fairly handy book that I read in one sitting. Enjoyed!
summary: Real travelers tell it like it is

Steve's books are hard to read.  There's so much description of the surroundings, in terms I just skip over that to me it's distracting.  Not sure how many ways you can describe darkness?  But Steve can do it a hundred different ways, and he often does.That aside, I read a LOT of indie stuff and it's mostly regurgitated stories from the past.  Old story lines told over and over again.  This stuff is different and I like a different story.  I like NOT knowing what's going to happen.  I like wondering which characters are going to die, which ones are useful and why.  I like that it's not easy to tell where the story is going.A lot of books I read just because I feel bad paying for a book and not reading it through.  These books I cannot put down. reviewText: First reviewed at New Adult Addiction - I received a free copy of this book from the author in exchange for my honest review.What a nice surprise this book was. I've never read any of Chrystalla's books before this one, and for that I'm sorry. She's a wonderful storyteller. First of all, the year of contemporary new adult might be over. I for one am just a little bit sick of contemporary romances, but yet - I still do enjoy them a lot if they are very original.Azure is something in between a contemporary and paranormal. It's quite subtle, and for that I seriously have to give Chrystalla props. It's something of a mermaid story - but yet... that's not even close to what it is. First of all, the main heroine, Olivia, is not in any way paranormal. And the hero, Kai, might not be either.So where's the paranormal aspect, you ask? Well, I'm not going to tell you. It's a spoiler that I'm not willing to give up, because half f what kept me reading was figuring out this little mystery these two characters have going.I love the setting - on the beaches of Crete. Chrystalla herself is Greek and I have this thing for reading non-American authors - and maybe it's more of a non-English thing... or a non-English as an only language thing... but anyway - I enjoy reading their take on storytelling in English when it's not their only language because the sentences and expression are so fresh. Chrystalla's storytelling is like that. She a breath of fresh air and really excels as keeping things interesting using word choices alone.Also - this is such a thoughtful book. It has original poetry at the heading of each chapter, complemented by Shakespeare, and I tell you, I liked the fictitious poet much better than I did the famous dead English one. ;) Those little poetic gems should not be skipped - they are delightful. In fact, these little snippets were so good, I actually went Googling for the poet! (She's not real, the poet is Chrystalla!)OK, on to the story - Olivia is in Crete with some German friends trying to get over a nasty break up with a boyfriend and get past a mistake she made with a friend not that long ago.Kai is in Crete because this is his home. Sorta. He's half American, he speaks perfect English, and he grew up in America. He's also very cryptic and moody - but that's because he's got some demons in his past as well.And everything about this story revolves around the sea... mermaids? Not quite. Sirens? Nope. Angry Greek Gods... sorry. Not it.And yet - it might be about all three of those things.This story is so original, I don't want to spoil it for you by giving away too much of the plot so let's just say it's a nice romance with some hot moments, some tension, some mythology, some history, and some poetry.I loved it, actually. Chrystalla pens a beautiful new adult tale that is totally by itself as far as what's currently out there in this genre. I definitely recommend this one to all romance readers.
summary: Such a thoughtful, original, new adult book

reviewText: Love, lust, and betrayal explosively collide in Shaun Harmon's stunning debut novel.Using a first person narrative, Harmon exquisitely describes Marcus's sadness, anger, and confusion at the betrayal of his fiancée, Tami. Lusty and erotic scenes laced throughout the novel add to the raw emotion of the story. At times, the characters' palpable emotions, spurred by the intense situations, coupled with stunning plot twists, left me staring at my e-reader with a shocked "O" on my face.By the end, this well written dramatic novel left me emotionally spent but looking forward to future novels.I was provided a copy of the book by BTS eMag for purpose of an honest review. reviewText: My Review:This is the second book in the series and it was just as good as the first. Liam is a shifter that we met in the first book who was Dserted by his mate. In this world, for shifter males, this is a fate pretty much worse than death. It leads to depression, complete separation from their animal, and eventual complete mental breakdown. Liam is 8 months into the torture when he feels his mate, Ava, die, but she isn't actually dead. There's someone out there determined to torture Liam and knows that for a shifter, that torturing Ava is the perfect way to do it.Ava has very good reasons for why she left Liam, but it was definitely not because she didn't love him. She doesn't understand his shifter side, but that wouldn't have been enough to drive her away. BUT she does have to stay away. Her torturer has left her no choice.This book is super-emotional as Liam and Ava work through exactly what is happening. Ava has no idea what it means to a shifter male to do what she did to Liam and as she learns about it, she is horrified. For his part, Liam has no idea why Ava has been doing what she is doing and with the knowledge that he is probably going to sink back into that dark place lurking, he's trying to figure out how to convince Ava to give them another try....at the same time, trying to keep her safe from this guy who has the mysterious vendetta against him.The book was good. The world is really interesting. I love Abby Niles' take on shifter mates and the biological vs. mental response to it all.My one disappointment with this book was there seemed to be a much higher than normal number of typos and editing issues within the book. I expect better quality from a professionally published book. A  handful of issues, I can see slipping by, but there had to have been close to twenty and that's just not right. I hope this doesn't mean that quality at Entangled Publishing is sliding....I do look forward to the next book in the series....Brit maybe???

It is also no wonder Patience got hooked on drugs. This book should come with a warning about the content. The story actually is over shadowed by the molestation. I couldn't feel the love.Faith and Finn story also has intense physical abuse. This story was unbelievably predictable for me though.The molestation just gutted me. It made me feel sorrowful, sad, and despondent. Next time I wish the author will give an advance warning.

I picked up Betting on You when I wanted something light and fun. Even better, it was free on Amazon. Although this book started off that way, and I loved the Georgia setting, it didn't end up having the emotional impact on me that I wanted.1) I thought that Lark forgave Mason way too easily in the beginning. He was gone for over 4 years without ever contacting her, and though she puts up what looks like a good resistance at first, she completely forgives him in 4 days. I will give Lark props for an inventive idea to make him understand how much he hurt her. But still, it was way too soon for me to trust him, or feel like I could believe their romance after that point. Lark also doesn't really ask Mason any hard questions or seek to get to know him deeper after he was gone so long. She forgave him on the most basic explanations. After she was destroyed when he left, I'd think she'd need a lot more time and effort to be won back. That said, I still liked Mason and I wasn't really worried about whether he would hurt her again (being inside of his head too helped). Even so, I was still angry at him when Lark was ready to start back where they left off. Eventually I did get over this and was fairly successful in getting back into the romance.2) That is until about halfway through we get a chapter/interlude from another character and learn that there is possibly some secret that Mason hasn’t told Lark about, however, we're not told the nature of this secret. Then in the very next chapter the book shifts back to Mason/Lark and a huge important moment of intimacy and bonding for them. Instead of enjoying this part I felt uncomfortable and skimmed the whole thing, because of this looming secret. Emotionally, it did not work for me to be able to connect to their relationship, when I knew there was still something big between them, even if they didn’t know it yet. For me, the previous chapter needed to be removed entirely, or placed after this one for this book to work. Honestly, that interlude pretty much ruined the whole emotional impact of the story for me. I have some friends who read this book and weren’t as bothered by this as I was, but I very much considered DNFing after this point. Especially, because I was already on shaky ground due to the quick reconciliation in the beginning of the book.3) Eventually we find out what the secret is and of course it’s a huge deal and causes major tension. Only, I didn’t think it should have been as big a deal as Lark thought it was, especially after Lark was able to so easily forgive Mason in the beginning of the book. I get that it was a wakeup call that maybe Lark did have some unresolved issues with Mason that she let go too easily before. But the extent to which she takes her reaction, just made me frustrated with her.Betting on You is a contemporary romance and the ending was satisfying, but as a whole, the book was too frustrating for me to be able to really enjoy it. That said, I am interested in Aria and Nash’s story, which was teased in this one, enough that I may give this author another chance.

I knew it! I absolutely knew that Tessa Bailey could blow me away again with her new book, His Risk to Take! It's a short and quick read, but has solidified the fact that Bailey has become a favorite of mine! His Risk to Take is yummy, dangerous and straight up over 100 degrees celsius HOT.I have one question for Troy and that's, can I be his risk to take? Because dear god, there is nothing hotter than a dirty talkin` sex machine Detective like Troy Bennett!  You would have never thought twice because Troy came off as quiet and reserved, but get him in the bedroom and clothes start flying. Troy's a man who is so manly he'll melt your panties off with one look. Troy was the type of man to make you want to be in his jeans as soon as humanly possible. Not only that, Troy's dominating, protective and oh so loving, Ruby wasn't the only one falling. I want one, please and thank you.I freaking loved Ruby! She was fire and ice and everything nice. The fact that she can play pool better than any guy I know and can talk right back to a man without hesitation is what I call a kick ass, fierce as hell chick. I wanted to embody her, not just to get in Troy's pants mind you, but to have the confidence and recklessness she carried with her. Ruby was a survivor and even though she could get herself into some sketchy stuff, she has her own back and can handle herself. I not only loved her snark, but her whole straightforward attitude as well.I am at Tessa Bailey's mercy, because wow, she has some serious totally impressive talent for writing passionate, intense, and lusty love romance like no other. This book is just sexy romance at its finest and one I call pure excellence. What's even better is that she mixes in this explosive seduction with hustling, gambling and suspenseful danger that had me bouncing on my toes with excitement. I want to live in Bailey's mind because daaaamn, I can't get enough of her writing, ever.   This book may be short, but it's packed with lip licking sex scenes, endless wit and intense drama to entice just about everyone!

There were two reasons I took a part of this book tour. The first one was the stunning cover, I loved it and decided to read more on it. Reading the synopsis I realized it was a Regency Historical Romance, then I was super excited to read this book that I read it way ahead of time.The book is about Thomas and Evangeline, both of whom are put in a predicament by their parents to marry in haste. Thomas' father would take away his allowance if he is not wed and having a child on the way by his thirtieth birthday. Evangeline's father on the other hand would choose her future spouse if she fails to find her own soon. As they are both caught in a predicament, they decide to wed and Evangeline begins to realize that almost everything her mother told her about marriage life was a lie. However, Thomas' scandalous past is threatening to be a part of his future. Would their marriage manage to survive that?I truly enjoyed the premise of this story. That and, the characters seemed genuinely different than one another. Which would have made for a great clash. I truly enjoy stories where one of the characters has their hand forced and tries to get out of said situation, it's quite amusing when the puppet strings are actually pulled by the parents. Sadly, I don't think the characters reached their full potential in this book. Like, if there was more bickering or argument it would have added more humor to the book. The book was good, just not as funny as it could have been what with the clash of characters. I think Thomas should have had to fight more before getting himself into the situation that forced him and Evangeline to wed.As I've mentioned before, historical romance is a genre I am very particular with because for me everyone enjoys a different style of writing. It took me a while to get accustomed to new styles of reading after being practically obsessed with Julia Quinn books. Nadja's style is different than the rest so, I guess I'll have to read more of her books before getting used to it. But I did enjoy the story!Rating: 3/5

I received this book in exchange for an honest review.Shifters, what is it about them that call to most of us. Is it the draw of something different that is still somewhat human or is the draw of having someone powerful, which can take care of us. What ever it is we like them. Most of the time we tend to read about wolf shifters, which to me is the most common and if its not then I need to read more but when I read the blurb for this story I was intrigued. Bear shifters. Now I think I definitely need to give this a try, another supernatural romance but a side of kink.Predator’s Kiss by Rosanna Leo is a wonderful love story about two people that have buried their hearts behinds walls after being hurt by people they thought they care for.Ryland a shifter and the owner of a resort created for shifter like himself likes peace and quiet and maintaining the secret away from humans. After being burned by one, now more than ever he believes in only staying with his kind and not to love again. But like always nothing stays like he plans. His brother shows up causing trouble but not as much as the next lovely person.Enter Ms. Lia a writer in the run from a crazy fan. She stumbles into Ryland’s resort bringing with her trouble of the staking variety, passion, lust and love for our poor heartthrob Ryland.When they meet there is an instant connection that they both do not understand and try to shake. Ryland thinks she is infatuated with his flirting brother and Lia thinks he hates her. Throughout the story they learn about each other and fall for one another but because of Ryland’s little bother thoughtlessness the crazy hits the fan faster than they expect and Lia is in trouble.I loved the chemistry between the characters. It took Ryland awhile to listen to his inner bear and love the woman but once he did the fireworks was incredible. While the sex was described it was not smut and was well written. But that is not all. After all the craziness with her stalker is over you would think ok happily ever after now WRONG! There was more and Lia once again is in trouble.The twist towards then end was great and I personally did not see coming. I would love to read more about this two character and what happens in the future with her and the new changes in her life.Predator’s kiss gets 4 olives/stars and I can’t wait to read more from the author.

3 out of 5 stars***This book was provided for free by the author in exchange for an honest review through the Goodreads “Don't Buy My Love” program***This is the 4th book in a series, and I admittedly did not read the first 3 (which the author refers to as short stories, whereas this is novella length).  It can be read as a stand alone, because the majority of the back story is either told or implied, but I think I probably would have enjoyed it more had I read the others first.Sean and Rusty are engaged, and living on a shoestring budget in Boston.  We meet them as they are performing in a choir concert that is a fundraiser for their church – and I loved that intro for a gay romance!  They are preparing to return to New Orleans for Christmas, where they both grew up.  For Rusty, this is a much anticipated return to a loving family, but for Sean it is a dreaded return to the town where his abusive father still lives, as well as a mother and sister who have ignored him for 7 years.  Each is aware of the other's feelings about the trip, and both are trying to be supportive, but find it difficult.I know writing about established couples can be difficult, because the excitement of discovering a new love is past, and the story is just about the (hard) work of maintaining that love.  In this case, one partner (Sean) has serious trust issues due to his background, and there is a lot of talk about the fact that he is in therapy, as well as the lessons he has learned from his therapist.  Rusty is also in therapy, trying to learn how to accept Sean, and help him get through these issues.  Much of the book is focused on the themes of letting go of past injuries, learning to accept love from others, and being open and communicating.  I think there were good lessons presented.  But if a reader is looking for the anticipation and adventure of a typical romance, it is not present in the book.  Even the sex scenes feel a little forced at times, and interestingly, the times the MCs do NOT have sex (due to anxiety or interruptions) are actually a little more memorable.There was a very nice resolution – Sean finally wholeheartedly accepts the love so freely given by Rusty's family, and Rusty learns that although you can't go home again, his home in Boston with Sean is what he wants and needs more anyway.  They've both grown emotionally from one short trip home, but that ending seemed just right.There were a handful of typos and textual errors throughout that could have been avoided with a careful proofread, but overall they did not detract too significantly from reading the story.

Night Watcher by Chris LongmierI received a copy of this novel for review purposes.This is the second novel I have read by Chris Longmier and have found both stories, though vastly different, to be intriguing.When Julie leaves her home, job, family and friends to get to the bottom of the mystery surrounding her estranged husband's suicide she is not prepared for the consequences. Believing the "other woman" to be the cause she embarks on a vendetta to bring Nicole to her knees. After she befriends Nicole, keeping her identity as the woman scorned to herself, her life is turned upside down as she begins to understand that there is something or someone else at work. Nothing is as it seems and the mystery begins to deepen.With non-existent clues the police are at a standstill, Nichole's life is in danger and Julie has put herself in the site of a killer. One who comes and goes without being noticed by anyone, a mystery man who has decided who will live and who will die.In order to save herself, Julie must use all her senses to escape the terror that is the Night Watcher.A well defined and written psychological thriller, mystery with a little romance to brighten the action, Night Watcher will leave you checking your doors and windows twice. Don't forget to close the curtains. You may be watched!Karen Bryant Doering,Parents' Little Black Book

I would give this 3.5 to 4 stars. Noah was/is a dragon who, about 2,500 years ago, decided to live as a man. In the first chapter, Noah is running his antique shop in Nashville when he meets Izzy and her boyfriend as they try to steal from him.  Lila, Izzy's sister, flies in to Nashville to help with her sister.  Very quickly, Izzy is dead - killed by the person who has discovered Noah's secret and wants his dragon blood.  The majority of the book is about Noah and Izzy trying to escape danger and hunt down the man who wants Noah's blood (which has dragon properties to it).The book was well-written with no big typo or grammar issues. I was immediately engaged in the story. Music was integral to the story in that Noah loved playing the saxophone and played one night a week in a bar. And I felt like the characters really did have chemistry between them. I felt like the two were drawn to each other (and I liked the fact that Noah was quicker to express feelings than Lila). Thus, it was satisfying as a romance novel.  It was an action-filled ride with little down-time.  In fact, that was my biggest issue with the book.  Everything happened so fast.  Basically, the book takes place over a few days.  I wish the story had played out a bit to let things develop more deeply between Lila and Noah. I wish we had seen more of Noah's life (e.g. playing the saxophone) or met characters he knew (for example, in Thea Harrison's "Dragon Bound", we see the hero's friends and the heroine interacts with them). Noah talked a lot throughout the book about how much music touched his soul and how much it meant to him and we know he plays the saxophone.  I wish we were told more of his favorite songs or how he came to play the saxophone (since it hasn't been around for 2,500 years!).  This type of background would have made the characters seem more grounded and real to me.I had two minor quibbles - one with a plot hole and another with the ending.  The plot hole that bothered me was that the villain "found out" about Noah as Noah kept returning to Nashville (and never aged). I did have a hard time believing that Noah would keep returning to Nashville.  There are many places around the country (or even overseas) that are known for good music where he could have played.  This made it seem more of a plot device and I wish there was a stronger reason the author developed that kept drawing him back to Nashville.Finally, the ending was just a tiny bit unsatisfying. While everything is resolved with the bad guy and the characters are together, it didn't have the feeling of a "happily ever after" (and how could it as they've only known each other for 4 days!).  I don't know if the author is planning a sequel, but I would be interested in seeing these two characters further develop their relationship.

A FEW COMMENTSFirst, I would like to say that this is a four star story with some three star editing issues, in my opinion. So I ask that you read the entire review before making a decision as to whether or not you think you would enjoy it. The fact that the review is so long should tell you I enjoyed the story enough to take the time and write a detailed account of my reactions to it. Thank you ahead of time for your patience.Second, this will be a long review. I will clearly section it off so if you don't want to read a particular portion, you can skip it. For example, toward the end, I will discuss the politics of the book. It you are not interested, you can just move right along.And finally, at this point I would like to include some details about how I review Independent Authors because that does play a part in this review. I am more lenient with Independent Authors. The main reason is that they don't have access to big time publishers and many don't have the money to hire top of the line editors. In fact, some do without. Books that are published with big time publishers go through many rounds of reading- beta reading, proofreading, copy editor, final editor and some other stuff with which I am not yet familiar. The same is not true of independent novels. Therefore, when deciding on a rating, I am more inclined to ignore things that I would not ignore in non-independent books.REVIEWIn the very near future, the U.S. government has slowly chipped away at individual freedoms and built up so called entitlement programs to the point that most Americans are completely dependent on the federal government, which results in an enormous debt to China. Unfortunately, China calls in that debt and the United States is unable to pay it. With no other options, the President hands over the United States to China who intends to bleed the country dry of all resources. First order of business- thin the herd.The story is told primarily from the point of view of a small group of country folk. Even in the country, most people are still dependent upon the government but a few see what is coming and do everything they can to be as self-sufficient as possible, Unfortunately, they face growing problems when one son is taken to a labor camp, thieves and murderers make frequent attacks on homes and the city inhabitants begin moving outside the cities and will soon arrive, looking for food and somewhere safe to live.This is what I refer to as political, speculative fiction. The scenes are frightening and captivating. At points, I couldn't drag myself away, and paid for it the next morning.I don't know who the target audience is or what the author's intent is. That makes a difference, especially with this type of book. So please, PLEASE, don't let my next statement scare you off, but I am just going to throw it out there- If you are a fan of Glenn Beck, you will love this story; If you are a fan of Rachel Maddow, not so much. Either way, it can be an entertaining read as liberals could read it with moral indignation; sometimes that's a bunch of fun too. I wish Roberts had included more of the opposite point of view and showed events unfolding from a Rachel Maddow point of view. The character Thomas gives the reader a little of that, but I would have enjoyed a much more in depth storyline from that perspective.There were a few places where I chuckled. I don't know if they were intentional. For example-Jean was simply irreplaceable, like a piece of old farm equipment, "they just didn't make em' like that anymore."My immediate reaction was, "Did he just compare his wife to farm equipment?" The other thing I found amusing is that Thomas and Mary Jefferson, who are liberals, have a son named Davis. Davis angers Thomas with his more conservative comments, but he attends University of Texas, which is a liberal school in arguably the most liberal city in Texas. Jefferson comments, "Is this the kind of thing you're learning at college?" He's going to UT so the answer is- not likely.WHAT WORKED FOR METitleI really like the title. At first, I was unsure. I thought maybe it came from a famous quote, but I couldn't find one that was close enough to support that theory. If not, I'm impressed-Man's past is filled with truth's shed blood.That's a good quote.IntelligenceI appreciate that the book is intelligent. I know liberals will argue otherwise, but there are intelligent points. And regardless of whether or not you think it works, there are intellectual discussions and what amount to short speeches.CreepyI'm a big fan of creepy and Truth's Blood has no shortage of creepy. And no one is safe. So if you have a favorite character, I wouldn't get too attached. I like authors who make none of their characters safe.WHAT DID NOT WORK FOR MEEditingTypos, misspelled words, grammatical errors and errors in syntax only affect my rating when there are enough to disrupt my reading. While these errors were not all over the place, there were many times they did interrupt my flow. Each reviewer has his or her own thing and this is one of mine. I have seen many people comment it doesn't bother them. And in all honesty, it was not enough that I wouldn't read any more books by this author. There were times I stayed up late because I didn't want to put the book down. So keep that in mind when deciding whether or not to read Truth's Blood.AccentThe Chinese are the new Russians, so I completely understand why they are the bad guys. That's not the issue. The issue is accent. It just came across to me as the Christmas dinner scene from A Christmas Story. For example-"I will not mince words with you American dogs," Ju-long spat. "America owe China moe than four trillion dolla and you are going to pay."I personally didn't think it was necessary. In fairness, you will get a lot of southern accent and slang as well.Repetition & SpeechesSome of the political talking points get a bit repetitive. And the speeches disguised as dialogue break the flow of the storyline. The initial classroom scene was done very well. It's the sitting in the living room or porch and two people who believe the same thing are going back and forth agreeing with each other. To me that is a clear "I'm making a point to the reader" moment. That happens a few times in the book.Internal MonologueI'm just not a fan.WHAT I HAVE NOT DECIDEDQuotesI think quotes at the beginning of each chapter can be extremely effective. However, I was not always clear as to how the quote was relevant to what happens in the chapter. Maybe that is my failing, but I don't think I should have to try so hard if the book is meant for entertainment. That's where knowing the author's intent would be helpful.POLITICSI kid you not, Truth's Blood hits a lot of talking points- business ownership, liberal elitism, government regulation, national debt, gun control, drone attacks, due process, entitlement programs, political correctness and more. I just want to make one observation.Keynesian EconomicsKeynesian Economics is brought up several times. At the beginning, there is a scene in a classroom where a teacher and student are debating Keyne's economic theory. Unfortunately, the reader either has to take the characters' comments on faith or must stop to look up the very advanced and intricate theory for him or herself.CONCLUSIONI do recommend Truth's Blood. If your political views are in opposition, skim those parts. In my opinion, there is enough in the book to make for an entertaining read if you are indeed interested in this genre. I thoroughly enjoyed the story.

I am a Becca Jameson fan. She writes excellent shifter books and her shifter/menage books take the explosive hotness of her stories to another blow-your-mind level. But this book - this book takes every book I have ever read of hers and blows it out of the water!I had the privilege of reading this book at the request of the author before publication. This is Becca Jameson's first foray into a BDSM book. She has used some light bondage or blindfolds in other books but nothing she has written has ever delved this deep or explored the lifestyle like this book. And nothing else of hers I have read has been this powerfully written. I still remember the goosebumps and in-drawn breaths, the sensations that moved through me as I read the words Ms. Jameson had written. I actually had to stop partway through and take a break to let my emotions settle because the honesty and intensity of this book affected me so deeply.One of the many things that I find so alluring about the BDSM lifestyle is the inherent honesty. Whether you are a Dom or a submissive, you MUST be honest with your partner at all time as well as with yourself. For most of the modern world, that means we have to learn what it means to be honest about what we feel and what our motives are. Honesty - especially being honest with yourself - is something that has fallen out of fashion in the fast-paced "get everything you can, you are the number one priority and the only one that matters so go ahead and be selfish" world of material gain that has highlighted the 21st century for many. This book explores that level of honesty in a way that is both haunting and beautiful.We are voyeurs with Aiden and Dane as Stephanie learns to be honest with herself about her needs and learns to express those needs. The men also have to learn to listen to someone else, to let her in to their twosome so that they can build this relationship that they desire. This book follows them all on their few days long journey of self and sexual exploration.I HATE SPOILERS so all I will add is this book is a masterpiece of the written word and I am a better person having read it.

reviewText: This is not my favorite series of Kristen Ashley's, in fact I have been very critical of this series in the past because it is the most dry of her books.  In the other series she writes it feels as if she is more excited about the characters and location.  Indiana is just sort of humdrum.  That being said, this was probably the best book in the series in my opinion.  I like Joe & Vi's story, but this one was a bit better.Frankie is a headcase.  No joke.  I have never seen any woman who is more twisted up than this girl.  She has a messed up family and a really tragic past.  We start this story with her being in the hospital after she was shot, be sure to read Joe & Vi's story to see this.  Her head is a mess and quite frankly, the fact that Benny would even want in there is staggering to me.  Frankie wasn't my favorite character, but there were things about her I really appreciated.  She is career driven and I totally dug that about her.  Also, once she gets out of her own head, she is actually a really good person who gets walked on a lot by others, namely her family.Benny is almost too sweet.  He has a bit of an edge, but it isn't really explored.  I don't know, I guess I like my KA men to be awesome with a devil may care attitude.  That is not Benny.  This guy screams commitment, family, & love.  He is one of the quiet KA heroes.  Not sure I love that, but it worked when pairing it with Frankie's craziness!  All in all, they made a great pair.Now I love Kristen Ashley.  I always have.  But I felt this book, and this series, was just a slower, older, and a bit boring version of the Colorado Mountain Series.  I have decided that Indiana men are just not for me.  =)  But Colorado men.....The book is sweet, gentle, and truth be told, a bit bland.  But like I have said, this is par for the course in the 'Burg.  A few bright spots, Mrs. Zambino is a riot & Gus is adorable!  The epilogue was amazing, as is the KA way, but not sure I will be diving into Merry & Cheryl's story.  It is going to be the last in the series so who knows.I give this 3.5 lipsticks.~B~

Review courtesy of Dark Faerie TalesQuick & Dirty: Strange take on the Dracula mythos that is entertaining and bizarre.Opening Sentence: She swam in an ocean of blood.The Review:A strange new take on the Dracula mythos, imagine if Vlad Tepes had actually been born a woman and her parents disguised her to live as a man, not even her brother knew her birthright. Valerie Tate spent the first 500 years of her life as a man until World War II when she faked her death, letting the world believe that the vampire named Dracula died. Valerie is out for revenge against her brother Radu for the crimes he committed during WWII.Cue to present day Portland, Oregon where a huge convention of supernaturals is scheduled. Valerie has journeyed to the city to finally get her shot at killing her brother Radu. As she is scouting the city, she doesn't expect to run into Lance Soleil, let alone be attracted to him. Valerie has neglected her female side vowing to finally give in to her female emotions once her revenge has been completed. Dracula's Secret follows Valerie as she learns to deal with her female emotions and the life lessons that she learns from Lance.This review has been hard for me to write because the story itself wasn't too bad. I enjoyed many aspects of it, how the world reacts to the supernaturals and the roles they played in the major wars, the unnatural nature of Lance and how the story didn't end like I would have expected. One thing that really turned me away from the story was whenever Valerie mentioned missing her mustache, and growing and shaving it. I don't know why this wigged me out so much but I don't like mustaches on females in any shape or form. Let alone how she was able to grow a mustache to begin with. I did have a hard time connecting with Valerie at times especially when she would reminisce about said mustache.Dracula's Secret jumps around to many different point of views as the novel goes along including Radu and John, a man from Lance's past. The novel is filled with enough action and mystery to keep you interested in the story. The atmosphere of the novel is dark and sexy and at times a little silly.If you want a story that is a little out of the box then I would recommend Dracula's Secret. Overall, it was a strange story that intrigued me enough that I would read the sequel, Dracula's Desires, to learn the next steps of Valerie's life.FTC Advisory: Kensington provided me with a copy of Dracula's Secret. No goody bags, sponsorships, "material connections," or bribes were exchanged for my review.
summary: Strange take on the Dracula mythos that is entertaining and bizarre.

reviewText: I thought this would be a pleasantly spine-tingling read for the Halloween season. The story of the 'haunted' wood was more a backdrop (and deus ex machina, I'm afraid) for the story of Izzy and her abusive ex-husband.  Most readers will enjoy the story so long as they aren't expecting something more in line with 'horror'.  The writing was done well, the characters were believeable, though not always likeable (I personally did not LIKE Izzy at all, though I could sympathize with her), and Kindle formatting was fine.  The writing was worth probably 4 stars, but I took one off due to the fact that this was promoted as more of a 'horror' or 'suspense' genre, which it really wasn't.

reviewText: Laura's parents own a catering company and have left her in charge while they take a year off to travel.  But the once successful business now seems to be losing its clients, and Laura can't figure out why.  Enter Alex Track.  Laura meets the handsome billionaire at an event she caters for him.  The next time they meet, he learns from her that her catering business is suffering financially, and he offers to get to the bottom of the mystery, for a price.....marriage to him.  Why does this handsome man want to marry a woman he barely knows?  And why does a spurned suitor turn aggressive when Laura refuses to sell the catering  business to him?  These are questions that plague the reader...until the very end of the story.  I found this book to be a very enjoyable read and definitely worth the 99 cent price tag.  A good short story that can be read in one sitting, and I would definitely recommend this book.

Sam's Story:  Book Three was just as wonderful as book's one and two.  Absolutely epic three part series following the life of Samantha Skylar.This author has a way with words that make you feel like you know the characters personally.  I still stand by my statement in my review for Book Two:  These books are worthy of a Pulitzer.  It's been a long time since I read a story that stayed with me as Sam's Story does...  and I read a lot of books.  I mean A LOT.  Hardly any of the books I read on amazon are worth a re-read.  Don't get me wrong...  there are some really really good books on amazon...  but to be worth a re-read for me, the story has to be as Epic as Gone With The Wind or The Stand.  Sam's Story IS as EPIC as Gone with The Wind and The Stand.  It is a story that I will probably re-read for years to come.  I just need hard copies now :)I would love to see the story continue with Lucy or with Chel and Jake :)  I really didn't want the story to end, I feel as though, after three epic books about Sam and her family, that I know them and now I want to see Lucy grow up :) I want to send her birthday cards and go volunteer at the animal shelter with Sam.  :)If you have read books one and two and are wondering if Book Three will be as good...  IT IS.  If you haven't read books one and two yet...  what are you doing here?  Go read books one and two!  This is a story WAY to wonderful to miss!I would recommend Sam's Story to anyone (and I am).  It is a truly captivating story that had me often in tears, of sadness, anger and joy, it had me often laughing out loud one chapter and screaming at my screen in another chapter.  Honestly....  it's a story that I can see being made into an epic three hour long movie....  do yourself a favor and read these books!I wish I could give this book a hundred stars.  And I am not exaggerating. :)
summary: An Epic Story that captivated me from Book One and didn't let go!

In Mid Life Love, Claire is dealing with a cheating (ex) husband, the loss of her (former) best friend, and the pursuit of a younger man.Now comes Mide Life Love: At Last where Jonathan and Claire are madly in love and planning their wedding.. The "marital counseling session" is HILARIOUS and one scene I NEVER want to forget. The bachelorette party is wonderful, alarming and funny. The little surprises Claire has for Jonathan are sweet. The climax is a shock.Jonathan and Claire are adorable. I love the way Jonathan treats Claire. He is absolutely so in love it's like...AWWWWW....Claire is almost as frustrating to me as she is to Jonathan. Still, I love them both.When Claire's ex-husband returns, all hell breaks loose. This part of the story is the biggest and most unwelcome shock. It's a bold and daring move that works brilliantly. The added thrills make this a mystery/thriller/romance. My heart is pounding just remembering all his stunts.Whitney wrote a realistic account of what couples endure. There are plenty of things that could, and often do, go wrong in any relationship. The couples that are truly in love have the patience to work it out, no matter what. At Last gives us Jonathan and Claire. Do they have the love to last?Incredible. I love it. A memorable, funny, thrilling romance featuring Jonathan and Claire.Received this ARC for an honest review.

The Kindle Book Review received a free copy of this book in exchange for a fair and honest review. We are not affiliated with Amazon or the author.The author has stated that this story was meant to be read aloud while keeping the interest of the reader. I can't really speak to that, as I don't have a child of the right age to test it out on, and the attention spans of those I do have available to me are way too short.King Cuthbert is the King of the island Insolvia. He's childish, self centered, and hilariously silly. When it is revealed to him that the reason for the recent (and deliberate) ineptitude of his servants is that they haven't been paid lately, he takes action. I won't say what, just in case you decide to read it. And then, the story comes, as promised, to a rather abrupt end.I found myself wishing that this had come with pictures. I am way beyond needing pictures to get into a story, but I would love to see illustrations of the darling and funny descriptions of the scenes in the story. We have, for instance, the King sliding down the bannister of a morning, to be greeted by a straight faced uniformed footman at the bottom, who helps the King keep track of his record times. I would love to see that! There was the spoiled King's dismay at being served nothing but a carrot (as a waiting for his breakfast snack). The footman reassures him that the carrot is full of vitamins. "Vitamins haven't been discovered yet," grumbles the King.He turns out, in the end, to be a good hearted likable guy. Well told, it can be read (aloud or otherwise) with a smile-the wording is clever throughout and it is delightfully British.Jane McBride~The Kindle Book Review

Unfortunately for me, this book didn't work out for me.  The author has a great imagination and she describes her world and her characters very vividly, which is a good thing.  She makes a disclaimer at the beginning that if you are grossed out about getting up close and personal with corpses, this may not be the book for you. The author has created a unique paranormal world with great characters.I was provided this book by NetGalley in exchange for an honest review.

This is my second Craig Saunders book and  it certainly won't be the last.  "The Love of the Dead" was an original, compelling and enthralling literary experience.  Initially, it subtly pulled me in and lulled me into thinking that "this is just going to be another "good" paranormal mystery with a bit of horror and gore."  Then, to my utter delight, somewhere along the way, BAM!, I found myself completely captivated by a  spellbinding, and refreshingly original literary encounter that had my senses reeling and my pulse ponding.  In fact, by page 247, I was on the edge of my proverbial seat hoping for the best but fearing the worse.  Most readers, if not all, definitely won't see the various plot twists coming.There are 4 main characters. Each is mulit-dimensional, empathy worthy and I like each one. The "villain" for lack of a better phrase is repulsive and, of course, I loath him.  The character development and the story's pace is spot on.  The author's writing style is engaging, vivid but yet concise.  Just the way I like it.  The author employs a style that describes the horror well but somehow causes one's imagination to amplify the scene and, thereby, making the read creepier and even more disturbing. I'd like to see a movie.  My recommendation: Buy it, Read it and Enjoy!Here's wishing Craig continued inspiration and success!JewelsSPOILER ALERT!I was rather baffled by the date at the very end.

2.5 out of 5I have never wanted to finish a book I wasn’t really in to more than this one.  It was the oddest thing.  There were definite elements I liked but at the same time I didn’t particularly care for the characters, the story was predictable, the sex hot but sometimes far-fetched and the writing a little cliché.  Still I could not stop reading until I got to the end to see what happened.  This book is very vague on details from the beginning, from setting to character development, very little is revealed, making it difficult to connect with anyone.  Eva, for me, was a pushover, and her waffling nature drove me a little crazy.  And then there is Julian, hired by Eva to escort her to the company ball, he really seemed more a-hole than alpha male to me.  But then again, with Eva so reserved, and Julian so abruptly inserting himself in her life, it would be hard to show any man not taking advantage of her.  There was definite chemistry between the two as he tried to draw her out of her shell, but it felt a little forced at times.  Still, I couldn’t put it down because, while predictable, I had an absolute need to see how certain situations resolved themselves and of course the ball.  The ball, now that was a crazy unique twist on a company function – no Cinderella/glass slipper story here!  I’m not sure if it helped or hurt my perception of the characters involved – crazy is all I can say.  With this being #1 in the series, clearly the story did not end here.  It wasn’t a dramatic cliffhanger by any stretch, but does open the door for so many questions and journeys.  I’m just not sure what to make of it all.  Strange.

You've gotta love a contemporary romance that's a happy blend of fluffy and substance. The Husband Maker is fun, with some sweet date scenes as well as some angst/drama. Yet it also addresses the more serious side of relationships - both friendships and romances. And I really enjoyed it!The writing is very engaging, and the main characters are great. The inclusion of family made the story both more realistic and more endearing. As for the story itself...I liked following Charlotte's dating journey, learning how she navigates romances and how she deals with difficult circumstances. While this is very much a story about love, it's also a story about identity, and I respect the characters and author for that emphasis.This is the first book in a series, so the ending exists but certainly leaves room for a whole new story (or two) to take place. Perhaps the conclusion isn't as satisfying as some romances, but because of the theme, it fits, and it leaves the reader with some thoughts to ponder/inspire.For a sweet contemporary romance that has a bit of a ordinary-girl-becomes-princess sort of vibe (no princesses, though...sorry!), as well as some depth amid the darling, The Husband Maker is a great start to a new series.*With thanks to I Am A Reader Blog Tours and the author for providing me with an e-copy of the book in exchange for my honest opinion.*
summary: A Happy Blend of Fluffy and Substance

Obsession and Sacrifice, by Tiffany Carmouche, is an intense follow-up to The Imposter. Immediately picking up where book one left, we follow Nicole's journey as she struggles to cope with the events of her past and her confused feelings about the two men in her life. Throughout Nicole's battles, she has the additional concern of fighting for survival in a world where she's not too sure who she can trust.Once again the author, Tiffany Carmouche, takes the reader along a passionate, romance fueled adventure filled with palpable suspense, drama and action. We closely follow the three main characters which successfully allows us to bond and identify with them all. It's impossible not to feel a connection with characters who are so creatively and realistically constructed.Tiffany Carmouche impressively weaves together a narrative complete with heightened tension, compelling the reader to pick up the pace and turn the pages as quickly as possible to be able to keep up with the rollercoaster of action. The reader is left with an element of satisfaction, in addition to yet another cliffhanger that will no doubt leave the reader shouting a little at Tiffany Carmouche's signature ending.Obsession and Sacrifice is a romantic suspense of epic proportions.Disclosure: Obsession and Sacrifice was given to Bex 'n' Books for free in exchange for an HONEST and not necessarily positive review.

If you are looking for a warm and fuzzy read this is not the book for you, if you cannot stomach books about man's inhumane treatment of man this is not the book for you.  But if you like post-apocalyptic stories that do not shy away from the hard decisions the survivors have to face in trying to establish a new world order out of chaos you will find this book intriguing but at times hard to read.After reminded me of The Walking Dead minus the zombies. A pandemic has decimated the population, the hardest hit were the women.  The bookbegins a couple of years after the "dying" and is broken up into 2 parts that  overlap.The first part is about Eva, a lone survivor that is captured by a group of men lead by an ex-military officer. They have established an all male society, their leader has made the decision that to keep order amongst the men and due to the almost extinction of women drastic measures must be taken if they find a woman. Her purpose will be to revive the human race. A lottery would be held to see who would get the privilege to impregnate her. The reader will be shaking their head no as they eagerly turn the pages to see what happens next.The 2nd part occurs 23 yrs after the 1st , our h Nix is part of the resistance forces, she reminded me of  Sara Connor from Terminator 2, a Rambette with a serious attitude and a take no prisoner mind set. She barely remembers a time before the dying when the world consisted of love between men and women, when family units were the norm and women were equal partners in all facets of life. To me her story was the most tragic and believable. Her need to liberate women and her utter hatred of all men was compelling, as a reader you totally understood her and the choices she made.I rate this book a 3 for the theme. On multiple occasion I almost put this book down due to the awkward beginning and the repetitive scenes.  I felt the author did not know if she wanted to show or tell the story.  There were moments when I did not know who was speaking.  Two things drove me batty throughout the entire book, 1. The lack of or bare minimum description of the characters, 2. I wanted to know what chain of events caused the world to change. It is not until well into the story the reader is given small glimpses into the past. The sex scenes although plentiful were demeaning as they were meant to be, but they were also not written very well. After reading a couple I skimmed the rest.  The scenes between Eva, John and Avery felt off to me. I had a problem with Eva's acceptance of her role as earth mother. I preferred Nix and Gareth scenes more, their relationship felt true to the world they lived in. The 2nd half of the book was better executed than the first.  The author successfully captured the effects of abuse the women and men suffered living in a world without love or tenderness.  Mothers would rather kill their babies than let them live in a world were females were hunted like animals and abused beyond belief.  And the males were trained to abuse the women or suffer for not doing so.I liked how the author ended this book with a feeling of better things to come. In spite of my negatives this book was a page turner, and I'm glad I did not put it down without finishing it.

I won't go in to specifics because that was one of the best parts about Rhi.I loved this serial enough that now I want to go back and read the beginning to this series. This serial is a part of Grant's Dark King series, and while it's not imperative to read the backlog before starting this, it would help in getting a feel for some of the characters who already had established relationships and mates. I fully intend to start the rest in the near future. And as with this one, they can be purchased in "parts", or collectively in Dark Heat, which contains all of the previous stories. I also fully intend to continue the series as a whole (after going back, of course), by reading the next novel in the series, Fire Rising. Fire Rising centers around Tristan, the newest King, and we were introduced to him in both parts 3 and 4 of the Darkest Flame.As for this particular serial, it is available in serial form in 4 parts, or collectively in the Darkest Flame novel. If you do decide to read the serial version, they need to be read chronologically to understand the complete story. And beware - each installment (with the exception of 4) ends on a major cliffhanger, so if this is something that bothers you, I would suggest the novel.**Book received on behalf of the publisher via NetGalley in exchange for my honest opinion.

reviewText: There is diet, there is exercise, and then there is 'lifestyle'.  Unfortunately, most commercial diets speak nothing of lifestyle and the few that do commit you to a lifestyle of diet\exercise. Z.R. Moore's book brings lifestyle to the forefront and by doing so, she takes the conventional weight loss plan and turns it upside down. What used to be addressed as merely 'tips' is now a cohesive and coordinated 'technique'.  One that prioritizes simplicity.As a former exercise professional, I will share my experience that most people adhere to their fitness beliefs much in the same way that they adhere to their religious beliefs. That can sometimes mean 'stubbornly and blindly'. After so many decades believing in strict diets and high-intensity exercise, it's time for people to believe that 'simpler is better'.Z.R.Moore's book is an important first step for the diet industry because it emphasizes simplicity and lifestyle. In fact, it's only a first step because there are many more than 22 Effective Ways. Hopefully her book encourages you to seek them.I recommend with 5 stars.
summary: The alternative to strict diets and super high-intensity exercise.  An alternative that is long overdue!

5****StarsAs the Review Chair for our Guild, I am the one who doles out books to my reviewers. When an Andrew Grey book is about to be released I receive many e- mails from the group all saying me, me like the birds in the Nemo movie saying Mine, Mine. Since I read them all for my own enjoyment, I thought today Mine, Mine.Andrew Grey's quiet casual writing style is so wonderful, it takes no time to be immersed in the world he is writing about, whether it be cowboys, or lawyers or Fire fighters and Police officers. The Fire Series is a favorite of mine with two wonderful men Lee and Dirk, (who by the way we get to share a scene with them in this story) It was great spending even the short time with them and seeing they are `good'Justin is a Police Officer, sweet and shy; having no other life than his career.  He has a hard time meeting people, being like the guy in your office that stammers and does not make eye contact when he does speak....awkward. But when on the job and all business Justin is The Man, able, controlled and on top of things.Rock is an EMT in the same town, and when a school bus has been in an accident and is hanging over a highway ready to plunge with all children aboard, Captain America Justin , calms the children, climbs on the bus and gets the kids out safely putting his life in danger as Rock watches him from afar.Justin has no idea why he has such a problem talking to men he is interested in as he and Rock slowly investigate the attraction they feel for the other. This story is a beginning for a young man to find himself and the answers are not always pretty. You hold your breathe to see if Justin is strong enough to follow his heart and not break his and Rock's along the way.The story is sensual, and loving and scary and breathe taking. We still have room for more from these men. This was a story about Justin, and although Rock seems to have it together, I think we need to hear more about him. So please Andrew Grey, what can we learn about Rock to make this relationship even more.I as always look forward to reading your stories....Keep them coming.Review by Gloria LakritzSr Reviewer and Review Chair for the Paranormal Romance Guild Review Team

This really needs to be a 3.5-star book.  Or three for most people and four for the exact target audience.Right.  If you don't like manga, don't read this book.  There are things that will drive you up the wall, absolutely nuts...because they will seem like madness to someone who thinks along the lines of Western books and comic books.Also, if you're an adult reading in adult mode?  This will also drive you up the wall.That being said, if you know manga and are a teen, this is a decent to good read.  Trapped on Draconica throws off the mindset of adulthood and wallows in teenagerness.  Everything teens like to do when thrown into a situation they don't understand is here.  But everything that annoys adults about teenagers is here, too, from the attitude to the goofy decisions that make perfect sense at the time.  It's almost scary.The only thing I really wanted was more polish to the language, to make it easier for my adult brain to read.  It wasn't a problem with grammar or spelling or anything, just the style...it sounded a lot like a teenager, through and through.  I loved the style when it started out, but I spent a lot of time rolling my eyes later on...just as if I were listening to a teenager go on and on...the author was so far into the mindset that I had trouble with it after a while.
summary: 3 stars for adults and 4 for manga-reading teens

I was totally unprepared.  I didn't even have cash and the ATM's were down.  Occasionally I will buy some bottled water but other than moving pictures in my bedroom so I don't sleep under anything heavy that could fall on me in a good shake, I've don't nothing to prepare.  This book was a wake up call.From the type of bag to get, backpack or duffel, to how purify water, this book is a compact guide we all need to preparing for an emergency.  The comprehensive check list is going to be my bible until I gather all the equipment I need in case I am still alive for the big one.  Where I live, you never know when it will happen.  I'm not going to get stuck like last time.

My son and I recently had the chance to read "The Treasure at Devil's Hole" together over the course of a few nights and I have to say that it was a wonderful hilarious adventure for both of us. Jody M. Mabry has a gift for weaving imaginative stories that spark with life and personality while unfolding a plot that is as engaging as it is infinitely creative.The book centers around the lovably endearing boy Francis “Bug” Mosser as he embarks on a strange adventure of epic proportions involving everything from hidden treasure to dastardly villains, all the while trying to impress his crush Melanie Grainger. With a high amount of vivid imagery and a smooth, hilarious tone that sucks you in and doesn't let go until the end, this book has all the makings of a modern classic (and not to rehash what other reviewers have said) just like "Goonies" or "Treasure Island".It's well written with a wonderful amount of character and world-building, setting solid plot foundations early on and building upon them as the story continues. The story is filled with an engaging mix of action, adventure, comedy and drama so that the reader always has something to keep them hooked until the very last page. Overall, it's a very entertaining read that I would wholeheartedly recommend for kids and adults alike.

Wow, this short story packs a ton of secrets, twists and hot sex.  Ruthie has had a rocky past.  Dumped by the man she was suppose to marry, goes to college as a 28 year old and hooks up with her 19 year old boyfriend.  Of course it is Christmas time, the time of the year when she has to travel back home to spend the holidays with her family.  A religious, straight laced, Republican family who she feels looks at her as the screw up in the family.  She can't go without Carter, she would never survive without him that long.So the secret plan begins, no physical contact, no looks, no kisses.......he is going to be there as her nephews best friend and nothing more.  As the story goes on we see how well that plays out.  This is where the cute part of the story begins.  Soon though it takes a turn for the dramatic and then we see the outcome when the truth finally surfaces.  One problem, Carter has already left because he gets sick of being the dirty little secret.In a few pages, the author has given us a complete story, with characters that are developed enough you can emotionally invest in it.  While it is a book of sex, HOT sex, the story of Ruthie and Carter take center stage.  Watching them balance out this lie that they know they can't continue, the protective older sister who figures things out faster than CSI, and parents who appear to hold their social standing very high, we get one heck of a ride.This is a quick, but fun read.  For such serious topics, the author does it without over loading us with angst.  I really enjoyed reading this and highly recommend it to you readers.

Miss Freddie Lambeth has written to her guardian Thomas Lord Stacks, she requests if she can visit him. Her Aunt and Uncle are trying to marry her to a gout ridden man of 70 years old, she is desperate to escape away from them and their odious but beautiful daughter Roxanne. Lord Stacks is quite looking forward to his ward visiting he is more of a recluse since the death of his wife Elizabeth, rumours are rife about her death and his involvement. He is pleased that he will have the company of his departed old friends son Freddie. Only when he goes to meet the coach he is amazed to find that Freddie is a she and not a he.I really enjoyed this story I have not read this author before and was pleasantly surprised. The characters are well developed and the story flows very well. lord Stacks is a good man even though he is the object of gossip locally and in London regarding his marriage. He makes every effort to give Freddie a warm welcome. Freddie is only eighteen but very mature for her age, her father had always blamed her for his wife's death, straight after Freddie was born. Although Lord Stacks is much older than her in his late thirties, it does not prevent Freddie falling in love with him. But Thomas has sworn never to marry again. A very
Good book. Can't wait to read part two because I know there will be one. Worth the money. Drama filled.

I was pleasantly surprised by this book. I originally thought this book would be about Skylar and Sebastian trying to overcome their pasts and their unfortunate connection, and it is, but it¡s so much more than that.Skylar Rose is dealt a crap life from the point her parents are taken from her. It has been more than most people could handle. She not only lost her very loving parents at the age of 16 but also had to deal with even more traumatic events before the story begins and after. Honestly, in most stories, the fact that one person had such a terrible past and kept stumbling into these terrible situations would be too much. I was unsure about it in this one as well, but I realized all of these events are the puzzle pieces that help develop Skylar and Sebastian¡s relationship. Skylar is strong in so many ways, but weak in others which just makes her more relatable.Sebastian Thorne has done nothing but torture himself since that terrible night and the first time he saw Skylar. He is definitely two different people, the good-looking arrogant business man that most people know and the unsure, tortured person who hates himself every day for destroying Skylar¡s life. Because he has these two different sides his behavior gave me whip-lash and infuriated me at times. He could be so frustrating with the way he seemingly toyed with Skylar¡s emotions, although in his two sided mind he seemed to think he was doing the right thing.The connection between Sebastian and Skylar is easy to feel. Mia definitely does an amazing job showing us their feelings throughout the book. The chemistry between the two is also very HOT! The indecision between the two and waiting to find out if they can make it work is a bit tortuous, but it¡s a good kind of torture One of the best parts of this book was the people in it that I did not expect to meet. There is more happening in this book than Skylar and Sebastian. There are more characters that are easy to love or perfect to hate that play a key role in this story. I won¡t give away anymore as I think the surprise of it was what made me like it so much.I also enjoyed the multiple POV¡s. Because there were more of these than I expected, I also thought this would bother me. But I really think it added a little something extra to this book.One of the things that I did not like about this book was all the coincidental meetings between Sebastian and Skylar. I know they had to happen for their relationship to progress, as nothing seemed to be working in their favor except the many coincidental meetings, but for me it just happened a little too often.Overall I enjoyed this book. I loved the emotions and the chemistry. I loved the unexpected things. I actually even like the somewhat cliff-hanger of an ending. It did not kill me and make me want to sling my kindle across the room, but it definitely left me wanting more! It¡s definitely worth the read, and I believe I will like how the story continues in book 2 even better!

reviewText: Perfectly good historic romance. Romantic, sweet but still clean. I would have liked to see some of the characters developed more with a few more mishaps or adventure. Still as it is reads just fine. Still enjoyable.

Yes, there's enough vampires stories and this genre has been done to death. So it's always refreshing when someone can actually breath some life in this done to death genre. Well, this is what the author of Fragile Things does. The author actually uses harsh subject matter that most people can recognize and mixes it with the supernatural to create a compelling horror story. This makes this story amazing. I highly recommend it because I think that you'll enjoy it thoroughly.This book is being billed as the first in a series of Horror stories, but it is so much more than that. These girls could be living in your city right now. There are many children forced to live in circumstances that lead them down a wrong road very early. Jennifer is just such a one, addicted to heroine from an early age she has finally beaten that demon, her boyfriend was her dealer but he has since gotten out and then she meets the vampire Ebony. They become fast friends, they bond on a level that few people ever understand.Ebony, looks to be about 17, but she is much much older, you see, Ebony is a Vampire. She had not been close to anyone, at least anyone who lived to tell about it afterward. There was just something about Jennifer that struck a chord with her. Being around her, caring for her kept the serpents within her at bay -- for a while. What seems to be a promising friendship suddenly spirals out of control. Jennifer unwittingly sets off a reaction that allows her to witness the monster that Ebony really is.Part I ends here and leaves you ready for more. It is a shame that we have to wait but it is sure to be well worth the wait if this first part is any indicator. The story moves fast without leaving you feeling like you are missing important information. Put this one on your must read list today.
