Margaret Addison is quickly becoming one of my favorite writers.  Her mysteries are true mysteries, as she dares the readers to find the clues.  I must admit sadly that I failed once again but it was a lot of fun.  If you like a good mystery I highly recommend this book, but read it carefully or you will suffer my fate.

This is the second book I have read by Sarah O'Rourke and I liked it better than the first in this series.The book picks up almost exactly where the first one left off, only focusing on a different McKinnon sister, Harmony. She is a woman who endured great suffering at the hands of her crazy ex-husband, Tanner, who has resurfaced. Enter Jacob Stone, DEA agent on vacation but working on his own side project. Jake and Harmony are drawn to each other right away but of course, Harmony is weary. Shes been burned before and she also has her daughter, Heaven, to consider. Heaven is an amazing addition to the McKinnon clan. I really enjoyed the relationship that developed between her and Jake; we got to see a softer but still protective side.Just when we think our couple is ready to ride off into the sunset, all hell breaks loose. The sparks fly for these two and everything is going well but Jake has secrets. Harmony finds some "evidence" of Jake's untruthfulness, and she shuts down. Eventually, with the help of the meddling sisters, they reunite after Tanner gets close to Harmony, Heaven and Honor. He actually does more damage to Honor in that attack than anyone else. Shortly thereafter, there is an attack on the Cafe where the sisters work and one is shot. From there, Harmony and Honor are taken and secrets are revealed. The whole ugly truth about everything comes to light. All the strings were tied up in a nice happily ever after bow.The other characters from the first book were also present. The cast of secondary characters in this series really make it so much more believable. There was wise old Aunt Orla, that woman reminds me so much of my grandmother I can't help but smile. I also loved learning more about Patience and Abel and Honor and Zeke. I know that both of their stories are going to be awesome.
A very good tale.  Janet makes happily ever after seem to be the norm.  Makes me want to find an old house to restore and asee what happens.

I enjoyed this for a light Christmas read.  The situation was compelling - love and loss and guilt over being left behind, and the characters were interesting and well-developed.I wish the author would have allowed the living characters and the situation to develop without the plot gimic of the conflicted corporeal spirit.  The story was compelling without Larry's physical presence.  Emma, as a young widow trying to keep going for the sake of her children but not feeling like there was any love left for her in the world, and Jake, keeping his promise to watch over his buddy's family but struggling with his feelings for Emma and his 'betrayal' of Larry's trust, could have carried the story just fine.  Perhaps we could have had a prologue with Jake and Larry that would have given us most of what was needed for that backstory (although I still don't know why Jake didn't share or Emma didn't know that Jake was in Larry's unit...) so that Larry's presence isn't needed to move the story along.
The concept is great and I'm going to purchase this ebook after my review. The beginning is so good that it makes you want to find out what happens between the two lead characters.

The concept behind the short stories Stir Sticks & Stilettos was a great idea.  I have read all the books in the series and have not been disappointed.These books are a quick read, with not only hot sex scenes but a story line.In this story we are introduced to Kamarj and Travis. Travis is Kamarj brother best friend.  They have known each other for ages.  Every time the two meet it like fire and water. Little did either know Kamarj brother wedding would change everything.  The way they finally end up together is not traditional but a result of wrong hotel key and bed.

This story is adorable. It's so much fun to read aloud. It has everything I enjoy in a children's book: great storyline and lesson to learn, cute illustrations, easy to add drama as you read it to the little ones and...kittens!

Wow, Lila really had some deep problems that she concealed under her fake smile & beautiful clothes! I was floored by Lila's past & really felt terrible for her, especially knowing that her mother tried to help her out & instead sent her down a path of addiction. Ethan and Lila have an amazing friendship & Ethan bails Lila out when she tries to escape through casual sex & alcohol but he has no idea of the deep extent of her problems. She doesn't have the financial support of her family anymore & tries to hide that as well. I always figured Ethan was laid back & casual & drank, had sex, did drugs on his own terms. But this book made me fall completely in love with him! He has a past that prevents him from moving on with Lila but he really wants her in every way. He is strong & supportive & seriously tries to help her break through her addiction and figure out where to go next in life in a more positive direction. In the end these two are wonderful together and find a way through their problems. Love them!

Caitlin Cooney's life has changed dramatically. Gabe Alexander has opened her eyes to a completely different world the night that they spent together at the beginning of the summer. Making her his accomplice in his quest to right wrongs in their South Carolina town, and drawing her into the explosive chemistry between them, he has awakened her and left her dissatisfied with the life that she has been living up to this point.'This Wicked Rush' picks up just a couple of weeks after Caitlin's and Gabe's adventure in 'One Wild Night.' Caitlin just wants to get back to her normal life, working and taking care of her family. She is determined that there not be a repeat of what happened between them, but finds herself more and more deeply drawn to Gabe. And when Gabe sweetens the deal, making it impossible for her to say no to him, she agrees to be with him just for the summer.Gabe knows just how to get Caitlin to agree to spend time with him, but is hiding a big secret from her. He didn't count on coming to care for her as deeply as he does, and, as the summer progresses, he faces some hard choices where she is concerned.Jessie Evans is great at character development. Caitlin is sassy and independent, having had to handle some very tough things in her young life, and Gabe is just delicious. He is smart and hot, and goes from simply wanting Caitlin to wanting to give her everything. The chemistry between Caitlin and Gabe is super-hot; they start out being very attracted to each other, but the attraction quickly deepens to much more as the story progresses. 'This Wicked Rush' made me think of a sort of take on 'Robin Hood,' with a whole lot of hot and sexy scenes. The story does end on a cliff-hanger, but not in an abrupt way. Jessie has done a good job of bringing everything together and setting us up for the continuation of Caitlin's and Gabe's journey in the next book, and I can't wait to see where they go.
summary: A Great New Series From Jessie Evans

reviewText: This story is a well detailed disaster novel.  Each character can easily be distinguished from the others.  The plots moves along smoothly with a few scenes for background information.The only complaint I have is the repeated use of the word "span" instead of "spun."  Span is the distance between objects where as spun means to spin and object.  From the sentences in the novel it was obvious the author intended "spun" but used "span."  Other words had similar problems such as of vs off.Other than that the book is excellent and enjoyable reading even though it is a bit depressing.

This was one of the last stories I've read from le Veque (I only have 4 or 5 more books to go from her arsenal) because, like "The Dark Knight," I felt the premise was not really to my taste.  However, just as in The Dark Knight, I found myself pleasantly surprised and this too has become one of my favorites from this author.  If you've read any of my reviews before, I adore the De Russe men.  I was pleased to discover that Lady de Moyen come from the de Russe line, but hated that she had to endure so much abuse.  I loved how Gart "Gabriel" arrived like the conquering hero...the most loving of men as a lover and father.  To me, he is the epitome of the strong, silent type with a pure depth of character.  I really liked this book and found myself with teary eyes on many occasiosn throughout the book.  I was like, Lord, am I about to cry again?!  LOL, enjoy this one, it's good.  My only gripe would be with Kevin de Lara's father - as an old war monger with 800 men at his disposal, how he allowed his castle to be breached and certain persons taken away is beyond me.  He was a sweet old man though (I also like the de Lara men).  I'm off to "The Lord of Shadows!"

Brad Ashton returns from a Viet Cong prison camp and finds himself on the run from a false murder charge that he murdered his wife. Like John Tipton in the film, The Marine, Ashton is a taciturn Man of Action for whom expressing feelings is difficult.Ashton hardly works up a sweat when he busts up three thugs with his bare hands, killing one.The book is free of errors in grammar and spelling. If there were any at all, I don't remember them. The writing is journeyman, which I do not mean as an insult. It does what it is supposed to do; it carries the reader forward without giving away the plot. If you are looking for memorable phrases or witty dialogue, you will not find it here.The story is plot-driven with lots of action. The supporting characters can be summed up with a word or phrase:Josie Bostworth -- The love interest. "What a dame."Amanda Pothmore -- Wealthy bail bonds agent, stand-in mother for Brad when he was growing up. "Savvy and motherly."Sgt. Hank Walters of LAPD -- Brad's comrade-in-arms. "Screw the rules; he's my brother. Oooh-rah!"Lt. Randolph Stratford -- Snake in the grass.Jeffrey Walden -- high-priced attorney. "Old smoothie."Willard Tuckman -- Brad's wife's uncle. "Oily businessman."The late Amanda Ashton -- sexually insatiable, cruel, predatory. "What a bitch."As you can see, Central Casting would know exactly who to send for the supporting roles.The plot device I disliked were scenes foreshadowing the murderer. The use of a specific trait to define him was overdone. Moreover, I think the plot would have been even tighter without this.I read this book to the end, so I could see how things turned out. At times, I was a little bored and wished I could read even faster than I do.
summary: Effectively Plotted with Many Shallow Characters

reviewText: Short but informative. Gives a great overview on the history and duties of a Pope. it was a free download. I recommend it if its free but I wouldn't pay money for it.

So far so good. Of course I would not have expected anything less from Ana Fawkes. After reading all her books this one is just another example of her exemplary writing skills. Alex Slader is a very lost, unhappy person. He is living the life of a Rockstar but you can feel he is missing something. Jessica Harpmae seems just as lost. One night changes everything for them both. But there is an evil plot brewing in the form of Jessica's roommate. So what happens next? Good question but i will be reading to find out. This is a fabulous start to the series. I recommend reading for yourself!

So I read Cross My Heart sometime ago and didn't know there was another book in Parker's POV. Let me start out by saying fiancée really? That is so sleazy even though nothing happened until he broke off the engagement. I think I liked the book from Jaden's POV better. I had more respect for Parker's character when I was in the dark about his dealings. I also didn't like the fact that Jaden was never told about the fiancée...and the proposal at the end was basically what happened with Callie...I mean come on.This book should have been integrated with cross my heart and just had a few chapters in Parker's POV.

I waited to write my review for this until after I read Laying a Foundation.  For me this is not really a prequel but is a great book that you can read to get to know a little more about the characters in the series.  I think it would depend on the person and how good they remember things on whether or not I would recommend this be read before or after Laying a Foundation.  For me I was glad I read it before Laying a Foundation.  If I had not read it first I would have been somewhat confused by some of the characters.  I am glad the author decided to write this because while some of these characters are just background characters in Laying a foundation I think it is important that the reader knows a little bit about them!
summary: Great way to get to know the character in the series!

reviewText: I enjoyed this book.The main character is a woman who discovered that she had special abilities as a child.  She uses this ability to help the police.

OverallFans of Spice 'n' Solace will probably love this story, but I had similar issues with this one as I did with the first, which is odd, since I love Burn's Cop Out. An enjoyable story with an interesting world, steamy sex, and a unique alien specie, but nothing that really jumped out and impressed me. I wanted to enjoy this story more than I did, and though I felt disappointed in some elements, overall it was a pleasant read.ReviewThe writing wasn't bad, but it didn't thrill me. It felt clunky, and while it didn't detract from the storytelling, it didn't really enhance it either. It could be personal preference, but it didn't do it for me.I liked the challenges that get raised for the lead males, but the solutions felt too easy, much like Spice 'n' Solace. Misunderstandings and a simple conversation clear up problems that needed more attention. Maybe I just like my characters to struggle. A lot.I love different takes on alien sex, and this series already caught my attention with the triads, but the anatomy differences were especially appreciated. They are cute and almost funny out of context (...though most sexual anatomy things are...), but in scene they are pretty darn sexy! Also, from the descriptions, I think I want to rub up on R'kos. He sounds divine.There was a good balance of science fiction and romance, and while romance/erotica is obviously the driving force, the science doesn't get ignored, although hard-core sci-fi fans would probably find it lacking. There is brief exploration of other planets and cultures, which was there to help explore parts of the characters that we may not have seen otherwise. I enjoyed those elements of it.

This set was equally as enjoyable as volumes 1-4. It was fast paced and enjoyable, a very quick read. The stories continue the adventures of Snow White.The twists and turns continued and left me guessing  until the end. In these volumes, Snow White falls into a deep sleep. She didn't just fall asleep, but she had a very exciting adventure while her loved ones worried about her for two years.I was happy with the one who's kiss awoke her. It wasn't the expected guy, but definitely a good choice. We were left with another surprising end and I look forward to reading the next set!

I have a business appointment on Monday and I found some valuable tips to help me with questions to ask. Seriously! We all need to network, and one thing I love about this book is that not only does it emphasize the importance of networking your way to success, it gives you simple,practical tips on how to do it! It can work for anyone, from the experienced business owner, to the college student. I love how the author talks about the mindset, and ways to snap out of it! I needed that reminder! An easy read, I recommend!
This is a must read, I have not had à book this great in a long time. I loved all the characters. I can't wait to read the part 2

If you are accustomed to Kattie McKinsey's novels, you know the author loves to mix genres and create unique and engaging stories. This one is no exception, involving fantasy and sci-fi in an epic and enticing reading. The characters contribute to the personalization in an extremely imaginative way  and it's impossible not to relate to the protagonist as you go along with his adventures. This story is a symbol about how great powers, can imply responsibilities  that if faced with courage can lead to a fulfilling and exciting life. I love to keep my mind between the clouds  and reading this novel is a great way of doing that! Looking forward to the second book if the series!

If you enjoy science fiction / fantasy, and are looking for something to read during your lunch break at work, I'd recommend this one.  Considering short stories don't leave you much time or room to lay down a plot and get you involved with the characters, I thought the author did a good job of quickly getting the reader up to speed and you felt like you were a part of the story vs. someone reading along.I originally picked this up for free during a Kindle promotion, and as I type this review I see it has reverted back to 99 cents: science fiction fans will certainly receive more than that in entertainment value.
I didn't care for the book, read it to the end.  The story could of been good if it had went in a few other directions.

This book kept me up at night reading it.  The characters struggle to reconcile their religious beliefs with their quest for answers, and the twists and turns are very reminiscent of the DaVinci Code.  Action packed, fun read.

reviewText: Star Rating: 4 STARSHeat Rating:  Simmering!I have been a Molly Harper fan since the Jane Jameson series (a fun and witty paranormal series that started with Nice Girls Don't Have Fangs) and I had "thought" I had read her entire back list until I was asked to review Rhythm and Bluegrass.  Turns out I missed a book, Bluegrass Baby, which is the first book in this series.  No worries!  You can read Rhythm and Bluegrass as a standalone (I did) and be completely fine.  I plan to go back and read it because Molly Harper is so much fun to read!Rhythm and Bluegrass was a quick, fun, witty, snarky and sweet book that actually taught me a lot about historic preservation (but in a fun-you-don't-realize-you-are-learning-way).  Molly Harper has such a sharp wit and it is reflected in her characters, she is able to create a cast with unique personalities and have them work in wonderful harmony.  This book is a fast paced, you can't put it down kind of book!  The story never hits a lull, the plot is interesting and gives you many interesting connections that ties the whole thing together.Bonnie and Will have great chemistry and it is very entertaining to watch them spark and interact with one another.  I really liked getting to see these two circle around each other and try and resist their chemistry even when they weren't on the same side.  Mud Creek came to life in Rhythm and Bluegrass and makes you feel part of the town (or makes you want to visit).  You get to know lots of secondary characters that really enhance the story and make you root for the town and for McBride's.Molly Harper is a go-to Author for me when I want a fun, flirty story with characters that have spunk and personality!  If you are a fan of small towns and quirky characters then Rhythm and Bluegrass is a definite 1-click!  I recommend any Molly Harper book and this is one is no exception.
summary: Molly Harper is a go-to Author for me when I want a fun, flirty story with characters that have spunk and personality!

reviewText: 3-3.5 starsThis was a good story and I liked the MCs, Kylie, Brad, Hemi and Finn. Their story is rather hard for me to rate as it's very short and contains mostly sex. The story isn't bad for what it is but doesn't give a good expectation for the rest of the books in the series (and the other books I've read are better...they still have sex prominent in the story but also have a bit more plot added in).Basically, Kylie is the manager of the resort and is getting it prepared for it's grand opening in a few weeks. While she's been getting the resort up and running, Kylie became involved with 3 very different men working at the resort (not under her direct supervision). She's been dating them for a few months and discovered that she has developed strong feeling for all 3 men. Kylie is convinced that she has to choose between the men and is stressing about it. The story takes place over the space of a day and basically revolves around the men each having individual moments with her and then coming together at the end of the night to take her all together in an effort to convince her they all want her and will happily share her. This works and the story ends with a 4-way HEA. :DOverall this was an enjoyable story but not a major amount of substance outside of the sex. Still it was a nice, hot little story and wasn't a bad way to spend an hour or so. :D

I got this book because I've always been really interested in writing my own book, but never really understood how or what to do after the book was written.  I struggled with understanding the technicalities, and because of this I kind of just categorized them as something that "I'll understand later," or "I'll pay someone else to figure this out when I can" or whatever.  These technicalities scared me into never finishing it, because I connected finishing the book to those categories that I didn't want to deal with.  But after reading this book (as well as a lot of other books on this subject) I got a better description of these things I was so afraid of, and the explanations made it all seem easier!  Now that I know the workings of what comes after the book is done, I wasn't so freaked out anymore!Not only does this book help the reader (aspiring author) to work out what they need to do or have happen after the book is done (like publishing, prices, who to give them out to, maybe touring, working with other authors, etc.) but it also gives good tips on the writing part.  All this encouragement is so helpful, and it really pushed me forward in my writing.  Thanks so much!
summary: MUST READ for serious aspiring writers

I didn't find it any more "gross" than other sex scenes I've read even with the archaic 'seed' terminology used by cowboy Matthew. He had a very primitive way of speaking about what he considered sex to be. I would assume from country and ranch living, so I just chalked it up to it. Different strokes.

This one surprised me as the tapestry of Sherman's cruel work is further revealed.  It had all the components of a Barton book... The strong magic woman/warrior and their vampire mate work out their power dynamic to find their way to each other.  Yet, it was the storyline and the character of Zane herself that was incredibly compelling.  I felt just like the Pixie she saves at the end of the book that doesn't want to leave her side because there was just so much more to discover. This character could have a spin-off series herself as she starts to create an identity in connection to herself and others much like J.D. Robb (aka Nora Roberts) does with the incredible compelling character of Eve Dallas.  A product of very cruel and inhumane labs established by Sherman, Zane's abilities as an immortal are limitless but it is her spirit that ultimately survives the horrors of this environment and soars.  This book establishes the beginning of Zane's journey but I couldn't help but want to go on the ride with her.
summary: best book in the series!.... so far

Acid reflux is easier to beat when you know what foods to avoid. And as someone with limited insurance, it was interesting to see the natural ways of relieving this common problem. There was also a lot of causes I wasn't aware of. If you suffer from Acid Reflux, this book will help you!

Full of such premise and inspired concepts, Forbidden Bond is a paranormal romance with a difference...something that stands-out within a very popular genre. As a fan of Rachel Vincent, Charlaine Harris and other authors of paranormal fiction I was really excited upon encountering a new Shapeshifter story (Wolves). The character-driven narrative is entertaining and interesting, keeping you glued to the pages and lost within the dazzling romance and thrilling action. Olivia and Eion's relationship was so cute and they melted my heart! Containing sizzling, seductive erotic scenes this book was literally smouldering in places. I would recommend it to all who enjoy reading this genre, as something refreshingly new and remarkable.Forbidden Bond {Short synopsis} ~Some bonds run soul deep...Eion is a wolf shifter and rising alpha, sent to high school to learn about Humans where he met and bonded with Olivia. Pack Law dictates that no human and wolf shifter can mate and so Eion is left with no choice but to abandon Olivia and leave. These forbidden star-crossed lovers still yearn for one another, despite their separation and Olivia moving forward in her life with a new guy.But forgetting a childhood crush is not that easy...Jessica Lee's novel is an exquisite mix of magical fantasy and otherworldly vision, fused together within a heated and intensely passionate characterization. I connected to the characters in such a profoundly personal way that I read the entire book in a single sitting; desperate to finish the entire story with excited anticipation! I would like to thank the author so much for providing me with an e-copy of Forbidden Bond to read and give an honest review on, as it was an impressive novel of such scope.I simply LOVED this amazing book with it's fantastic characters {both main and lesser ones}, and in-depth details regarding the Wolf Pack. I am a new No. 1 fan of Jessica Lee and I cannot wait to add more of her books to my wish list in a hurry.5 STARS!!!
summary: A phenomenal paranormal romance that's heartrending and wonderfully original!

I really liked the story of a man who falls in love with a mother and son who help him in many ways. While trying to escape his past, Joseph meets the widow Ellie Simms and her son Matthew. Ellie is trying to raise her son with love and devotion, but something is missing. She sees a man at the general store in her hometown being very nice to Matthew. The five year old can't understand why his mom won't buy him candy. Joseph spies the cute kid and treats him to a bag of sweets. Ellie looks at the  handsome cowboy and thanks him for being so nice to her son. Joseph is instantly smitten by the beautiful woman and wants to kiss her. But being a gentleman, he offers to escort them to the widow's homestead. Ellie and Matthew are totally taken aback by Joseph's caring manner. She is thinking thoughts no woman should think and Matthew sees someone who pays attention to him. Love is the key to an honest relationship, while trying to overcome obstacles along the way.  You will love this cute story of everlasting affection and love.

The latest book about the rollicking, rowdy Ridgeville residents ROCKS! Maya and the menagerie of mates are giving bad ass lessons again and helping the emotionally ravaged Honor to recover from her experiences with the London pride.Honor had gone to England to earn a prestigious university degree, but was so traumatized she fled home to hide from everyone. Maya, the ever wisecracking Prima, provides her own special brand of advice and laughter among her supportive activities. Meanwhile Grayson, who's been waiting years for Honor to grow up and experience her first Heat so he can claim his mate, insists on patiently and gently helping in the healing process.But the evil of London follows Honor back to the U.S. Soon the International Council is involved in the investigation of several London pride irregularities. Everyone wants the lions brought to shifter justice, but Grayson just wants Honor safe from future threats.Celia Kyle's Ridgeville series is awesome, and I'm clamoring for more!

reviewText: I don't normally read vampire/paranormal romance novels, but sometimes we need to step out of our comfort zone. I'm so glad I was able to read this book. I loved it!! It has a vampire sister (Delilah) & brother (Morgan Ward) & a human (Angelina).  Angelina has been working as a Private Assistant for Delilah for almost 5 years now. Angelina has never met Morgan, only spoken to him on the phone when he calls to talk to his sister. On the eve of his 40th birthday bash, which he is hosting, Delilah brings Angelina with her to the most talked about event in New York City. It's a "who's who" list of attendees. There's some mind control & did that really happen or was it my imagination? This story flowed very nicely & I would love to have more of Morgan Ward & Angelina. Please tell me there will be more. Definitely a hot, steamy quick read. I will be reading more books written by this author because I enjoyed this book so much.I was offered this ARC to read & give my honest review.

What an emotional read with a great story. I read this in a day and could not put it down. I had to leave for a bit and the whole time my mind was on the story. I love this author and can't wait to see what she will write next. I felt every emotion that the characters were experiencing and that takes a gift. Well done.

The first thing that struck me about this book was the colourful and detailed world. The author really painted a vivid picture in my head. The writing style is solid, consistent and realistic, with well worded descriptions of the surroundings and well thought-out dialogue which fits with the rest of the narrative. This all helps to keep the reader involved and maintains the often gripping atmosphere.The thing I liked about this story is that the plot constantly throws up little questions in my head. By that I don't mean annoying plot inconsistencies, I mean intriguing descriptions and nuggets of information which aroused my curiosity and made me want to read more. I found this an exciting read and I would love to read more of this story as I feel like this was just the beginning.Stealing Time comes highly recommended and, as a writer, C K Garner promises to be excellent.

reviewText: This was a captivating story. It was truly hard to put down. I enjoyed learning how mankind had been revered back to living without technology. I felt so much compassion for the heroine. To be sold to pay her husband's debt. Loved the ending. Very satisfying.

Emory Maxwell and Shelby Moon have been inseparable since second grade and childhood sweethearts ever since. Emory joined the Army and Shelby stayed behind in the rural town of Sweetness, Georgia to work in her father's grocery store.Emory is back home on leave for five days and intends to propose to Shelby despite the tensions in their relationship regarding her loyalty towards her father to stay in the town that offers no prospects for the future. But they've been together for so long; she won't say no, will she?Charming albeit corny novella. It wasn't long enough for me to care about the h/h. Emory loves Shelby so much that he's easily frustrated with her unwillingness to choose him over her father, even though she wants to. She doesn't want to hurt either man and wants to remain unconfrontational. Not realistic in my opinion. It takes an F5 tornado to make everyone realize their mistakes.Seeing as this was a prequel to the Southern Roads trilogy, I didn't expect this to be lengthy, but for me it fell short of making me itch to read said trilogy and see the Armstrong brothers (Porter Armstrong is Emory's Army buddy and best friend) rebuild the destroyed town of Sweetness. I may still do it one day.
summary: Charming albeit corny prequel to Southern Roads trilogy

reviewText: After a recent check-up, it became clear to me that I really need to improve the way I eat.  Not really looking forward to the transition, I downloaded this book and was pleasantly surprised after trying out a few recipes.  This book does contain several recipes for smoothies and vitamin drinks, but here's what I love.  It also has recipes for great comfort dishes like chicken pot pie and enchiladas - just cooked in a healthier fashion.  I love this.  I need to eat healthier.  It's a must.  I'm just not willing to give up the enjoyment of eating while doing so.  This book solves that problem by letting me eat healthy and still have great tasting meals.  The recipes are easy to follow, too.  Love it!

Northern Light is a very short but good story about love lost, second chances, and ghosts. It follows art investigator, Luke, on his latest assignment. A forgery of a long since dead artist has made an appearance in a gallery, and Luke has been hired to find out where it came from. An art forgery isn't so unusual, except that no one has ever seen this painting in real life, only read descriptions. So who recreated it? His search leads Luke right to the doorstep of  his ex-lover and painter, Stefan. Stefan doesn't exactly deny the accusations that he's forging art, because he can't exactly remember anything he paints. What follows is a slightly creepy ghost story with some romance thrown in as Luke and Stefan try to figure out what on Earth is going on.I quite enjoyed Northern Light. I had never read about art investigators or forgers before, so I liked learning more about this field. I also really liked the characters. Luke and Stefan are both damaged men after losing each other, then their following lovers due to unexpected tragedies. The mystery was also interesting, even if it was predictable. It had just enough of a creepy vibe to be slightly dark, but without being scary. I always enjoy a good paranormal twist, and this story definitely has that, even if ghosts don't tend to be my thing. I just wish there had been more romance! I need more M/M romance in my life, so that one scene between Luke and Stefan wasn't enough! As it is though, I liked the story and I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a quick mystery to pass an hour.*Disclaimer: I received this book from the publisher through NetGalley for review. No compensation was offered or accepted.

Shakespeare once complained:  "As flies to wanton boys are we to the Gods.  They kill us for their sport."Certainly true in this most gigantic of monster romps---where the monsters are world destroying gods, each devastating and horrific in their own way.  Usually in this sort of story mankind bonds together to fight the common threat and often emerges victorious a la Well's War of the Worlds.  However this modern and more cynical version shows mankind's nature in siding with the strong against the weak, perhaps reflecting our current divisive political/social environment, or not.  Good horror and sci-fi novels and movies often provide social and political commentary commentary.  Whether the subtext is there or not, I found this novella on its surface to be a compelling horror apocalyptic tale with a chilling ending that I did not expect.  And it is perhaps more.

reviewText: I truly enjoyed this story. I wished it was longer, but feel that it spoke to the heart of true romantics such as myself.

Ryan's inner bear is driving him crazy but he's determined to give his mate time to accept him and not force a mating.  Glory is afraid to let the scrumptious Ryan close - she's been abandoned by everyone and has major issues. But when the danger again comes haunting the women of the Synful tattoo parlor, all bets are off and Ryan will do whatever it takes to keep his mate safe and happy.I liked Bell's Halle Shifters even though the smexy parts are definitely in the erotic category language-wise, these light PNR had enough of a story in between (so I guess that makes them Romantica)that they still work for me. I really loved Ryan, he is a super sweetie in this story, even though it's taking its toll on him, for him it is all about Glory - I don't know how she resists him for so long. Since this is the third book in this series, there are plenty of cameos of the previous pairs as well as almost everyone from Bell's other related series - if they don't get screen time, their name is at least 'dropped' at some point. And Bell is still going strong - she sets up at least two more pairs, moves things along for the next up pair, and adds some new characters to the world as well.If you are new to the series, Bell does a good enough job of recapping things that have come before, so as long as the mention of a zillion and one characters doesn't bug you, you should be able to start here.If you are a fan and missed this little short, Bear With Me, on Bell's website was cute(it's Christmas with Bunny's parents - Bunny's dad tells the story of how he claimed his mate. Thanks to Kaleigha of the awesome Wicked Scribes blog for putting this on my radar.)
summary: A honey of a bear, finally gets his 'Glory'ous HEA

reviewText: Following on from Grey's Hidden Fire is this book. We now see Mica and Grey living together with full acceptance from the fire crews and Mica's family. Grey is meeting them for the first time at Christmas. This is a tough time for him because he lost his parent just before Christmas. They had traditions and made a huge deal out of Christmas and now Grey devotes himself to helping others and covering shifts for other firemen. But not this year, Mica has pushed Grey into going to home and meeting his family. We see quite a lot of another young fireman named Simon who will be one of the main characters in the next Firehouse Six book.This is a nicely written and paced story which is entertaining, descriptive and shows that love can bring you everything you ever wanted...and be wearing a fireman's uniform. I liked Grey's Hidden Fire and Fused by Fire, the next in the series.
summary: Two firemen, Christmas and real love - what more could you ask for?

reviewText: I was looking for something lite to read with a Christmas theme.  The characters were likable and I was interested in them right from the beginning, though I thought the story ended abruptly.  This was a cute short story.

This book reminded me of Elizabeth Reyes bookNoah (5th Street #1)as it also is about a younger man/older woman romance.  I am not a huge fan of younger boys with older woman, but I guess 6 years in this instance is not all that much.  Gianni already acts so young, that it is hard to imagine an older woman finding his juvenile behavior endearing.  I get that his body would be alluring, but how long before the girl became too insecure about her own?Gianni is the baby of the Santini brothers and a PJ in the air force.  He is home from Afghanistan on medical leave as his helicopter landed hard and he got a concussion.  Before he left on deployment, he briefly met Kianna (who I guess is black?), an older woman who was a teacher at the university and couldn't stop thinking about her. "You are ashamed of your younger... white....lover." When he gets back, they hook up and all is great until the misunderstanding, then the reconciliation.  Like I have said in the previous reviews, these all have the same formula and can be read individually.Again, I read this whole series in one day as the stories are short and pretty similar (even the sex scenes, although there were more in this one).  I do like Melissa Schroeder's writing style and enjoyed these stories since I got them for such a low price.Would I/Did I buy it? Yes (.99)Would I read it again?  NoWould I recommend it to friends? Yes at .99 or free

First the positive:  "In 666 Words" is a collection of lightening-fast horror stories; each 666 words long.  Individual stories can be read in a matter of minutes and are not limited to any specific horror sub-genre.  Most of the stories are pretty good (there are a couple of duds).The Negative:  I gave this book four stars for one reason only -- the limitation of the format.  I recognize that what the author attempted to do here was difficult.  However, I feel that the format was too limiting.  The stories weren't that great simply because there was not enough "room" to develop anything.  Also, after a while the stories begin to get a little formulaic with a plot twist in every story.  There were so many plot twist that they eventually became expected rather than unexpected.I received this collection of stories for free from Amazon.

Wow, where do I even begin? I've read both Amy Lane and Aleksandr Voinov before and let me just say that the idea of them pairing up to co-write a book never came into my head as even the remotest of possibilities. But they came together here, and let me just say, it was awesome! The moment I finished this book, I wanted to go back to the beginning and read it over. Stock trader Malcolm and Owen, a recent college graduate vacationing in London, are the unlikeliest of pairings. They meet in a dive pub and their chemistry is instantaneous and fierce. From the moment they leave the pub until the end of the book, they are almost constantly together. I loved their banter. I loved the fact that there was so much more to Malcolm than his slick, cocky businessman exterior and that Owen might have been a country mouse, but had a spine of steel all the same.Such a great book. Highly recommended!

"A New Dawn Rising" by Michael Joseph is a well written crime thriller/mystery. It kept my interest from the blurb on. It was not only a riveting mystery, it was humorous in parts, revealed an interesting character with more human traits than your average cop or ex-cop. The man learned the necessary things about himself for his new beginning. It would be interesting to see how he does as he moves on. I hope the author has more plans for him.

Twin Curse by Rinelle GreyTwin girls are born together and wed together and it has been the law and will always be so.  Yet Brianna does not love the man her sister loves.  She has no choice but to run and in running she finds a love she knows she cannot have.  Twins however have a way to communicate and when you add the fact that they are magi and hold an ancient magic they know when trouble threatens. Brianna must return to save her sister and flees again this time from the one she loves.The ancient law is not to be broken. Yet will the one that loves Brianna seek her out, and in finding her find out that the law is really a beginning of an ancient curse.  Curses can be broken but how will they all find the magic to break it.  If two bring more strength to the one will not four together bring even more strength .  What secrets do Brainna and her lover find in the tombs of her village, and what can they do to change the curse…. This is a book you have to read.  This story is full of twists, turns, magic, trolls, and Magi. …Read Twin Curse to find out if the power of love can prevail and undo a curse that has held so many for so long or are the lovers domed as the first twins were at the beginning of the law.…Bella Doerres12/26/2013

I like to make a lot of gifts for Christmas presents so I was on the lookout for some new things to make this year. I was excited to find this book on how to make my own caramel at home. The recipes included in this cookbook show you how simple it is to make and how to include the caramel sauce in many different recipes. This cookbook has given me so many new possibilities on how to share sweet treats with my family and friends this holiday season.Dulce De Leche is a fancy name for a caramel-like sauce you can make at home. While it takes some attention to detail and patience because of time, once you've made it, you can use it in many different recipes.And Monica is right--it is so much better than store bought caramel sauce!

I was excited to read this.  I love the mystery and the history that surrounds this event.  What really happened 75 years ago to Amelia Earhart.  Eric Wilson gives his take on this historical event and does a great job.  This is Eric's first novella and I cant wait for more.  He does a great job recreating what lead upto the event and then what happened to cause it.  He starts off with right before the event takes place, then goes a few years into the future, then to the present day and then right back to Amelias last days.  He does a great job bringing the characters to life and adding his own twist and thoughts into the mystery.  I have always loved how Eric adds some historical events to his books.  I know this is a short read(novella) but it is well worth the read.  Eric always does a great job researching for his books and this is no exception.  I love the fact that he also included a little about the Navajo code talkers from World War II.  Is this the true story of what happened?  It is a possibility but we may never really know what happened 75 years ago.
summary: What Really Happened to Amelia Earhart?

A very selfish and greedy dragon, Ethel the Red (love that!), lives in a small cave where she keeps all her treasured possessions. Ethel is a great hoarder and lives amongst a mountain of goodies purloined from others. She also has a real problem sharing anything with anyone. Terrified of someone else benefitting from her belongings, which are now spilling from her cave, she decides to move the whole caboodle to a larger and safer place.Her new choice of residence is a beautiful oasis furnished with nothing more than a small picket fence with a sign saying "The Giving Tree - Please Do Not Cross" So determined is the wilful Ethel to do whatever she wants to do, and never what anyone else asks her to do or not do, she decides this is just the spot for her. "It shall be mine, mine, mine!" she selfishly cries.Having made her decision she flies back to her cave to collect her goodies. Dumping them on the lush green grass, with no regard whatsoever for the poor little sapling beneath them, Ethel then goes about her usual business of grabbing and snatching anything she has taken a fancy to; this time it is a small child's teddy bear. Ethel flies back with her booty to her mountain of plunder only to find a storm has scattered all her possessions so far they can no longer be seen. The only thing she can see is the grateful, but withered, sapling. Then after spending a year in a huge sulk, dragons are apparently prone to long sulks, life begins to take on a whole new meaning as the sapling, having been left free to grow, has turned into a beautiful and bountiful tree. Thus begins Ethel's conversion.I like this book, a lot.  It is well-written and fun.  I enjoyed the descriptions and phrases used. The illustrations are colourful and endearing and the message is delivered in a simple and easy to understand way. David Lee Martin does a great job here with this by showing children just how important it is to both give and share, and to forgive and be nice to others. He takes the most self-centred creature of its kind and transforms it into a loving, giving animal, thus showing how even the toughest hearts can be won over.In all; an inspiring and hugely readable book illustrating some true values.Also published at mungaiandthegoaconstrictor.me

Joseph is down on his luck and running a little dive bar in London. When he feels he can't go on, he decides to hang himself. As he is making preparations, a guy, Joshua, walks into the bar and asks if he needs some help. From there they start talking and Joshua offers Joseph a job. Realizing there is nothing left for Joseph, he agrees.Joseph is then taking to another planet and taught about the history and inhabitants of the planet. This is one of the dead planets that Nua'Lath has killed with his horde. There were some survivors that have slowly rebuilt. Joseph is now part of the Resistance, a group of people that are trying to stop Nua'Lath. Joseph is supposed to find the last stand of the former inhabitants and to find out what happened.Joseph is then left to his task. He starts walking down an abandoned road and finds Bailey. Bailey is a scavenger that recycles everything that is found in the abandoned lands. He then sells that to the few communities. Together they look for the final stand of the people of this planet.I really liked this story. There was great imagery and imagination. This was a quick read but I couldn't put it down. I can't wait for other books in this series. I really want to find out what happens next.I received this book for free from the Library Thing Early Reviewer program.

Dirty Trick - 3.5 Stars.This is Book one on the perfectly Matched Series.I have to say that I don't think I have ever read a bad Entangled: Brazen book. Not having much luck in the love arena herself, she has spent most of her time lusting after her best friend Trick Matthews, a Hot, sexy SWAT officer.Trick is the opposite of Grace, he has plenty of experience in the bedroom and is not afraid to show his skills, unfortunately he is also madly in love with his best friend (Grace) and so the fun begins!Christine has given us great friends to lovers tale, which I have to say are one of my favorite genres, and a particularly memorable Halloween party to boot. The sex is imaginative and well written and the characters likeable. I wanted them to get their happily ever after, and I have to say I laughed my socks off in places.ARC provided by Entangled, in exchange for the above honest review.

One final note---I love the ocean and hurricanes fascinate me in some weird way.  The description of this book made it sound as if the hurricane was a big part of the storyline.  This couldn't be further from the truth.

Lou Harper had been heavily recommended to me by many friends I trust, and when I read the blurb I was interested immediately because something told me this story would probably make me laugh. I was right. Since I'm also a giant pet lover with three dogs and two cats of my own, a pet psychic set off the goodwill radar. And, the down on his luck, life has beaten him down guy paired with young, bubbly, and sweet did me in the rest of the way. This book is, in fact, two short stories combined so I felt that I was getting two for the price of one.I fell in love with Leander (Andy) about two seconds into this read. Anyone who says, very offhand, that they don't have any friends, and they seem completely okay with that fact, has me at hello. And the more I read, the harder I fell. I mean, who doesn't like a guy who watches football to root for the underdogs and cheers on guys who don't even have the ball? I tell you, halfway through this book, I just wanted to take Andy home. He is a psychic who finds things, anything that has been lost, pets, keys, cars, people, etc. He also works as a paid audience member on TV shows to fill up seats. Yeah, I know, I thought that was adorable, too. Andy's parents died when he was young, he was raised by his grandma, he reads a lot, and loves herbal teas.Jon is a cynic. An absolute grump. Granted, after what he's been through, it's perfectly understandable. He used to work construction, but an accident that killed his wife and messed up his shoulder left him depressed with nightmares and sleepwalking. He is completely gay, but explaining the marriage and wife would be a spoiler, so you'll have to read the book. Taking a chance, he's going back to school, although his initial thoughts of automotive maintenance or electrical were thrown to the wayside when his advisor saw his drawing skills. Now he's majoring in art with an idea to work in advertisement design.In the first case, when Andy impresses an officer by spot-on describing where a body can be found, the officer lets his uncle, a homicide detective, know. The detective comes a'calling to see if Andy can help identify a woman murdered almost twenty years ago that is a cold case but still bothers the detective that she could never be identified. Unfortunately, there's not much for Andy to go on as the woman was found naked in a motel room with no personal items. Hmm. In the second case, the mystery comes along a lot more insidiously. Jon and Andy run into an old acquaintance of Jon's and his partner while out wandering the neighborhood after a horrible windstorm. In an incredibly roundabout way, Jon and Andy manage to solve a crime that hadn't even been reported, but lost some acquaintances in the process.This was my first foray into a Lou Harper book, but I can guarantee it won't be the last. I loved the writing, the characters were solid and strong, it sort of reminded me of an old detective dime store novel except with gay men, and the mystery stories were excellent. Thank you to all my friends who recommended this read!NOTE: This book was provided by the author for the purpose of a review on Rainbow Book Reviews.

In the book, The Horror Diary, written by Brendan Verville, we are introduced to a little girl names Kendra who is 7 years old. Kendra has two young friends named George and Aaron and together, the three of them are about to face a terrifying adventure that no child should ever have to face. This wonderful work of horror literature was spellbinding to say the least. Kendra is an innocent little girl who lives with her Mom and Dad and is facing something so horrible that even she has somehow placed the terrible things which have happened to her, in a deep space in her mind, locked away and hidden so that she doesn’t have to truly face the things which happened. As many families do, Kendra and her family move from place to place without ever staying long enough for her to make any friends. She does make a friend though somehow. A little boy named Ben, who comes to her only in her dreams. She and Ben become quite close friends, and eventually, Ben not only comes to Kendra in her dreams, but also in her waking life as well. Ben shows Kendra things that she could only imagine, and one day, he not only shows her happiness and playful things, but he shows her the truth of what she has been through. As I read the book, I could visually picture little Kendra and all of the things that happened around her. It takes a truly great author to be able to bring someone into their work of literature so much that they can feel the surroundings as being described in the book. Brendan Verville has accomplished bringing his writing to life in this enthralling thriller! I look forward to reading more from Brendan Verville as he has now become one of my favorite authors! I recommend this book to all. Especially to those who enjoy a good mystery and want to read one that will keep them glued to the pages from beginning til the very end!

Brooke did a wonderful job with Burn. I was able to read this book while it was in the process of being written so I’ve had to reread some parts several times over, yet I never got tired of reading it.  This story had me sitting at the edge of seat the entire time and let me tell you the twist and turns were completely unpredictable. I was not able to put this book down!Velaney hasn’t had very much people to trust in her life. Aside from her best friend, Carissa, she has been pretty much alone. So when Eric first came waltzing into her life, she didn’t know how to react to him. He brought on feelings she has never felt before and didn’t know what to do with them. So what was she to do but push him away? However, when she finally realized she couldn’t live without him, she ran after him and got what she wanted.Velaney and Eric have overcome a lot of obstacles to be together. In Spark, their relationship has been tested several times and they were able to find their way back to one another. In this book, there are many more obstacles that rest their relationship, putting it more at risk. Will they have enough faith to keep them together?After reuniting with one another, Eric takes Velaney back with to his childhood home in Texas. Eric was always brought up with the loving family atmosphere. This brings some unknown feelings to Velaney since she has never experienced that kind of love from her family at all. Even though his family just met her, they welcome her with open arms. This is all a very overwhelming experience for her, but one she is happy to embrace. All the while she is with Eric at his family’s ranch, her nightmares are returning, and so is her paranoia of seeing her brother Aiden everywhere she turns. She feels as if he is watching her every move. It’s as if he is there stalking her. His control over her has reappeared and she doesn’t know how to shake the feeling.When they both return home they try to return back to their normal lives. But being back home brings back old feelings for Eric. A secret from his past is haunting him every day. He feels the need to tell her, but it is so painful that it’s hard to relive over again. But since he doesn’t know how to tell her, he pushes her away instead. Velaney knows better than to walk away though, instead of letting him, she doesn’t push but rather wait until he is ready to talk. This small gesture makes him fall in love with her even more.Velaney’s horrible mother bullies her into being the saving grace of their corrupt family. She makes Velaney feel that she needs to desperately save her brother and that she is the only one that could do that. As much Velaney hates her brother Aiden, her faith in God doesn’t allow her do that to him when she can be the one that could save him. This entire situation is one big f*ed up mess. It brings on a whole lot a problems for Velaney and Eric as well. Eric has already lost two people who he deeply cares about. He can’t even begin to imagine his life if he lost Velaney as well but Velaney won’t budge on her decision. She is determined to get this over with and be done with her family no matter the consequences.Velaney blames herself for the situations that have occurred and instead of facing them, she runs from them to handle them herself. It’s the only way she know how to deal with them; alone. She needs to find herself again. She feels alone. She pushes everyone who truly cares about away from her. Carissa and Eric both love her and want what’s best for her. But how can you help someone who keeps pushing you away?Will Velaney finally be able to seek help from those that love her? Or she continue to deal with her problems alone? How much can Eric take before he gives up on Velaney? Will Velaney continue to blame herself for putting herself in these situations? Will she ever break free from her family and not live in fear ever again? Can Velaney and Eric finally find happiness with each other?There is a lot of push and pull between Eric and Velaney’s relationship, I mean a lot. I kind of had me wondering if they were ever going to be together or not. Velaney shows enormous strength in this book. It was great to see her grow and mature as well. The situations that she had to endure and live through, I do not wish upon anyone. But she able to push through every single one of them and continue with life with the help of Carissa and Eric. It was also amazing to see them grow as a couple. They both have never been in relationships before so they are experiencing this together. Without a doubt you see the connection that they share. But, boy, in the bedroom the physical connection is HOT I tell you! Eric had his own fair share of problems but I loved how he always put Velaney before himself. He always wanted to protect her and keep her safe. Carissa is the best friend every girl should have. She is simply amazing and is always there when you need her. Absolutely loved this book and can’t wait for more books by Brooke!This review was done by Jennelyn.I received an ARC of this book for my honest review.

I found "The Last Elf" filled with some truly fun and charming characters -- which carried the story nicely for me, despite some real flaws in the editing/proofreading of the book.As other reviewers have mentioned, it's a nice adventure story suitable for all ages. I can see reading it to some kids, and I enjoyed it as an adult. I enjoyed the characters and found myself rooting for them all the way through and smiling at some of their gentle quirks. I especially enjoyed the concept of a sympathetic vampire "hero" with a heart of gold.Because of my feelings for the character, I'm giving it a 4/5 stars, although the poor quality editing/proofreading work done on the book is extremely distracting. I found several cases where the characters' names are wrong in the narrative. I found myself saying, "No, that's Mindy, not Penny," in one case where the names are switched within a paragraph. Another very jarring error is the misuse of "then" instead of "than" in 3 or 4 places throughout the story. It's very frustrating to see such flaws in an otherwise charming and enjoyable little story.I would sincerely hope the author would consider revising this book and send it past a good editor and proofreader in the process.
summary: Charming Characters Carry the Story for Me

A vicarious vacation to Florence, complete with a wedding and murder.  It just doesn't get any better than that.  The premise is unconventional, to say the least, but that adds to the fun as Carlina first tries to cover up her grandfather's untimely death and then tries to cover her tracks as she becomes suspect number one.  Where will it all lead? To a crazy Italian escapade that will keep the reader engaged from beginning to end.Beate Boeker's voice is light and conversational, as if sitting down and talking with a friend.  She paints the scenes so well you can feel the timbre of the city and taste and smell the delicious food offerings of Florence.  With a sprinkling of Italian-speak thrown in, I swear I was bi-lingual by the time I finished.  This is cozy mystery writing at its finest.
summary: Cozy Mystery with an International Flavor

reviewText: Traveling back to her grass roots, because of the death of her grandfather who has left her his home place.  While in route she sees a man driving a pickup who looks like an old acquaintence - - a girl chaser.  Arriving at her Aunts place she tells her who she thinks she saw and the aunt is very nervous.  Our lady insists on visiting Grandpa's place and the Aunt tells her there is a renter in the back cabin.  Arriving at the run down home, they notice the cabin is well kept and in good repair and surprize of surprizes to find living there but her unwanted man friend.  Why would he be out here in this small town?  This man has had a change of heart and as life goes on he attempts to prove he is a new person and is willing to help her fix up Grandpa's place into a bed and breakfast establishment.He hopes to win her heart - - - in with the repairs and changes necessary to the old home.

This was a good read although there are spelling and typo errors. I wonder if there will be a sequel since Chauncey was not apprehended?
This made for excellent reading! It kept my interest from the very beginning and I hated that it had to end. Thank you for such great reading material, Phoenix Sullivan! I loved it!
I like the story was going but it ended with me feeling it wasn't finished.  Only eight chapters I would have  been upset if I didn't have part one for free.

This story had a lot of voice which helped create a really strong MC. Elise, the MC, also shows a little character development, which was interesting to see unfold a little.Elise was transparent from the beginning: she had personality and lots of it. It worked well, and stayed consistent in this story. I haven't read much of modern day books with witches, and this didn't totally disappoint in that regard. There is strong language, and some sex (although not much), so if that's a turn off for you, you may not click with Elise's personality.As far as the paranormal aspect, it involves werewolves, vampires and witches. I'm interested in witchcraft, but not vamps or werewolves. Fortunately, Young doesn't go into a lot of detail regarding the vamps and werewolves, which made it bearable for me. They were there, but they weren't sucking blood like crazy, so I didn't mind them.Overall, it was an easy read with a strong magic system. If she had anything going for her, Young seemed to really know how the magic worked, and she kept that consistent. It was interesting to read about the spells they'd cast, the way they used their magic, etc. I liked this aspect, and it made me want to keep reading to see how Young would introduce different things.My biggest issues come from the characters and their relationships. It felt like it went from love triangle, to square, and back to a different triangle. By the end, I still didn't have a good understand of what her relationship with Van was. I clearly understood that they weren't committed, but why was he so annoyingly possessive and protective then? Mona, a sweet little girl, was good in herself, but I didn't really understand her purpose. She's very powerful for a ten-year-old, but by the end, she just seemed to fizzle out. With that kind of build up, I thought her power would mean something for the story, and it didn't. Elise speaks about how much she cares about Mona, and how unexpected her feelings towards Mona were. She says it a lot. Almost too much. At the end of the book, I wasn't sure I really connected with any character. Elise is supposed to be the Head Mistress, but she comes off like a 16-year-old through most of the book. That got really annoying, but at least Young kept her consistent. I'm still not even sure her actual age. She wants to reintroduce 'fun' into the school system, and just ends up acting immature most of the time. It wasn't believable for someone who should be taking responsibility for other people.Because there was a lot of backstory and history, it led to a lot of telling. I started to skim in some parts. Elise tells the history of her people at the beginning, but since I didn't know them as a reader, I wasn't too invested in learning about it.There were several misspellings, repetition in words, and some grammar mistakes, but I've seen much worse before. It wasn't too distracting, and they were mostly spaced far apart.The ending definitely threw me for a loop, but I felt no real sense of closure in it. It stirred up too many questions and introduced something out of the blue that made me feel like I'd missed something and had to go back and check.

Got my first art of love series gratis, it was carved in stone. then I bought the next book in the series right after finishing one, I got through the entire series in less than a week. Shane's story is my favorite however, I love the whole family and by the end of this one, I think I have become a close family friend. Love love this series. Looking forward to more books from this author.

reviewText: Taking an hour to read from start to finish, Mountain Hero was a wonderful short story loaded with suspense, a spunky heroine and a four-alarm hot fireman hero. Michelle, recently blindsided by betrayal between her fiancée and best friend makes plans to go to her mountain cabin to recoup and recover despite a severe winter storm barreling down on the mountain. Her brother, Zack, always told her to think first before reacting. And she tried. She really did. But her emotions always seemed to overpower her logic. She should have listened to big brother. Stranded on the mountain, miles from shelter or people, Michelle is attacked by two low-lifes..uh..men as she seeks shelter. Off-duty fireman Jason happens upon the attack and rescues Michelle but is stranded with her after the attackers steal his vehicle and disable hers. Jason rescued her once and is determined to rescue her again...from the storm and from the two men still at large.
summary: Can I have a sexy fireman hero, please?

reviewText: i remember how nervous I was for my first tryout for little league baseball.  I could not sleep the nigh before in anticipation. Ethan had similar experiences with his tryout for his little league team.  The messages this book relates to children are wonderful. All kids need to learn about setting goals, taking action to achieve your goals and reaching your dreams as a result of your commitment to your goals.  This book does a wonderful job of reinforcing all these valuable lessons in life. Another great book by KP Baker
summary: Baseball Ethan .... made me think of my youth.

reviewText: This review will be a little different. I'm going to review 2 books at one time. I recently reviewed Mona Hodgsons' book Dandelions on the Wind: The Quilted Heart series. I really enjoyed the novella and had the opportunity to review the third one in the series but I didn't want to skip the 2nd one. I purchased Bending Toward the Sun from Amazon and then received Ripples Along the Shore to review from the publisher.I really enjoyed these two books just as much as the first one. The characters continued and new stories developed. The second book focused on Emily Heinrich the storekeeper's daughter.  It also continued with the previous story of Maren."Divided between the love of her father and the desires of her heart, Emilie Heinrich must rely on the love and wisdom of the women in her quilting circle for support. Since Emilie is dedicated to her education and to helping her father in his general store, she is convinced she doesn't have time for love. But when a childhood friend returns to St. Charles, Missouri, after serving in the Civil War, his smile and charm captures Emilie's eye and her heart."I really loved the stories behind the quilts in the quilting circle. The first novella didn't mention a lot about the quilting portion of the books but the author seemed to incorporate more in the second and third books. Emily struggles with wanting to please her father and go to school but she also wants to follow her heart.In book three Ripples Along the Shore once again continues with Maren and Emily and their new lives and adds another character: Caroline."When Caroline Milburn steps off the boat and back into her hometown of St. Charles, MO, part of her wishes she could step right back on board and sail away. St. Charles, though home to her beloved friends and quilting circle, hasn't felt like home since the death of her husband. And living with her sister, Jewell's family hasn't provided much balm for her grieving heart. Caroline knows something needs to change--but for now she's stuck sharing her sister's home, and enduring the anger and bitterness of her brother-in-law."Also, it this book a lot of it centered around the ladies and their quilting circle, but this time the circle is going to be broken. Some of the ladies and their families will be leaving to go west and others will be staying. They decide to make 2 different quilts. Caroline is determined to go west but it wouldn't be proper for a widowed lady to travel alone. She's very disappointed when she thinks she isn't going to get to go.With each book new characters are introduced and old characters remain. I assume there will be more novellas in this series. I believe you should start with the 1st one and move through. They are very short around 100 pages and are quick reads. There aren't a lot of surprises but the storylines are fun to read and I really feel like I could be right there with them. If you are looking for a quick and easy read this is the series for you.

I am a big fan of homemade gifts for Christmas (or anytime, really) but I often get overwhelmed with the time and skill required... so I just drop the whole idea.  But now, I can pick myself up and start crafting away because this little book has REAL frugal fun gifts that are easy to make.The gifts in jars are wonderful, both the food and the beauty items.  But, what I really love are the kids gifts - that is both gifts FOR kids and gifts kids can make by themselves, or almost by themselves.  Rather than having a list of supplies from the craft store, the ideas in this book focus on turning things you probably have around the house (or can find at resale stores or rummage sales) into fun items.  I LOVE that idea... Reduce Reuse Recycle... very cool, indeed.Thanks for this fun book.  I know I'll be putting many of these ideas to work soon.
summary: Easy fun gifts even I can make!

reviewText: I really liked this book.  The H was vulnerable, but absolutely not wimpy, which I really liked for a change of pace. I thought there was good character development, and no one was doing stupid things just for a dramatic ploy.  Bedroom scenes were hot and you could feel the emotions of the H and h. I would recommend this book.

** 3.5 stars **I discovered The Science of Temptation series at RT2013. I really appreciate the cleverness in the title, and hoped to read it sooner rather than later. Well, that didn't happen, and before I knew it, book three was up on NetGalley. I was still interested, and decided to give the entire series a go in one shot. I'm glad I made that decision because I thoroughly enjoyed the series.The Science of Temptation series has often been described as BDSM meets The Big Bang Theory. I think that is a great description, besides the fact I found these characters to be far more appealing. I would also say that the series is more "BDSM-lite". Yes, it does play an important role in the series, but for me, the stories focus more on people who happen to enjoy the lifestyle instead of the lifestyle running them. To put it a little more plainly, the characters enjoy aspects of the D/s life, but it doesn't define them. Outside of the bedroom, or club (the scenes of which were more interesting/entertaining than sexual), you'd hardly know.In The Theory of Attraction we have Ivan seeking help from neighbor Cami in being less socially awkward. Cami sees Ivan as her gorgeous but serious neighbor. But she soon realizes that Ivan's serious nature translates into a controlling man in the bedroom (or club), a man who becomes the Professor. Cami saves Ivan in the real world; Camille submits to the Professor. I liked seeing this man who is easily frazzled in situations he cannot control, become a dominant man who takes back control in the most pleasing manner. Their relationship was endearing, and I loved seeing them continue to bond and develop a closer relationship throughout the series.If you're looking for stories that a sexy and very real, I encourage you to give this series a try.Favorite Quotes"You're already pretending to be my date. So focus on that part. Are you going to be a boyfriend? Or are you going to be some guy who's hoping to get...um, get me to go out a second time?"The Friday evening traffic occupied his attention for a few minutes before he finally answered. "Were you going to say 'laid' and then changed your mind?"Crap, so much for being subtle. "Yep.""That one. I'll be that one."He called it taking but I felt as though he were giving me these things, these actions, like pieces of himself. Challenging me to receive these odd gifts, because they were all he had to give. His attention, his regard. His respect, which was the strangest thing of all, because I had expected to feel degraded at some point in all this and instead I felt valued beyond measure. Cherished. Strong.

I live in AZ, and in the summer time my wife and I hate to cook. It is just too hot. So we thought about mixing juicing into our diet. We got this book and have been very pleased with the recipes. We both feel more alert and less sluggish. The house does not get hot and this is something that both of us feel that we can do. With the wide variety of juices and the instructions found in this book. We will be in great shape for the rest of the summer.
Very good story line with great characters.  Much too short though. I would have loved it if it would have been longer

Tristan is a douche, not gonna mince words. He uses women & then kicks them right out of his bed, but then we see the flip side of the coin that just once he would like a woman to make it a little tougher on him, give him something to chase, but these bimbos are mostly married or engaged & are just looking for a quick romp too. But when Tristan met Leah all those years ago she made him wait, she bantered with him & made him crave her company, not just her body. Once they finally got down to business & had the most fantastic night of their lives, big misunderstandings occurred. In Leah's mind, it sealed Tristan's fate as a permanent douchebag loser. And that is why in book #1 we find his brother Dre, his girlfriend Kathryn, and Leah all teaming up with a terrible plan that totally throws Tristan under the bus. It saves their youngest sister Piper but yet it was totally unfair to Tristan. Dre & Kathryn's wedding day approaches and that is why Tristan & Leah suddenly find themselves in the same city relieving their old misunderstandings. Tristan's father is completely heinous, to all three of his kids, so much so that they've shut him out of their lives. But the one advantage is they decide to finally bond together. Once Tristan gets out from under his father's influence he seems to make a complete change in his life - not really believable but ok. Can't really go from douchebag deluxe to suddenly being a philanthropist helping out all of Dre's friends! There are many interesting side parts to their story, like Leah's mom's battle with cancer & how she may be affected. Luckily it makes her live her life to the fullest & take advantage of this new opportunity with Tristan to start fresh & establish a real relationship with him! And we also learn what happened to Piper as a teenager. I haven't seen anything about the third book in this series & I'm crossing my fingers that it involves Piper - she is a spitfire & I'd love to see her get her happy ending.

The story is enjoyable but hard to follow at times. There are places where parts of the book seem to be missing. It was hard to really feel anything for the characters and I don't know if it was the reserved, no nonsense manner of storytelling or the editing that caused this problem. As to the editing there was a mess of wrong gender pronouns, missing pronouns, prepositions and all sorts of other words. Sentences that were written one way and then another and ended up being written both ways. Here's a sample: "...she gave her a sly smile slyly." I think with some proper editing the story would really shine.

Holy hottness, Sawyer. I love him and that he finally found what he was looking for. Even though he didn't think he wanted it. The connection and banter between him and Emmett was incredible. He is such an amazing person and has a huge heart. This is by far one of the best serious I have read. I can't wait for the next one

Ok, so as said in the first review this had to be the hardest ever to write.This is the second part to Aubrey and Alex's story. It picks up exactly where the first left off and as in the first you wont be able to put it down until you have finished it.I already told you about the characters in the first book, however I left one out.
