4 StarsFrom the opening scene of the book, I fell in love with Reid Galvin. He's a Navy Seal doing what his country has asked of him. Pulling fellow service members from the wreckage of a downed Chinook atruegemawardand then going out to avenge their deaths. It's the only thing on his mind. Except when he closes his eyes, all he can see is the face of a woman who stole his heart the last time he was on leave - Becca Anderson.When Reid goes back overseas, Becca continues writing him, telling him all of her fantasies. Not knowing how to respond and dealing with the death of his fallen comrades, Reid makes the mistake of not answering her, leading to some confused emotions on both sides.The night that Reid does decide to answer Becca, she's actually on a date with another man. A date that eventually requires Reid to literally save her life.There were lots of things I loved about this book and I believe other readers will love. The relationship between the two of them was very true to life. Because Reid hadn't answered her emails or made an attempt to contact her before getting stateside, Becca of course had many doubts when it came to his feelings for her.The one thing they never doubted? Their sexual chemistry....which is off the charts hawt!! The way Reid calls Becca beautiful makes my heart melt every time he says it. It's obvious he cares deeply for her and will do whatever it takes to make the miscommunications between them right.He also proves that he will protect her no matter what. When she stumbles upon an encrypted file that she unencrypts for a friend and unknowingly sets into motion a string of events that leaves one person dead and the bad guys after her, Reid shows her just how much she means to him. He does whatever it takes to keep her safe and in the process does his best to prove to her just how real his feelings are.If you like your sexiness with some intrigue and hot military men...then this is definitely the book for you!Review copy provided for an honest review.

This piece is really a prelude to a full length with same main character.  It is a "teaser" to tempt you or interest you enough to move on to the other work.  Seeming - works. Likely a series type character.  Which can be irritating if expecting more, but, the author sets forth the agenda in his intro.  So, fine.The character is not fully fleshed out - which is likely due to length - in part.  Part is likely due to character will be fleshed further in the full length.  The small problem with so little detail on MC is that there is nothing told to make one like the guy.  There is nothing to draw interest of reader (in this particular work) so that they think "mmmm...I can see why he does what he does or how he came to such..." I wanna know more.  I want next installment.  Just does not happen.The shortfall on MC can and will be forgiven by many readers. After all, it IS just a prelude and taking another chance is not a huge deal.  As long as other draw (voice, style, wit, etc.)there.  I find myself trying to find another draw to show the readers.  I am coming up short.  The affect was bland.  I think the writer was going for wry humor with MC dialogue and Blase' thoughts.  But, some felt flat and forced as I read.  I think there may be something in a longer work that just did not show effectively here.  The story premise is a good one (if a bit cliched) - is the second one of this type I have read in past 3 days.  Still, the writer may pull off unique scenes if given longer time to set pace.This was a fast read.  For length.  Some of the writing was stilted and predictible.  The female character was very much a cliche character.  In description and dialogue.There are several errors related to punctuation and grammar (incorrect /missing /wrong words and punctuation) .There is a substantial inconsistency in story with a weapon and also with the timeline.  The MC got done working at midnight, had an encounter /scuffle, went to a bar, met a man and had a pretty indepth conversation with him - then ended up at another bar called "Hell" a little after midnight.  That was some fast moving.It is really not believable that this guy completed his contract in a mere 4 hours either.  Perhaps I read too much and am just used to more storyline via surveillance - but a rush to complete contract seems like a good way to get MC killed.  It is also not that believable that the person to be the "mark" was as ill prepared for something like this as he showed to be.  Mob hit men don't stay alive very long unless they are prepared for themselves being a hit.  He would have had a weapon or something close by.I think that is the crux of my dissatisfaction:  the hit was just too contrived, beginning to end.

So I was a bit confused going in to this story, the first Men of Silo book has wolf shifters in it, I was expecting more of them in this one and that's not what this book is about. No paranormal at all. Which is fine, I'm happy either way, just wasn't what I had expected.Ed appears in the first book as Chris's ex bofriend, who is kind of an ass. He's really not, he's just lonely and looking for love. In a small town with not many gay men.Then we have Duncan. I was confused with him as well! There is some hinting that he is a Dom at one point, but that doesn't play out much. He has some serious issues, missing part of an arm, PTSD, abandonment and commitment phobia. At times I liked him, at times I didn't. He tried so hard to not get close to Ed, but just kept going back. I wanted him to commit or leave Ed alone. It felt at times like he was using his issues as an excuse to hide.The Search and Rescue story line was good, I wished it had been used more. I liked Margo the dog, she's in it quite a bit, partly as a rescue dog, then as an accessory for Duncan. Another rescue, a job offer, something that used that side of Duncan more would have been nice.There is lots of will they/won't they, not sex which they do quick, but will they be a couple? Will they commit? Will Duncan let Ed in, literally and figuratively? I wanted him to fully commit to Ed by the end and have that moment of complete surrender and openness, but we don't really get that. The ending felt rushed, and abrupt, although it was a happy ending. That may not make sense, but it went from angst to living together really quickly.I liked the book, I really did, I liked the characters most of the time, I liked the story most of the time, I liked the ending mostly, I LOVED Margo, and I liked the glimpses of Chris and Jamie.I'm curious to see what the next one will be, contemporary? Paranormal?

5 stars...and coming from me, that's saying a lot!!!Sometimes good things can come from great sadness.  Julia has given up her life and moved to Sommersgate house to care for her nephew and two nieces as part of her brothers final wishes after his and his wife's tragic death.  But Julia isn't alone in her task.  Per their wishes, she is to raise the children in England, in this house with the houses master, her brother in law Douglas.  For the first time Julia lays eyes on Douglass fifteen years ago there is something about him that she is drawn to buts he can tell he is broken.  Over time, she has suffered an emotionally abusive marriage and as a result locked away her heart.  Now she is back with Douglas after all this time, dealing with death and heartbreak and the desire she still feels for him.Douglas has been attracted to Julia from the moment he first met her fifteen years ago.  She is different from every women he has ever known in that she challenges him at every turn.  After spending more time with her, Douglas comes to a decision, she will marry him and decrees it to be so.  When Julia once again defies his wishes, Douglas has to rethink his plan of approach.  A cunning business man, Douglas is emotionally broken after enduring years of emotional abuse from his father and complete lack of indifference from his mother.  He knows he will have to open himself up to Julia is he has any chance of winning her but can he take a chance with his heart?I loved, loved, loved this story.  Any of you who read my reviews here know that I rarely give 5 star ratings.  To get one from me, the story has to touch me...make me feel for the characters...frustrate me at times...and not want to put the story down.  This one did all that and more!  I loved Julia...her strength and devotion to the children and her fire when fighting with Douglas are such a joy to read.  And Douglas....typical KA alpha (and on the list of my favorites after this read). Beautifully broken, with do much to give once it is finally pulled out.There is a supernatural element to this story, which is a beautiful, tragic love story all it's own.My thoughts:Character development: 5Level of Romance between characters: 5Passion/Heat level: 5(chemistry between Douglas and Julia is sizzling right from the start but because of the story elements, it is a slow build.  So worth the wait!)Angst/Heartbreak: 5 (oh the hurtles and heartbreak, my heart is still recovering and at times, I was teary)Cliffhanger?: No, although part of a series, this is a stand alone book and comes with an amazing epilogue.Overall, I can't believe I didn't read this one sooner.  This is the one KA series I hadn't tackled and I am really enjoying them all so far.  I will say that this one is a slow start, but there is a lot of back story to build so stick with it...once you hit the 17% mark won't want too put it down. MY THOUGHTSABSOLUTELY LOVED ITBrinley, the queen bee of Georgetown Academy, an elite prep school for Washington's elite, is starting off the school year by getting her classmates in social order with the help of her boyfriend, the son of the Vice-President.  Her best friend, Ellie, is the daughter of a powerful senator but her boy friend, Hunter is the son of her mother's political enemy.  Taryn, has just transferred in from California, with her father set to be the first Hispanic President and she is about to learn that the stakes are higher in this backstabbing arena of global power.  Evan is a bookworm that gets her shot as an intern at a highly political television show.Much like Gossip Girl, this cast has a lot to lose if the the rumors get out of their social circle and could be devastating on a national level for their parents careers.  When Brinley decides to take down newcomer, Taryn by starting a rumor about her trading sex for drugs, she sets off a chain of events that can only end in heartbreak for all involved.  Secretly, I have a death wish for Brinley unless she redeems herself in upcoming installments.  Taryn is so down to earth and you feel like she has been thrown into the deep end of a pool of sharks but I have high hopes for her coming out on top. There are so many little subplots in this first one, that it could take multiple episodes to resolve.Remember those cool "Choose your own adventure" novels back in grade school?  You had to flip the pages to get to the next section and the story could go in one of many directions depending on the character you chose to follow and what you decide they should do.  Well, this takes that to the next level.  Taking advantage of technology, you can click on a link to pick your character and action!  I admit, I did cheat a bit and read each character's detour.  This is such a fun and quick read that anyone will love to get their hands on. Parents:  there is kissing, mentions of drug use, and some language.

Is she not that recognisable or do people not care? If I saw a celebrity in my town I would freak out. That’s just me.Second, the issue with Layne’s PTSD. I think this could have been better addressed. It is so common to say that someone in the military has PTSD, but if you use the storyline you should embrace it. I felt that the author tiptoed on this one.  The author has this medium that could have been used for educating others about it. I wish that she would have dove more into that storyline.Does all this mean I hated the book? No. I am still a fan of the series. I just didn’t love this one. I liked it. I enjoyed the fact that we got more Meredith and Tyler time. I hope that they get a novella in the future.Mrs. Briscoe is an excellent writer and her books are entertaining. This is an engaging and confident first book from a natural storyteller. Kath Middleton was already well-known as a reviewer of fiction and a champion of indie authors everywhere, but now it seems she’s going to successfully carve a new career as an author herself!Ravenfold is a tale of families, power and revenge, set in medieval England. This is portrayed with just enough detail to feel authentic, although the focus is less on history and more on the characters. When young Romelda is forcibly married to the monstrous Lord Oswald, her life and those of her parents and friends are twisted out of shape forever. The story takes some surprising dramatic turns along the way, incorporating what may even be shades of the supernatural.The structure resembles a children’s fable, with a framing story of a man relating Romelda’s tale as a bedtime story to his grandchildren. But this is actually a very adult book, including some strong scenes that do not shy away from depicting the brutality of medieval life. Kath handles these with a light touch but paints some gruesome pictures in the imagination. There is also plenty of gallows humour that had me chuckling aloud, but is most definitely not for young readers!Ravenfold is a darkly entertaining tale that promises even greater stories from this author in the future.
summary: A darkly entertaining tale of medieval times!

reviewText: This is a very short story that is currently (I am not sure if it always is or not) free on Amazon.  It is written as a teaser and includes a chapter to the full length book "Intangible".  After reading this 16 page short and also reading the chapter, I will give you a little word of advice.  Do not read it... unless you already purchased the full length book to follow it with as it is one heck of a teaser and you will be kicking yourself or rushing to get the book the second you finish it because you just need to know what will happen next, immediately!!  It is a much better idea to just have it already to go the very moment that you finish.This short story is so very well written that in just 16 short pages you find yourself already attached to the characters, picturing the beautiful Vermont mountains in your mind perfectly (and I have never seen them myself, but I now feel like I have), and worrying about things that I won't mention because I do not want to give anything away.  This author has a way with words that just pulls you into the story and holds you there until the very last word and even then you just do not want to be let go.  It is a very enjoyable short and I recommend it fully.

If you buy only one short Christmas story to get you in the holiday mood, you should definitely make it “Sugar Plum Kisses.” I ran across it in one of my meandering internet crawls, when I’m not looking for anything in particular, but something particularly good all at once. Melissa Blue’s story jumped out at me because I’m a writer of IR romance myself, and I’m always interested in stories like my own.As I read this wonderful little story, I was first drawn in by the most clever, realistic banter I’ve read in a very long time. Ms. Blue has a skill that many authors struggle with: crafting believable, authentic dialogue. It seems effortless in this story (and one of her Cupid Shorts I’ve read). So, I guess it’s safe to say, Ms. Blue has found herself another fan in me!Sugar Plum Kisses is so short, I won’t bother writing a synopsis because the one provided for the story suffices. What I will say is, you won’t be disappointed by this sweet story. The female protag struggles with coming to term with her mother’s death in the midst of harboring a huge crush on her boss. This is conflict at its zenith. Read to see how Simone and Blaine come to terms with their shared, yet somehow unrealized mutual affection.If I had one nitpick, it would be the story was too short. Another uber hot scene with Simone and Blaine might have been in order. Ahem.

From the beginning Pruitt has taken me on a journey that I cannot predict. It has been a pleasure to follow along, and certainly makes me feel better about my own life in the process. Sheesh she does not pull punches when it comes to her characters.Everyone is put through the ringer in Alliance. Joanne and her team are famous among The Winged and the Fallen - and not in a good way. Her relationships seem to be working for her, though it really has turned into the Michael show, I missed Raphael in this story. He is around but not as much or in the same capacity as Michael. reviewText: This story leaves no doubt about who the good guys and the bad guys are.  And amazingly enough although it uses the same slang and old fashioned heroics, it is thoroughly entertaining.  As older teenagers, Huck Finn and Tom Sawyer joined the Confederate army during the Civil War, and as they admitted, for adventure, not because they were abolitionists.  Tom was shot in the arm and after Huck saw piles of amputated arms and legs as the doctors' procedure for savings a life, Huck had read that a Frenchman said the wound had to be cleansed well to save the limb.  Huck gave Tom a bottle of whiskey to drink, pried out the small lead ball in this arm, and then washed it out good.  The young men were sick of army life and they hid out until Tom regained his strength and they could travel.They decided to go West and spent a few days with a southern farmer and his family.  While Tom was recuperating, three Union soldiers came to the farm house, the Sergeant was drunk, mean and decided to take the farmer's wife and beautiful eighteen year old daughter to the barn to satiate his lust.  But Huck was in the barn with Tom and Huck shot the Sergeant and then one of the privates who raised his gun.  The other private raised his gun, but then lowered it.  The southerners didn't know what to do with the surviving private, but eventually they learned he was real young, his name was Jed Blevins and they released him.Huck, Tom and Jed continued going West.  Huck was going to Missouri; Tom wanted to go to China after hearing about it; and Jed decided to go to California.  The story then splits between the escapades of each of these three men, adventures which matured them and gave them a philosophy by which to live.  The book ends with the three of them meeting up again and joining forces to make life better for others.Although it is doubtful that we would enjoy Samuel Clemons' stories and colloquialisms today as much as we did when they were new, reading this story of these children/young men now well experienced heroes is truly entertaining, reads easily and actually becomes a page turner, making it a quick read.  I loved it and I think many readers will also, no matter how sophisticated their usual reading literature is.I was given this book for an honest review.

reviewText: Right off the bat, I have to say that I loved the premise of this book. It showed a wealth of creativity and a real penchant for writing unique and memorable stories. Reading the summary was enough to make me want to buy it, which is unusual, as I typically go off the recommendations of friends or stick with authors that I've read in the past. However, this stuck out, particularly because the author is so well-versed in Biology, so I assumed that this would be in the high-science variety of science fiction, a section of the genre with which I am familiar and a fan. With all of that as the lead-up to reading the novel, I must say I was slightly disappointed, not in the quality of the story or the intention of the author, but of the writing itself. There were those brief, beautiful moments when I felt myself being drawn into the story, losing myself in the imagined world of Pericles and his mythical creation/adventures....but then I was promptly tugged out by a nearly illegible passage, a glaring syntactical mistake, or a leap between two ideas that was impossible to follow.The reason I give this book four stars is because as I trudged my way through some of the more frustrating sections, I could see the work and creativity that had been poured into the narrative; I just wish that there had been a few rounds of edits and proofreading to bring this book up to snuff. If you don't mind doing a bit of close reading to discern what something is intended to mean, then this book will be wonderful. I did enjoy it at times, and I think the author has a real talent for painting a landscape with his words, particularly given his cultural background and experience in that part of the world. He could see the images he was trying to describe, and in many cases, he succeeded in sharing that vision with the reader. It was the too-common stumbling block passages that interrupted my enjoyment, not necessarily the story itself. It's hard to criticize a non-native speaker for not being perfect...you'll have to make that decision for yourself!

Brutally beautiful. As noirishly dark as the deep depths of the Pacific Ocean that spawned them. These stories of the people, places, exploits and exploitations of the islands of the Pacific will haunt you long after you close the book. Important literature for the 21st century. They are stories of tragedy and triumph, genius and depravity. Tales of love and betrayal told in a voice at times as soft and reassuring as the whisper of the sea yet as powerful as a tsunami. There is perhaps no better, nor more important story teller alive, recounting tales of Americas fiftieth state and the people, islands and waters surrounding and embracing her shores.Assassin Orders Peking Duck - The opening story recounts the reactions and fears of Hawai'i after the events of 9/11, by the populace as well as a Navy SEAL. In prose as vivid as a sunset, it is a tale of paranoia fulfilled in a world gone mad.Mysteries Of Rapa Nui - Transports you in a time machine to 1849 when Blackbirders hunted the Pacific Islands for slaves and the means and methods a proud, dying race would go to to protect the few men left, and their way of life on Easter Island. It tells of a clash of cultures, one doomed and the other doomed in their soul.Cannibal Nights, Colonial Afternoons - Recounts the last days of the painter Paul Gauguin and how he comes to understand that it is neither love nor lust that drives him insane, but his art.These and the other stories in Cannibal Nights Pacific Stories Volume II are told in sparse realistic prose, yet the words convey a depth that is somehow poetic. You will feel the power of the sea and the power of the spirits of the people that inhabit the islands. Beautifully brutal and brutally beautiful, Kiana Davenport is a master story teller and chronicler of the deep history, beauty, spirit and emotion of the Pacific Paradise and all her peoples. I've heard Ms. Davenports work described as "Pacific Noir" yet it is so much more than that. Noir conveys a sense of souls lost, and not worth redeeming.  True, these are tales of murder, rape, lust and doomed love. They are tales of greed and exploitation, tales of theft of wealth and innocence. They are stories of loss, but not irredemption. The individuals may be irrevocably lost, a swim in a dark sea, yet their souls, their hearts and dreams are admirable and most definitely will be and are worthy of redemption. Simply put, great literature for the 21st century.

“You were my unexpected chance.”I was over the moon with excitement when I got my hands on this book. I had devoured and fallen in love with book one, Unexpected Chance, so I was desperate to find out more about Aubrey and Alex. And after that ending? Well, let’s just say My Chance did not release fast enough. If you have not read the first book, stop reading here and go buy it. It’s truly fantastic!My Chance picked up exactly where Unexpected Chance ended. Yes, in that jaw-dropping scene. Honestly, I did not know what to expect from this book. I had no idea where the author would go with Alex and Aubrey’s story, so I was a bit nervous.“I can’t lose you. You’re my missing piece.”To say Aubrey was floored with the surprising turn of events, would be an understatement. Logically, things were off to a very rocky start. Aubrey did not want to be a burden in Alex’s life, so she pushed him away. She figured he deserved better…someone who was whole. But Alex didn’t agree. He wanted her. He loved her.“I want to take care of you and make you happy. I’m nothing without you.”Alex was a true romantic. All he did was show Aubrey how much she meant to him. He left everything behind to be by her side. Hands down, he became a better man for her. Once Aubrey realized how much they needed each other and how badly they belonged together, things got better between them. They gradually adjusted to having each other back in their lives for good. For Aubrey, this meant she had to learn how to move past Alex’s past, which sometimes was easier said than done.“I love you, Aubrey. I never stopped; I never will. You’re my one and only…”Overall, My Chance was a light and sweet read. There really wasn’t any angst where Aubrey and Alex were concerned. It was nice to see them work through their issues together and grow stronger, both individually and as a couple. I really liked seeing Aubrey grow out of her shell with Alex’s help, support, and love. There was no doubt in my mind that Alex would do anything for his girl. If any couple deserved a beautiful happy ending, it was Alex and Aubrey. Safe to say, I finished reading with a smile across my face.“You have my heart and my soul. You’re my life.”I can’t end this review without taking a moment to mention the secondary characters. I loved seeing once again the couples we met in book – Mark and Val and Brett and Julie. They all had such AMAZING side stories!! I was super interested in reading about them, to the point where I kept anticipating scenes they were in. They kept me turning the pages wanting to see their stories develop. My heart ached for Brett and Julie. OMG!! I could not read enough about their heartbreaking situation. I. Need. More. Sigh. There were a lot of things left hanging where the secondary characters were concerned. I am hoping, praying, and crossing my fingers, the author gives in to my harassment and writes spin-offs! :) I am not too proud to beg! *giggles*Well anyway, if you are in the mood for a smooth, quick read with a very romantic and swoon-worthy male lead character, then this is most definitely the book for you.“You and me, forever.”***An ARC of "My Chance" as provided in exchange for an honest review. Thanks!!**

I only give a five-star rating if a work clearly blows me away, and this short story by LJ Holmes certainly qualifies. It's just as much a love story as it is a mystery, which means it has universal appeal. Take me, for example. I usually read dark fiction, science fiction, crime fiction, etc., so I had some doubts at first. However, I like to keep an open mind and venture outside my typical genres from time to time. In this case, I am glad I did. It's difficult to disclose much without giving away the story, as this is a mystery after all, but the build-up of suspense and anxiety was masterful. I felt as if I was in Jonathan's shoes throughout the entire story. Has his wife left him for another man? Has she been kidnapped? Is she involved in some sort of conspiracy? These are all questions the reader encounters. When the big reveal finally comes, it shocks you. Maybe others will see it coming, but I can honestly say I never did. We see despair and beauty at the same time. Thinking of my own wife while reading this story, I couldn't help but feel a variety of emotions. In fact, I haven't been this emotionally drawn to a story since reading Flowers for Algernon, and Holmes managed to do this in a much shorter work, which shows just how talented she is. I would recommend this book to ANYONE, regardless of what they typically read. If you're human, you will enjoy it. It's that simple.

I just finished reading Jean Henry Mead's Murder on the Interstate on my Kindle today, and I recommend it as a fast-paced, lively read. Two little old ladies--well, they're about 60, which from my vantage point is still the flush of youth--have the rather odd and dangerous hobby of solving murder cases. Dana Logan and Sarah Cafferty are toddling along in their RV when they discover a car that's gone off the road. They stop and discover that the driver has been shot dead. Soon they realize that as witnesses they become targets themselves. Eventually Dana's daughter Kerrie gets dragged into the adventure as well, making the case a family enterprise. The women are relentless. Between the fact that "A beautiful young woman died needlessly" and "It got personal when he tried to kill me as well," the bad guys ultimately don't stand a chance.At the beginning, it looks like an ordinary murder case, but our heroines soon learn that they have uncovered a plot with national implications. What first seems like a relatively light mystery turns dark and tragic, but the women never flinch and remain in the thick of the trouble right to the end.Mead's road mystery made for a good summer read as I took my own RV road trip this week. It's a nice addition to my Kindle library.

Gioia Clementine has arrived at a shifter’s resort/camp believing it is her last hope to stop the isolation that her son has been quickly placing himself in. With her mate and the father of her son dead, Gioia has come hoping that the resort’s owner can find a way to break through the wall her son has raised. But when she learns just how he wants to do it, Gioia is unsure she wants to bring in a playboy.Soren Snow is an internationally renowned musician and a playboy by choice. He is also a polar bear shifter. When Soren receives a call from his brother about a troubled boy he is working with who idolizes him, Soren can’t say no to coming to the isolated resort in Northern Ontario, even if the great outdoors is definitely not his thing. Imagine his surprise at his shifter’s self instant reaction to the boy’s mother. Mating is the last thing on Soren’s to do list.Gioia is surprised by the real man that Soren is and how he gives so much to her son. She would even give a second chance to a playboy for the smiles he brings out of her son. As the days go by, Gioia finds herself drawn more and more to Soren with an intense attraction. Just as a break through comes in both her son’s acceptance of his past and the passion that has flamed between Gioia and Soren – a new arrival to the resort blows everything up. When the smoke clears will Gioia and Soren have a clear chance to achieve the future that awaits them? And will her son be able to accept the relationship between his idol and his mother?A desperate mother and a playboy musician join to help a troubled boy with the result being a true love that will encompass all three of them. Gioia and Soren find that love in Predator’s Serenade. I would have never guessed that Soren would drop everything and return to the fishing camp/resort in the great outdoors. And yet he instantly stepped up once he met Gioia and her son. Gioia wasn’t really looking for a new relationship when she arrived at the fishing camp/resort but once she met Soren passion was immediate. I watched as Soren quickly grew from being a playboy without a care into a man who wanted the responsibility of having a mate and her son. When the surprise person came in to their relationship, I thought that would be the worse hurdle they would have to overcome but I was wrong. The worse threat was different entirely. I loved when Soren gave Gioia her greatest joy and how he did it. What a way to proclaim your love. Predator’s Serenade combines passion with suspense with twists of humor and a young boy’s trust.This book was reviewed by Jo for Joyfully Reviewed (JR), and was provided by the publisher/author at no cost to JR for the purpose of being reviewed.
summary: A desperate mother and a playboy musician join to help a troubled boy with the result being a true love that will encompass all

My Review:This book is settling into the series and as such seemed to move a bit slower for me than the first did. It picks up just a couple of months where the last book left off. Connor and Riana are still working behind the scenes with the rebellion Front. Mikel is back after establishing a new identity outside the Union. Things are going along pretty much as normal for this small group until it becomes apparent that the Zealots are ramping things up.Suddenly there are attacks on the capital and the Union that make it look like the Front is getting violent. That's completely untrue. For some reason the Zealots have decided to get rid of the Front and this is their method for doing so.Things are also ramping up between Mikel and Riana. In this society, sex is extremely blase. It's simply a physical act. For those within the Front, they still believe in meaningful sex and marriage. Mikel has asked Riana to marry him, which she refused and he wants to have sex with her, but she refuses to take that final step also. This completely confuses Mikel. He's given up everything for Riana, even though he truly doesn't believe in what the Front stands for. He doesn't really believe that their little rebellion can make a difference and he hates that her participation puts Riana in danger. But you have to love the guy...he is 100% supportive of her. He doesn't pressure her or try to convince her otherwise. This is NOT a guy trying to change her. He accepts her beliefs and even though he doesn't share them, he does help out because he knows it will help her in the end. I love his character for that.Then there's Connor. He continues to hide his feelings for Riana knowing that she's in love with Mikel. He just wants her to be happy. Although he doesn't think that things can last with Mikel because they have a different belief system, he won't be the guy who messes that up for her. Again, this is a guy that you can't help but love because he is putting Riana's needs above his own.Then there's the end. OMG, can we say cliffhanger?? Not in the way that you want to rip the book in  half like some author's do, but Susannah Noel definitely made it so that you NEED the next book as soon as humanly possible. OMG...I love where this series is going and can't wait to see what happens next...I love what these books stand for. Seriously, if you love books and what the written word means to society, you need to read this series. Here's a quote that I pulled out of this book. Susannah, you need to market this quote. I want it on a coffee cup and maybe a journal or two. Seriously, powerful..."If you write it down, a word endures."I received a complimentary copy of this book in return for an honest review.

Located slightly east of the middle of Tennessee, Sparta would have never had cattle ranches and cowboys in 1860, as described here. It contained lots of curse words, however. Although the story was slightly entertaining, I was disappointed at its shallowness.

The three stars above are rather weak. The main reason I read this book is that it is the prequel to PickingUp The Pieces by the same author. Now Patriotic Treason is not bad, but there are some things in it that disturbs me a bit. I mean there is nothing wrong  for a writer to borrow a few things here and there but Nuttall goes a little further than that. He could at least have given a little tribute to all the writers that has influenced him among which you would find Robert Heinlein, Jerry Pournelle, S.M Stirling, John Ringo, Tom Kratmann and Michael Williamson to mention some. That said however, the story works. Set in the far future when the United Nations dominate the known Universe (hello Williamson and Kratmann) a young naval officer finds out that the UN has become a tyrant and is also on the verge of collaps. He decides to do something about it, collecting some likeminded around him. I won't tell you what happens, wou will have to do as I and buy the book. Beside having borrowing heavily from other writers there is something else that bugs me. Nuttall is British but the novel is full of mis-spellings and grammatical errors. It is like the author have'nt had time or resources to correct the language before publishing the novel. Proof-reading is the word I think. To sum it up, Christopher Nuttall definitely shows promise and I am going to read his next novel in this mini seies Picking Up The Pieces.SincerelyHans

reviewText: I loved this book! Krystal gets all aspects in her characters. The evil mother. The bully's, The boyfriend, the protector and the damsel in distress. Her writing is so smooth and I couldn't put it down. I'm glad that this was not an insanely large story, because then I didn't have to worry about not being able to finish it before bed. When I am this into a book I will usually stay up until I finish and the morning comes quicker than we think!Sam is a noble and the oldest daughter. She is 25 now and that age has significant meaning in the noble wolf packs. It means now she is at the age where her parents want to find her a mate. Therefore they handpick nobles to participate in a hunt to claim her. She does not realize this is going to happen when she comes home from school for break. If she had known she would not have come.She bumps into Chase at the airport and feels the instant connection and recognizes him as her mate. Her mother later overhears her telling her sisters she would be a little more willing to participate with the hunt if a contender of her choice could participate. Which begins the Chase for Sam. There are a lot of obstacles in Chase's way. He will have to come face to face with more than just other wolves to get to Sam.I would definitely recommend reading this book and I am going right ahead to read the next book!

reviewText: Not a bad book.  I would recommend trying it, it's only 99 cents.. and you can always get a sample, like I often do before purchasing a book.  Willow is a teenager that unfortunately has put all her eggs in one basket so to speak, and the unthinkable happens... they get broke... lol... Lots of teenagers are like this though.  We join Willow on her journey as she struggles to rebuild her life and figure out who SHE is as a whole.  A lot of teenager girls' identities are centered around their boyfriend's and that was Willow's issue. Teenage girls need to be who they are and who they want to be with or without a boyfriend.  A boyfriend shouldn't be their sole identity.  Not my usual genre but I have found that I'm reading more and more of this style book, and I'm enjoying it.

Having been hurt by her ex-boyfriend and issues with her mother, Mia makes a promise to herself to never allow anyone close enough to matter. She prefers one night stands with simple rules. No personal connections. No Sleepovers. Sex only and go home. Well some rules are made to be broken. When Mia meets Grayson she tries to treat him like her past conquests. No attachments but Grayson doesn't play by those rules. He slowly shows Mia that he's different and that he wants more than a sexual relationship. He wants all of Mia. Over time Mia lowers her walls that she built around her heart and attempts to let Grayson in. Mia struggles with her new found feelings and must decide if she will allow Grayson to become much more to her or revert back to her old habits with men. This was an interesting read for me. I enjoyed the book but I found myself liking Grayson more in the story. He had issues of his own to deal with but he was open to moving on. I think he deserved a new beginning maybe a little more than Mia did. Overall this was a good story of self discovery and second chances.

John Medler delivers a powerhouse book in “Fountain” mixing equal parts Indiana Jones and Clive Cussler to create a compelling narrative. Charlie Winston is a character that is definitely on par with some of the great action stars, but in a more subdued manner. This isn’t Stallone trying to act like a teacher, it’s more along the lines of Nic Cage, but maybe someone a bit lesser known. Whatever the case is, the story is sharp, taking on a historical idea and running with it.Fans of adventure novels are going to be delighted with this one, as Winston must look into a variety of different pieces of the past to discover if in fact the founding of America is as the history books say. Alongside the “Contagion” scenario, and a variety of other subplots, you’ll find yourself tightly wrapped around Medler’s story that features so much in such a powerful play, that you will swear it’s a mini-series or a movie. “Fountain” is smooth flowing, and features some quality moments, and perhaps compels Professor Winston to be an iconic character that is bound for more adventures. This is an instant classic for me, a popcorn thriller and adventure in a book, with lots of elements of science fiction, historical mystery, and more. I recommend it.

I love how the author focuses on the main characters but also the supporting ones.  I for one cannot wait for the next in the series. Vincent and Lisa will be wicked hot. As a reader, I can honestly say that I love this series but most important I love how this author makes me want more.  Only bad thing was it was over to soon.  I want so much more of the whole series and especially Rush and Addison.

This short story left me wanting more. Did the grandchildren fill the void for Elise' s parents?  A story on the dynamics of forgiveness and all it can bring to  broken family, a lost love is always worth reading. It offers a ray of hope for those who experience it.

I really enjoyed A Terrible Love immensely but this was so much more!  Cas' story is quite literally brutal and beautiful.  Cas along with his federal partners are assigned to find the murderers of some young women students  at the university that Jewell is attending and also to protect her because she is their next target.  I liked Cas' hard edged gutsiness and his protective stance towards Jewell.  Of course he falls for her and is the type of man that conveys his love through his actions and not so much with words.  There was more depth and detail in his story, through experience, he is always motivated by his gut felt intuition, and this was always on the mark.This is more than 5 stars.  Well worth reading, especially as it is refreshingly different to the first book.  I sometimes regret purchasing the other person's POV in a series because all that changes is the gender.  Marata Eros delivered Cas' story to perfection.  An awesome book.

Drawn is definitely an intriguing book.  It is so different, that it falls into many different genres:  YA, paranormal, mystery, action/suspense with a little bit of romance.  Gray draws the reader in immediately and I found myself reading through the book quickly.  Sasha has so many facets to her character; while I felt like I couldn't relate to her because of her lie detecting ability, at the same time I felt connected to her desire to fit in and have friends, while at the same time trying not to care what other people thought.  I enjoyed going on this amazing journey with Sasha and the unlikely friends she made along the way.  My one tiny complaint is that the author left me wondering at the end....so does that mean there is another book or will I never know the answer?  Hopefully that means there is a book two in the future!  I think many types of readers will enjoy this book because it crosses so many different genres.  I received a copy of this book via Netgalley.

Brant, mayor of Bright City, doesn't want shifters in his fine city. In an attempt to run out the shifters who have purchased a bar in the inner city, he meets with Rabb, alpha of his wolf pack and unwilling to give in without a fight. But both men have bigger issues. Someone is killing shifters and Rabb and Brant know they need to work together to find the killer.This book is so full of potential you choke on it. I wanted more, I needed more, so desperately did I desire more. I am fascinated by this world where humans, vampires, and shifters co-exist, where vampires and shifters have politics and prejudices, where vampires can stand in the sun and not drink blood to survive. But the book loses two stars because there is too much left out.The world building needed so much more fleshing out, the shifters and vampires needed more explanation (why doesn't a vampire need to drink blood to live?), and Rabb and Brant need more backstory because we find they were lovers many years ago and though we know Brant ended it the reason alone doesn't make sense.But I enjoyed the characters, Rabb and Brant are interesting apart and fun to watch together. Though Brant never bit Rabb which I really wanted to see. The mystery behind the killer is well written and I didn't figure it out till the end.If the author had spent more time expanding this story I could easily see this moving into 4-5 star territory. It has series potential and I'll admit I'll be watching to see what this author does. It would be a shame to leave this world behind completely.I received a copy of this story from the author at no charge in exchange for an honest review

I've really grown to like serial novellas. They're quick reads, there's not a long wait between releases like there can be for full-length books and when they're done well, you get a great story and characters. More bang for your buck, so to speak. Teaching Willow is an erotic serial, so you get an added dose of sexy with this one. Session One did just what I needed the first book in a serial to do: sucked me in and made me want more of the characters.I love the idea of this serial and I believe it's off to a great start. It was unique and sexy and even a bit mysterious. There's a lot to these characters and their story and I can't wait to see how it unfolds. The dynamic between Willow and Sage was interesting and I'm looking forward to more from the twins. I know there's bound to be some fallout sooner or later. Willow and Ebon together are fantastic. They're passionate and sensual. There's a definite chemistry. Yes, he's her professor, but they're all consenting adults. (Did I mention student/teacher romances are one of my guilty pleasures? They totally are.)I devoured this novella in about half an hour. I was completely sucked in from the start. It was smoking hot and the deceit made the story more interesting – and I know it's only going to get more interesting from here on out. I can't wait to see where Paige takes readers with the next novella. I'm hooked.I received a copy of this book from the author in exchange for an honest review.

I've struggled with my weight all my life. I've tried so many diets...even the weird ones. Can we say grapefruit diet! I have to maintain a sense of humor about it all because it really is a source of shame for me. Unfortunately, in our society, we are judged by our appearance. If you are overweight you are seen a sloppy and lazy. No one cares if you are going through some real deep personal stuff and food is your outlet. I can tell you that food has always been my outlet. I eat when I am emotional and the consequences of that are very real. Recently, a friend of mine recommended this book to me. The first words out of my mouth were: oh, another one. She said: No, this ain't another one. I know you love Japanese food so I though this would be perfect for you. You know what, she is RIGHT!!! I was blown away by the simplicity of the types of foods. The diet is actually doable!! Unlike other diet book authors, this author really makes the material really easy to understand. I am so excited to start this diet. Something has to change for me. If you have struggled  with you life like I have and truly make a difference, then get this book. I don't regret it one bit and I bet you won't either!!

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by this book.I should give fair warning that sports books are not my favorite. I read them, but I don't have any fantasies involving athletes and I don't get anything special out of the theme. However, I wanted to try "Rush Me" because it is Carina Press's first go at the New Adult genre and it is based in New York, my neck of the woods.Another preface is that I am a New Jersey Jewish girl. You wouldn't think that that would be relevant but it kinda is here. This book is very religion-y and very Jewish. They talk a lot about having Shabbat dinner and going home for Rosh Hashannah. There are a lot of Jewish references. The reason that I said I was Jewish before stating this next statement is so no one thinks I'm being a jerk: I didn't like all of the religious talk in this book. I don't like reading much about religion in general and here it felt out of place and odd. Just saying...I also didn't feel the romance between Rachael and Ryan. In the first few scenes he is a complete jerk to her and she still lusts over him and wants him. It just came across as desperate and like something a girl with low self-esteem would do. reviewText: "His Indecent Proposal" is the second book I've read by Lynda Chance, and from that reading two things are obvious: Chance has a distinctive writing voice and a fondness for Alpha males. Both of which I enjoy immensely. This book's premise is based on the standard boss/employee scenario. Jenna Hardin has worked in the accounting department of David Benton's family's company for six months. Although Jenna and David haven't spoken to each other, there's an intense animal attraction between them. The story reveals that David needs to marry in order to cement his future leadership of the company. For her part, Jenna needs money to pay off her overwhelming debt load. David proposes a marriage of convenience. He'll pay Jenna $200 000 if she marries him for two years. She agrees. This is where things get a bit hinky, and it's all because of the story's time line. In less than one week (somewhere around four or five days), the two characters go from not speaking to each other to a marriage of convenience to David's eventual suggestion they disregard all previous agreements and live together permanently as a proper couple. Really? That's madness. No matter how much I enjoy Chance's work, no matter how much I want to believe this is possible, the whole premise is unrealistic. I, as a reader, cannot abandon reality to that extent. Basically, what it comes down to is that Chance tried to cram way too much into too short a period of time. It makes her story unbelievable.

"The Witch Who Cried Wolf (Cry Wolf #1)" by Sarah Makela3 out of 5 starsIf you are looking for a light, quick read then stop here on the first book in a new series by Sarah Makela.  Mia has a huge secret.  To her family she's an unemployed college graduate who dabbles in Wicca and has no career prospects.  In reality, Mia is a powerful witch learning to harness her magic under her mentor Jessa.  When her long-time crush, Ethan, arrives on leave from the Army the two of them get caught up in an adventure that will change their lives forever.  With only each other to lean on and years of attraction between them they must decide whether to trust in love or go their separate ways.Ethan is your typical alpha male lead.  He's hot, well built (thanks to the Army), and fiercely protective of Mia.  In his mind she is out of his reach but that doesn't stop him from wanting her and aching to close the gap that exists between them.  I would have liked a little more character development before his world was turned upside down and I thought he accepted the supernatural world's existence a bit too easily.  However, I appreciated his internal struggle when it came to his relationships with Mia and her brother/his best friend Nolan.Mia could have used more development, too.  She seems very closed off and lonely.  She exists in a world where not many really know who she is and that includes her family.  Mia tries very hard to fit into a mold that she thinks will make her family love and accept her.  However that wasn't the impression I got from her family.  Her parents seem very laid back and I felt like they would have understood had she come clean with them about her magic.  I got the sense that her brother, Nolan, knew she was hiding things from him and wanted nothing more than her honesty.  Plus, he seemed to be pushing Mia and Ethan together a little at times.  It's almost as though Makela underestimated her characters and it showed through in the story.I enjoy a quick read and it's nice to finish a book in one sitting....BUT...the pacing here is off in comparison to amount of story Makela is trying a get through.  I honestly think the book would have been better had Mia just been a known witch.  Had that been the case, Makela could have focused the story on the werewolves without all the angst of Mia hiding her powers, too.  Perhaps Makela will adjust these things in subsequent books to come.  For now, I will continue the journey with these characters and see where the road leads.*I was given a complimentary copy of this book in exchange for an honest review.*Shannon, My Secret Book Spot

*I received this book from the author in exchange for an honest review*I love fairy tales. On shelves in my office lie the complete works of the Brothers Grimm and Hans Christian Anderson. I also have quite a collection of non-English fairy tales as well. What I wouldn't give to see the Museum of Magical and Rare Artifacts, not to mention Everafter itself.Bianca Frost is an ordinary teenager who works with her mother at their fairy tale museum. She always thought it strange that only family is allowed to work at the museum. Of course, she also thought the exhibits were all reproductions of famous fairy tale items. One night she learns just how real it all is when she returns home to find her mother battling a witch with magic. Thus begins Bianca's journey into the world of magic and the importance of their guardianship over the real artifacts in the museum.The secondary characters were interesting. Best friend Ming was a bit annoying and whiny, but I think that just added to the realism. Not all girls like being dumped in the middle of a dangerous (and dirty) quest. Add to that the lack of toilets and showers...well that could make one crabby girl. Bianca sucks it up and does what she needs to, which makes Ming seem all the more whiny. Prince Ferdinand is everything I'd expect a fairy tale prince to be: charming, brave, gorgeous, and witty. Terrence is Bianca's love interest and Prince Ferdinand's best friend. He may lack the prince's outward charm, but he more than makes up for it with his quiet perseverance. Ferdinand would be lost without Terrence (so would Bianca). The bear is just the best (don't get it?...sorry no spoilers...you'll have to read and find out for yourself).I love the flowing imagery Liz DeJesus uses to describe the fairy tale world. It was so easy to picture the scenery in my mind's eye. The artifacts that Bianca drags along on her journey add whimsy to the story. This is a quick read. Once I picked up First Frost, I didn't bother putting it down until I was finished.I recommend this book to everyone, middle school and up, that has a soft spot for fairy tales.You can also find this review at [...]

Redemption is the story about Ayanna and Jonathan that we met in Release, the first book in the Iris series by Rebecca Lynn. I was looking forward to reading this since I enjoyed Release so much. This is a stand-alone and not a continued story from the first book, but I highly recommend you read Release before you read Redemption. One, because it is a better book and Two, there is a spoiler in Redemption for how the first book ends. I thought Redemption was OK, but definitely not as good as the first in the series and will not be on my re-read shelf. I loved the story of Ryann and Jeremy in the first book. I felt like there was a good balance of sweetness, romance, and suspense. In Redemption, I felt like we lost some of this balance. The "suspense" was minimal and over quickly. I enjoyed the build-up to Ayanna and Jonathan's relationship, but once they were together, I felt like the story stalled out. There was minimal conversations and plot and just steamy scene after steamy scene. I like an erotic romance as much as anyone, but I feel like that was all we got after that point. Once they became a couple, there was no more plot. The writing was done very well and there were minimal editing errors, but, in my opinion, the second half of the book could have been condensed into one chapter where you get their HEA. I did enjoy the glimpses of Ryann and Jeremy that we got and we do get to know other friends and family members better in this book, I am assuming this is to set us up for the future books in this series. Will I read the next one? At this moment in time, I am unsure if I will.

reviewText: Okay, I admit it. I finished the last book in the Seasons of the Moon series and I just couldn’t say goodbye. Crazy, I know, but such is the life of a book addict ;)The approach of this series is a little different than the Seasons of the Moon. Basically because the first 4 installments are short (this one was only 53 pages.) That doesn’t mean that it is lacking though. An awful lot happened in those 53 pages. The pack has fallen into a routine and they’re even growing in numbers. Both sanctuaries are running full force with Rylie watching over the wolves in her pack. She’s still not comfortable running things alone, but she has plenty of support from both Seth and Abel.In true S.M. Reine fashion, things don’t stay peaceful for long. There’s tension within the pack and danger from outside it. Then there’s the fact that there’s something going on between Rylie and Abel that even they’re not sure about. I’m not sure I’m happy with where things are going – even knowing where they end up (just another friendly warning to read these series in the right order.)I picked up the first book in this series by itself then I immediately got my hands on the box set that contains books 1-4. It’s about the size of a short novel combined (246 pages) and it’s really broken up into ‘episodes’ instead of books. I’m pretty sure that’s how I’m going to read and review the rest of it. Mainly because the cliff hanger in New Moon Summer was brutal… o.O

reviewText: I have been waiting for this for a while and it's just as good as I wanted it to be!The good: We get a bit of a break in that Rowan isn't investigating or fighting anything. She's supposed to be a Liaison and keep the peace during talks between vampires and humans. The plot pulled me in with the mystery of who was trying to instigate war but kept me reading on into the wee hours with the exploration of Rowan's relationship with her adopted father. That was really refreshing to read about. The romance between Rowan and Clive deepens and becomes more public as well. I just love the way those two are written - their relationship is more than lust or instantaneous attraction. It's mutual respect and admiration as well. So much sexier than that "magical soulmates since birth" stuff that's being written by others.The bad: I can't actually think of a single thing I didn't enjoy about this book. Maybe if I had to nit pick I would say that at times the political descriptions can get a bit tedious but the way it's described, you can tell there are undercurrents in the way the characters vote in the meetings.Bottom line: A great addition to the series. It looks like the author set it up for another book and I can't wait!

There are memoirs or autobiographies that are entertaining, or interesting, or funny reads, that are enjoyable on a base level.  This is not one of those memoirs.  Instead, it is a heart wrenching, and at sometimes depressing and upsetting real life story, that ends up being very inspirational, and gives you a different outlook on life.Trevor Kleinhans has not had an easy go of things in life.  Growing up gay in 1980's South Africa, he has had to live through sexual abuse as a child, apartheid in his home country, being forced into military service, finding out he was HIV positive, and battled a crack cocaine addiction.  Like I said, he has not had an easy go of things.  But through all of the struggle and hardships in his life, he has come out the other end stronger, and ultimately successful, career-wise.It says this book took 5 years to write, and I believe it. I mean technically, since it is the story of his life, it has taken him his ENTIRE LIFE to write the story, but actually putting it down into words was probably no easy task.  It feels like it comes from a very genuine place (I guess it would be weird if it felt false...), and I feel very fortunate to be able to read his story, and share his experiences with him.  Even though I have no first-hand experience whatsoever.This book is one that will change your perspective on the mundane and trivial problems in your life that everyone lets bothers them, and hopefully change your outlook for the better.

reviewText: 3-3.5 starsThis was a cute and sexy story. I liked Jimmy and Lia and their story was enjoyable.Lia is the daughter of a Governor and a nice woman. She unfortunately has gotten caught up in her father's political career, especially since her mother has had health issues that keeps her out of the lime light. Another downfall of this is that her father is trying to push her in to marriage with the son of a Senator because it would make a good political connection but Lia isn't willing to go that far.Jimmy is a marine and works for a team that does a lot of undercover work. He and his brothers grew up on a farm but Jimmy and his brother, Jack, joined the Marines and are now on the same team. Jimmy has never had any problems getting women but has never found one to settle down with.Jimmy and his team are tasked to go undercover as waiters at a black tie affair due to a possible security risk. Lia and Jimmy catch each other's eyes and they exchange glances multiple times. Lia slips Jimmy her number and he calls her as soon as the event is over. They meet at her hotel and have a hot night but they don't get much time together. Lia still thinks that Jimmy is a waiter when he leaves the next morning but hopes he'll call regardless. Jimmy had planned to call Lia as he found an unexpected connection with her. Unfortunately, Jimmy's team gets sent to catch a terrorist and Jimmy is sent undercover almost immediately.After being gone about 6 months, Jimmy gets caught up in a bad situation and gets injured and sent home to recover. Jimmy has been thinking about Lia during the whole time he's been gone and thinking of her helped him get through some tough spots. He wants to call Lia when he gets back but it's been so long he doesn't feel he can. Lia has been thinking of him all this time as well. She wanted him to call her and has been on the lookout for him at every event she's attended since then. Lia liked Jimmy a lot and was definitely upset that he didn't call her again. They meet back up unexpectedly and their connection is just as strong and hot. They both want to get together in a more permanent way (yeah, it's kind of an insta-love) but have some mis-understandings to get through. They get to a good point though and the story ends with them starting their HEA.This was an enjoyable story. It was short and therefore not greatly detailed but the story was cute and I liked the characters and how it ended. I may try more of the series in the future. :D

The hero is an ex-pirate (OK, privateer or maybe pirate who pirates only from pirates) so I expected a little emotional swashbuckling here.  But no.  This is a generic, somewhat uninteresting romance.If you readThe Ugly Duchess (Happily Ever After...), you know all about Sir Griffin Barry, cousin of the hero of that book and renowned pirate who left his bride on their wedding night before consummation of the marriage and found himself on the high seas.  He spends the next 14 years pirating from pirates and slave ships, releasing the slaves, investing booty wisely and becoming a rich man.  An injury to his leg requires him to give up his pirating ways and he heads home.Griffin's wife Phoebe has been living an independent life and is not looking forward to or hoping for Griffin's return.  I, on the other hand, as a reader, was looking forward to this reunion, expecting major fireworks, with resentment, distrust, disgust and dislike of the hero on the part of the heroine.  Major groveling on the part of the hero would also have been good and most of the novel spent in a long and difficult reconciliation.But no.  Hero returns home.  Heroine is there with three children.  Hero sleeps with heroine.  That's basically it.  Everybody is happy.  (Except, I guess, for me.)  I also forgot to mention that there was some sort of estrangement between hero and his father and that also turned out to be a nonevent.So I found this to be disappointing and a bit boring.  I wanted some conflict between H and h.  I got nothing.  BTW, the novella takes up only 76% of the download.  The rest is Eloisa James promoting her other work.  Is she hard up for money lately?  She does a lot of self-promotion in her books' afterwords.

I have been a fan of this series from the beginning and I admit, I enjoyed when Denis and Marcia got a chance to step to the forefront in Books 2 and 3, but the real heart and soul of this series has always been Brian Yi.  This self-sacrificing kid with a short shelf-life and a thing about the cops who keep trying to kill him jumps out in a book set just days after the dark aftermath of the DC attacks.  Brian is back, center stage here, and he brings with him a whole bunch of revelations that rocked me as they came marching out.  No spoilers, but the title is meaningful on several levels.  All the old favorites are back, including Penny, and we get to find out a little more about her background as well, probably in advance of her own book, which word on the street indicates she is getting sooner or later.  This story just races along and even the slower scenes seem carefully crafted for one effect or another.  Author P.S. Power is clearly on top of his game here.One of the most important features of this book is the growth we get to see in Brian as a multi-dimensional, fully developed character.  Sure, he was always crazy brave, thanks to his first modality, but here we get to see him grow in experience and learn about regret, and forgiveness, and develop some the wisdom he will need to survive what is to come.  This book was a little shorter than I like, but other than that I have to give this latest entry in the Infected saga all 5 stars.

This M/M erotic romance sports a lot of assets:- it has a nice, elaborated, character-driven plot that is always compelling, except perhaps halfway through when Josh meets Julian again. Tension slacks in those pages but it takes off again after a little while. I would have appreciated it if the author had made more use of the work-setting of the characters but the story is complete as it is.- its characters are exotic enough (musicians and actors) to be more interesting than average people but they are also fully rounded, likeable and make one wish one could meet them in real life (at least I wish I could meet Josh, Corey and Travis, I really do). My only issue is about Josh and Corey being 24 when they clearly need to be closer to 30 to be entirely consistent with their behaviour and thoughts.- sex scenes are many, raunchy and very sexy. They are very sexy not because they are unbelievably well written (though they ARE well written) but because one always gets the feeling the people involved care deeply for each other and that is sexy in itself.Reading the blurb and a couple of pages in the first half I worried a little. Authors (especially lady-authors, truth to be told) have this pervasive fetish for dominance and submission. They do like to put their gay characters into tight little boxes, filing some as strong-dominant-active (and usually big and brawny) and others as conflicted-submissive-passive (and usually lean and blond and boyish). Some go so far as to transform erotica into something frankly unhealthy where the need to be dom/sub goes beyond the wall of the bedchamber. A selected few even try to pass on the idea that rape and enslavement are sexy...At first I thought Mr River was bound to follow that unfortunate path.There are a couple of pages at the beginning, when Travis debates his own feelings with himself, that had me cringe because he seems to be willing to relinquish control permanently to Corey. I do not know whether the author changed his mind halfway through or had it planned from the start but luckily things change. The BDSM element is relevant and shown explicitly but it remains just that: a kink that is part of the characters' sex life but is not all encompassing. BDSM being just a nice little game, it is sexy to read those kinky scenes.AND the lovers here are all versatile, thank goodness for (not so) small favours!- the love story is incredibly satisfying. Travis and Corey fall in love a little too fast and I presume the author could have devised a way to have them get to it more slowly but other than that the whole of it is incredibly heart-warming.- writing is neat and fluid. The POV shifts between the three leads from chapter to chapter and sometimes the same scene is seen again through different eyes which is not entirely new a device but it can work well if well used.There are no typos but grammar is faulty at times. Nothing too bad or evident but this work could use a revision which should also take care of a couple of mistakes in characters' names: Corey becomes Cody and Julian Jules. Characters break the fourth wall often which is fine as the author manages to give an individual voice to each. Only here and there the characters describe things they cannot possibly know, for example I remember Travis saying "...my eyes smoldering..." but there are several other examples of this mistake in logic.That said this is a nice, romantic read I can only recommend. But, please, someone change the model on the cover...

He breaks down the science of habits and how you can finally free yourself from old addicting unhealthy habits and instill healthier habits. Determined to make it into the most elite reviewer club Amazon has, I showed up at the appointed time.  As instructed, I was dressed in some comfy reading clothes, including my favorite baggy cardigan.  If I made it into the club, I'd get first crack at the best self-published writing that Amazon has to offer.  I knew that it was a long shot, but I'd do anything to make it in.I had a thrill of nervousness when I found out my test would be to read this short story.  In all my clumsy fumblings, I'd never before reviewed a college secret society-themed erotic short with elements of heavy domination and humiliation."It sounds so implausible," I murmured.  "I don't know if I will be able to read . . . all of it.""You can and you will," the bookish young man standing in front of me growled.  "Now download this story immediately."I downloaded it to the Kindle App on my phone.  The phone's memory is pretty small, so I wasn't sure if it would all fit.  Fortunately, this file is small too, but not so small that I didn't feel a thrill when I saw that it was done downloading."Is that it?" I asked, biting my lip.  "All I need to do is read it and write a review?""Not quite."  The bookish young man pushed his glasses up on his nose and smiled slowly at me.  "Come over here in front of this window.  Read it right here.""But members of my book club are standing out there," I stammered.  "You mean they are going to see me reading this?"  I had already opened the file and noticed how clumsy the author's language was, how she didn't even use "abuts" correctly."Oh, yes," he murmured back, his fingers running slowly over the screen of my phone where the words pulsed electronically.  "They are all going to see you reading this."Thinking of how much I wanted to be in the club, I slowly walked over to the window.  With their eyes on me, I dutifully finished the story."I don't think a jet of water can penetrate anally without causing internal injuries," I protested.  "Also, I really don't understand how this club operates.""Save your opinion for the review," my tormenter sneered.Finally, it was over.  I was confused and mentally sore, but determined to write my review.  As I asked if he had a computer available, the bookish young man smiled."That was part one of the initiation.  You will have to purchase, read, and review the rest of the series in order to be in the super-secret-awesome-reviewer club.""Forget this," I cried.  "I'd rather review on my own forever than pay for this stuff!"TL; DR:  This story is not very good at all.

Rating 4 1/2 StarsThe first thing that popped in my mind by the time I finished the story was unique. Yes, the heroine is a bit of a blue-stock, but so are her sisters. Normally, you just find one young woman in the family whose a bit of a blue-stock instead of all the sisters. However, they are vary of degrees of blue-stocking. In Cara Elliot's Scandalously Yours, we focus more on the eldest, Olivia Sloane, who is considered odd by the ton. She goes out of her way to be different, because she doesn't care what society really thinks of her. While her ideas would be a bit off the wall, this charming young lady holds some secrets.Then we meet the Earl of Wrexham, who would be consider a stick in the mud. He's on the hunt to find the perfect countess, after all he has a young boy at home who is in need of a mother. So, he's trying find the perfect woman among the "simpering featherhead" young ladies. Of course, he believes he has  found a likely candidate in Lady Serena, yet his son, Prescott would disagree. Nope he sees her as Lady Steel Corsets. So, Prescott sets out to find the perfect match for his father. Oh dear.Let's just say that Scandalously Yours is a fun witty read. I mean you have John (Earl of Wrexham) has his handful throughout this book, as he's trying to find his a step-mother for his son, his son trying to find the perfect woman for dad, and he's trying to match wits with Olivia. While he's doing all this he's trying to fight social reform, if only he can find a mysterious writer. I truly enjoyed this book with the on going match between John and Olivia. Predator's Kiss by Rosanna Leo was such a cute, funny, and sexy bear shifter tale that I couldn't get enough of! I haven't read that many paranormal romance novels featuring bear shifters, but I am totally in love and want a bear shifter of my own now. Rosanna, can you please send me a Ryland? Pretty please? :)From the beginning, I just knew that this was a type of read I was going to enjoy from start to finish and I certainly did. There was a nice blend of romance, suspense, humor, and a sprinkle of action with a good pacing to go along with it. I also really adored the main characters Ryland and Lia. Here was this big bear shifter and this petite human erotica romance author (who has a fear of furry animals by the way) and you wouldn't think that would fit together, but they complemented each other well. I also liked that Ryland and Lia didn't jump into bed right after meeting each other. There was a nice buildup and anticipation and when they both finally gave in to the temptation let me just say that it was very sexy. The thing Ryland did to Lia with that jar of honey was oh-so-hot!Aside from the main characters the secondary characters definitely made an impression on me too especially Ryland's rockstar musician brother Soren. He definitely is someone I would love to read more of and get to know better. He was quite the character. Soren was responsible for most of my laugh out loud moments while reading this book and for that I took an instant liking to him. What can I say? I love a man who can make me laugh (in real life and in fiction). I can't wait to read his story and see what kind of woman will bring him to his knees.Overall, Predator's Kiss was a very entertaining read that I found myself enjoying a lot. Having not read a Rosanna Leo book before, Predator's Kiss was a fabulous introduction to Rosanna Leo's writing. I found her writing style and voice to be easily engaging. Without a doubt, she'll be an author who I will be reading more of in the future. Now, I need to get my hands on Soren's book ASAP!*I received a review copy from the author in exchange or an honest review.

His dad was old and was put into a nursing home.  John stayed and turned the dealership into a legitimate business.Things were going well for awhile until a prostitute was found dead in the trunk (boot) of one of his cars.  Because  it was one of John's cars and because of his family background, he was the top suspect.  When asked where he was on the night of the murder, he did have an alibi, he was sleeping with one of their detectives.  Their next suspect, was Freddie Metcalf, John's one and only salesman.  John knew thatFreddie couldn't have murdered the girl, so he decided to investigate the murder on his own, giving the cops the information that he found.The book was good with interesting characters.  I will be looking forward to more books from John Barlow.
