Well, this was quite an interesting read. Michael F. Stewart has definitely delivered an entertaining and complex read. Stewart mixes both Egyptian and Christian religions. The story revolves around a war between two opposing sides. The story is about the fall of the phoenix. The balance of good and evil must be restored. But it seems the evil side, Shemsu Seth, have special plans in play to make sure they break the coming prophecy.I won't lie, I had a tough time getting into this book. It started off interesting then took a bit of a turn and slowed down. I am all for worldbuilding, but I couldn't connect with the characters. They don't really have any discernible personalities that make them different from any other. We know they are preparing for a war. One side is killing off the other, the Shemsu Hor, who protect the 24 bones of Osiris's spine. They are trying to stop the Shemsu Seth from killing off the companions that hold pieces of the spine and giving them to the Pharaoh of Shemsu Seth. The book follows Sam (Samiya) is the child of shadow and is the leader of the Shemsu Seth. Her mother, Tara, is the a part of the Sisters of Isle. The Sisters keep the balance of good and evil. Along with Samiya, on the opposite side is David (Dawid). David left Canada to go back to Egypt from a message he receives from in his email. He also has a relict that may be a very big discovery. But he is means more to the war that he originally thought.Like I said, the book was a little slow, but once David and his story is introduced, he kicks up a bit. The book really kicks off in about the second half. I loved it. Lots of twists and turns. The characters and the plot change pace. I love the action. This isn't your usual Urban Fantasy and it is makes it stand out. The book is suspenseful with some paranormal aspects thrown in. I really loved where this book went.Overall I would recommend this mainly for the second half. I enjoyed it, it just needed a bit more of a pick me up in the beginning. It may be hard to wrap your head around a few things in the book. Like terms and such that could use an explanation or too. The book can be a little confusing at times. But the buildup is still good once you see the connection between the stories. Sam becomes quite the character in the second half and you will love where the story goes. I won't spoil you, but it is good. I love Stewart's take on Urban Fantasy. 24 Bones was pretty dark and intense. But the book takes on more than one genre and is well written overall despite some of my complaints. I say check it out.
summary: A beautiful and complex Urban Fantasy read.

Disclaimer: I received a copy of this title from the author in exchange for an honest review. This has in no way affected my opinion of the book.When Ms Reine contacted me and asked if I'd like to read Sacrificed in Shadow, I thought Sure. I mean, I read Six Moon Summer a little while ago, and have the following books in that series of S.M.'s to check out (if I ever get five minutes to do so), and I enjoyed what I sampled of her writing, so I figured I'd be safe. What I hadn't banked on was the massive part played in SiS by certain characters from SMS (I don't read blurbs--so, shoot me), and the fact I suddenly realised just how much of their development I've missed by not having read those already.That being said, this didn't hinder my enjoyment of Ms Reine's latest read. It merely made me want to get my finger out and read those books of hers even more. There also seems to be a crossover (though smaller) from her other--Death's Hand--books, but other than to mention what I have already, I'm not going to delve into that because I think you should find out how they all intertwine for yourself.Now, onto the story. We have a few of POV's in this title--what I'm going to consider as the two MC's--as well as very small amounts from another POV (I *think* I recall there being only one other).Elise seems to be the biggest player through the book, despite it not being her POV that opens the story, and in truth, I wasn't so sure I'd like her at first. I mean, those female MC's with an attitude that seems borne of just their knowledge that they're faster and tougher than most usually makes me annoyed with them, and means they have to work harder for my approval. Well, Elise most certainly managed to pull me over to her dark side, and trust me when I say it wasn't long before I totally TeamE and egging her toward working everything out.Alongside her, we have Lincoln--the seemingly straight-laced, law-abiding, small-town, good Christian (did I miss anything?) cop. Now, don't be fooled by my description, as this guy is not all that he appears, and he certainly has plenty of demons (heh) of his own to battle, as well as inner turmoil, and boy, oh boy, did I want him to be strong--because, man, I LOVED Lincoln's character. He's so ... FULL! And HOT, but without even seeming hot. Hot, in an understated, unassuming, unaware, kind of way--if that even makes sense?And around both of those, we have everyone else. And there are a LOT of them. However, the only place I found myself slightly confused and straining to keep up was the second time we get to meet the brothers, Seth and Able, as well as everyone else who comes with them, and I had to try and keep track of who all of these good folk were. Not to mention the `baddies', and the sturdy sidekicks working for Elise from the sidelines, and the ex-lover, who I simply could not get a handle on because he was just THAT good at manipulation he easily had my mind yanking in all directions. I guess what I'm trying to say here is, YES, there's a big cast. But Ms Reine does such a fab job of making each and every one of them so individual, hence making them easily recognisable, that getting to know them was a cinch. This is certainly one full-bodied bunch of peeps.And then we have the plot. This plot will keep you guessing. EVERYTHING about this book will keep you guessing. Any time I thought I had it all figured out, I turned out to be wrong. Any time I thought I had a character's number, turned out I had them all wrong. Even characters who were on the `good guy' team kept me on my toes and trying to figure them out--because this is so craftfully weaved, it appears so many times that pretty much any one of them could be on the `dark side', and absolutely not a one of them is safe from manipulation and betrayal--NONE of them are as safe as they think.To wrap up: this book has mystery and intrigue and sex appeal from the off, and each of those combined with a great body of characters will keep you turning the pages for more. From werewolves, to demons, to angel, and filled with magic, it pretty much covers all bases, and I'm really looking forward to finding out where S.M. takes this tale next. Hopefully, I'll have read the preceding books by then and caught up.

"Come on, don't be a tease. You can call that a preview. Now I want the whole show."Boy, this book IS the whole show! Nothing sexual is off limits, which makes sense because the main character is an escort. Coop has been an escort for 8 years, so you have to know that he has tried it all and seen it all - at least for the most part. He understands his clients' needs, and even with new ones, he plays along, even experiencing some m/m action - that excites and disturbs him at the same time.This is a raw story, more so than I expected - it is hardcore sex, and it leaves nothing to the imagination, but it had to be done this way because it is told from Coop's point of view, and he lives the life - so readers get an up close and personal view, and yes, the kink might disturb some, but the synopsis provides a warning for what's to come.It's a fairly quick read that sucks you in and takes you on an erotic ride and then lets you, literally and figuratively, get off and become invested in the tragic back story of Coop and Nic as well as Coop's old/new relationship with Mia.The male POV is perfect for a story like Tease. Readers are allowed to get into Coop's psyche - even if that in itself is a bit disturbing. Missy makes her readers understand why Coop chose this path, and despite the fact that we may not agree with what Coop is doing, by getting the story from his point of view, we can at least see his reasoning rather than hearing it second hand from a female point of view.The hardest part I had with Coop is that he doesn't own his choices - it's always because his family needed him to do this, and he didn't see any other way, even though it doesn't seem like he tried too hard to figure one out; Also, the fact that he didn't walk away for love and only does it when one of his clients gives him an out is baffling to me.  But I think this is exactly what Missy wants us to feel - we seem to be TEASED throughout the entire story, and it is a brilliant way to draw readers in and keep them engrossed until the end.If you're in the mood to walk on the kinky side and read from a tell it like it is male perspective, take that walk with Tease!Complimentary copy provided by author/publisher for an honest review.4 poison apples! My heart breaks a little every time I read R.H. Ramsey’s work. What leads a person to address abuse, mental illness and addiction? It’s so easy not to talk about these tough topics, and yet they’re clearly issues that Ramsey seeks to bring to the forefront. The first short story of the novel, “Fist”, is a story of abuse told from the perspective of the abuser. Ramsey gives us pathology of a man who terrorizes his young daughters and wife. The rage of the abuser and fear of the children and the hints of brutality are soul ripping. The story is written with a beautiful flow that makes no excuse for this antagonist, but shows the helplessness of everyone involved.Undone: Excerpts, short stories and other musings is free form. The placement of the excerpts and stories feel random brought together by theme. The snippets of the novels chosen work well in this format.  We meet Landon of Just Beneath the Surface II: Landon’s Story (Volume 2) at the start of his novel when he walks into his home to find his girlfriend strung out again and he wearily works to sober her up. Tying into that excerpt is a short story entitled “Oxycotin” which chronicles a young life absorbed by addiction. There is consideration given to theme and an inability to escape terrible and destructive situations that may have more in common than a reader may have originally thought.“My Mother’s Shadow” tells the reader symbolically that bringing these issues to light opens them to the world and gives the reader hope in the poignant oppressiveness of the issue.Ramsey’s stories are hard to read. They are raw, meaningful and intended to make a reader think and they accomplish that goal in spades. Hug your children tight and pick up Undone: Excerpts, short stories and other musings if you’re not sure Ramsey’s writing is for you and fall for her clean style and leave a bit of your soul behind.

This book has a healthy suggestion for prevention of Alzheimer's based on scientific research studies and covering nutrition, physical exercise, mental exercise through continuous learning, cultivating social networks, and spiritual practice.Here are several tips from the book:NUTRITIONOne study showed that people who drank fresh fruit and vegetable juices more than three times a week were 76% less likely to develop Alzheimer's disease than those who drank juices less than once a week. The study showed the protective benefits of juice appeared to be particularly enhanced in people who had a genetic marker linked to an increased risk of Alzheimer's disease known as ApoE-4.In one study scientists in Germany found that increased physical activity was associated with a lower incidence of dementia. Those who exercised at least three times a week were half as likely to have developed dementia as those who reported no physical activity.In a study at Loma Linda University, a study group found that a daily glass of pomegranate juice could halve the build-up of harmful proteins linked to Alzheimer's disease.Men and women who reported eating fish at least once a week had a 60 % lower risk of getting Alzheimer's compared to those who rarely or almost never ate fish.A study on the effect of blood caffeine levels found tat older adults who drank the equivalent of 3 - 4 cups of coffee per day were protected from developing Alzheimer's.The researchers found that people who drank more than 2 cups of green tea per day had a 50 % lower incidence of cognitive impairment. EGCG is an antioxidant found in green tea that researchers frequently study for its health benefits.  The researchers used EGCG to effectively untangle the proteins causing Alzheimer's and restore the pristine state of brain tissue.People with diabetes - especially type 2 diabetes - are at higher risk of eventually developing Alzheimer's disease. Taking steps to prevent or control diabetes may help reduce the risk of Alzheimer's disease.  Alzheimer's is being called Diabetes Type 3 by some researchers.  Researchers found that insulin is not just produced in the pancreas, but also in the brain.  And they discovered that insulin and its growth factors, which are necessary for the survival of brain cells, contribute to the progression of Alzheimer's.In Alzheimer's patients portions of their brain start to atrophy, or starve, leading to impaired functioning and eventual loss of memory, speech, movement and personality. In effect, the brain can begin to atrophy from starvation if it becomes insulin resistant and loses its ability to convert glucose to energy.  Ketone bodies may restore and renew neuron and nerve function in the brain after the damage has set in.  They are found in coconut oil.  A bit over two tablespoons of coconut oil (35 ml or 7 level teaspoons) would supply with equivalent of 20 grams of MCT which is indicated as either a preventative measure against degenerative neurological diseases, or as a treatment for already established case.PHYSICAL EXERCISEThose who exercised at least twice a week in middle age were 50 % less likely to develop Alzheimer's disease in old age.  Population studies have suggested that exercise which raises your heart rate for at least 30 minutes several times a week can lower your risk of Alzheimer's.  Physical activity appears to inhibit Alzheimer's like brain changes, slowing the development of a key feature of the disease. A lack of exercise affects Alzheimer's disease in a profound way.Resistance training is particularly beneficial for improving the cognitive abilities of older adults.  Those who weight lift experience the greatest improvement.Exercise not only prevents the normal shrinkage (atrophy) from occurring, but also stimulates neurogenesis - the formation of new brain cells and connections!  So, not only can you keep your brain from shrinking, but you can make it even bigger and stronger.INTELLECTUAL STIMULATION and MUSICIntellectually stimulating careers and hobbies, like learning a new language, playing a musical instrument or doing crossword puzzles or word games, build extra brainpower.It is important to challenge your brain, as in memory recall, learning or doing something new.  Find what's interesting to you, master it and move on to the next challenge.Learning different languages and musical instrument training may reduce the effects of mental decline associated with aging.  Studies showed that bilinguals experience onset symptoms of dementia years later than monolinguists.Sustaining musical activity during advanced age may enhance thinking ability, neutralizing any negative impact of age and even lack of education.  Musicians scored higher on tests of mental acuity, visual-spatial judgment, verbal memory and recall, and motor dexterity.The mental process required to play a musical instrument may work in the same way as juggling a dual languages to strengthen the connections in your brain over time.RELAXATIONDeep breathing, relaxation, stress reduction, laughter - help to protect from Alzheimer's.SPIRITUALITYNegative or "toxic" thoughts affect our mental, emotional and physical health.  Thinking and feeling anger, fear and frustration, causes DNA to change shape according to thoughts and the associated feelings.  The study showed that the poor quality of the DNA codes was reversed with feelings of love, joy, appreciation and gratitude!Un-forgiveness may be the most damaging toxic thoughts, according to the neuroscientist Dr. Leaf.  We can literally protect our brain and heart by extending forgiveness.

The main characters for this installment are Ian Gregson and Tessa Lockwood, whom we both meet in Serendipity. Ian is the Managing Director for his family’s company, Gregson’s Resorts and Tessa is a member of the Management Support Team that works for Ian. Born and raised in a wealthy English family, Ian is the poster child for professionalism and self-control.When Tessa Lockwood is transferred to San Francisco to be a part of Ian’s Management Support Team, she immediately catches Ian’s eye. Tessa is unobtainable for Ian, as he finds out she is a married woman. True to his English Boarding School morals, this is a line that he refuses to cross. He watches her and fantasizes about her but refuses to act on it since she is a taken woman. Ian works hard to keep his attraction to Tessa under wraps. After two long years of pining away for Tessa, an opportunity opens for Ian.Tessa’s marriage of convenience to her Journalist husband Peter abruptly ends when Peter take a job in Bahrain. He leaves the country and files for divorce leaving Tessa completely alone. After a few months, Tessa finally lets her co-workers including Ian know that she is now a single woman. Their attraction for each other becomes palpable and is something that neither one of them can deny. Breaking all of his rules, Ian and Tessa finally give in to their desires and admit that there is more to their employee/employer relationship.This book is written in third person and does have a HEA. Author has a beautiful writing style. Her writing is very descriptive and does a great job of relaying the emotion of the characters. reviewText: I tried my first Puzzlebook a little more than a year ago, and I've played most of the ones that have been released since then, and I still love the challenge of solving the puzzles. Like the earlier Puzzlebooks, "100 Puzzle Quizzes" is a single-player collection of mind exercises/brainteasers with no time limits, so there's no pressure to solve a puzzle unless you want to set your own time limits.All of the one hundred puzzles are visual. I started with #1, and as I advanced, the difficulty of the puzzles gradually increased. I didn't have too much of a problem solving the first dozen or so puzzles, but they became progressively more challenging, and with some of them, my first answer was incorrect (you can keep guessing until you get it right). The first puzzle that gave me a problem was #6 - Wire Signs, but once I understood how the "Wire" puzzles worked, I was able to solve the later ones. One of my favorite puzzles was #25 - Bird Totem Pole. You could solve this with some geometry and basic mathematics, but take a shot at it using only deductive logic for a simpler but more elegant answer. The puzzles don't have to be solved sequentially - you can begin anywhere and work in any order. The solution pages show very clearly what the correct answers are and the logic behind the solutions.The puzzles included a number of different types, most of them fitting into the categories of visual, spatial, counting, geometry, matchstick, coins, searching, and deductive logic. I've seen similar types of puzzles on IQ tests, so these would be great practice for such a test. I know very little about the functioning of the brain, but I think these puzzles will give your logic circuits a pretty good workout.I worked the puzzles on my Kindle Fire HD tablet. These are the same puzzles that are in "100 Puzzle Quizzes (Interactive Puzzlebook for E-readers)," but they're in color, and they're intended for devices with color touch screens.As much enjoyment as I had with "100 Puzzle Quizzes," I'm really looking forward to turning some of my whiz kid nieces and nephews loose with the puzzles some rainy day. They've worked several of the Puzzlebooks, and they love solving the puzzles as much as I do.
summary: Challenging fun for the whole family

He believes that a successful trader should only consider the theory as a tool.  More importantly, the market must be carefully studied and analyzed. First things first, I need to get something out of the way.TEN YEARS??? T. E. N. years. As in a lot of cases I had not read the synopsis for book two before I started. I almost died. Ten years. I am still in shock. My heart hurt. Like it actually, hurt. Ten friggin years."There were so many things Sebastian and I had to work out: we'd both been single for so long that blending our lives together wasn't going to be easy.  I'd promised Sebastian we'd find a way. He deserved to be loved for everything he was. And for whatever crazy reason he had, he loved me, too."Okay, so that little freak out is over. Let us discuss the book. I didn't think it was possible to fall more in love with Sebastian, but somehow it happened. I simply love this man.Sadly, Caroline started to annoy me a little. I completely blame her for her and Sebastian being apart for ten years. I know she has always worried about the age difference but I just never felt she gave a justified reason for not going back after him when she promised she would. Then, she has the audacity to blame Sebastian for his behavior while they were apart? In my opinion, she has no right to have any kind of opinion on how he spent their time apart. He thought she was gone, never to be seen again. I don't hold anything he did during that time against him, she has no right to either. Okay, rant over."Why didn't you come back?" he sobbed."I waited and waited for you, like I said I would, but you never came back! Why? Why didn't you come back? I love you I love you I love you."And Sebastian... *sigh* Sebastian. Honestly, he is just perfect. He is such a swoonworthy character. He has a way with words that just makes you want to melt. He is so open and honest with his feelings. I adore him.What could have made it better? Again, I am going to say that I wish this was written from Sebastian's point of view. The Education of Sebastian was good from Caroline's perspective, but The Education of Caroline really should have been from his. Because really that is what it is, he is having to prove over and over to her that he loves her. Would have been great to be in his head."He'd asked me once if I was brave enough to take a chance on love. I finally knew the answer. "I love you, too, Sebastian. More than you'll ever know."This is the last in the series, and my only major complaint would be the ending. Sebastian and Caroline go through a lot of trauma and heartbreak toward the end. We are left with the idea that it is getting better, and we even get a lovely epilogue. But, I just wanted to see them a lot happier at the end. I wanted to actually witness Sebastian being in a wonderful and peaceful place in his head before we got to the epilogue.All in all, I can not suggest this series more. You will fall in love with these two, your heart will beat with theirs, break with theirs and be put back together with theirs. You will feel every emotion as they come along, and be overjoyed as their obstacles are overcome.ChristineRainy Day Reads

His is a great war story of chaos, war, love, life, and reality.  The love story within the book captivates your attention.  These insta-read summaries are a great buy for any book because without them you might end up realizing if you had checked the insta-read out first you will know if you would love the book or not.  This author does a great job in doing this for all readers.  I highly recommend reading this insta-summary to get you captivated in knowing the entire story.  I would give more information but it would give away all of the details that lie within the book.  A must read, well written and well summarized version.  I highly recommend this book to others.  It’s not just about war but about life.  Even those who do not like war books will love the characters and the way they rise above in the times of war.  Leaving you wanting more to purchase the full version.The blind woman gives you a great view in the world she cannot see but with her perspective you can learn a lot from her view and understanding of times like these.  I highly recommend this book.

reviewText: Lycanthrope book I, by Robert Clark: review, by Dorothy A. BellFollowing a discussion regarding the probability of Lycanthropes, werewolves, existing, walking among them in the guise of regular human beings, a close-knit group of college students mark themselves with a pentagram on the palm of their hand, a calling card to all Lycanthropes in the area to attack at will. That is all but one member, who refuses to indulge in the experiment, leading the reader to think--ah ha, but no, wait. Come the full moon, two of the members are murdered, or I should say, ripped to shreds, disemboweled, ingested, you name it--dead, dead, and real dead.The way in which Robert Clark weaves into his tale the science behind the forensic and law enforcement procedural methods when investigating a horrific murder is what made this novel a compelling read for me, and made it imperative that I read Lycanthrope, book II.

It was an interesting in most places, but there were a couple of spots that I thought were a little slow, but overall it was pretty good.  I would recommend it to other readers who like a little fantasy mixed in with their reality.

reviewText: Finding Penelope follows a thirty-something bestselling Irish romance novelist after her move to a Spanish beach town. Her writing success has enable her to leave Dublin and the suffocating influence of her controlling father and drug addicted brother. Once in a new place with nothing to do but concentrate on her writing and hanging out at the beach with her friend Gwen, she is free to reflect on her family and upbringing, but also poised for new things. Ramon, a handsome school teacher with nothing to do over the summer but playing volleyball in the beach in a fetching swimsuit, is that new thing. A gentle romance is an invitation into living a life Penelope Eames had not been able to previously.Lawless writes with warm, fluid lucidity, and the book flows along nicely, but interestingly it hits two different genres:  following a woman romance writer “finding herself” puts the novel in chick lit territory, which is interesting as the author of the novel is male. At the same time, it is based around reflection and reconciliation of memory and the need to move forward, which is very much what British and Irish literature has been revolving around for the last ten years. Although someone like Ian McEwan is regarded as “literary,” he is writing using the same mix of emotion, memory, and the need to reconcile and change.  Lawless, however, doesn’t have McEwan’s penchant for writing in historical mode (which is probably how McEwan evades the chick-lit label), but Lawless’ contemporary world of ex-pat Brits and Irish having a chance to warm up and grow in different climes actually seems a little more honest.
summary: Finding Oneself in a New Place

Auri is a no-nonsense "Empire" officer; he's just received a promotion and is serving on a new ship.  The first mission is a diplomatic one and Auri has his first encounter with the Felinian race.  Yep... Cat people.  The Felinians are seen by the Empire as barbarians, a simplistic tribal race.  But they are physically larger than humans and have managed to not be defeated by the Empire when the two groups went to war, so the Empire makes peace.Auri has an encounter, mainly he makes eye contact, with the Felinian King, and the King falls for Auri, feels that instant connection and negotiates to have Auri stay with on the planet and become his make.  The Felinian King is assured that Auri has agreed to this arrangement, though that is not the truth.I liked Auri immediately.  He's smart and quick, yet a bit shy, socially inept even, in a way that makes him appear hard nosed to his fellow soldiers.  He grew up on the streets and has the scrappy survival instincts to prove it, as well as the trust issues.The first meeting between Auri and his new Mate does not go well, but I was pleased to see that Auri gave as good as he got, he didn't just go cheeks up for the big hot cat man.What I liked:*This is an interesting world and an interesting culture.  The author did a good job of giving the felinian race depth.  The cat men are sweet and fun, but big, strong and butch as well, I think the author did a good job of integrating cat behavior and instincts into the actions and reactions and behavior of this race.*The progression of the love story was good, not overly rushed.  Hot, sweet, and authentic.  Well, authentic if there where actually space travel and an Empire, and cat people.  The first intimate encounter between Auri and his Cat Man is definitely dubious consent, if you are sensitive to rape and almost-rape then you should be aware that there are definitely some lines crossed in this book.  But I found the first love scene very hot, Auri is on the run and our Felinian King's base instincts take over and he hunts down and claims his mate, it is a scary and rough, but intensely pleasurable experience for Auri.  And King Cat Boy is very sweet and sensitive to Auri's trauma afterwards.*The author does a good job of dealing with the issue of multiple partners, or 'harems'.  I was a little put off by this idea at first, but found that it was well handled.  These are NOT large groups of whore-boys waiting around for their master's attention.  The harem becomes a sort of family, like 'brother' mates, they all share intimacy and come to love each other enough to not have problems with jealousy.  This may not be realistic, but I found it refreshing to read a manaege story that didn't get bogged down in the petty logistics of integrating multiple partners, it's fiction after all, if you want absolute realism then you shouldn't be reading a sci-fi fantasy about Cat People.*The plot beyond the main love story is interesting and well done.  There a twists and turns, our Auri does not stop trying to escape after just one go.  And there is another big plot twist that is well-foreshadowed and worked well within the overall story that added to the overall development of the love story.What I Did Not Like **SOME SPOILERS BELOW**:*There is a rape in this book.  Straight-up, rape.  It is not between our King and his mate, but it does involve a main character.  It was not described in great detail, and the trauma and the after effects are dealt with in a sensitive and realistic manner, but still, be warned.*At one point Auri escapes the planet and is on the run, we end one chapter in the midst of the 'escape' and start the next chapter 2 years later.  This transition was very VERY abrupt, what really bothered me about it was that after Auri is returned to the Felinians this 2 year absence is not addressed when it should, or could, be.  There is a glancing conversation about it, but the time lapse is not really well represented in the overall story, at most points it seems as if no time has lapsed at all. But in the end this was not a big detractor to me.Overall I really enjoyed this story, I hope the author writes more of the Felinians.

This Kindle cover has a beautiful etched leather look and feel. I recently replaced my Kindle Keyboard with a basic Kindle and it just hasn't felt right in my hand, largely, I think because it's not as long, so it doesn't feel right to hold it in one hand. The cover gives the Kindle a more book-like feel simply because it makes it thicker, more like a traditional book.The interior is firm, but has just a slight padding to it so that I feel comfortable shoving it into a purse or diaper bag without having to worry that it would bang against something. Sure, it could still get smashed if slammed around, but the cover provides adequate protection for normal situations.The one drawback to my new cover, and I don't know if it was this was unique to my cover or something that is common to all the Verso covers, but the cover does seem to have some, not exactly wrinkles, but slight rolls in it. They're not immediately visible, but had I picked this in a store, I would have gone through every cover on the shelves to make sure that the "leather" was more tightly stretched so that it didn't have this "flaw." This doesn't at all deter from the usefulness of the cover, nor its overall look, but it does need to be mentioned. For some, it might not be a consideration at all, but if you're paying nearly as much for the cover as for the device it's covering, sometimes it's the little things that make the difference between a 4- or 5-star review.

This is a book that I think should be required reading for anyone who sees the VA as a source of funding to cut, or those who cry for the country to go to war without volunteering to go themselves.It is not just about the severely wounded, and how a few of them have coped with surviving injuries that would have likely killed them in earlier conflicts, it is about the debt the country owes them.It is about the wounds that can't be seen, and the fact that they are just as dangerous - or more - than ones everyone can see.It puts a picture and faces to the people who are owed something for their sacrifice - more than just a paycheck, housing benefits - and it serves as a reminder that we must improve how our wounded veterans and servicemembers are treated.

reviewText: T.L. Burns and K. R. Hughes did a wonderful job recounting the events surrounding Marilyn Monroe's death in this compelling page turner.The story is based on an interesting theory populated by a series of conversations over time, and the authors did a tremendous amount of work recreating the dialogue, setting and characterization of each person and celebrity involved in Marilyn Monroe's demise.I'm familiar with the history behind the assassination of JFK, the life of Jackie Kennedy and even a little regarding the Rat Pack, but this was my first experience learning about Marilyn Monroe.  It was definitely an enjoyable one.  The authors made the dialogue and setting so realistic, you could almost see the Rolls Royces driving down the street and hear Frank Sinatra singing at the piano bar.I enjoyed the pacing of the novel as well; they were careful not to stick to any one subplot for too long.  This technique helped to keep the reader on their toes; at the end of almost every scene there was a cliff hanger.  It got a little tough to follow towards the end as I found there was a lot of jumping back and forth, but it didn't deter from the overall story.Since reading this novel I've definitely become interested in learning a lot more about Marilyn Monroe and others mentioned in What She Knew, and I look forward to reading more, as well as the second novel in the trilogy.Here is an excerpt I particularly enjoyed:"Oh, they'll be all right.  We've known the family they are staying with for years, so no need to worry.""Yes, we do.  Don't you see?  I think Aristotle likes your wife."  Bobby started at his brother, "isn't that a good thing?"  John took another sip."Not when you consider that even the devil can be charming."Well done ladies!  Keep up the good work!
summary: You could almost see the Rolls Royces driving down the street...

reviewText: Linda McDonald has become my newest Favorite Author. I love her writing style, she doesn't waste words on describing the sunset or how the town came to be or blah, blah, blah. It's all action all the time.I wasn't quite as captivated with this book as I was with "Here Comes the Night" but there were parts where I just couldn't put it down. You all know....."just one more chapter", then next thing you know it's one hour later.If you don't mind losing sleep for a day or two pick up any of her books, you won't be disappointed.

I found this book when  friend messaged me on Facebook asking if I had heard of it. She is a fellow lover of biker books. I bought it and here we are!I want to start off by saying that the editing is by no means perfect. A few things are redundant, some words are spelled wrong, and some words are just wrong in the sentence. This wasn't enough to deter me from reading the book because the story is good. This is was the debut book and book two has an editor.This book is about four friends finally being together as they should be. Just kidding. That isn't all it is about. This is a biker book! Bad things happen, sexy things happen, happy and sad things happen. It is a roller coaster of emotions!Editing errors aside (I am trying to emphasize that it is worth reading anyway, folks!) I devoured this book. I put it down only because the author tried to upload a better edited version and had some issues. (I have a nook and I opened a live chat to see if I would get an updated version of my already purchased book and I was basically told they don't know. They also said I was welcome to try putting the book in the cloud archive and re-downloading it to `see what happens' and to `not worry' because they would bring this to the management's attention. Really BN? REALLY?!)Where was I? Oh right, my review. I really enjoyed reading about Hem and Shame. They are both huge, sexy bikers. Mace and Sadey are BFFs that have been in love with their guys since forever even through their differences in age. There is just something that gets me every time about a badass alpha male that feels so strongly for his woman.I even enjoyed reading about a few of the other guys in the Lights of Peril MC. I hope to read more about them in book two. I am told book two will hopefully be out in February 2014 so I will mark that in my calendar!

Also, the list of permitted and disallowed foods comes handy. I loved the interviews as well, the one with Dr Loren Cordain is very informative and the others are interesting as well.I highly recommended this book, Good job by the author, Thanks

This is a great dive into understanding panic attacks, how to deal with them and how to prevent them. Told by an author who has personally experienced them, they understand what you are going through, the stress and worry you must feel when you feel like you are about to die, simply from sheer anxiety. Well this author goes through how to tell the difference between anxiety and normal life stress, how to be prepared for panic attacks, how to deal with panic attacks while you are having one (various steps to reduce their severity), and steps you can take to potentially reduce or remove the panic attacks from returning. The author also talks about who to turn to and when to seek help when you are suffering from panic attacks. Great resource.
summary: Wonderful information from someone who's been there

I've never read anything like this before. Clockworkers is a very good urban fantasy that adds a dark and interesting twist to creatures we often find in fairy tales.Awesome characters. The main character, Sam, is easy to dislike, but I admire her for being ambitious and practical. She knows what she wants and she works to get it. I also like that she's simple and refuses to be dictated by the norms just so she can sell her watches. And the Kith! I love Piv. I like his innocence and childlike nature. He's funny and smart and his elf-logic, though sometimes frustrating, is astonishing. The other Kith are amazing, too. They have different personalities but they're all interesting and talented. Even Hax is a colorful, albeit creepy, character.I really enjoyed reading this book. I loved the twists and turns of the story. There was a bit of a slack in the middle but I was really hooked into it that I didn't mind the dull parts that much. It had the right amount of mystery and suspense while sticking to the fantasy genre. There were bits of humor, too, courtesy of the Kith. The different tales about the Kith were rich and nicely delivered. The author did a good job in incorporating these tales to his own story.Clockworkers is an amazing fantasy read. I definitely recommend this book to those who like their fantasy with a dark twist.

reviewText: In this story, we follow young Todd as he travels to his grandfather's village and meets new people, some his own age like Andrew and the lovely Marigold, some older like Shaun, and some really old, but all interesting and weird in Todd's opinion. Todd unravels his past bit by bit as he encounters friendship, love, greed, and hatred. The author's incredible writing talent and descriptions put us right into the setting of Wildwood and let us discover the magic of the forest through Todd's eyes. No one can weave suspense and paranormal the way H. Scott-Taylor does. Add to that action, emotion, and humor, and you have a highly enjoyable story I highly recommend.

5 stars!!!<I received an ARC from the author in exchange for an honest review>I loved this book! It has so many of the elements that I love in a great romance book. First we have hot Cowboys. Who can resist these men? Second we have a beautiful love story. Third and best of all, the book’s suspense story will keep you on the edge of your seat.With that said let me hop right into the nitty-gritty. Sean O’Connell is on the down and out. He is a Champion Bull Rider that has got caught up in the life behind the chutes instead of his career. His drinking and partying is keeping him from a life he could have. Sean feels alone. He and his sister are estranged because of blame and Sean being drunk all the time. Catherine is a hard-worker, dedicated to her family and a real jewel. She is called out of college to take care of her ailing Uncle Ray and his son Junior. (I loved Junior) She does not regret her choice at all. They saved her many years ago and she will do anything for them. Catherine carries around a tragic past and is afraid to trust anyone. A stranger in a truck one night and saving him from the cold will change her life forever.Sean and Catherine have chemistry. The angst and tension in the story are palpable in every chapter. The story is quite angsty that a few times I was yelling at my kindle to these characters. (good writing) The sex was very well written you had to use your imagination. Very refreshing. You are a fly on the wall for all of the ups and downs. I shared the characters joy, tears, heartbreak, sadness and many laugh out loud moments. Catherine is a strong heroine and I love a story that has a strong female. She is not going to settle but is willing to forgive. Catherine’s emotional baggage is so heavy she can hardly pick up the suitcase. Sean is a hot alpha male cowboy that knows what he wants and is not afraid to go after it. But he’s afraid of love and commitment bottom line. Together they’re strong and have an amazing passionate relationship.Stephanie did a beautiful job writing this story. It flowed so smoothly until the last words. If you want to know about how ranching and rodeoing life really is then this story will give you that insight. If you just love to dream about this life then you will have a stunning picture painted for you. The cowboys in this story live the real cowboy lifestyle. This is working their ranches 6 to 7 days a week no matter the weather conditions are. It was like I was riding right along side on my beautiful sorrel working the cattle and watching spring come to life.The suspense in the story will keep you biting your fingernails. I was ready to jump right into the middle of all the action. The story has it all tragedy, suspense and beautiful healing. The secondary characters are incredible and make the story complete.I would highly recommend this book to all. I am looking forward to reading the next installment in this series. Keep ‘em coming Stephanie!My Favorite Quotes:He was the whole package, candy to her sweet tooth.“An old Indian proverb says if you save a man’s life, you’re responsible for him forever,” Sean said.“Honey, two weeks might as well be two years unless it involves bull riding. Everything else is just fluff.” – SeanShe worked to keep her wild woman caged. Sean owned the key. – Catherine“What’s a quilt show? Some kind of movie about blankets?” – SeanCowboy law said a man walked away from an injury unless he was unconscious. It was one of the laws in the code of the west, and tough cowboys followed the code. – Sean
summary: Hot Cowboy + Strong Heroine = Amazing Love Story

reviewText: The prologue- even the text prior to it was a little emotional and I wonder if I could survive the novel with my heart intact.Tori was Will's smart-mouth redhead. They thought everything will go on smoothly. They have liked each other since forever and was about to go in their first date. BUT THEY WERE SO WRONG. Because during their supposedly-perfect date - something bad happened and it had been haunting Tori.She had been through a lot. I think most of us wouldn't really know the extent of her suffering unless we experience what she had (I hope none of us will). Tori had been strong, but the incident weakened her. She lost herself, opted to be alone and suffer rather than sought for help. She ran away from it. She thought it was her fault.Will - awwww. He was not just a great boyfriend, but he was a greater friend. He didn't leave her side when he finally knew what was going on. He didn't pressure her to do anything she wasn't ready for. He supported her decisions and was always there for her. He may have done something that night that has been eating him up - but it was a reflex on his part to save his ego. Nevertheless, this guy stole my heart!The secondary characters, namely Charlie from Love Notes (Book 1) & her mother were pretty great too. They were the best support system anyone could have. Charlie had needed her on the first book, and now Tori needs her, but she doesn't ask question even though the nightmares that her friend is having concerns her. She knew that when Tori is finally ready, she will tell her.Tori's journey in overcoming her guilt, seeking for help, finally accepting that it happened to her and learning to open her heart is indeed emotional. Heather Gunter made an incredible novel about a journey of a girl who's world fell apart after one night, found her strength and was brave enough to fight for what is right. I like the strength of her character, and the person she had become by the end of the novel. This story gives HOPE to girls who have underwent the same nightmares as Tori did. It is an inspiration, that somehow there is always a rainbow after the storm, and  not all men are beasts because time WILL come that a prince charming will still find he's way to sweep you off your feet.Although part of the series, you can read Heartstrings as a stand-alone. I think I'm hooked with this series and I couldn't wait to get my hands on the next one - Ashley's story: Changing Tunes. Who can resist a reformed bad-girl falling in love with a good boy?*ARC Copy was given in exchange for an honest review.

Being Chased is a romantic suspense, so the summary implies, but the real suspense is whether our protagonists will grow up. I had to keep reminding myself that our characters are not 15 years old but adults.  I only got to 25% of the book, but that portion of the story was simply... I like you, no I don't, yes I do, okay maybe I do but I shouldn't, okay I will keep my hands to myself, nah I think I will make a pass at you, whoopsy lets be friends, why don't you like me?  Seriously!I am sure that there is a mystery and suspense somewhere but I cannot get passed the immaturity of our characters. They are just that annoying.  They do annoying things, think annoying things, and "speak" like a horny teenager.  If I had a choice between being locked in a room with them or fighting werewolves, I would choose werewolves.I can end on a positive. Characters aside, the writer does have potential and maybe a better editor is necessary to cut out the 50% of annoying hot/cold conversations and bubblegum speak. Sorry I really wanted to give it a chance but I just did not know when I would get off the rollercoaster. Thanks.

reviewText: Wow, Wake was absolutely fantastic.  This incredibly engaging and totally addicting book kept me reading long into the early morning hours.  It is a beautifully written, compelling, emotional and sometimes humorous story of two very damaged souls who fall in love in the midst of illness and tragedy.Jem Harper is in cancer remission.  He has been at this school since his cancer was first discovered and has no friends.  He is lonely and miserable, tired and sick.  He is no longer the popular, gorgeous and friendly guy he once was at his old school.  Willa Kirk comes back to her old town and is suffering from a tragic past of her own.  Her sister died of cancer and she is angry, hostile and feels responsible for her death.  Jem and Willa become frenemies then friends and eventually lovers as they bond over their mutual loss; Jem's loss of his former healthy self and Willa over the loss of her sister.  Willa takes care of Jem by feeding him and loving him physically and emotionally.  She often tries to convince him to love himself for who he is now as she does and to see himself as beautiful.  Jem tries to help Willa to forgive herself and to move on from the death of her sister. He has some issues with how she handled things with her sister, but knows she is a good person and wants her to realize it too.This touching love story will leave you emotionally exhausted and rooting for Jem and Willa to be together despite the odds against them.  I highly recommend this incredible story about survival, love, sacrifice and giving oneself over completely to another.

I was gifted a copy of this book.Pierce is a hard, brooding, and sometimes down right angry, but he has a side to him no one ever sees. A side that is brought out by a loud, blunt, speaks her mind woman. Rachel is who she is and makes no move to change that. One unexpected night of lust and passion, leaves Rachel more involved with Pierce than either one of them had planned. Little did each of them know, that they had found the key to finally becoming happy.“You made me, you broke me, and now you’re going to save me.”Amanda Heath has created a world that will literally suck you in. Book one, Make Me owned me, I devoured Break Me, and Save Me sucked me in from the beginning. One of the things I love the most about these books is the facet that all the characters are friends/enemies and are in each book. This book was focused on Pierce and Rachel’s strange yet beautiful relationship, but we still got to see plenty from all the other amazingly hilarious characters.Reading this story from a complete male point of view was great, because you really got to see the real Pierce and not the dick he always portrayed himself to be. We finally got to see Pierce’s happily ever after, and truthfully after the ending of Break Me, he deserved it.“Yeah, I love you. I think I might die if I didn’t love you.”Rachel is loud, makes people uncomfortable, says what is on her mind and I loved every minute of her! There is honestly nothing I would change about her.“I know Pierce and Annabella hung out with us, but it wasn’t much. Now we get stuck with emo Pierce. A least Annabella was nasty, which made things fun.”Some how with Pierce and Rachel being completely different, they were still very much a like. They both found happiness and love in something they never thought they would find.Even though the series isn’t over, I feel like Pierce and Rachel’s story was such an epic conclusion. After finishing Save Me, I was left so happy and content. This book, as well as the others in this series, has just enough angst, heartache, funny moments, and a whole lot of sexy to keep just about anyone interested. Overall, this was an amazingly written book that I couldn’t put down and I would highly suggest this series to just about everyone.[...]

reviewText: ***Received from Tasty Book Tours for an honest review***"I love you."It takes a fair amount of bravery to announce your sentiment for someone else because these three words can either scare the receiver to death or compel them to say the same. The hope is the feelings are mutual and you will hear "I love you" in return. But the flip-side is, it doesn't always happen that way.Rebecca's declaration of love left Zach speechless enough for her to believe he didn't feel the same. It took seven months of separation for him to realize he did feel the same and it took just as long for him to say it. The problem: their relationship was non-existent and might be irreparable at that point.There are plenty of highs and lows in this story as Zach and Rebecca try to move on--with or without each other--after meeting again after so many months apart. They circled round and round with their emotions and hearts carefully guarded until they reached a place where they were fairly open with one another. Well, more open than before.Still, secrets lay between them and happiness, secrets that eventually came to light and not in the most tactful way possible. Perhaps the tactless revelation could have been avoided if Zach had been more honest with Rebecca. I mean, he knew her secret (which wasn't a secret at all) and still he chose to hide things from her? *tsk* I wanted to slap him for his reluctance.I enjoyed this story. It moved a little quick for me, and there were moments when I thought emotions were lacking, but I liked watching Zach and Rebecca work through their issues. Ms. Charles wrote a very sweet love story that not only shows a couple falling in love again but is a good opening to her "Time for Love" series.
summary: A Time To Fall In Love Again

reviewText: This is Book 2 in a series of 5 full length, dramatic, sexy, and addictive paranormal romantic suspense stories, revolving around the lives of contemporary Lycans. There's a lot of heart ache, with enough humor so you don't want to kill yourself. They could be stand alones, but have connecting characters and a continuing story line, and should be read from the beginning. I do wish authors would number their books, and my thanks to reviewer Carole for putting them in order.Eve is an artist, working in a bustling city. She is also a Fae, and when her "Gift" kicks in, she is completely over-whelmed. She leaves the city and rents a cabin in the woods, hoping the solitude will help her sort out her new-found abilities.Rafe is a Werewolf and owns the cabin in the woods. He's not happy about renting, but needs the income to renovate his property. Eve is unaware that Lycans exist, and he needs to make sure she never finds out. To make things worse, a rogue wolf has invaded his territory!I'm going to be vague about this next part, because I don't want to give anything away, but for those of you who have read the first two books, the person we have all worried about, gets dealt with later on in the series. Whew!Some of the other books got a little caught up in too much detail, and I skimmed over parts of them. Eg: If you get stuck in a cave, get in, get out, get on with the story. And I have a complaint about The Keeping. There was absolutely no need to kill off a certain character. It was not intricate to the plot, and all it did was make me feel bad. Please, Nicky, do not do that again.I chose to write a review about Betrayed because it is fast paced, with a great blend of action, dialogue, and romance. I'm so wrapped up with these damned wolves, I can't wait for the next book to come out!The Law of the Lycans:BondedBetrayedThe MatingThe KeepingThe Finding

He has undergone tragedy in his young life, but has a fast friend in his master's daughter, Jade. His penchant for getting into fights lands him first into trouble and then into training to become a prize fighter.There are many great things about this book. I could tell that the author had a lot of experience with wrestling/fighting and the details felt very real and spot on. I thought that Jade, Earnest, Grace, and his master were wonderful characters. The book was easy to read and fast paced.My main issue with this book is that it feels like the first episode in a series. Perhaps this was the intent of the author, but I like to feel some sense of completion after the first novel. Furthermore, the story is very predictable, and although I enjoyed reading it, because I can anticipate the ending of the whole series, it didn't seem incredibly important to continue reading.That said, I believe that this is a very good read for young boys, especially those who don't like to read-- this is an easy to like, well written and fast paced novel with great characters and description.

reviewText: As a native Hebrew speaker, I know very well the difficulties of learning English as a second language, and this book nails it. The only way to learn a language is to use it, and the best way to use it is through immersion in the daily natural conversation.A language is also a culture; humor, history, literature - you can not get it from a tape. You need the stories, the expressions...As a young man, I learned English best through traveling, and when I didn't have English speakers around, through reading and corresponding. Not as good as natural conversation, but much better than artificial studies. I later in my life had a chance to study another language, very intensely, but with little natural conversation - it didn't work nearly as well. My experience is that this book describes the best way to learn a new language.

Scott Rhine has always had the ability to create amazing characters, which is one of the things that I have always loved about his books. This book is no exception. His bad guys make you want to take a shower, or run away, and everyone else is a shade of grey - just a regular human being, with your standard quirks and foibles that come with the territory. What Scott does is make each unique and interesting, then he makes their interactions on any level, emotional or otherwise quite a kick. He always makes you think as a reader, and that is fabulous. I hate it when an author thinks a reader is stupid and spells every last things out for you three times over.Now in this book, you add a lot of hard science to that mixture and some power hungry executives and governments,some really bad people, war, and a very mentally messed up scientist, and the stage is set for some interesting things to happen, especially when most of the characters are living on an alien spacecraft with a job to do, and a world in chaos. Wow! As a fan of hard science books, I have no problem with the technology or the science, and I am sure some people will, but the human factor that Scott adds into the story turns this into a real human interest tale instead of just a geeky story about aliens and scientists. It is so much more than that - in fact in is in a completely new class by itself when it comes to these things.There are some sensitive subjects here, including rape, that will put some people off - especially women. If you can get beyond that, and you have read the other books in the series, because it is worth it to read the other books, they are outstanding - then read this one too. Scott has done it again. He has created a new genre which wraps hard science and human interest into one. ( I could combine the titles but by combining the first words we come up with something obscene, so i won't name the new genre). Bravo Scott! I can't wait to read Oblivion. It is bound to be spectacular, and I am waiting to see what is going to happen with that alien spacecraft.
summary: Amazing Mix of Hard Science and Great Characters

reviewText: Three Sisters introduces us to Emily Castles.  Emily lives in London and is attending a neighborhood Halloween party.  What a party this turns out to be!  With so many strange things happening you don't know if it is part of the show or not.  Emily is grieving the loss of her Golden Retriever, Jessie and thinks of him often while trying to enjoy the party.  When an act goes horribly wrong, Emily is sure that she has witnessed a murder.  The only trouble is, no body!  With the help of the quirky Dr Muriel, Emily will snoop around until she finds out what is going on.I enjoyed reading this short story and being introduced to Emily.  I am also a dog lover so that part of the story drew me in.  I usually don't read short stories but this one was good.  I would like to learn more of Emily's back story and get to know her character better.  I also like the London setting.  You will breeze through this book.  If you like a good cozy mystery, I recommend reading this one.

I received a free copy of Outsiders from Bailey Vaughn for my honest review.This was a quick, interesting read. The whole time I really had no idea how it was going to end or where it was going; it was a page turner. It has great potential and it was developed very well.The grammar wasn't the best and it was often confusing. Usually, I won't be too harsh about it; I understand it's difficult for an independent author to have professional proofreading done. But, this really did take away from the story and was rather distracting. Also, I feel like the author could have been more descriptive. There were a lot of times where it was hard to picture the situation.Being from a small town in Pennsylvania myself, I understood how life was before the Outsiders overtook them. I could relate to the weather patterns and everything.I enjoyed this book and I really liked how Hannah's situation did work out. It was depressing, but as she said, it was better the way it did end up. It's a nice refreshing change from those typical miraculous endings to so many books.

Honestly, I wasn't sure what to expect when I first saw this book and started to read it. I was expecting it to be a highly religious book, but I was pleasantly surprised to find it is much more than that. I'm not a very religious person, but I am not against religion and I actually enjoy reading into the history of where religion comes from.The beginning of the book seemed very bleak for poor Tony, losing his wife and seemingly having nothing left in his life going for him. I feel like everyone hits this point in their life to varying degrees, and it makes the whole story line very easy to relate to. I love the journey that this book brings you on, and at many parts I could feel myself becoming emotional. My favorite part of the book is the romance between Tony and Miri, and I love the way that Ron Deloy implements love and other elements into his book to create much more depth than just simple religious teachings.I would recommend this book to everyone with an open mind. It has many life lessons that can be learned, regardless of your religious beliefs. "The Jesus Cure" by Ron Deloy is an amazing and insightful book that you will not regret reading.
summary: An amazing journey for everyone–regardless of religious beliefs

The PremiseIn the final book of the Hat Trick Series, Garrick, Savannah and Rhian have to learn to navigate this new and unexplored territory.  *old timey radio soap announcer voice* How do Savannah and Rhian share Garrick?  How do they feel about each other?  Who's watching Rhian?  A soapy triad romance...next after these sex scenes. :DThe GoodThis series has been a fully developed revelation in menage romance.  In previous menage books I've read (MMF and MFM), I've had a hard time believing in the equality of feelings for all participants and it usually ended up feeling like what it usually is - PWP (porn without plot).  I've thought that one relationship, whether it be MF or MM, is the "main" one and the additional person is just that - more body parts to play with.  In this trilogy, Ms. Wayland took the time to develop each relationship individually so that when they all eventually come together (c'mon - who could resist? :P) it all plays out in such a way that I truly believe they all love each other.  That's a rare thing.A good portion of this final book is all about Rhian and Savannah connecting with each other, with believable bumps along the way.  I almost looked at it as their own romance within the context of their love for Garrick.Oh, and um, HOT. Triad. Sex.The Not as GoodAs much as I enjoyed the triad sex, I could have done with less of it and more of Rhian's family story - that part felt rushed and underwhelming with his mother/brother being cardboard villains with little purpose other than to create external tension.  As much as I understood Rhian's emotional neediness, sometimes it was a bit much.  Also, while it was cute to integrate Ms. Wayland's other triad romances, it felt a bit much to have that many triads popping up left and right.The Bottom LineGood series, with erotica and emotional development. It may not be for everyone, but it entertained me lol.
summary: Excellent Ending to a Excellent Triad Romance Trilogy

Contrary to what people might think, it's easy to write a surprise ending for a book... just have someone do something completely unexpected, the more unexpected, the bigger the surprise. Unfortunately, it's not that easy to write an effective surprise ending because, in addition to being fooled, readers must feel the ending flows logically from what's gone on before, even if they didn't see it coming.Aaron Patterson's thriller novelette, "The Craigslist Killer," is a generally effective story that's unfortunately dragged down, in the last couple of pages by an ending that doesn't make sense in the context of the story. The book concerns a group of college age buddies who come up with a challenge bet for one of them. They dare a smooth operator named Bill that he can't meet a total stranger on Craigslist and get two dates with her within thirty days. Somehow, the bet goes from $10 to $50,000 in a matter of minutes, a sum Bill doesn't have; in fact, he doesn't even have a car at the moment. I'm not sure what type of college students bet that kind of money, no matter how drunk they are, but, the bet drives the plot.By naming his story "The Craigslist Killer" instead of something more innocuous, author Patterson starts playing a mind game from this moment on with the reader, who knows based on that title that something bad is going to happen as a result of one of Bill's attempted hookups. And Bill does hookup rather easily and quickly, with a good looking girl named Amy. For anyone thinking of dating someone on Craigslist, the story provides some good, entertaining do's and don'ts. What is more likely to keep reader interest however, is the inevitable following of the details of the encounter between Bill and Amy so that the reader can try to spot signs of something bad coming. Patterson is able to build suspense fairly well through use of the title gimmick.I don't want to spoil anything, but, as the story title suggests, there's more involved here than a big bet about a date. Some very unexpected things occur, and the story actually has two successive surprise endings. The first probably won't come as too much of a surprise for those who read the story carefully, but it is satisfying. If Patterson had ended the story at that point, I'd have given it a higher rating. Unfortunately, he tries to "top" himself with a second, completely surprising ending in a two-page epilogue. It's this second ending that will have readers scratching their heads trying to figure out where it came from. And, since the final ending doesn't really add anything to the story, it merely diminishes the effectiveness of everything Patterson did before that.Patterson knows how to write a solid thriller. Although the story is less than 40 pages long, the author provides all the plot details needed to construct a scenario that feels realistic. Even the character development, especially that of Bill and Amy, is more fully established than in a lot of books ten times as long. If Patterson had chosen to end the story before that unfortunate epilogue, I would have enjoyed it considerably more. As it is, the ending breaks the mood solely for the sake of "surprise." However, while the surprise is certainly unexpected, it's also anticlimactic. As a result, a killer of a story feels a lot less lethal.

reviewText: Juliana Jones aka JJ, divorced and jobless, decides to put her worries behind her one drunken night when she and her travel agent pal book her on a cruise, hoping she’ll find fun, sun, and maybe a little fling. However, her plans seem to run ashore once she discovers that the cruise isn’t quite what she expected it to be…it’s a Second Honeymoon cruise for senior citizens! Kate’s dismayed to find herself young enough to be the granddaughter of all the golden aged couples on board. However, fortune smiles upon her when she meets Kane, the young and hunky fitness director who has his own past that he’s running away from…and there’s instant chemistry between the two of them.Lust and laughter ensue, from secret kisses in the broom closet to the geriatric cruisers who get up to some amusing hijinks of their own, including a secret betting pool on just how far things will go between the young couple. What are the odds that JJ and Kane can sail off into a happy ending?

Finding this book was serendipity. My daughter-in-law gave me her old Jack Lalaine juicer a week before. We just moved to an area of California that has year round harvest and there is a great farm stand near our house. I had no excuse not to try juicing.I need specific direction when trying out something new and I found it in the book. Elizabeth Swann explains in detail why doing a juice fast is beneficial. Exactly how to achieve success by preparing for it with guidelines, the top ten benefits, dos and don'ts, a shopping list of what to have on hand, and how to ease into it. You'll know what to expect and the side effects possibly experienced.Twenty delicious recipes are included. What I found the most helpful is the list of fruits and vegetables and how to juice them. I'd been having a horrible time with kale jamming up my juicer, but she explains to roll the leaves and follow with a firmer product like an apple quarter or part of a cucumber. It worked wonderfully. Allowing the pith of a lemon because it aids in the digestion of the essential components of lemons was very interesting.The chapter on ORAC values was intriguing. I have a hefty collection of Wisdom of the Earth essential oils that can be ingested and plan on following the guideline in the book using oils in the juice.Using the three day juicing fast as a personal retreat fascinated me!The book was so inspiring, I am really looking forward to increasing my juicing days now.
summary: Excellent, motivational guide to juicing for health and weight loss

Improper Relations is a debut novella from Juliana Ross and is perfect if you're looking for a quick, sexy, historical read. At around 60 pages there isn't a lot of time for character building and to develop the relationship between Hannah and Leo but it was still a satisfying read.Hannah was left penniless after her husband's death so was grateful to be offered the position of ladies maid to his aunt. As the poor relation she isn't exactly welcomed into the family but at least she has a roof over her head and food to eat. Leo is the younger son and the black sheep of the family, she has always been intrigued by him but it is when she catches him getting down and dirty with one of the maids in the library that she becomes really fascinated. Although Hannah is no virgin she is innocent. She never felt pleasure with her husband and was brought up to believe that sex was something that women had to endure so it shocks her that the maid seems to enjoy Leo's attentions. When he offers to teach her how pleasurable love making can be she can't resist.Leo is more than willing to teach Hannah everything he knows and I did like the fact that she was able to put her shyness to one side and go for what she wanted. The lessons were certainly steamy but I have to admit that when someone so innocent that she has never even seen a man naked before becomes a deep throat expert on her first attempt at a BJ it really irritates me. Improper Relations is great if you just want a steamy read that you can finish in one sitting but I would have enjoyed it a lot more if there had been more time to flesh out the characters and make me really believe that they fell in love. Juliana Ross has a promising writing style though and I would love to see what she can do with a full length novel.

If you ever doubt the ability of a male author to spin a beautiful love story, pick up this set by Charles Sheehan-Miles. He's amazing.Just Remember to Breathe:Dylan and Alex have a past. They have broken each other's hearts and ripped each other to shreds. And now they meet again, years later, placed in a situation where they must work together. As they set out to put rules in place to allow them to do their job without focusing on their past, their history refuses to be ignored, and they find themselves slowly working through it, and falling in love again. But they're both broken in different ways, and they have to battle not only their shared past, but their own individual insecurities. I couldn't put this book down. The story tore at my heart and made me want to wrap Dylan up and hug him. Loved that while the ending is what I wished for and wanted to happen, it wasn't wrapped up in a tidy bow of perfection.A Song for Julia:Once again Charles has given me everything I could ask for in a book. Characters I fall in love with, backstories that take my breath away, and a story that sucks me in and won't let me go until I've read the last word.When we first meet Crank and Julia, I thought they were going to be the typical "rich girl" and "punk rocker." I've never been happier to be proven wrong. Julia's history is heartbreaking, and her strength in overcoming it, despite having virtually no support system leaves me in awe. And Crank. Sigh. How can you not adore Crank? From his touchy relationship with his dad (whom I ADORED), to his complete devotion to Sean, he's completely lovable, and at the same time so far from perfect that he's believable.Together they're something that so many authors strive for, but fall short of, and that's REAL. Their story isn't easy. It isn't all roses and rainbows. They carry the reader on a ride that is breathtaking and heart stopping and completely memorable.The Last Hour:When I first met Ray and Carrie in "Just Remember to Breathe," I was intrigued. I knew that there just HAD to be more to their story, and was thrilled when I heard that Charles was writing a book ALL about them. Everything about their relationship was full throttle, no holds barred, and no holding back. The fact that normally reserved Carrie went full tilt into it, gave some insight into how the rest of their story would go.So...when I was given the opportunity to read "The Last Hour," I jumped at it. Within the first 3 pages, the book took my breath away. The accident. Gosh how I cried, and spent the entire book praying for Ray's recovery. I loved the insight we got into his thoughts, how he felt, and his reactions to what was going on around him. Learning what Ray and Carrie had faced in their brief time together gave me an understanding of the two of them that made me love them more. And in the end, Ray's choice, though it killed me, proved what a truly good and unselfish man he is.Charles has written a story that jerked me into it from the very first words and kept me there until I finished. There is NO way I can do justice to his work with my words. All I can say is, read this book. It will make you laugh and cry, and leave you feeling like you've just been through the wringer, but it's worth it.
summary: I wish I could give more stars

reviewText: Another great Ben Hood adventure.This one starts with Ann Kelly.Kelly is a 49 year old woman who runs a cattle ranch in far North Queensland. A ranch that she's running with one hired hand.Kelly is also a woman who's six year old daugher was kidnapped two years ago. A daughter who was taken two months after her husband had left her.Parts of her daughters bloodstained clothes were found and the coroner has finally declared her dead. This is something her Mother just can't accept.Kelly's other daugher, Margarett, is housed in a facility for the insane. Kelly's life is in the toilet and she wants answers about her missing daughter.Kelly has called Rod from VIP and requested Ben Hood be sent to find her missing daughter or find out if she's dead.Rod contacts Ben who's really not interested in the case . Its an investigation and he really doesn't like to do investigations. Ben doesn't like dealing with the police which is something he would surely have to do.However Ben decides to go to North Queensland and see exactly how much the police have on the case and if its something he can help with.So begins one great read.This one has two missing six year old girls, a biker gang, assorted locals who know more than they are telling, Margarette who is no more crazy than Ben is, Margarette who knows more than she's told anyone, April a friend of Margarettes who also knows more than she's told the police, the beautiful police inspector in charge of the case,  law enforcement who can only do so much as they have to follow the letter of the law, a Superintendant who want the biker leader in jail, a few bikers who take runs at Ben, dead bikers, bikers in the hospital and  Ben Hood who's able to put the pieces together and solve the crime.Just one super read and well worth those five stars mate.
summary: Another great one from Lindsay. Hood just rocks.

reviewText: I read this book in just a couple of hours and was disappointed, the story was unrealistic, in the span of a couple of weeks the main characters go through about five or six life changing events and then all of a sudden they are in love and live happily ever after? Character development was poor and the main characters sounded like they were in their early twenties instead of closer to forty. If just one of these events happened to me, it would take months to start to get back on my feet. If the book had been longer and the events had more detail it would have been plausible. Surprise attack of Protectorate forces isn't that plausible either. Don't Earth fleet and planetary defense keep any watch of surrounding space?But despite these blunders the book is a good distraction from our boring mundane life, so I'll at least try the second part of the series.
